records.version_scope: Set 17 guide plus version-unspecified general economy guide, accessed 2026-09-02
records.rule_support: Gold can be allocated between interest, leveling and rerolling; shop odds and unit pools vary with level.
records.practical_support: Both guides distinguish win/loss-streak, reroll and Fast 8/9 lines and recommend spending early when health or board strength requires stabilization.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact thresholds and timings are set- and lobby-dependent; this record does not preserve a numeric leveling recipe.
records.mechanism: Interest is an opportunity-cost engine rather than a mandatory savings cap.
records.engine: Round income, interest, streak income and level-dependent shop odds
records.state_resource: Gold, experience, health, streak and shop pool
records.trigger: Each preparation round and any health/tempo inflection point
records.scope: Player economy and current board
records.payoff: Earlier board strength or later access to higher-cost units
records.survival: Spend before the nominal economy cap when continued losses threaten elimination
records.spatial_condition: Indirect; the purchased board must still be positioned to realize the spend
records.payoff_owner: Current board when stabilizing; future high-cost carry when leveling
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Choose between holding interest, leveling, slow rolling and rolling down based on health and available pairs.
records.counterplay: Opponent tempo and shared-pool contestation shorten the safe saving window.
records.failure_explanation: A loss can be attributed to greed, mistimed leveling or an unsuccessful roll-down, while shop variance remains a limitation.
records.transferability: Use health pressure and visible enemy strength to make saving versus spending a real choice.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project is single-player and need not copy interest brackets or an eight-player shared pool.
records.project_question: What enemy preview and health pressure make an early stabilization purchase rational in a tower run?

records.version_scope: Version-unspecified practical guides accessed 2026-09-02
records.rule_support: Items are assigned to units and consume components that cannot simultaneously be reserved for another completed item.
records.practical_support: The guides recommend flexible early item slams and temporary item holders to preserve health before transferring direction to a final carry.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Transfer details and component recipes vary by set; the sources are from one practical-guide publisher.
records.mechanism: A temporary holder bridges early survival and late payoff ownership.
records.engine: Immediate item completion on a currently available unit
records.state_resource: Item components, holder availability, health and future carry options
records.trigger: A usable component pair arrives before the final carry
records.scope: One temporary unit and the board it stabilizes
records.payoff: Convert dormant components into current combat power without fully locking the final composition
records.survival: Frontline, sustain or flexible damage items reduce health loss during transition
records.spatial_condition: The holder must occupy a safe or effective role-appropriate position
records.payoff_owner: Temporary holder first, final carry after transition
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Recruit an adequate holder now while keeping multiple final carries compatible with the item profile.
records.counterplay: A narrow item slam can become stranded if the compatible carry is contested or unavailable.
records.failure_explanation: The player can distinguish holding unusable components too long from committing them to an overly narrow holder.
records.transferability: Provide explicit bridge units or transfer rules so early equipment is useful without predetermining the run.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project may not allow TFT-style free item movement after selling a unit.
records.project_question: Which equipment can be safely transferred, and what cost preserves commitment without creating dead early rewards?

records.version_scope: Version-unspecified practical guides accessed 2026-09-02
records.rule_support: Units, items and augments are separate acquisition channels that jointly determine available board power.
records.practical_support: Guides advise choosing a composition from shops, items, augments, economy, health and contestation instead of forcing a preset list.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This is a guide recommendation rather than measured population behavior; all three pages share a publisher.
records.mechanism: Composition direction emerges from several partially independent signals.
records.engine: Repeated offers across shop, item and augment channels
records.state_resource: Owned units, components, augments, gold, health and opponent contestation
records.trigger: Each offer and major stabilization point
records.scope: Whole composition
records.payoff: Select a line with both reachable pieces and a viable payoff owner
records.survival: Prefer a cheaper stable line when health and economy cannot fund the theoretical ceiling
records.spatial_condition: A candidate line must still field sufficient frontline and protect its carry
records.payoff_owner: The carry selected by the converging signals
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Delay hard commitment until signals converge, but avoid repeatedly pivoting after costs become sunk.
records.counterplay: Opponent contestation weakens a line even when its items and augment appear suitable.
records.failure_explanation: The record separates premature forcing from over-pivoting; both can destroy resource coherence.
records.transferability: Let roster offers, equipment and relics cross-check one another instead of assigning a build from a single tag.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has planned enemy packages rather than human contestation.
records.project_question: How many independent signals should agree before the UI labels a tower-run direction as established?

records.version_scope: Version-unspecified practical guides accessed 2026-09-02
records.rule_support: Players place units on a bounded board before automatic combat and can inspect other boards during preparation.
records.practical_support: The positioning guide uses scouting to move a backline carry away from jumps, hooks, stuns and burst and to use the main tank to influence targeting.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Advice depends on the current unit roster and on which opponent is selected; the sources share a publisher.
records.mechanism: Scouting converts enemy information into a limited precombat spatial adaptation.
records.engine: Visible opponent layouts and manual unit placement
records.state_resource: Preparation time, board cells and probable opponent set
records.trigger: Before each automatic combat
records.scope: Formation and first-contact targeting
records.payoff: Extend carry uptime or redirect initial enemy pressure
records.survival: Backline protection and main-tank placement
records.spatial_condition: Side, row, adjacency and access path relative to hook, jump, stun or burst threats
records.payoff_owner: Protected carry
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Positioning can rescue a compatible board without buying replacements, but cannot repair a missing frontline role.
records.counterplay: Opponents can also scout and swap sides, so the adaptation is probabilistic rather than a solved puzzle.
records.failure_explanation: Initial targeting and threat access make spatial mistakes observable, though uncertain matchmaking limits certainty.
records.transferability: Telegraph the next enemy package and let formation be the response window.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Single-player combat does not need last-second human mind games.
records.project_question: Which enemy intents must be previewed so a formation loss feels attributable rather than arbitrary?

records.version_scope: Set 17 leveling guide cross-checked with general economy and comp-selection guides
records.rule_support: Level changes shop odds and a shared finite pool affects the chance of finding repeated low-cost units.
records.practical_support: Reroll lines stay at a cost-appropriate level, preserve enough economy for repeated shops and alter timing when health or contestation becomes unsafe.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact roll odds, pool sizes and viable reroll carries are version-specific.
records.mechanism: Foregoing levels increases repeated access to a low-cost payoff owner.
records.engine: Cost-weighted shop odds plus duplicate-based upgrades
records.state_resource: Gold, level, copies, bench space, health and shared-pool availability
records.trigger: Reach the target level and sufficient copies/economy
records.scope: One low-cost carry and its support board
records.payoff: Three-star low-cost carry power spike
records.survival: Frontline items and a timed roll-down prevent elimination before completion
records.spatial_condition: Carry must avoid direct backline access while the frontline buys uptime
records.payoff_owner: The upgraded low-cost carry
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Slow roll while safe; roll down or abandon the chase when health, copies or contestation fail the line.
records.counterplay: Contest the same copies, accelerate lobby damage or attack the carry's position.
records.failure_explanation: Missing copies, excessive greed and unsafe positioning are separable failure causes.
records.transferability: An upgrade chase needs both a statistical completion window and an explicit abort condition.
records.incompatible_assumptions: A PvE roster may not use a shared unit pool.
records.project_question: What observable progress threshold tells the player to continue upgrading a low-rarity core or pivot?

records.version_scope: Set 17 leveling guide cross-checked with general economy, item and comp guides
records.rule_support: Higher levels improve access to expensive units and increase board capacity, at the opportunity cost of reroll gold.
records.practical_support: Fast 8 uses economy and a strong transitional board to reach high-cost carries, with flexible items and holders preserving health before the roll-down.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Timing and exact carries change by set; the guides do not guarantee success when a roll-down misses.
records.mechanism: Current-board efficiency finances early access to a future high-cost payoff owner.
records.engine: Streak/economy accumulation followed by leveling and a timed high-level roll-down
records.state_resource: Gold, experience, health, item flexibility and current board strength
records.trigger: Reach a safe economy/health threshold for level 8 and retain roll-down gold
records.scope: Whole board transition
records.payoff: High-cost carry plus complementary frontline and utility
records.survival: Strongest-board play and item holders bridge the weak middle phase
records.spatial_condition: Main tank establishes contact while the final carry avoids backline threats
records.payoff_owner: One selected high-cost carry
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Abandon Fast 9 or an ideal carry when health, economy, items or contestation require a cheaper stable board.
records.counterplay: Faster opponent tempo, high-cost contestation and direct carry access punish delayed payoff.
records.failure_explanation: The player can identify an underpowered transition, greedy level timing or an unlucky roll-down as different failure sources.
records.transferability: A late-core plan needs an authored bridge package, not merely a larger final reward.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project may use floor rewards rather than an open reroll shop.
records.project_question: Which temporary units and transferable equipment keep a late-carry tower build alive without becoming its final answer?

records.version_scope: Set 7/8 official retrospective interpreted alongside general comp-selection practice
records.rule_support: Dragons combined elevated cost, two team slots and large trait contribution in one recruit.
records.practical_support: Composition guidance depends on preserving pivot options; bundling several budgets into one recruit reduces the number of viable bridges and replacements.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The diversity diagnosis is official developer analysis, not an independent quantitative reanalysis.
records.mechanism: One unit simultaneously consumes population, economy and trait budgets, overcommitting composition direction.
records.engine: High-impact multi-slot recruit with oversized trait contribution
records.state_resource: Gold, team slots and trait breakpoints
records.trigger: Recruit and field a Dragon
records.scope: Whole composition structure
records.payoff: Large individual and trait power
records.survival: Power is concentrated in the recruit, but alternatives and bridge slots shrink
records.spatial_condition: Two-slot occupancy reduces formation flexibility as well as population flexibility
records.payoff_owner: The Dragon and its enabled trait package
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Replacing the unit unwinds several investments at once, raising pivot cost.
records.counterplay: Punish the concentrated unit or exploit missing utility roles created by slot pressure.
records.failure_explanation: A failed composition may be structurally overcommitted rather than merely under-statted.
records.transferability: Do not let one hero or relic simultaneously provide the engine, payoff, defense and most tag progress without explicit cost.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project's party-size and trait rules differ from TFT's two-slot implementation.
records.project_question: How many independent build budgets may one roster choice satisfy before it erases meaningful composition tradeoffs?

records.version_scope: Set 8 official retrospective cross-checked with general composition guidance
records.rule_support: Threat units supplied useful standalone functions without requiring normal trait investment.
records.practical_support: Composition guidance values units that solve current frontline, damage or utility gaps while preserving the option to pivot.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The transfer claim is a design inference; no evidence here says every traitless unit is healthy.
records.mechanism: A low-lock-in functional unit patches a composition gap without opening another vertical trait commitment.
records.engine: Standalone unit power and role utility
records.state_resource: One team slot and recruitment cost
records.trigger: The board lacks a specific role and a compatible plug-in unit appears
records.scope: Local role gap with whole-board consequences
records.payoff: Immediate frontline, control or damage utility
records.survival: A plug-in frontline or control unit can stabilize a fragile payoff owner
records.spatial_condition: The unit still requires a role-appropriate cell and may alter targeting
records.payoff_owner: Existing carry or board, supported by the plug-in unit
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Use the bridge temporarily and replace it when a coherent final package becomes available.
records.counterplay: Standalone power must remain below a level where every composition takes the same universal answer.
records.failure_explanation: The player can see which missing role the bridge solved and what was sacrificed to field it.
records.transferability: Offer horizontal bridge units/items for cleanse, control or shield break without forcing a full new system.
records.incompatible_assumptions: A fixed PvE reward pool may make universal answers more dominant than in a contested PvP shop.
records.project_question: Which counter roles need bridge options, and what prevents one bridge from becoming automatic in every run?

records.version_scope: Set 8 official retrospective plus general scouting/positioning practice
records.rule_support: Hacker/Assassin-style access could bypass the normal frontline and rapidly reach a backline carry.
records.practical_support: Positioning guidance treats jumps, hooks, stuns and burst as threats that force side swaps and carry protection.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The official source establishes developer dissatisfaction, not a universal player-sentiment measurement.
records.mechanism: Direct access invalidates the survival layer when it removes the payoff owner before formation can respond.
records.engine: Jump or access rule that changes initial target reachability
records.state_resource: Carry position, frontline geometry and preparation time
records.trigger: Combat start or access ability activation
records.scope: Enemy backline payoff owner
records.payoff: Rapid carry removal
records.survival: Side swapping, bait units and deeper protection are intended responses
records.spatial_condition: Whether the attacker can bypass or land beyond the frontline
records.payoff_owner: The access unit; the denied owner is the enemy carry
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Recruiting a durable secondary carry or peel utility reduces single-point failure.
records.counterplay: Positioning must materially delay or redirect access; otherwise the counter is only nominal.
records.failure_explanation: Readable access and targeting can explain the loss, but near-instant deletion leaves too little corrective feedback.
records.transferability: Backline counters should pressure a carry while preserving a telegraphed response window.
records.incompatible_assumptions: A single-player game can preview the exact threat and need not use hidden opponent swaps.
records.project_question: How long must a defender have to react before a backline-bypass enemy stops feeling like a fair counter?

records.version_scope: Set 8 Hero Augment retrospective plus general augment-selection guide
records.rule_support: Hero Augments attached a high-impact rule change to a specific champion offer.
records.practical_support: Augment guidance evaluates choices against current board, items, economy, health and composition direction instead of isolated average strength.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The acceptable amount of reroll/control is context-dependent; no numeric threshold is established here.
records.mechanism: The more an offered rule rewrite determines payoff ownership, the more selection control the player needs.
records.engine: High-impact augment offer tied to a champion
records.state_resource: Offer slots, rerolls and sunk composition investment
records.trigger: Augment selection round
records.scope: Champion and often whole composition direction
records.payoff: A new carry or support rule with build-defining power
records.survival: A compatible support augment may stabilize the existing board; an incompatible carry augment can strand it
records.spatial_condition: Champion-specific effects still require the chosen owner to survive and reach targets
records.payoff_owner: The named champion or the board it supports
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Rerolls or broad alternatives let the player reject an offer that conflicts with current investment.
records.counterplay: Opportunity cost and compatibility constraints prevent taking the theoretical strongest augment automatically.
records.failure_explanation: The offer, owner and incompatibility must be visible so the player can distinguish a risky choice from bad luck.
records.transferability: A relic that converts defense to offense should explicitly name its owner and offer a reject/pivot route.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has no PvP fairness requirement but still needs run-level agency.
records.project_question: When a relic creates a new payoff owner, what minimum alternative or reroll control keeps the choice fair?

records.version_scope: Space Gods retrospective cross-checked with Patch 14.1 multi-system live changes
records.rule_support: The Realm mechanic attempted to alter multiple foundational distribution systems, while live patches tune portals, traits, items, augments and economy on separate axes.
records.practical_support: Riot reports that the broad mechanic produced balance and production-schedule problems, illustrating the cost of coupling several axes into one themed rule.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This is a production/lifecycle lesson from a live-service environment; small static games have different patch costs.
records.mechanism: A mechanic that rewrites several foundational systems at once multiplies balance interactions and obscures causality.
records.engine: One seasonal rule modifies augment and core-item distribution together
records.state_resource: Multiple offer pools and their balance budgets
records.trigger: Seasonal rule activation
records.scope: Whole match and content pipeline
records.payoff: Strong thematic variation and novel decision space
records.survival: Not a unit-defense mechanism; project survival depends on keeping affected axes testable
records.spatial_condition: None directly; some rewritten rewards later alter formation
records.payoff_owner: Entire ruleset rather than one unit
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Players and designers lose clean pivot points when several offer channels change simultaneously.
records.counterplay: Separate toggles, caps and diagnostic reporting bound the rewrite.
records.failure_explanation: Multi-axis coupling makes it harder to tell which distribution change caused an unhealthy outcome.
records.transferability: Keep first-version relics focused on one conversion or one ownership rule and expose caps/guards.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project is not a seasonal live service, but has less capacity to repair opaque interactions after release.
records.project_question: Which foundational axes must never be rewritten by the same first-version relic?

records.version_scope: Lore & Legends retrospective cross-checked with general item and composition guides
records.rule_support: A seasonal structure asked players to invest in an initial carry and later transition resources to another carry.
records.practical_support: Item and composition guidance treats item ownership and sunk recruitment as core direction signals, so a forced second handoff creates both economic and cognitive friction.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The official retrospective supplies the negative diagnosis; independent statistics are not included in this batch.
records.mechanism: A forced late change of payoff owner conflicts with earlier concentrated equipment and roster investment.
records.engine: Sequential unlock of two intended carries
records.state_resource: Carry items, upgrades, roster slots and player commitment
records.trigger: The second carry becomes available after the first is already built
records.scope: Primary damage role and supporting composition
records.payoff: Higher late-game ceiling if the handoff succeeds
records.survival: The original carry may be necessary for transition but becomes an inefficient final owner
records.spatial_condition: Each carry may demand a different protection or range pattern
records.payoff_owner: Changes from the first carry to the second
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: The player must sell, bench, re-equip or otherwise unwind the original investment.
records.counterplay: Opportunity cost should be voluntary and visible; forced handoff without compensation is the cited failure.
records.failure_explanation: The system should report that ownership changed and which earlier investment became stranded.
records.transferability: Prefer complementary tank/carry pairs or an explicit inheritance rule over surprise replacement of the main payoff owner.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project's equipment binding and replacement rules are not yet fixed.
records.project_question: Can a shield package empower one ranged carry without later requiring the player to discard the first owner?

records.version_scope: Lore & Legends retrospective interpreted alongside item and augment selection practice
records.rule_support: Artifacts were changed from sharper, more specialized effects toward safer broadly usable effects.
records.practical_support: Item and augment guides value compatibility with the current owner and board, showing why specialization creates real selection and ownership constraints.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The claim that distinctiveness was lost comes from the official retrospective; no player preference survey is available here.
records.mechanism: Removing ownership constraints increases floor usability but can erase a build-defining peak and identity.
records.engine: Rare item with an unusual owner requirement or rule rewrite
records.state_resource: Artifact offer, eligible owner and opportunity cost versus general items
records.trigger: Artifact acquisition and assignment
records.scope: One owner, sometimes influencing the whole composition
records.payoff: A specialized high-ceiling build interaction
records.survival: A narrow item may have a poor floor when no eligible owner survives or appears
records.spatial_condition: Owner requirements may include range, targeting or exposure constraints
records.payoff_owner: Explicit artifact holder
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Recruit or retain a compatible owner, reroll/reject the artifact, or accept a lower floor.
records.counterplay: Specialization should expose a counterable condition rather than grant universal unconditional power.
records.failure_explanation: UI must show both why the item is currently weak and what owner would unlock it.
records.transferability: Preserve sharp relic identities with previewed compatibility, rerolls or fallback conversion rather than flattening every relic.
records.incompatible_assumptions: A small first-version roster may not support very narrow owner requirements without dead rewards.
records.project_question: How narrow can a defense-to-offense relic be before the available roster makes it a dead offer too often?

records.version_scope: Set 17 Primordian Reroll page published 2026-04-11 and updated 2026-07-29, cross-checked with a Set 17 reroll guide
records.rule_support: Set 17 reroll odds reward staying at levels matched to 1/2-cost targets; the named guide assigns Briar as the primary carry and uses Rogue aggro drop to transfer focus to a nearby tank.
records.practical_support: The build guide prioritizes Briar items and Evenshroud, reassigns tank items from a weak or uncompleted Cho'Gath to Rek'Sai, and describes slow-roll, hard-roll and post-completion leveling stages.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The source is a historical Set 17 page viewed after the site moved to Patch 18.1b; its patch blocks and comments must not be combined into one timeless best board. Counter claims beyond those stated by the guide are design inferences.
records.mechanism: Controlled early aggro lowers a front-positioned carry's health to activate attack-speed payoff, then transfers focus to a nearby tank.
records.engine: Low-cost reroll completion plus Briar's low-health attack-speed passive and Rogue aggro drop
records.state_resource: Gold, low-cost copies, Briar health, Rek'Sai growth, item components and shared-pool contestation
records.trigger: Briar takes opening aggro, reaches her desired low-health state and drops aggro
records.scope: Briar as primary carry, adjacent tank handoff and supporting Primordian board
records.payoff: High attack-speed carry window backed by armor reduction and secondary damage
records.survival: Rek'Sai or another viable tank takes focus after Briar's aggro drop; early item slams preserve health while rerolling
records.spatial_condition: Briar starts exposed; the tank is placed close enough to receive aggro after the drop rather than before it
records.payoff_owner: Briar; Evenshroud holder and tank are support owners, with Kai'Sa/Jhin or Bel'Veth as secondary damage options
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Slow roll while safe, hard roll when the completion window closes, then level; if contested or key tanks cannot complete, change the roll timing, tank owner or exit the reroll line.
records.counterplay: Burst or control can remove Briar before the handoff, and poor tank proximity can break the intended aggro sequence; these structural counters require version-specific validation.
records.failure_explanation: The combat report should distinguish failure to reach three stars, wrong item ownership, Briar dying before aggro drop and the tank failing to receive focus.
records.transferability: A risky front-positioned carry can convert controlled damage into offense if its handoff timing and support owner are explicit.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project may not reproduce TFT's shared pool, Rogue aggro rule or exact item recipes.
records.project_question: Can a shield or low-health carry intentionally expose itself, then hand incoming pressure to a tank, without making targeting opaque?

records.version_scope: 2019 base rules, with Season 13 practical opportunity-cost cross-check
records.rule_support: Official base rules state that tavern Gold cannot be saved for future rounds and can be spent on recruits, refreshes, tier upgrades and other actions.
records.practical_support: The Season 13 guide evaluates expensive Trinkets against the number of buys/refreshes left in the same turn and warns against paying for a speculative payoff without an economy engine.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact costs and seasonal purchase channels changed after 2019; the use-it-or-lose-it structure, not old numeric prices, is retained.
records.mechanism: Round-limited currency turns every unspent point into a lost action rather than long-term savings.
records.engine: Recurring per-turn Gold plus temporary economy effects
records.state_resource: Current-turn Gold, remaining actions, tavern tier and health
records.trigger: Each Recruit Phase ends
records.scope: All tavern actions in the current round
records.payoff: Immediate board strength, shop access or a seasonal rule reward
records.survival: Tempo purchases reduce incoming combat damage
records.spatial_condition: Purchased minions still need board/hand space and a viable combat position
records.payoff_owner: The bought unit, upgraded tavern or selected Trinket effect
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Spend the last Gold on refresh, unit, tier or effect according to immediate survival and engine completion; banking is not an option.
records.counterplay: High-cost speculative rewards consume the actions needed to stabilize.
records.failure_explanation: The player can see whether Gold was spent on tempo, access or a failed speculative engine.
records.transferability: Use expiring floor currency only if the project wants to emphasize action allocation over saving curves.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The tower run may need cross-floor saving and therefore should not inherit Gold reset by default.
records.project_question: Which currencies expire at a floor boundary, and what decision quality does that expiration create?

records.version_scope: 2019 triple rule and 2022 Buddy-era leveling guide
records.rule_support: Three identical minions merge into a Golden minion retaining prior buffs and grant a discover from the next Tavern Tier when played.
records.practical_support: The curve guide times upgrades and early triples to access specific higher-tier snowball units while balancing board width and tempo.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The curve examples are Buddy-era history and not current 2026 leveling recommendations.
records.mechanism: Duplicate completion is both a unit upgrade and a timed access token to a higher rarity pool.
records.engine: Shared-pool duplicate collection and Tavern Tier gating
records.state_resource: Copies, buffs, Gold, Tavern Tier, hand/board space and health
records.trigger: Acquire and play the third identical minion
records.scope: One merged unit plus one higher-tier discover
records.payoff: Golden effect and early access to a build engine
records.survival: Buff retention prevents the merge from erasing prior tempo investment
records.spatial_condition: The merged unit frees a board slot, which may enable summons or a new engine unit
records.payoff_owner: Golden unit and the discovered higher-tier card
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Players may delay completing or playing the triple until after a Tavern upgrade to change the discover pool.
records.counterplay: Shared-pool contestation lowers completion odds; delaying the triple risks health loss.
records.failure_explanation: The miss can be attributed to duplicate scarcity, discover outcome or mistimed tier access.
records.transferability: An upgrade can deliberately combine immediate power with a previewable access reward.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project may not have a shared shop or automatic three-copy merges.
records.project_question: Should roster upgrading also open a controlled higher-rarity choice, and can its timing be understood before commitment?

records.version_scope: 2019 base combat rules cross-checked with Season 13 cleave positioning
records.rule_support: Friendly minions attack from left to right; target selection is random unless Taunt constrains it.
records.practical_support: The Season 13 Pirate build puts a large Blade Collector leftmost to attack early and recommends a weak far-right Taunt to reduce an opposing cleave's adjacent value.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Specific keywords and minions rotate; the official 2019 page does not describe all modern targeting exceptions.
records.mechanism: Player-controlled friendly sequence combines with constrained-random enemy targeting.
records.engine: Left-to-right attacker order plus Taunt target eligibility
records.state_resource: Seven positions, attack order, Taunt placement and adjacent units
records.trigger: Each combat attack
records.scope: Active attacker and legal enemy targets
records.payoff: Early activation of cleave, deathrattle, shield break or setup effects
records.survival: Taunt redirects attacks; Divine Shield absorbs one damage event
records.spatial_condition: Leftmost attacks first; edge Taunt can deny one side of cleave adjacency
records.payoff_owner: The specifically ordered attacker or protected unit
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A utility minion can be recruited as a positional counter without changing the entire tribe build.
records.counterplay: Use Taunt, edge placement, shield breakers or a different first attacker to disrupt sequencing.
records.failure_explanation: Attack order and legal targets are inspectable, while random selection among legal targets remains explicit variance.
records.transferability: Expose deterministic source order and target constraints separately in combat reports.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project may use a spatial battlefield rather than a seven-slot line.
records.project_question: Which combat events require deterministic ordering, and which target choices may remain random without harming attribution?

records.version_scope: Season 13 / Patch 35.2.2 only
records.rule_support: Recruit-phase Gold actions feed a board whose combat sequence can be controlled by left-right placement and Taunt.
records.practical_support: The guide requires Sky Admiral Rogers, Proud Privateer and Brann Bronzebeard before full commitment, uses Privateer Portrait/Trusty Crowbar/Miniature Ship as Trinket routes, and assigns leftmost payoff to Blade Collector.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This is one author's Season 13 guide and is obsolete for Season 14 pools; 2019 rules only cross-check the stable combat-order layer.
records.mechanism: Gold/Battlecry cycling generates repeated Bounties that are multiplied and converted into stats, more Gold and a cleave payoff.
records.engine: Sky Admiral Rogers plus Proud Privateer and Brann-driven Battlecry/resource cycling
records.state_resource: Gold, Bounties, Battlecry triggers, turn time, Tavern Tier, available tribes and health
records.trigger: Spend/gain Gold and resolve multiplied Bounties during the Recruit Phase
records.scope: Pirate board with cross-tribe cycle pieces

records.failure_explanation: Logs need source, target validity, exhausted counter and queue position.
records.transferability: Deterministic replay, state guards and recursion caps are first-version requirements for complex shield/summon chains.
records.incompatible_assumptions: None; deterministic PvE still benefits even without asynchronous PvP.
records.project_question: What event id, source id and trigger-budget fields are needed to reproduce every automated battle?

records.version_scope: Official Update 34

records.practical_support: The official announcement states an aim for more developed archetypes; the later guide shows strawberries as a pack-specific engine requiring Hummingbird and strawberry-equipped friends.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The announcement does not provide unit-by-unit failure reasons or outcome metrics, so only the rework scope and stated goal are established.
records.mechanism: A content package can be rebuilt around clearer internal engines and a consistent state language rather than isolated themed effects.
records.engine: Pack-wide pet/perk interactions such as strawberry ownership
records.state_resource: Pack slots, equipped strawberry perks and compatible pets
records.trigger: Pack selection and perk-based abilities

records.payoff_owner: The strawberry-equipped friend and supporting pack engine

records.counterplay: No specific counter claim is supported by the official rework note.
records.failure_explanation: Visual language should distinguish equipment/perk state from triggered abilities.
records.transferability: Element or shield content should ship as complete engine/owner/survival packages, not a list of same-colored effects.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project does not sell fixed packs, but still groups first-version content into authored systems.

records.version_scope: Daily Mode release 2026-04-08 plus Arena strategy guide updated 2026-06-04

records.practical_support: A fixed sequence permits comparison of shop, scaling and positioning choices against shared enemy packages instead of hidden opponent sampling.

records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Adapt purchases and formation to repeated knowledge of the fixed package if retries reveal it.
records.counterplay: Authored enemies can deliberately test summon, single-core, sniper or self-damage lines.
records.failure_explanation: Same-enemy comparison isolates decision differences better than random asynchronous matchmaking.
records.transferability: Use authored floor enemy packages and repeatable test seeds to validate each build system.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project may reveal enemies before combat rather than through repeated daily attempts.

records.version_scope: Official 1.0 and 1.1 interface rules with March 2024 practical layouts
records.rule_support: Items occupy a grid and expose affected slots or recipe links; official updates add affected-item highlighting, separate bag/item editing, grid storage, recipe feedback and history version labels.
records.practical_support: Both IGN builds require exact adjacency, star coverage, container placement or acceleration-bag placement rather than merely owning the listed items.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The 2024 guides predate 1.0; they establish spatial build grammar, not current numerical balance.
records.mechanism: A build is a spatial dependency graph embedded in a finite inventory grid.
records.engine: Bags, shaped items, recipes, affected slots and adjacency
records.state_resource: Free cells, bag bonuses, recipe progress and valid affected-item links
records.trigger: Shop rearrangement, crafting completion and each affected item activation
records.scope: Whole backpack with local item neighborhoods
records.payoff: Activate, accelerate or convert only the items reached by the intended links
records.survival: Defensive items must fit without disconnecting the main engine
records.spatial_condition: Orientation, star slots, left/right neighbors, containment and overlap determine validity
records.payoff_owner: The item whose effect resolves; bags and adjacent pieces are enablers unless their own text pays off
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Buy grid space and sell expired components when the final dependency graph cannot fit.
records.counterplay: Control or burst can punish a layout that spent too much space on acceleration and too little on startup protection.
records.failure_explanation: The UI can attribute failure to an unlinked item, an item outside the required bag, a blocked recipe or insufficient free cells.
records.transferability: Represent team formations and equipment auras as visible links with explicit missing-link feedback.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project uses battlefield units rather than a free-rotation inventory puzzle.
records.project_question: Which formation or equipment links must be visible before combat so a shield or affinity engine is auditable?

records.version_scope: March 2024 Early Access guides plus official 1.1.7-1.1.8 balance
records.rule_support: Weapons can consume Stamina, while official patches independently tune Stamina cost, reduction, maximum use and refunds.
records.practical_support: IGN adds Bananas or Topaz when a second weapon is fielded; TheGamer uses no-Stamina Dragons to avoid that weapon bottleneck.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Dood's claim that Stamina shortens all item cooldowns is broader than the other sources support; this record only retains the weapon-throughput conclusion.
records.mechanism: Displayed weapon damage is constrained by a shared cadence budget.
records.engine: Weapon activations consume Stamina while items or gems replenish or reduce demand
records.state_resource: Current Stamina, regeneration, cost per activation and number of active weapons
records.trigger: Each Stamina-consuming attack
records.scope: All weapons competing for the same Stamina pool
records.payoff: Sustained realized DPS instead of an unsustainable paper-damage peak
records.survival: No-Stamina summons or a one-weapon layout frees slots for defense
records.spatial_condition: Topaz and Fanny Pack placement must accelerate the intended weapon or Dragon
records.payoff_owner: The weapon or Dragon that completes the attack
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Do not add a second weapon until its Stamina supply and grid cost are affordable; pivot to no-Stamina payoffs when supply is the bottleneck.
records.counterplay: Stamina removal and long fights expose an overcommitted multi-weapon layout.
records.failure_explanation: Combat reporting should show delayed attacks and which weapons exhausted the shared budget.
records.transferability: Give attack and spell engines explicit shared throughput budgets instead of allowing every trigger to scale independently.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project may use per-hero attack cadence rather than one backpack-wide pool.
records.project_question: Which first-version actions compete for one cadence resource, and how is starvation shown in the battle report?

records.version_scope: March 2024 Venomancer guide, July 2026 practical run and guide updated August 2026
records.rule_support: Mana-consuming items stop when their pool is unavailable; Moon equipment can turn Block into Mana and Glowing Crown consumes Mana for defense.
records.practical_support: The 2026 Golden Pan run remained half-activated after its apparent core arrived because Magic Orb and sustained Mana were late.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact generation, consumption and cooldown values are version-dependent and are not normalized here.
records.mechanism: A visible core item is inert until production, consumption and action timing form a closed resource loop.

records.trigger: Block generation or a Mana-producing item activation

records.incompatible_assumptions: The project may distribute Mana per hero rather than globally.
records.project_question: Should a build preview quantify time-to-first-cast and sustainable casts rather than only total Mana gain?

records.version_scope: March 2024 Pyromancer guide plus July-August 2026 secondary analysis

records.disagreement_or_limit: The sources span Early Access and 2026 and do not establish one current Heat formula.

records.version_scope: March 2024 Venomancer build with August 2026 secondary mechanics cross-check
records.rule_support: Poison accumulates over time and can be cleansed or resisted; Venomancer adds Snake protection and a Death Scythe threshold payoff.
records.practical_support: The named build uses Storage Coffin, Poison Goobert and adjacent poison items to reach the threshold while Moon equipment supplies enough survival time.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The historical 35-Poison Death Scythe threshold is not asserted for 1.1.8, and Dood's other numeric threshold claims are not used.
records.mechanism: A status build combines production, persistence protection, threshold payoff and survival.
records.engine: Storage Coffin activations, Poison Goobert and poison items
records.state_resource: Enemy Poison stacks, Snake Luck, cleanse attempts and elapsed combat time
records.trigger: Item activation, Goobert activation count and threshold reach
records.scope: Enemy status stack plus the local Venomancer grid
records.payoff: Persistent damage and Death Scythe critical payoff after the historical threshold
records.survival: Block, Mana and Glowing Crown extend the stacking window

records.payoff_owner: Poison and Death Scythe; Snake protects the state but is not the main damage owner

records.failure_explanation: Distinguish low stack production, successful enemy cleanse, missed threshold and failure to survive until payoff.

records.incompatible_assumptions: The project may use finite encounters rather than asynchronous long attrition fights.
records.project_question: Which status thresholds have a visible owner and how much counterplay exists before detonation?

records.version_scope: Named March 2024 Early Access Ashbringer build; not a 1.1.8 strength claim

records.practical_support: The guide specifies Phoenix, Chili Goobert, Sun Armor, Burning weapons, Fanny Packs and exact Lantern/Armor/Goobert neighborhoods.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Current item values and meta rank are unknown; 1.1 added and adjusted many items after this guide.

records.state_resource: Maximum/current health, Heat, affected Fire/Dark item count, Goobert activations and Stamina

records.version_scope: Named March 2024 Early Access Venomancer build; not a 1.1.8 strength claim
records.rule_support: Snake protects Poison through Luck, Death Scythe pays off accumulated Poison, and Moon equipment can convert Block events into Mana for Glowing Crown.
records.practical_support: The guide supplies exact recipes and a transition from sale weapons/Fly Agaric into Scythe, Poison Goobert, Moon Armor/Shield and Crown.

records.version_scope: Official 1.0 and 1.1 conversion wording
records.rule_support: Patch 1.0 changed Smelly Wall so Poison triggers only from Block generated by its marked tiles; patch 1.1 separately describes Mercury Elemental as gaining Block from damage.
records.practical_support: The mechanics guide treats mitigation and retaliation as different outputs, reinforcing that conversion direction and source matter.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No source explains the balance motive; Mercury Elemental is damage-to-Block, not evidence that all Block converts to damage.

records.version_scope: Official patches 1.1.7 and 1.1.8

records.practical_support: The adjacent patches show that both reward slope and usage ceiling/side effect were active balance levers.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Official notes give no win-rate data or reason, so this record does not label the 1.1.7 version overpowered.
records.mechanism: A resource-scaling payoff is governed by both a counted-resource cap and a self-disruption cost.

records.state_resource: Stamina consumed up to a versioned maximum
records.trigger: Resource use and the item's self-Stun event

records.payoff: Buffs proportional to counted Stamina within the cap
records.survival: Self-Stun creates an exposure window
records.spatial_condition: No additional spatial rule is established by the patch notes
records.payoff_owner: Hogus Bogus
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Its value depends on whether the build can supply Stamina without sacrificing the rest of the grid.

records.version_scope: Official 1.0 retrospective and 1.1 expansion
records.rule_support: The developer states that an early version's late game could only end in Bloodthorne or Lightsabers because those were the only late-game weapons; 1.0 reached 439 items and 1.1 added another class and dozens of items.
records.practical_support: The expansion history shows that a large set of early ingredients does not create build diversity when too few late-game payoff owners exist.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The sources do not prove that every later item produced a viable route or that content count alone solved balance.
records.mechanism: Build diversity is capped by the number of reachable late-game payoff owners, not by total ingredient count.

records.trigger: Mid-to-late-game pivot into a final payoff

records.spatial_condition: Final routes must be physically compatible with available bags and support pieces
records.payoff_owner: A terminal weapon, summon or subclass converter
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A shop can offer many pieces yet still force the same ending if only two owners convert them efficiently.

records.project_question: How many genuinely different payoff owners does each first-version shield, affinity and summon family need?

records.version_scope: March 2024 historical builds plus July-August 2026 practical counter guidance
records.rule_support: Stun interrupts item activation, Poison can be cleansed or resisted, and Mana/Stamina constrain different actions.
records.practical_support: Slow fire prioritizes anti-Stun and early Poison resistance; Venomancer protects stacks from cleanse; Phoenix and Crown builds use revival or invulnerability to survive startup.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Counter strength and item availability vary by version, and no matchup statistics are accessible.
records.mechanism: Counters attack production, persistence, payoff timing or survival as separable layers.
records.engine: Opponent Stun, Cold, cleanse, resistance, burst or resource disruption
records.state_resource: Startup time, status stacks, resistance, Mana, Stamina and remaining health
records.trigger: Preparation scouting and the first combat cycle
records.scope: Opponent build chain rather than a single numeric stat
records.payoff: Delay, erase or outpace the targeted engine layer
records.survival: Targeted helmets, gems, armor, shields, revival and cleansing preserve the threatened layer
records.spatial_condition: Counter items consume scarce cells and must cover the relevant core
records.payoff_owner: The counter item or status source that actually interrupts the chain
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Patch the previous fight's specific failure while refusing low-value counters that dismantle the whole main line.
records.counterplay: The original build can buy resistance or accelerate, but each response costs grid, gold or output.
records.failure_explanation: State whether the engine never started, its resource ran dry, the status was removed or survival ended before payoff.
records.transferability: Design enemy packages that challenge one layer with a visible adaptation offer before combat.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Asynchronous opponents are not equivalent to authored tower enemies.
records.project_question: Which enemy preview and reward choice gives a fair window to answer shield break, cleanse, anti-summon or cadence disruption?

records.version_scope: Mechabellum Wiki snapshot updated 2026-06-17 in the 1.11 period
records.rule_support: Units generally target or move toward the nearest opponent, with facing and explicit technologies such as Aerial Specialization modifying priority.
records.practical_support: Both named compositions place expendable bodies or tanks first, clear enemy chaff next and preserve control or single-target units for valuable locks.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The maintained wiki does not publish a complete frame-level tie-break algorithm for equally distant targets.
records.mechanism: Deployment creates a deterministic-enough first-target chain that controls which role acts on which enemy layer.

records.trigger: Battle start, target death, flank spawn or target-priority change
records.scope: Each squad and the battlefield
records.payoff: Chaff absorbs locks while clear and single-target damage reach appropriate targets in sequence
records.survival: Backline payoff units remain outside the first lock
records.spatial_condition: Front/back spacing, side, orientation, range and flank proximity determine the chain
records.payoff_owner: The unit that completes the attack, hack or kill after the chain opens
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Recruit missing chaff-clear or tanking before adding more backline damage that cannot acquire useful targets.
records.counterplay: A flank, Mobile Beacon, sacrificial squad or altered target priority can redirect the chain.
records.failure_explanation: Report first lock, retarget cause and time spent on low-value blockers.
records.transferability: Formation should determine who absorbs, clears and pays off rather than granting a flat row bonus.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project may permit tactical commands after battle starts, unlike Mechabellum's locked battle phase.
records.project_question: What target-lock and retarget fields must the combat report expose for formation decisions to be legible?

records.version_scope: 1.11-period maintained wiki
records.rule_support: Flanks open from round 2, first-time flank deployments spawn after a delay and nearby flank units can redirect target selection.
records.practical_support: The Sledge-Marksman guide blocks the attacked tower route and uses an outside Sledgehammer to cover surprise flanks.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Specific teleport cards and modes can alter timing; this record does not assume every flank is a direct tower kill.
records.mechanism: A delayed side deployment trades immediate force for later target displacement and tower pressure.
records.engine: Flank deployment area and spawn delay
records.state_resource: Round, teleport delay, defender coverage, tower state and mobile redeployment access
records.trigger: Round-two flank availability and delayed unit arrival
records.scope: One side lane plus units whose nearest target changes
records.payoff: Pull defenders away, expose a tower or surround the main army
records.survival: Cheap flank defenders or an outside tank delay the threat
records.spatial_condition: Side distance, tower route, spawn position and Mobile Beacon path are decisive
records.payoff_owner: The flank squad or frontal army that exploits the retarget
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Do not overinvest in a flank that is difficult to protect; use enough force to create a target split.
records.counterplay: Cover both flanks, deploy an outside defender or exploit the attacker's delayed arrival.
records.failure_explanation: Show whether the flank arrived too late, was cheaply stalled or pulled the wrong part of the army.
records.transferability: Side routes should alter arrival and targeting with visible timing, not operate as a hidden damage modifier.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project may use authored PvE maps rather than a symmetric two-tower board.
records.project_question: Which tower floors use delayed side threats, and how much preview prevents them from becoming formation traps?

records.version_scope: 1.11-period maintained wiki with contemporary high-MMR role guidance
records.rule_support: A unit upgrade costs half its base cost for another level-one stat increment, while higher-level deaths grant larger experience rewards.
records.practical_support: The sources warn that levelling chaff accelerates enemy chaff-clear and that level-one Sledgehammers often perform their tank/clear role without becoming efficient counter targets.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact experience formulas come from a maintained wiki rather than a first-party manual and must be rechecked after major updates.
records.mechanism: Vertical power also increases the reward paid to the enemy when the upgraded squad dies.
records.engine: Supply-funded levels and kill/assist experience distribution
records.state_resource: Unit cost, level, accumulated XP, survival probability and enemy counter levels
records.trigger: Purchase upgrade and unit death
records.scope: One squad and enemy units participating in its kill
records.payoff: Immediate stat growth and potential snowball if the unit survives
records.survival: Keep temporary chaff or role-complete tanks at low level when counters will still kill them
records.spatial_condition: A protected high-level unit can realize growth; an exposed one feeds the enemy
records.payoff_owner: Upgraded squad while alive; enemy killers if it dies
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Compare a level to another squad, a technology or a counter unit instead of auto-upgrading available XP.
records.counterplay: Focus the expensive leveled squad with an efficient hard counter to capture its bounty.
records.failure_explanation: Attribute enemy growth to the specific high-value death rather than generic snowballing.
records.transferability: Hero upgrades can carry visible death or opportunity costs so horizontal roster growth remains viable.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project is single-player and need not transfer XP directly to enemies.
records.project_question: What non-PvP opportunity cost prevents every early shield or chaff unit from being upgraded indefinitely?

records.version_scope: 1.11 rules and maintained wiki snapshot
records.rule_support: Unit Reinforcements appear once in each of four round windows, offer four units and unlock the selection; 1.11 added a skip option with supply increasing by round.
records.practical_support: Sledge-Marksman uses Wraith and Farseer drops as low-commitment bridges into chaff clear and anti-air rather than forcing more opening units.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Offer weights and all specialist exceptions are not available.
records.mechanism: Periodic constrained offers trade immediate unit access against flexible currency and future pivot capacity.
records.engine: Four scheduled reinforcement windows and four-unit offer sets
records.state_resource: Round, offered units, existing deployments, unlock state and skip supply
records.trigger: A reinforcement window occurs
records.scope: Player unit pool and current board
records.payoff: Add a counter/bridge unit or obtain flexible supply
records.survival: A free or discounted counter can stabilize without deep technology investment
records.spatial_condition: The selected unit still needs a valid lane, range and target role
records.payoff_owner: Selected reinforcement or the later purchase funded by skipping
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Take a unit when it closes an observed role gap; skip when the board needs technology, devices or a different counter.
records.counterplay: Opponent sees the deployed reinforcement and can answer it next round.
records.failure_explanation: Separate a weak offer, a poor selection and incorrect deployment of an otherwise useful unit.
records.transferability: Tower rewards can offer a small counter set plus a currency fallback so no reward screen forces a dead build piece.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project may not expose an opponent who can react after every selection.
records.project_question: Should every authored reward set include a bridge/counter option and a flexible skip value?

records.version_scope: Named 1.11-period Arclight Hacker Defense guide
records.rule_support: Hacker controls ground targets after a preparation period, while range, barriers, chaff and shields alter whether a valid lock completes.
records.practical_support: The build fields chaff and Range Arclights first, then spikes three Range Hackers around round 4/5 and expands to four-to-six squads with counter support.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The deployment images are not transcribed as absolute coordinates and the guide predates 1.11.1's animation/ATK adjustment.
records.mechanism: Chaff clear exposes medium units so protected Hackers can turn those units into temporary allied frontline.
records.engine: Crawler chaff, Range Arclight clear and Hacker control beams
records.state_resource: Supply, round, enemy medium commitment, Hacker level/range, barriers and battlefield coverage
records.trigger: Enemy chaff clears and Hacker completes a target lock
records.scope: Both lanes and enemy medium squads
records.payoff: Controlled enemy squads reverse target pressure and create extra bodies
records.survival: Chaff, Hacker Barrier, Range Mustangs and missile interception protect the control line
records.spatial_condition: Arclights clear ahead of safely ranged Hackers; four-to-six Hackers eventually cover the battlefield
records.payoff_owner: Hacker for control; hacked unit for subsequent attacks
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Reserve early supply by avoiding Vulcan overinvestment; commit after the opponent has multiple medium packs and a tech, using the 1,050/1,100-supply round-four/five spike described by the guide.
records.counterplay: Barrier blocks hacking, air avoids ground control, chaff wastes locks, high-HP targets delay conversion and fast pushes threaten towers.
records.failure_explanation: Report whether clear failed, a barrier blocked control, a target died before the hack or battlefield coverage missed a lane.
records.transferability: A control build requires an opener, target-enabler, payoff owner and counters; control tags alone are not a system.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project should not copy permanent enemy ownership or open PvP scouting without a separate design decision.
records.project_question: Can charm/control exist in a deterministic tower run without obscuring unit ownership and population counts?

records.version_scope: Named 1.11-period Sledge Marksman Defense guide
records.rule_support: Sledgehammers can serve as front-line delay/chaff clear while Marksman technologies switch target role toward assault, air or range matchups.
records.practical_support: The guide deploys Sledges inside and slightly ahead of towers, Crawlers behind, then adds Marksmen on the attacked side and stops investing when the opponent changes target classes.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The round-two/three purchase sequence is one documented game, not a universal build order.
records.mechanism: A temporary medium frontline preserves a ranged payoff until a later counter-specific carry replaces it.
records.engine: Sledgehammer delay, Crawler chaff and dedicated chaff-clear additions
records.state_resource: Attacked side, tower route, unit drops, Marksman target time, levels and technology budget
records.trigger: Opponent commits to aggro and chaff clears enough for Marksmen to acquire medium/air targets
records.scope: Defended lane and both flanks
records.payoff: Marksman single-target damage during the protected range window
records.survival: Field Maintenance or Armor Sledges and outside flank coverage
records.spatial_condition: Sledges sit inside/slightly forward of towers, Crawlers behind/backline and Marksmen outside first-lock distance
records.payoff_owner: Marksman until the late carry pivot
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Use Assault Mode only into Steel Ball/Hound/Typhoon, add clear from unit drops and stop buying Sledge/Marksman when Raiden or supertanks invalidate the line.
records.counterplay: Hacker, Fortress, Phoenix, Overlord, Scorpion or War Factory pressure Sledges; supertanks require Fortress or Melting Point rather than more Marksman tech.
records.failure_explanation: Show Marksmen wasting time on chaff, an uncovered flank, inappropriate Assault Mode or failure to stop investing after an air/tank pivot.
records.transferability: A starter shield/tank package can be an early bridge rather than the forced final carry system.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has persistent heroes across floors rather than fully replaceable PvP squads.
records.project_question: How does a defensive opening signal when to stop vertical investment and hand payoff ownership to a late-run carry?

records.version_scope: 1.11-period build guides and current high-MMR unit guidance
records.rule_support: Different units specialize in absorbing locks, clearing many light bodies, controlling medium targets or damaging single high-value targets.
records.practical_support: Both named builds delay purchasing their payoff until chaff and chaff clear are ready, and both add another role when the payoff remains stuck on low-value targets.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Role boundaries change with technologies and levels, so this is a formation grammar rather than a fixed unit taxonomy.
records.mechanism: The value of a carry depends on earlier roles delivering the correct target at the correct time.
records.engine: Chaff, tanking and area clear
records.state_resource: Living blockers, time-to-clear, current target and payoff uptime
records.trigger: Front layers contact and die or clear opposing blockers
records.scope: Whole formation
records.payoff: Control or high single-target damage lands on valuable units
records.survival: Disposable bodies and tanks buy the delivery time
records.spatial_condition: Arrival times must overlap while chaff stays slightly ahead
records.payoff_owner: Backline Hacker, Marksman or other specialized finisher
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Fill the missing delivery role instead of buying another copy of a carry with no useful lock.
records.counterplay: Split arrival, flank the backline, shield the key layer or overwhelm the clear budget.
records.failure_explanation: Attribute low carry output to target delivery separately from insufficient damage stats.
records.transferability: Shield systems should define how durability delivers an attacker to payoff rather than expecting shields themselves to be the only damage source.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Mechabellum squads are disposable between matches, while project heroes may have persistent identities.
records.project_question: Which first-version systems use defense as delivery, and which use an explicit defense-to-offense converter?

records.version_scope: 1.11-1.11.1 official rules and contemporary strategy guides
records.rule_support: Barriers can block Hacker and battlefield powers; Stormcallers break shields, missile interceptors answer Stormcallers and Heavy Missile increases missile durability at the cost of attack interval.
records.practical_support: The Hacker guide expects shields, recommends Stormcaller, then recommends Mustang or anti-missile devices when the opponent invests in Stormcallers.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No matchup statistics quantify when each answer is efficient, and exact technology values remain patch-dependent.
records.mechanism: Defense, shield break and projectile interception form a counter-counter loop with a light-unit weakness at the end.
records.engine: Barrier or Energy Shield
records.state_resource: Shield HP, missile HP, interception capacity, attack interval and chaff count
records.trigger: Shield absorbs a control/attack event, missile launches and interceptor engages
records.scope: Protected area and projectile lane
records.payoff: Preserve Hacker targets or break the shield so control/damage can connect
records.survival: Barrier and interception protect backline; chaff punishes slow heavy missiles
records.spatial_condition: Shield coverage, missile path, interceptor placement and target density determine the exchange
records.payoff_owner: Shield owner for protection; Stormcaller for shield break; interceptor for denial
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Buy each layer only after scouting the previous commitment because every technology consumes supply and opens a new weakness.
records.counterplay: Heavy Missile counters interception but its slower cadence is inefficient into light units.
records.failure_explanation: Log absorbed shield damage, intercepted projectiles, surviving heavy missiles and wasted overkill on chaff.
records.transferability: Shield counters should attack generation, coverage or breaking cadence without universally deleting all defensive builds.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project may not use interceptable projectile simulation for every attack.
records.project_question: Which enemy packages counter shields through burst, sustain, bypass or generation denial, and which player responses reopen the loop?

records.version_scope: Official Vortex versions 1.10 and 1.11
records.rule_support: Vortex launched with proximity links that increased attack and a fixed-attack-count area shield; 1.11 reduced link scaling/cap and made each subsequent shield require more attacks.
records.practical_support: Because targets and coverage depend on formation, clustering linked Vortexes combines spatial offense with repeated defensive area coverage.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The patch does not publish a win rate or explicit balance diagnosis, so only the scope/cap rework is established.
records.mechanism: A proximity network has capped offensive scaling while repeated shield generation has increasing activation cost.
records.engine: Vortex units linked within their proximity rule
records.state_resource: Linked-unit count, attacks since last shield, next threshold and shield HP
records.trigger: A link exists and the required attack count is reached
records.scope: Linked Vortex cluster and local shield radius
records.payoff: Capped attack amplification plus periodic protection
records.survival: Accumulator Shield covers the cluster but becomes slower to recreate
records.spatial_condition: Units must stay within the link distance and the generated shield protects a local area
records.payoff_owner: Each Vortex's link and shield trigger
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Additional linked units lose marginal value after the cap and compete with broader formation coverage.
records.counterplay: Area damage, shield break or forcing the cluster to split attacks the spatial concentration.
records.failure_explanation: Display active links, capped contributions and the rising next-shield threshold.
records.transferability: Cap team defense-to-carry links and add rate limits so dense formations cannot scale offense and defense without bound.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project's units may not form free geometric networks.
records.project_question: What link cap and trigger escalation prevent all-team shield broadcasting from becoming the only rational formation?

records.version_scope: Official Update 1.11 and post-remake 1.11.1
records.rule_support: The developer removed all old Typhoon technologies, moved it from rare status into the core pool and rebuilt it around frontline chaff-clear and anti-air.
records.practical_support: The stated problem combined severe snowballing, unique removal of Range Enhancement and one of the lowest use rates; the current counter guide treats Typhoon as a situational tanky anti-light unit.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No pre/post usage numbers are published, and 1.11.1 continued balancing the new kit.
records.mechanism: Restricting access and removing common tools to contain a snowballing unit can also erase its usable identity.
records.engine: Old rare-unit availability and snowball-oriented technology set
records.state_resource: Availability, range access, levels, technology choices and usage rate
records.trigger: Full 1.11 unit remake
records.scope: Typhoon's role and entire technology set
records.payoff: A more defined core-pool frontline anti-air/chaff-clear role
records.survival: New maintenance, reassembly or entrenchment options define defensive variants
records.spatial_condition: Range, entrenchment and frontline placement are part of the new role
records.payoff_owner: Typhoon
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Core-pool access makes the unit a normal counter option rather than a rare high-roll commitment.
records.counterplay: The remake explicitly nerfs runaway snowball and exposes standard range/counter relationships.
records.failure_explanation: Separate overpowered ceiling, low availability and low usage instead of treating them as contradictory metrics.
records.transferability: Do not solve an over-scaling hero by making it rare and tool-starved; narrow the scaling loop while preserving a clear normal role.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project is PvE and may not measure ladder usage rate in the same way.
records.project_question: Which planned systems rely on rarity to contain power instead of having a healthy baseline role and bounded ceiling?

records.version_scope: Official 1.11-1.11.1 with current strategy cross-check
records.rule_support: Update 1.11 added a preparation time before Hacker controls a new target to reduce small-unit efficiency while preserving medium/large control; 1.11.1 adjusted animation and attack to improve specific medium matchups.
records.practical_support: Both strategy sources recommend chaff against early Hacker and medium investments as its intended target class.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No matchup rates quantify the exact change, and later versions may retune preparation.
records.mechanism: Control throughput is rate-limited per new target so it cannot dominate both swarms and valuable bodies.
records.engine: Hacker target acquisition and preparation time
records.state_resource: Target count, target size/level, preparation time and control progress
records.trigger: Hacker starts controlling a new target
records.scope: One control beam and selected ground target
records.payoff: Reliable medium/large conversion with reduced swarm efficiency
records.survival: Range and barriers keep Hacker alive through preparation
records.spatial_condition: Chaff in front consumes target acquisitions before valuable units are reached
records.payoff_owner: Hacker
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Use chaff as a cheap counter or buy Hacker only after medium commitment is visible.
records.counterplay: Increase target count, block with barriers, switch to air or kill Hacker during preparation.
records.failure_explanation: Report canceled preparations and time lost per low-value target.
records.transferability: Charm, detonation and shield-consumption effects need per-target rate limits so one payoff is not best into every population shape.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project's control may use durations rather than permanent ownership conversion.
records.project_question: Which effects need per-target, per-cast or per-second limits to preserve swarm and elite counter identities?

records.version_scope: Official Update 1.11 with Sledgehammer role cross-check
records.rule_support: Update 1.11 allowed each Abyss attack to hit Sledgehammer up to twice instead of once.
records.practical_support: The developer said the prior outcome let Sledge withstand attacks that rapidly killed similarly sized units and confused many players; guides otherwise present Sledge as a normal medium frontline with legible counters.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The note establishes confusion and consistency intent but provides no player-study or exact hitbox specification.
records.mechanism: Multi-hit behavior is aligned across visually similar squad sizes so combat results match player expectations.

records.state_resource: Per-attack hit count and squad body layout

records.scope: Abyss-versus-Sledge interaction
records.payoff: Consistent damage relative to similarly sized targets
records.survival: Sledge still uses maintenance/armor rather than an unexplained hit-count exception
records.spatial_condition: Body spacing and attack coverage determine multiple hits
records.payoff_owner: Abyss attack
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Players can evaluate the matchup from unit roles instead of hidden geometry exceptions.
records.counterplay: Use explicit defensive technologies or positioning rather than relying on an accidental one-hit cap.
records.failure_explanation: Combat logs should show hit count when one area attack contacts a multi-body squad.
records.transferability: Large attacks, summons and multi-body units need visible hit-count rules consistent with their presentation.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project's unit scenes may use different collision/target abstractions.
records.project_question: How are multi-hit abilities reported when they overlap formations, summons or linked shields?

records.version_scope: Official Update 1.11.1 plus contemporary strategy pages
records.rule_support: Update 1.11.1 nerfed Mustang's most popular technology and buffed its least popular option to diversify choices; it also nerfed a popular Vulcan while buffing less-used technologies.
records.practical_support: Strategy guides choose technologies only for observed roles and often recommend skipping carry technologies that distort the unit's job.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No raw adoption or post-patch data is published, so the success of the intervention is unknown.
records.mechanism: Option distribution is a diagnostic signal for whether technologies create real conditional choices.
records.engine: Mutually competing unit technologies
records.state_resource: Supply cost, observed opponent role and technology adoption
records.trigger: Technology purchase decision and balance update
