records.payoff: More context-dependent selections instead of one default upgrade
records.survival: Defensive technology can replace damage when the formation needs time
records.spatial_condition: Range, armor and target-role technologies change deployment requirements
records.payoff_owner: The upgraded unit
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Skip technology when a new counter unit or formation repair yields more value.
records.counterplay: Opponent scouting can punish a predictable default technology.
records.failure_explanation: Track selection by context, not only aggregate pick rate, before calling an option dead.
records.transferability: Equipment/relic choices should be evaluated by conditional usage and abandoned options, not just average power.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project may offer randomized relics rather than a persistent four-tech loadout.
records.project_question: Which equipment choices are genuine branches and which are mandatory taxes for the unit to function?

records.version_scope: MechaMonarch page accessed 2026-09-02; exact patch unstated
records.rule_support: Units have distinct target, range and technology roles rather than a universal purchase rule.
records.practical_support: Surrey explicitly interprets higher tiers as units that are correct in more situations, not units that should always be bought; the low-tier Hacker still anchors a complete anti-medium build under the right board commitment.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This is one high-MMR author's subjective tiering without a sample table or patch id.
records.mechanism: Tier placement measures breadth of valid situations more than peak strength in a named composition.
records.engine: Situational unit roles and counter availability
records.state_resource: Number of favorable board states and cost of entering/exiting the unit line
records.trigger: Scouting reveals a board for which a unit is an efficient answer
records.scope: Meta evaluation rather than one battle rule
records.payoff: Use specialized low-flexibility units when their precise condition is satisfied
records.survival: A narrow unit remains viable when the rest of the formation covers its counters
records.spatial_condition: The favorable situation includes deployable range, target access and lane coverage
records.payoff_owner: The situational unit within its complete formation
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Do not force a high-tier unit when the board lacks its target; do not reject a low-tier unit when it closes the observed gap.

records.failure_explanation: Separate low flexibility from low peak effectiveness and missing formation support.

records.incompatible_assumptions: A curated PvE run may intentionally control how often each favorable situation appears.
records.project_question: Does every first-version unit have at least one common, signposted situation where it is the right purchase?

records.version_scope: Early Access guide updated after 1.0 plus initial-1.0 strategy guide
records.rule_support: Flame is both run health and a payment source for rerolls, campfires and Reborn, while Gold, Trophies, shops, elites and events open different acquisition routes.
records.practical_support: The guides recommend spending Flame instead of preserving a full meter, taking elite paths for relics when survivable and solving the current act before chasing a theoretical final build.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact route values and difficulty curves span Early Access and 1.0; the transferable claim is opportunity cost, not a numeric route script.
records.mechanism: Health-like run currency links survival, rerolling, upgrades and deterministic build access.
records.engine: Map routes, fight losses, shops, elites, events and campfires
records.state_resource: Flame, Gold, Trophies, current party strength and future reward access
records.trigger: Every route, reroll, campfire, hero upgrade or Reborn decision
records.scope: Whole run and current party
records.payoff: Convert risk and currency into a coherent build before later enemy scaling
records.survival: Keep enough current strength and Flame to survive the next act rather than maximizing greed
records.spatial_condition: Indirect until enemy previews and formation determine whether the purchased strength is usable
records.payoff_owner: The party line whose missing engine or survival piece is purchased
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Accept a temporary low-level mismatch, reroute to a shop when the opener lacks a tank/carry and spend current resources before an act bottleneck.
records.counterplay: Harder paths, enrage and boss mechanics shorten the window for saving or speculative synergy.
records.failure_explanation: Separate losses caused by greedy routing, excessive rerolls, weak current power and an unrecoverable late commitment.
records.transferability: Make recruitment, relic and upgrade offers compete for visible run resources and current survival.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has not accepted spending cross-floor health as currency or TLF's three-currency economy.
records.project_question: Which run resource makes strengthening now versus preserving future flexibility a legible tower-floor decision?

records.version_scope: Initial-1.0 strategy guide and 1.0-updated general tips
records.rule_support: Equipment belongs to heroes, relics and Origins affect the run or team, and AD, SP, Attack Speed, Mana Regen, Max Mana, HP and Defense benefit different action owners.
records.practical_support: The guides consolidate early heirlooms on a tank and carry, preserve strong bases for later forging, use AD/SP coverage to reduce reroll cost and replace heroes or passives when another source supplies the same function.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Transfer, dismantle and reroll rules are TLF-specific and should not be assumed for the project.
records.mechanism: Distinct ownership layers let one channel create state and another hero consume it.
records.engine: Hero equipment, run-level relics, Origins, passives and reroll/forge actions
records.state_resource: Item slots, recipes, heirlooms, compatible stats and replaceable hero functions
records.trigger: An offer supplies a missing stat owner, generator, converter or payoff
records.scope: One equipped hero plus team/run broadcasts
records.payoff: Concentrate multiplicative stats on a carry while support and relics provide unavailable dimensions
records.survival: A dedicated tank and team sustain protect concentrated equipment value
records.spatial_condition: The equipped owner must still occupy a valid tank, ranged, coverage or targeting position
records.payoff_owner: The hero whose attacks, casts, shields or tank stats actually read the equipment
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Use bridge heroes to consume awkward early items, then replace a hero, passive or Origin when an equivalent function appears with better fit.
records.counterplay: A single concentrated owner can be disabled, outranged or forced into a bad target while unused stats become dead slots.
records.failure_explanation: Report whether a stat lacked a reader, a converter lacked input or the payoff owner never reached its action window.
records.transferability: Keep hero equipment and run relic ownership explicit so a team-wide stat conversion still has an identifiable beneficiary.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project may impose higher replacement or equipment-transfer costs than TLF.
records.project_question: Which first-version equipment is a bridge, which is a build lock and who owns each converted stat?

records.version_scope: Named January 2024 Early Access Endless Flame Master party
records.rule_support: Pyro supplies frequent Burn/AOE, Giachi scales from Defense, shield and Burn, while tank and sustain effects can convert defensive investment into team or personal offense.
records.practical_support: The guide starts Pyro plus Atreos, adds Giachi and Arya/Kara, transfers tank ownership to Giachi, names shield/Defense/Mana equipment and later replaces economy/passive or hero slots before Endless.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This is a historical pre-Early-Access-release build and does not establish 1.0.3 strength or exact current item values.
records.mechanism: A caster clears early while a shield tank gradually becomes the defense-to-damage payoff owner.
records.engine: Pyro/Atreos Burn, Giachi Mana cadence and external first-shield support
records.state_resource: Burn stacks, Defense, shield, Max HP, cast rate and time before Enrage
records.trigger: Giachi repeatedly casts after enough Mana Regen and an initial shield survives
records.scope: Main lane, Giachi and enemies carrying Burn
records.payoff: Pyro AOE early and Giachi shield-break/reflect-style damage after the tank transition
records.survival: Atreos bridges early; Giachi uses Guardian Helmet/Gloves, Sierra, Runic Shield and optional Crown of Life team healing
records.spatial_condition: Kara can start deep to split initial aggro then return, while Pyro and Arya stay outside first focus and Giachi eventually fronts the main pack
records.payoff_owner: Pyro before the transition; Giachi after shield and Defense scaling comes online
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Do not force Giachi at opening; recruit him mid-run, add an ADC for physical drops, switch to Dream Catcher/Templar and replace Kara or a passive with Nox/Gerald utility before Endless.
records.counterplay: Burst before Giachi's first shield, inadequate Burn delivery, slow casting, Enrage and late enemies that invalidate an HP-only bridge tank.
records.failure_explanation: Attribute failure to missing first-shield input, insufficient cast cadence, broken backline protection or Pyro failing the pre-Enrage clear window.
records.transferability: A shield system can change payoff ownership over the run instead of forcing the starter tank to remain the final carry.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Exact TLF heroes, items, five-slot roster and free mid-run replacements are not project authority.
records.project_question: Can a first-version shield line visibly hand payoff ownership from an early damage bridge to a later defense converter?

records.version_scope: Named June 2024 Early Access No Healer? No Problem! party
records.rule_support: Shock increases stun value, Arya and Zotz cover a small AOE, Orion supplies single-target control and Realm Creator converts sustain into team defense.
records.practical_support: The source names Orion, Zephys, Arya, Alaric and Zotz, their starting passives, stat ownership, Origin, tank matchups and the Healing Shield fallback.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Item screenshots omit several names, but hero, passive, Origin, attribute and formation ownership are readable; current 1.x strength is unknown.
records.mechanism: Two tanks and layered AOE/single-target control replace a traditional healer while one ranged hero owns damage.
records.engine: Zotz Shock, Arya repeat casts and Orion single-target stun
records.state_resource: Shock stacks, stun duration, AOE overlap, tank HP and Realm Creator shield/heal output
records.trigger: Shock-bearing enemies enter Arya/Zotz coverage and repeated casts maintain control
records.scope: A clustered enemy group plus the highest-DPS target assigned to Orion
records.payoff: Arya AOE DPS and extended control uptime, with Alaric as secondary spell damage
records.survival: Orion tanks the highest-DPS enemy, Zephys tanks trash, summons/lifesteal bridge and Realm Creator supplies team sustain
records.spatial_condition: Both tanks start directly in front; Orion faces highest DPS, Zephys faces trash and Arya/Zotz must cover the same roughly 3-4-hex area from safety
records.payoff_owner: Arya for damage and AOE stun; Orion/Zotz own target control and Shock delivery
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Forge MR/SP for Zotz/Alaric, AS/AD/crit for Arya and HP/Defense/heal for tanks; replace a tank passive with Healing Shield when control cannot carry survival.
records.counterplay: Enemy spread, Enrage reducing effective stun duration, missed highest-DPS assignment and backline focus all break the no-healer premise.
records.failure_explanation: Show Shock application, control coverage, reduced/immune duration, which tank held each target and whether the backline was reached.
records.transferability: Element and defense systems can cross: Shock is a status supplier, stun is survival and Arya remains the damage owner.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has not accepted continuous stun locks or TLF's Realm Creator Origin.
records.project_question: How can a status-control formation substitute for healing without creating permanent enemy denial?

records.version_scope: Named April 2025 1.x Karina One Man Army speedrun build
records.rule_support: Karina gains critical chance from shield and has attack-speed casting plus Omnicrit, allowing shield and offensive multipliers to share one payoff owner.
records.practical_support: The guide targets roughly 1150 shield, uses duplicated One Man Army passives to exceed 100% crit, obtains shield from Golden Armor, shield rings or Realm Creator plus lifesteal, then replaces early crit items with damage.
records.disagreement_or_limit: It is a single-hero challenge and a Japanese author guide, not a standard party or general meta sample.
records.mechanism: Current shield is converted into critical chance and then multiplied by AD, crit damage, attack speed and separate damage bonuses.
records.engine: Shield generation from equipment or overheal conversion
records.state_resource: Current shield, critical chance, lifesteal, item slots and offensive multipliers
records.trigger: Karina enters combat with enough shield and maintains the shield source
records.scope: One Karina payoff owner
records.payoff: Guaranteed critical attacks and Omnicrit-enabled spell/item damage
records.survival: One shield/lifesteal slot also prevents immediate death while the remaining slots maximize damage
records.spatial_condition: The challenge largely removes formation dependencies because no allied protection or target split exists
records.payoff_owner: Karina
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Use early Musket/Dagger/Pistol crit, then replace crit chance with AD/crit damage after the shield engine reaches the cap.
records.counterplay: Shield denial or burst removes both offense and defense; standard Act 4 bosses also punish single-owner and single-tank compression.
records.failure_explanation: Report shield uptime separately from crit cap, damage multipliers and the attack/cast event that consumed the window.
records.transferability: A shield-to-offense item can empower one shooter without turning every shielded ally into a carry.
records.incompatible_assumptions: One Man Army duplicates a passive and removes standard formation demands; the project should not copy its coefficient or cap.
records.project_question: Should a shield-to-attack converter read current shield, generated shield, maximum shield or bonus defensive stats?

records.version_scope: Early Access and initial-1.0 guides; exact item values excluded

records.practical_support: Karina, Giachi, Jalen Reborn and the tank/sustain archetypes use different generators and converters rather than one universal shield payoff.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Some examples are historical or author-specific, so this record supports the structural pattern rather than current balance.

records.payoff: Critical chance, AD/SP, direct damage, reflected damage or team buffs
records.survival: The original defensive state must retain enough value to buy operating time
records.spatial_condition: Tank aggro, aura coverage, allied shield coverage and protected carry location remain distinct requirements
records.payoff_owner: Karina, Giachi, a designated carry or the explicitly broadcast team
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Acquire a converter only when the run already has a viable defensive generator and beneficiary; otherwise keep generic survival or pivot.

records.failure_explanation: Attribute generation, conversion, beneficiary and lost defensive uptime separately.

records.incompatible_assumptions: TLF item names, coefficients and unrestricted team broadcasts are not accepted project rules.
records.project_question: Which first-version relics broadcast tank bonus HP/Defense to one carry versus the whole formation, and what caps prevent quadratic scaling?

records.version_scope: Initial-1.0 strategy explanation plus official 1.0/1.0.1 lifecycle
records.rule_support: Surge is a shared fight battery: Energy raises Surge levels, levels do nothing without payoffs and Slowdown raises later level cost.
records.practical_support: The guide puts generators on support heroes and when-you-Surge payoff items on carries; the official patch removed seven hidden Slowdown costs that were not described.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The exact initial-1.0 baseline and item values may have changed after the guide's labelled period.
records.mechanism: Team generation and one or more explicit readers share a cadence meter with escalating cost.
records.engine: Baseline and item/hero Energy generation
records.state_resource: Energy, Surge level, level cap and accumulated Slowdown
records.trigger: Each 100 Energy threshold after applicable Slowdown
records.scope: Whole-team battery with individually owned payoff effects
records.payoff: When-you-Surge stats, casts or direct level-reading effects
records.survival: Support heroes can own generation while protected carries reserve slots for payoff
records.spatial_condition: Indirect unless a generator requires attacks, damage taken or aura coverage
records.payoff_owner: Each hero holding a Surge payoff; not the meter itself
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Do not buy payoff without a strong generator, and avoid excessive Slowdown unless generation scales with it.
records.counterplay: Early burst, disabling the generator or forcing long gaps before later thresholds reduces payoff frequency.
records.failure_explanation: Report Energy by source, each threshold cost, Slowdown, triggered payoff and beneficiary.
records.transferability: Shared meters require source attribution and do not intrinsically grant power without an authored reader.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has not accepted Surge, a 100-Energy threshold or its level cap.
records.project_question: Could a shared shield/status meter support several payoff owners without hiding escalating trigger cost?

records.version_scope: Initial-1.0 strategy guide and 1.0 hero reference
records.rule_support: Summon builds distinguish summon-count payoffs, attacking-summon payoffs, crit/on-hit routes and hero-specific requirements such as Zephys maintaining three Elementals or Dagon preserving shield.
records.practical_support: The strategy guide estimates four or more contributing heroes plus passives/Origins for a full line and warns that high commitment is not necessarily stronger; the named shock party uses Zephys summons only as a survival bridge.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Accessible text does not specify complete occupancy, spawn-order or cap rules, so no population conclusion is inferred.

records.failure_explanation: Report summon creator, live/count basis, missed spawn or death, received buffs and actual damage owner.

records.version_scope: Initial-1.0 strategy guide and 1.0-updated boss tips
records.rule_support: Act 4 bosses combine top-DPS stun/rot, linked healing, split cleave, distance-targeted orbs, summons and enrage rather than only higher stats.
records.practical_support: The guide uses multiple damage owners into Vizera, clustered AOE into Corruptors and two tanks plus an orb-soaker, splash spacing and summon clear into The Hands.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The detailed boss recommendations come from one expert guide; exact damage thresholds are not preserved as universal rules.
records.mechanism: Bosses test payoff redundancy, AOE, split tanking, distance targeting and add clear as separate capabilities.
records.engine: Previewed boss skills and authored target selection
records.state_resource: Damage owners, tank assignments, positions, orb line, AOE throughput and sustain time
records.trigger: Boss casts, top-DPS selection, linked heal, cleave, orb launch and summon waves
records.scope: Whole party and boss arena
records.payoff: A formation that passes the specific capability checks rather than merely maximizing sheet DPS
records.survival: Team sustain, two tanks, cleave sharing and an isolated orb-soaker
records.spatial_condition: Cluster Corruptors; assign one tank per Hand; keep the furthest-from-Lefty orb target on a clear line and outside tank splash
records.payoff_owner: At least two damage heroes for Vizera; AOE owner for Corruptors/adds; assigned tanks and soaker for The Hands
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Before Act 4, add a second damage owner, AOE, team sustain or another tank when the preview exposes a missing capability.
records.counterplay: The encounter counters single-core, single-tank, pure single-target and dense unplanned formations in different ways.
records.failure_explanation: Show the disabled top DPS, healing target/link, tank assignment, cleave shares, orb target/splash and time spent on summons.
records.transferability: Use previewed enemy packages as readable exams for system completeness and pivot windows.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project should author its own grid/target rules and cannot copy TLF arena geometry or boss numbers.
records.project_question: Which early tower bosses separately test multiple payoff owners, AOE and split-frontline positioning?

records.version_scope: Official 1.0 Reborn launch and initial-1.0 practical guide
records.rule_support: After the Act 1 boss, one hero per run can Reborn for a player-chosen mixture of Flame, Gold and Trophies; the chosen variant is static and can trade away parts of the base kit.
records.practical_support: The guide treats a build-around Reborn as a guaranteed half-combo but skips it when no variant fits or its three-resource cost would weaken the run.
records.disagreement_or_limit: 1.0 announced follow-up tuning and 1.0.1 rebalanced content, so individual Reborn power is version-dependent.
records.mechanism: One deterministic hero transformation reduces RNG at the cost of a unique run slot and several currencies.
records.engine: Owned hero plus campfire access after the Act 1 boss
records.state_resource: One Reborn permission, Flame, Gold, Trophies and the retained/lost kit parts
records.trigger: Player confirms a Reborn at campfire
records.scope: One selected hero and any explicit team-wide effect
records.payoff: A guaranteed build-around component or alternate role
records.survival: The player may preserve current resources and skip the transformation when it would destabilize the party
records.spatial_condition: Depends on the transformed hero's resulting role and coverage, not on Reborn itself
records.payoff_owner: The selected Reborn hero or its explicitly named team beneficiaries
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Wait for the other combo half before consuming the unique Reborn and mix payment currencies around the run's current bottleneck.
records.counterplay: A narrow transformation can lose value when enemy packages or acquired items demand the discarded base function.
records.failure_explanation: Expose the selected variant, lost functions, payment mix and which promised combo input never arrived.
records.transferability: A deterministic capstone can provide build direction without making every random offer responsible for consistency.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has not accepted hero transformation, campfire timing or a once-per-run Reborn slot.
records.project_question: Would a deterministic late-run specialization reduce offer variance without erasing earlier equipment commitments?

records.version_scope: Official 1.0 recap changes and 1.0-era strategy guides
records.rule_support: The game exposes a previous-fight recap and 1.0 added the Surge Gauge to that recap; general tips distinguish attack and ability damage in meters.
records.practical_support: The strategy guide explicitly tells players to press R to identify who did what and how much before changing items, passives or formation.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Accessible text does not enumerate every recap field or source-attribution edge case.
records.mechanism: A shared-resource build remains diagnosable when meters expose both contributors and payoff owners.
records.engine: Combat event logging and previous-fight recap
records.state_resource: Damage type, healing, shield, Surge level and per-hero contribution
records.trigger: Fight completion and recap inspection
records.scope: Previous battle and all participating heroes
records.payoff: Evidence-based item, passive, role and position adjustments
records.survival: Healing/shield and first-death evidence distinguish insufficient sustain from insufficient damage
records.spatial_condition: Reports should retain target and position consequences rather than only totals
records.payoff_owner: Each concrete damage, heal, shield, status or shared-meter beneficiary
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Use recap evidence before spending rerolls or replacing a hero assumed to be underperforming.
records.counterplay: Boss disables, target selection and blocked coverage can make a strong item owner appear weak in aggregate totals.
records.failure_explanation: Separate source generation, conversion, trigger, beneficiary, target and final total.
records.transferability: The project's shield/status reports need contributor-to-converter-to-payoff attribution.
records.incompatible_assumptions: TLF's exact recap UI and key binding are not project requirements.

records.version_scope: Official 1.0 Early Access retrospective and contemporary guides
records.rule_support: By 1.0 the game had 65 heroes, 325 items, 150 relics and 60 Origins, while recipe locking, Soft Ban and staged unlocks changed what players were likely to see.
records.practical_support: The developer explicitly reports negative feedback about item dilution; independent guides describe daunting option density, no trait/set-bonus starting reference and the need to preserve AD/SP coverage to avoid excessive rerolls.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The developer also attributes some complaints to underusing cheap rerolls; the sources do not quantify how much each cause contributed.
records.mechanism: A large content pool needs relevance filtering, locking and staged exposure to keep complete build paths reachable.
records.engine: Unlock sets, Soft Ban weighting, recipe locking and rerolls
records.state_resource: Unlocked pool size, relevance signals, reroll currency and current build direction
records.trigger: New unlocks enlarge the pool or repeated rejected offers reveal low relevance
records.scope: Hero, item, relic and Origin offer pools
records.payoff: Maintain build reachability and learning progression without deleting variety
records.survival: Immediate-role coverage reduces the need to gamble current strength on narrow future pieces
records.spatial_condition: None directly; filtered content must still preserve formation-role coverage
records.payoff_owner: The player's current build plan and each offer channel
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Lock relevant recipes, reroll cheaply and unlock complex hybrid content after basic systems are learned.
records.counterplay: Over-filtering can become invisible railroading while under-filtering produces repeated dead offers.
records.failure_explanation: Distinguish missing knowledge, insufficient reroll use, true pool dilution and a build with too few interchangeable pieces.
records.transferability: The first version should validate system paths with a constrained pool before multiplying heroes and relics.
records.incompatible_assumptions: TLF's Soft Ban algorithm and content counts are not specifications for the project.
records.project_question: What relevance rules keep shield and element paths discoverable without forcing the same offers every run?

records.version_scope: Official patch 1.0.1 and initial-1.0 Surge explanation
records.rule_support: Seven rare-to-legendary items carried 5 or 10 Surge Slowdown that was absent from their descriptions; 1.0.1 removed it.
records.practical_support: The guide explains that Slowdown compounds threshold cost and can make an apparently complete Surge package much slower, so an undisclosed value directly hides opportunity cost.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The sources establish the undisclosed rule and removal, not its population-level win-rate impact.
records.mechanism: An undisclosed rate-limit cost made equipment performance diverge from player-visible wording.
records.engine: Item-specific Surge Slowdown
records.state_resource: Cumulative Energy threshold cost
records.trigger: Equipping one of the affected items and attempting later Surge levels
records.scope: Shared Surge meter and all payoff holders
records.payoff: Removal restores the described item value and overall Surge cadence
records.survival: Faster shared triggers can restore defensive or offensive timing before enrage
records.spatial_condition: None
records.payoff_owner: All heroes whose payoff depended on the slowed shared meter
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Before the fix, players could not correctly price affected items because the drawback was invisible.
records.counterplay: No fair counter is created by hidden cost; rate limits must be disclosed as authored rules.
records.failure_explanation: Expose every cadence modifier and the resulting next-trigger time in equipment text and reports.
records.transferability: Any recursion guard, trigger cap or shared-meter slowdown must be visible to the player.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project need not remove rate limits; it must make them explicit.
records.project_question: How will equipment text show shared trigger cost, caps and cooldown changes before purchase?

records.version_scope: Official patch 1.0.2 plus 1.0-era campfire strategy
records.rule_support: Patch 1.0.2 made rerolling Origins at campfire also heal 8 Flame because the option was used less than other campfire choices.
records.practical_support: Guides describe campfire actions as high-value and Flame-expensive, recommend choosing an Origin that helps the current team and delaying a replacement until a later campfire when the full team is clearer.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No before/after usage rate is published, so effectiveness of the buff remains unknown.
records.mechanism: A pivot action gains partial survival compensation when its opportunity cost makes it unattractive.
records.engine: Campfire Origin reroll
records.state_resource: Current Origin fit, Flame health, campfire opportunity and future route access
records.trigger: Player chooses Origin reroll at campfire
records.scope: Run-level Origin and Flame
records.payoff: Replace a mismatched build modifier without falling as far behind healing or upgrade choices
records.survival: The added 8 Flame directly offsets part of the health opportunity cost
records.spatial_condition: None directly; the new Origin still needs to fit the current formation
records.payoff_owner: Whole party or qualifying heroes affected by the replacement Origin
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Avoid rerolling the first Origin solely for a dream line; revisit at a later campfire when team and item commitments are visible.
records.counterplay: Repeatedly fishing for a perfect Origin still spends a scarce campfire action and can leave current strength unresolved.
records.failure_explanation: Show the retained/replaced Origin, healed Flame, skipped alternative and which current units gained value.
records.transferability: If a pivot option is consistently ignored, compare its whole opportunity cost instead of only buffing its final combat number.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has not accepted campfire rerolls, Origins or health restoration as pivot compensation.
records.project_question: What compensation makes abandoning a mismatched run-level modifier a real choice rather than a trap?

records.version_scope: Road-to-1.0 official perk design plus 2.0 community rules answer
records.rule_support: The 2.0 answer states that each major boss grants an Army Size increase and two pre-tournament bosses lead to six normal slots; XP level-ups grant perk choices. The official pre-1.0 patch separately documents Army Size perks and their tradeoffs.
records.practical_support: Army growth arrives at authored milestones while perks can alter it earlier or beyond baseline, so players price immediate composition against future capacity.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The exact current campaign tutorial is not publicly readable; the six-slot and boss-growth wording is a community answer and is version-scoped to 2.0.
records.mechanism: Boss milestones grow normal deployment capacity while level perks can rewrite capacity with explicit costs.
records.engine: Boss victories, XP level-ups and Army Size perks
records.state_resource: Current Army Size, XP, perk slot, boss progress and enemy compensation
records.trigger: Major boss defeat or level-up selection
records.scope: Campaign army and subsequent combats
records.payoff: More simultaneous role owners or a smaller vertically invested army
records.survival: Extra bodies can add frontline and healing, but a capacity perk may strengthen enemies in exchange
records.spatial_condition: Each added unit still requires a legal board hex and a useful target/coverage relationship
records.payoff_owner: The newly deployed unit and the roles it enables, not the capacity number itself
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Hold bench candidates for the next boss slot or choose a perk only when an additional owner is worth its enemy-side cost.
records.counterplay: Enemy scaling, limited equipment and board congestion can make nominally larger armies weaker.
records.failure_explanation: Report unused capacity, missing legal placement, perk opportunity cost and which role the extra slot actually supplied.
records.transferability: Population growth should expose milestone, physical space and compensating cost separately.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project's ordinary population destination is 10 with an 18-cell ceiling, not T&T's six-slot campaign baseline.
records.project_question: Which tower milestones unlock population, and what explicit price makes early extra capacity a build rather than an automatic pick?

records.version_scope: 1.0.61-era March 2025 discussions
records.rule_support: A unit can accumulate up to three upgrades, normally three items and multiple traits; rarity changes availability but does not carry those commitments automatically.
records.practical_support: Players advise retaining a tier-4 common or correctly equipped caster when a rare replacement would lose upgrades, item fit or a desirable trait pair.
records.disagreement_or_limit: These are community heuristics rather than a complete official value formula, and individual traits change the conclusion.
records.mechanism: Replacement compares total invested role value rather than unit rarity alone.

records.state_resource: Tier, rarity, equipped items, trait breakpoints, shop availability and replacement candidate
records.trigger: A higher-rarity unit appears or a current unit no longer fits the army
records.scope: One roster slot plus any traits and equipment it supports
records.payoff: Preserve a proven carry or pivot to a unit whose combined role value is genuinely higher
records.survival: Do not discard a mature tank, healer or caster until its survival function is replaced
records.spatial_condition: Range and formation role can prevent a statistically stronger unit from substituting for the current owner
records.payoff_owner: The retained or replacement unit after all investment layers are counted
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Price lost upgrades, item transfer and trait breakpoints before selling; rare scarcity can make late upgrading harder.

records.failure_explanation: Show value lost by sale, missing replacement function and any trait tier that collapsed.
records.transferability: Recruitment UI should compare responsibility and committed build layers, not imply rarity is a strict upgrade.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has not accepted T&T's three-upgrade or three-item limits.
records.project_question: How will a recruit comparison explain when a lower-rarity invested hero remains the better role owner?

records.version_scope: 1.0.61 build discussion, 1.4.3 unit guide and 2.0 removal rule

records.practical_support: Guides assign Mana Regen/SP to Fritz, Mana Regen rather than SP to Flash's Ignite uptime, and Mana Regen to high-cost Deshret, while other examples use item effects to create a carry or defense-to-damage owner.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Removal pricing is community-reported and version-specific; recommended stats are from one 1.4.3 author, not universal best-in-slot.

records.version_scope: Early-1.0 Ladder 15 route cross-referenced to 1.4.3 roster and trait rules
records.rule_support: The 1.4.3 guide identifies Lime and Micky as the two 1-cost Dragons and Brim and Kio as the two 3-cost Dragons; four Dragons use first-cast fire to tier up allies that contact it.
records.practical_support: The Ladder 15 guide preserves Dragon during random banishment, takes both 1-costs, uses two unrestricted Clovers for both 3-costs, equips Brim with two Attack Speed and one recovery item, tanks Micky/Kio and adds Noble plus a banner.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The build is historical and the Banner holder is not named. Mapping the guide's Chinese 'hammer Dragon' to Brim is roster-based and explicitly labelled.

records.survival: Micky/Kio own tank gear while Brim combines Attack Speed with recovery

records.failure_explanation: Report Clover targets, first-cast timing, fire-contact recipients, tier deltas, Banner source and Egg occupancy.
records.transferability: A trait can require supplier, formation and recipient ownership instead of granting a passive global stat.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has no accepted Dragon/Noble traits, Clover rarity bypass, bench Egg or tier-up fire.
records.project_question: Could an element or shield generator create a spatial field whose recipient, rather than generator, owns the payoff?

records.version_scope: Post-1.2 September 2025 party with 1.4.3 role and 1.4 lifecycle cross-checks
records.rule_support: Fritz provides multi-target damage and Shred, Flash multi-target/Ignite pressure, Deshret healing and death prevention, while later official patches confirm their targeting and cadence are version-sensitive.
records.practical_support: A Mountain Dwarf/Berserker/Find Love/Occultist run used Fritz, Flash, Deshret, Gourmand and Noctus to defeat Lel'Thas three times according to the author; Gourmand off-tanked and penetrated while Noctus supplied Stifle.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This is one player's report. It names neither exact items nor exact hexes, so only roles and later guide-recommended stat directions are recorded.
records.mechanism: A five-slot army closes damage, shred, control, off-tanking and healing instead of maximizing one trait.
records.engine: Mountain Dwarf team modifier, Forbidden Path stats and five complementary unit skills
records.state_resource: Five reduced-capacity slots, equipment saturation, Shred, Ignite, Stifle, Ward/healing and boss duration
records.trigger: Combatant selection, unit acquisition and each unit's cast cycle
records.scope: Fritz, Flash, Deshret, Gourmand and Noctus
records.payoff: Fast multi-target clear plus penetration and control, sustained through final-boss pressure
records.survival: Mountain Dwarf resistance, Gourmand off-tanking and Deshret healing/ward
records.spatial_condition: Role assignment requires Gourmand to take part of the front while protected casters/support act; no fixed source-verifiable hex layout is claimed
records.payoff_owner: Fritz/Flash damage, Noctus control, Gourmand penetration/off-tank and Deshret survival
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Use Find Love units as sellable bridges, restart if the required Forbidden Path is absent, use Clovers for targets and replace Koda's pure tank slot with Deshret's healing for the final requirement.
records.counterplay: Anti-heal, backline access, Ward targeting constraints and the lost sixth body attack different party layers.
records.failure_explanation: Separate damage owners, Shred/Stifle uptime, Ward target, healing, off-tank damage and the missing role after any replacement.
records.transferability: A build family needs explicit role closure and replaceable owners, not only a shared trait label.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The combatant classes, five-slot Mountain Dwarf cap and named units are T&T content.
records.project_question: Can a shield composition still visibly reserve owners for damage, control, healing and armor penetration?

records.version_scope: 2.0 launch player route and official Uber Item design
records.rule_support: 2.0 adds Uber Items that double core stats and enhance effects, explicitly raising one-unit ceilings; the community rule answer gives six normal late-game slots.
records.practical_support: The reported route uses Rainbow Slime Bottle plus three Cosmic Mediums, save/load and reroll offsets to force a 3/4-star 3-cost carry, then Ultimate Eternal Scythe, two Legendary supports and immunity; one clear used only three units after two capacity reductions.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The author calls the method cheesy and unintended and supplies no population-level data. Save/load manipulation is not a normal build recommendation.
records.mechanism: Extreme tier and equipment investment can replace several ordinary bodies and make unused capacity intentional.
records.engine: Transformation materials, reroll-dependent RNG state, Uber/Ultimate equipment and Legendary supports
records.state_resource: Gold before first shop, reroll count, transformation result, carry tier, item slots, Army Size and overtime
records.trigger: First-shop transformation and later overtime scaling
records.scope: One selected carry plus two supports
records.payoff: A single high-star owner survives into overtime and clears after the rest of the board dies
records.survival: Lifesteal, debuff/CC immunity and support effects keep the carry active
records.spatial_condition: The carry must avoid early control/focus while supports remain in effective range; the source does not provide fixed hexes
records.payoff_owner: The transformed carry; support and item contributions remain separately owned
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Bank Gold, choose the carry before buying later offers, and direct all items/perks/banners around it; aborting after early lock-in is expensive.
records.counterplay: Direct carry counters, anti-lifesteal, burst before overtime, crowd control and support removal attack the compressed structure.
records.failure_explanation: Expose RNG manipulation boundary, carry tier, unused capacity, immunity sources, time-to-overtime and support contribution.
records.transferability: Population builds need a vertical alternative, but deterministic RNG exploits must not become the consistency tool.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project does not accept duplicate-item Uber crafting, save/load result enumeration or T&T's capacity-reducing effects.
records.project_question: How much team-stat conversion may one carry receive before ten-body roster play collapses into a three-unit solution?

records.version_scope: 1.0.61 community comparison plus 1.4.3 trait guide
records.rule_support: Traits differ structurally: Marksman continues rewarding width, Dweller reads total tier, Dragon/Engineer use breakpoints plus tier or spatial readers, and banners can add a missing trait point.
records.practical_support: Players advise building tank/damage/heal roles first, using banners and duplicators as bridges, and selling early momentum traits rather than forcing every race/class to maximum.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Demon width is disputed because random Demonlord assignment and a weak death perk point in different directions; no consensus tier list is inferred.
records.mechanism: Breakpoint activation, post-breakpoint width, total-tier scaling, random beneficiaries and bridge items are distinct trait functions.
records.engine: Unit tags, trait counts, unit tiers, banners and duplicators
records.state_resource: Active breakpoint, bodies beyond breakpoint, total tier, beneficiary pool and bridge inventory
records.trigger: Recruit, sell, merge or equip a trait banner
records.scope: Qualifying units, a random owner or a trait-created battlefield object
records.payoff: Role stats, scaling turret/fire, economy momentum or access to a second trait family
records.survival: Role-first construction prevents a nominally complete trait from lacking tanking or healing
records.spatial_condition: Some traits add adjacency, fields or objects; count alone cannot guarantee activation value
records.payoff_owner: Explicit qualifying unit, random selected carry or object-generated recipient depending on the trait
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Use common/uncommon bridges, banners or duplicators, then sell scrappable momentum units when a mature role owner arrives.
records.counterplay: Trait disruption, beneficiary dilution, poor object placement and rare-unit upgrade scarcity attack different variants.
records.failure_explanation: Display threshold, excess contributors, total tier, selected beneficiary and which bridge prevents a role gap.
records.transferability: Do not encode every system as a single 2/4 count; label the reader and count basis separately.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project's traits, banners and merging rules remain undecided.
records.project_question: Which shield and element bonuses are breakpoints, which continue with width, and which read one owner's tier or state?

records.version_scope: Road-to-1.0 Mythic rework and 1.4.3 practical positioning
records.rule_support: The official rework changed Legend to Mythic, removed extra cost, grants Valor to the Mythic and one random adjacent ally, and adds Mana Regen when Mythics receive Valor from one another under a two-unit cap.
records.practical_support: The 1.4.3 guide recommends two Mythics adjacent only to each other so random Valor cannot land on an unintended ally.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact current numerical Valor values are version-dependent; the positioning recommendation is one author's optimization.
records.mechanism: A limited premium pair converts adjacency control into deterministic mutual buff ownership.
records.engine: One or two Mythic units and start-of-combat Valor assignment
records.state_resource: Two-unit cap, adjacent ally set, Valor recipients and bonus Mana Regen
records.trigger: Start of combat
records.scope: Each Mythic and one random adjacent ally
records.payoff: Damage amplification/resistance and mutual Mana Regen when the pair isolates together
records.survival: Valor resistance helps the two owners survive without requiring a global team buff
records.spatial_condition: Make a two-unit island; any third adjacent ally reintroduces recipient variance
records.payoff_owner: The Mythics and the ally randomly selected from their adjacent set
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A second Mythic consumes the premium-unit cap but can stabilize recipient ownership and cadence.
records.counterplay: Forced displacement, adjacency constraints or splitting the pair removes the mutual guarantee.
records.failure_explanation: Show candidate adjacent set, selected Valor recipient, mutual Mana bonus and any displacement that changed it.
records.transferability: Random adjacency can become controllable when board shape makes the candidate set visible.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has no accepted Mythic cap or random-adjacent buff.
records.project_question: Could a shield relic select one adjacent carry while allowing formation to deterministically control the candidate set?

records.version_scope: Road-to-1.0 rework, 1.2 follow-up and 1.4.3 guide
records.rule_support: Engineers gained a max-health shield and a Turret whose damage scales with Engineer tier; stage II adds repeated AOE, and 1.2 later increased starting and per-tier damage.
records.practical_support: The 1.4.3 guide says 2 Engineers are easy but low-impact, while 4 transforms turret speed/AOE; a special hammer works best on a high-Mana-Regen Caster.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No usage or win-rate data quantifies the rework outcome, and the guide's strength judgement is not official.
records.mechanism: A trait-created turret was changed from fixed damage to team-tier scaling after its late-game payoff failed to grow.
records.engine: Engineer trait count, total unit tier and turret firing
records.state_resource: Engineer bodies, total tier, stage II, turret attack cadence and hammer holder Mana
records.trigger: Combat start, turret shots and hammer-holder casts
records.scope: Engineer holders and one shared turret
records.payoff: Scaling physical shots and stage-II AOE rather than a fixed early-game projectile
records.survival: Each Engineer starts with shield; the turret remains useful only if the team survives long enough to fire
records.spatial_condition: Turret targeting and hammer-holder safety matter even though total-tier scaling is global
records.payoff_owner: The turret for damage, Engineers for tier input and the hammer Caster for ammo/cadence contribution
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Duplicators and power rolls can raise total tier, but four-body commitment competes with role coverage.
records.counterplay: Kill low-tier Engineers, rush before repeated fire, or separate targets to reduce AOE value.
records.failure_explanation: Report each Engineer tier, turret shot cadence, AOE shots, hammer casts and shield absorbed.
records.transferability: Shared summons need an explicit scaling base and contributor attribution so they do not become obsolete or opaque.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project's summons and temporary-unit occupancy are not specified by T&T's single Turret.
records.project_question: Should a team construct scale from contributor count, total upgrade tier or a dedicated equipment owner?

records.version_scope: 1.0.61 targeting observation, 1.2 targeting rule and 1.4.3 trait guide
records.rule_support: Official 1.2 makes Taunt override even skills with special target filters; the 1.4.3 guide documents Chaser backline access and Aquatic fountain cells that can benefit enemies.
records.practical_support: Players treat composition, equipment and positioning as separate high-difficulty layers and observe enemies moving toward the nearest available target to reduce incoming damage and increase friendly output.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Nearest-target behavior is community-observed rather than a complete official targeting specification; Chaser strength is one 1.4.3 author's view.
records.mechanism: Taunt, nearest-target movement, fixed PvE layouts, backline access and dual-benefit cells interact as spatial control channels.
records.engine: Authored enemy formation, target filters, Taunt, Chaser movement and fountain hexes
records.state_resource: Reachable targets, distance, backline exposure, occupied fountain and terrain override
records.trigger: Target acquisition, Taunt application or stepping onto the battlefield object
records.scope: Individual attacker/target pairs and units occupying the object
records.payoff: Redirect focus, bypass frontline or gain Mana Regen from a controlled hex
records.survival: Bait units and protected backlines manipulate first contact; enemy access to the fountain can reverse the benefit
records.spatial_condition: Chaser exploits fixed rear positions; fountain can cover pit/fire/mud and higher tiers demand formation around it
records.payoff_owner: The unit that acquires the target or stands on the object, regardless of team unless the rule says otherwise
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Recruit Taunt/backline access or change placement only when the previewed enemy package creates value.
records.counterplay: Move the vulnerable owner, offer decoy targets, block reachability or contest/avoid the dual-benefit object.
records.failure_explanation: Show target candidate set, Taunt source, path/distance, object occupant and which side received the benefit.
records.transferability: Fixed PvE layouts require stronger preview and counter placement because the enemy cannot respond like a human lobby.
records.incompatible_assumptions: T&T's exact pathfinding, Chaser and fountain terrain replacement are not project rules.
records.project_question: How will authored floors prevent backline access from becoming a one-sided hard counter while keeping formation meaningful?

records.version_scope: 2.0 launch through 2.0.14
records.rule_support: Developer replies confirm Boss Minions incorrectly gained Tiers/Runes, Boss Heart text displayed nonexistent resistance, and Zolton was dominant before a Mana-cost nerf; 2.0.14 confirms multiple boss/tournament setup bugs.
records.practical_support: Players report needing counter items for late opponents; the developer specifically identifies Ignite as valuable into Zolton because it is stronger against high HP and reduces healing.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Lel'Thas respawn and Shred-o-matic power are individual reports. No matchup rates or exact Zolton Mana delta are public.
records.mechanism: High-HP healing, cadence, illegal tier/rune inputs and misleading tooltips create distinct boss failures and counters.
records.engine: Boss Heart, Boss Minions, Zolton casts, healing and Ignite
records.state_resource: Actual boss modifiers, minion tiers/runes, Mana to first cast, max HP, healing and anti-heal uptime
records.trigger: Boss setup, minion spawn, Zolton cast or Ignite application
records.scope: One regional boss package and the player's counter holders
records.payoff: Delay the dominant cast and reduce high-HP healing with a visible counter rather than raw DPS alone
records.survival: Crowd control, anti-heal and accurate modifier values let the party survive the first ability cycle
records.spatial_condition: Respawn/backline reports and boss target patterns can bypass formation; exact Lel'Thas behavior remains unresolved
records.payoff_owner: Ignite applier, crowd-control owner and each boss/minion source must be separately attributed
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Acquire anti-heal or cadence control before the boss only if the route preview guarantees that the offer is relevant and available.
records.counterplay: The boss counters slow no-anti-heal teams; the player counters high HP/healing, while corrected setup removes unintended power.
records.failure_explanation: Display actual versus described Boss Heart stats, minion tier/rune source, Zolton first-cast time, healing received and healing prevented.
records.transferability: Enemy packages must separate intended counter checks from setup bugs and expose the counter before commitment closes.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project must author its own bosses and cannot assume a random shop will supply mandatory anti-heal.
records.project_question: Which tower boss previews guarantee access to shield break, anti-heal or cadence disruption before testing them?

records.version_scope: 1.0.25 player report and official 1.0.28 fix
records.rule_support: A Receiving Ring on the benched unit copied by Spirit and a Giving Ring on an active Spirit redirected damage to a non-targetable invulnerable ghost, while that ghost persisted until all Spirits died.
records.practical_support: The reporter explains the closed loop as a physically unkillable army; the official patch names the same holder arrangement and fixes the negation loop, including analogous Stasis cases.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The reporter's proposed trait-disable or instant-kill counters were speculative and are not retained as verified counterplay.
records.mechanism: Two ownership effects formed a zero-loss damage-redirection cycle through an invulnerable persistent proxy.
records.engine: Spirit copy, Giving Ring, Receiving Ring and ghost invulnerability
records.state_resource: Active Spirit, benched source, redirect link, ghost targetability and persistence condition
records.trigger: Any damage to the ring-linked active unit
records.scope: Linked Spirit/ghost pair and eventually the whole army's ability to lose
records.payoff: All incoming damage is negated without consuming a finite resource
records.survival: Permanent invulnerability replaces normal mitigation and creates a combat softlock/stalemate risk
records.spatial_condition: Bench versus board ownership is essential even though grid distance is not
records.payoff_owner: The active Spirit benefits while the invulnerable ghost receives the redirected event
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: The combination used ordinary item ownership states, so prevention must occur in rule validation rather than shop rarity alone.
records.counterplay: The official solution removes the loop; fair combat should not depend on an undocumented kill bypass.
records.failure_explanation: Trace original damage target, redirect edges, invulnerability consumption, proxy persistence and loop termination guard.
records.transferability: Shield, redirect, immunity and summon inheritance require an acyclic or resource-consuming resolution contract.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project does not have Spirit ghosts or paired rings, but can reproduce the topology through relic conversions.
records.project_question: What validation rejects shield/redirect conversions that return damage to an immune source without consuming state?

records.rule_support: The developer states that reaching rare units quickly was too consistent and Kio, Noctus, Brim and Wolfgang dominated high-tier play; the subsequent official patch raised PvP Rarity costs.
records.practical_support: Players describe Tactician rank as samey and Dragon/rare rush appearing early, while the developer says changes were already being tested in Experimental.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This is PvP high-rank feedback without pick-rate data and cannot establish Classic Campaign balance.
records.mechanism: A reliable vertical rarity rush compressed strategic variety around the same premium units.
records.engine: PvP rarity upgrades, shop timing and high-tier unit pool
records.state_resource: Star Points, rarity level, round timing and shared opponent snapshots
records.trigger: Early rarity upgrade reaches the rare pool
records.scope: High-rank PvP metagame
records.payoff: Consistent access to premium carries and tanks
records.survival: Early high-tier bodies outscale diverse lower-tier formations
records.spatial_condition: Dominant units still exploit formation, but rarity access is the upstream bottleneck
records.payoff_owner: The early rare units and army that can tier/equip them first
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Raising rarity cost delays access and restores a window for lower-tier investment or alternate lines.
records.counterplay: Economic delay is a system counter; requiring one narrow unit counter after the rush would not fix pool homogenization.
records.failure_explanation: Track time-to-rarity, repeated unit identities, lower-tier opportunity cost and diversity before/after pricing changes.
records.transferability: If one recruitment tier is too deterministic and universally efficient, content diversity becomes cosmetic.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project is single-player and has no PvP rank or shared opponent pool.
records.project_question: What prevents higher-grade heroes from being automatic replacements for invested early heroes?

records.version_scope: 1.0.61 community difficulty through official 1.4 adjustment and 2.0 cheese observation
records.rule_support: Official 1.4 reduced PvE Leader health from 50% to 30%, noting Brutal 5 doubles Leader bonuses and the goal was to reduce Act 1 'restart until you high roll'; it also capped Damage Resistance at 90% to prevent invulnerability softlocks.
records.practical_support: Earlier players describe some high-difficulty early item rolls as near auto-loss, while a 2.0 player later uses save/load and reroll offsets to force a first-shop carry and explicitly blames overtuning.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The 2.0 author's causal claim is subjective and later than the 1.4 fix. It corroborates a recurring behavior pattern, not the same unchanged balance state.
records.mechanism: Excess early enemy scaling turns run health into reroll pressure and can reward restarting or deterministic RNG exploitation.
records.engine: Leader bonuses, Brutal multiplier, first-shop variance and save/load state
records.state_resource: Run hearts, early board strength, shop result, difficulty multiplier and restart time
records.trigger: Act 1 enemy high roll or failed first-shop stabilization
records.scope: High-difficulty campaign opening
records.payoff: A fair survival buffer should allow adaptation instead of making the optimal response immediate restart
records.survival: Run hearts absorb an awkward fight, but doubled Leader stats can exceed the intended recovery window
records.spatial_condition: Formation remains one response layer, but cannot compensate for every early numerical gap
records.payoff_owner: The whole current army; no single unit should be mandatory merely to pass the opening
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Spend or pivot before the first boss when recovery remains possible; avoid designs where save/load selection is more reliable than normal offers.
records.counterplay: Difficulty tuning, visible enemy packages and multiple valid stabilization offers reduce restart pressure.
records.failure_explanation: Distinguish enemy high roll, greed, formation error, missing role and unavailable counter offers.
records.transferability: Tower difficulty should preserve a recoverable adaptation window and hard caps against accidental invulnerability.
records.incompatible_assumptions: T&T's Hearts, Leader multipliers and save format are not project requirements.
records.project_question: How many floors of recovery should remain after an early counter mismatch before a run becomes irrecoverable?

records.version_scope: 2.0 launch to official 2.0.14
records.rule_support: 2.0 introduced a distinct unit set and Knockout opponent loop; 2.0.14 confirms enemy difficulty was selected from all levels, several boss packages had unintended bonuses, and Set 2 now uses separate Challenge Climb progression.
records.practical_support: Players who returned at their former Set 1 difficulty reported first-boss and counter-item failures; the developer separates real learning transfer from bugs and adds a warning against jumping directly into old high levels.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Community reports cannot isolate balance from unfamiliarity. The official patch names concrete bugs but does not prove every remaining Set 2 complaint was solved.
records.mechanism: A new content set needs separate mastery state when its counters and unit language change, especially if opponent packages are difficulty-authored.
records.engine: Set selection, Challenge Climb unlock state, difficulty-filtered enemy packages and first-time warning
records.state_resource: Set-specific mastery, chosen difficulty, opponent package tier and unlocked challenge level
records.trigger: Starting Set 2 Classic/Knockout or loading a migrated profile
records.scope: All Set 2 runs and difficulty progression
records.payoff: Difficulty reflects current-set knowledge instead of inheriting a misleading old-set credential
records.survival: Correct enemy filtering and lower re-entry difficulty restore time to learn new counter packages
records.spatial_condition: New units and direct carry counters can invalidate old formations even when nominal difficulty is unchanged
records.payoff_owner: The player's set-specific progression record and each correctly selected opponent package
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Teach new-set items/traits at lower levels before requiring narrow late-game counter purchases.
records.counterplay: Separate progression, previews and correct filtering prevent unseen top-difficulty armies from masquerading as intended learning tests.
records.failure_explanation: Log selected set/difficulty, actual opponent package difficulty, migrated unlock state and any unintended boss modifiers.
records.transferability: Difficulty state must be scoped to the rules/content version that created the player's mastery.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project is not a seasonal multi-set live service, but future regions or rule variants can create similar mastery drift.
records.project_question: When a tower region introduces a new mechanic family, which difficulty unlocks and tutorials should remain region-specific?

records.version_scope: Late Early Access cadence with 1.1 and 2.0 intervention continuity
records.rule_support: Units resolve movement, targeting, attacks, Mana and skills automatically while cards, pause, limited manual target/move orders and End Turn form a separate intervention layer.
records.practical_support: Players describe a late-EA cycle of auto-pause, discard/draw, Energy refill, unlimited thinking time and real-time resume; the developer explains why End Turn can deliberately hold the timer at half cadence.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The seven-second, five-card and full-Energy values are community-documented for Early Access and are not asserted as current 2.1.18 values.
records.mechanism: A discrete card-resource turn periodically interrupts an otherwise continuous automatic battle.
records.engine: Automatic unit simulation plus pause, hand, Energy and End Turn
records.state_resource: Battle time, card-turn time, hand, Energy, Mana and limited manual orders
records.trigger: Card-turn timer, Energy-producing effect, manual pause or End Turn
records.scope: Player hand and selected unit/tile while all units continue under automatic rules
records.payoff: Precise timing can protect a cast, catch an AOE window or redirect a critical unit without direct continuous control
records.survival: Pause and protection cards create reaction time while the automatic frontline still carries incoming damage
records.spatial_condition: Manual target/move and area cards depend on current unit and tile positions
records.payoff_owner: The card or manual order owns the intervention; the affected unit owns its later automatic action
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Deck size, draw and Energy sources change intervention frequency, while unit recruitment changes what those windows can exploit.
records.counterplay: Resource exhaustion, use limits, target legality and minimum cadence prevent permanent interruption.
records.failure_explanation: Display whether time, card turn or both are paused, why End Turn is required, target legality and the source of any auto-pause.
records.transferability: Keep automatic combat ownership separate from a small, visible tactical-command layer.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has no deck, hand, periodic Energy refill or unlimited card plays; it has two commands and three shared tactical points per battle.
records.project_question: Which command timings should pause combat, and which remain valid only while simulation time advances?

records.version_scope: November 2021 Early Access
records.rule_support: Draw-generated cards can trigger Sentinel, Shield and Might have separate producers/readers, and relics can react to repeated damage events; later 1.1 explicitly rate-limited Knife Tentacle.
records.practical_support: The named Inquisitor Draconic/Relentless party uses Warg, Marble Gargoyle, draw/shield cards and Knife Tentacle/Pink Gem, with Shield Throw and a Might cashout as finishers.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This is an EA player build and cannot establish current strength; exact blood-card and draw-relic names are not invented where the post omits them.
records.mechanism: Repeated draw and Shield events fan out through Sentinel into survival and global damage conversion.
records.engine: Inquisitor, Warg, Sentinel Marble Gargoyle, draw/shield cards and reactive relics
records.state_resource: Hand, Energy, draw count, Shield, Might and trigger count
records.trigger: Draw a card, generate a card, grant Shield or cash out accumulated Might
records.scope: Frontline Gargoyles, selected carry and eventually all enemies
records.payoff: Shield Throw, Might cashout and Knife Tentacle convert defensive/event volume into lethal damage
records.survival: Marble Gargoyle and repeated team Shield keep the engine alive before settlement
records.spatial_condition: Frontline bodies must survive first contact; generated AOE reduces but does not remove formation dependence
records.payoff_owner: The selected damage/cashout holder owns the finish; Gargoyle owns Shield and Sentinel event production
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Golden Warg, a second Gargoyle or Minos are optional upgrades; without draw/relic signals the party remains a conventional Shield line.
records.counterplay: Opening burst, Silence, key-frontline removal and cadence disruption attack separate links.
records.failure_explanation: Attribute each draw, Sentinel activation, Shield grant, Might conversion and relic damage to its source and final owner.
records.transferability: A Shield family can use a distinct offensive reader rather than asking every tank to deal retaliation damage.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has no card draw, Sentinel alliance or Hadean relic package.
records.project_question: Should one equipment holder convert a bounded percentage of team bonus Health/Defense/Shield into its own attack stat?

records.version_scope: September 2021 Early Access with 1.1 Permatrap and 2.0 occupancy cross-checks
records.rule_support: Permatrap affects traps created during the battle, while later occupied/overlapping-tile fixes confirm that trap placement and board legality are mechanical constraints.
records.practical_support: The Nightblade build forms ranged/clone units into a frontline 3x3, centers Shield/Heal/Might traps, waits for enemies to settle, then overlaps Stun/Decay/damage traps under Double Trap Range and Crucial Permatrap.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The build is historical and exact 1.1/2.x trap upgrades differ; the later Toxic Archer/Swamp example corroborates structure, not identical cards.
records.mechanism: Two spatial trap zones convert repeated triggers into simultaneous friendly sustain and enemy control/damage.
records.engine: Ranged and clone units, protective traps, hostile traps, Double Trap Range and Permatrap
records.state_resource: Trap cells, overlap, trigger count, Decay, Shield, Might, clones and persistent traps
records.trigger: Play or trigger a trap after allied and enemy formations have settled
records.scope: Friendly 3x3 zone and overlapping enemy area
records.payoff: Enemy Decay/control and friendly Shield/heal/Might resolve from the same trigger sequence
records.survival: Protective center, stationary ranged units and clone bodies absorb the opening
records.spatial_condition: Center coverage, doubled range, free tiles, enemy clustering and ranged attack distance are mandatory
records.payoff_owner: Individual traps own their effects; protected ranged units or status readers own continuing damage
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Without Permatrap the line remains battle-local; ranged/clone recruits are preferred only when they preserve the zone.
records.counterplay: Displacement, backline access, spread formations, occupied cells and fast opening pressure break the two-zone plan.
records.failure_explanation: Show each trap source, covered cells, overlap count, persistent boundary, illegal placement and affected owner.
records.transferability: Devices need explicit cells, coverage, trigger ownership and persistence instead of a generic area buff.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project does not accept a trap deck or cross-battle Permatrap state.
records.project_question: Can one limited tactical command place a device whose coverage supports a formation without becoming a permanent battlewide engine?

records.version_scope: 2021 Early Access with a similar 1.0 player report
records.rule_support: Hadean separates unit Health, team Might and a card/relic layer capable of converting stored resources into all-enemy damage.
records.practical_support: A five-unit party sacrifices one high-Health tank, doubles the Might granted to survivors and removes all team Might to damage all enemies; another player reports a turn-zero Fragile plus Might cashout.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The 1500/3000/12000 example is author-reported EA arithmetic and not current tuning; no official nerf rationale is available.
records.mechanism: One tank's lost Health becomes distributed offense that a separate settlement effect collects.
records.engine: High-Health tank, Sacrifice, Double Might, compact deck and draw/Energy support
records.state_resource: Tank Health lost, survivor count, per-unit Might, hand order and Energy
records.trigger: Sacrifice then double then remove all Might
records.scope: One sacrificed tank, all surviving allies and all enemies
records.payoff: A single global damage event scales with both defensive investment and survivor count
records.survival: A second tank can alternate sacrifices while the remaining party stays alive until settlement
records.spatial_condition: Global cards bypass most formation once assembled, which is itself the compression risk

records.version_scope: 2.0 Moonhunter launch through 2.1.18 content maintenance

records.version_scope: 1.0 launch builds to official 1.034 response

records.version_scope: 2025 Glory Mode response to prior unlimited campaign time
records.rule_support: The developer states that unlimited time let players grind through even the hardest modes and adds an optional one-to-seven championship lose/skip limit ending the game when exhausted.
records.practical_support: Earlier guides explicitly recommend retrying next month, replaying old arenas, waiting for revives and rebuilding after permadeath because normal campaign time has little or no terminal pressure.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No outcome data shows which Glory allowance is fair or whether grinding was undesirable for all players.
records.mechanism: A finite checkpoint-loss budget converts unlimited recovery time into a run-level survival resource.

records.payoff: Detonate compresses delayed Burn into immediate piercing burst
