records.spatial_condition: Pyromancer needs protected uptime; Paladin and supports need adjacency; Assassin uses Hidden/front-row backline access
records.payoff_owner: Pyromancer owns the main cashout; Assassin may become a separately equipped fallback owner
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Prioritize Druid items/orbs, then Pyromancer cadence; use base-effective Cleric/Assassin when upgrade supply is short.
records.counterplay: Displacement, opening backline damage, cleanse, DOT/piercing pressure on the tank or killing Pyromancer before Detonate breaks the chain.
records.failure_explanation: Attribute Burn by supplier, show state removed by Detonate, piercing damage owner and whether Pyromancer died before its expected cast.
records.transferability: Element builds need distinct suppliers and one legible settlement owner rather than team-wide generic elemental damage.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The exact heroes, items, Burn percentages and static board are not project content.
records.project_question: Which first-version elemental family has a supplier-consumer split clear enough to read in the battle report?

records.version_scope: pre-v1.5 old Corruption 20 effect
records.rule_support: Old C20 began with two heroes and ended with four; v1.5 later moved that old effect into an optional Omen.
records.practical_support: A documented win starts Druid plus Ronin, adds Frostmancer and Berserker, then equips Berserker with Realm Tooth/Whirlwind Axes and Ronin with Symbiote/Enchanter's Rod so the key damage owners survive the normal final boss's Revenge.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This is one player's approximately sixth attempt and no fixed hex map is provided; it is historical after v1.5.
records.mechanism: A tank/healer buys time for two ramping damage owners while Frost and Disarm delay enemy throughput.
records.engine: Druid sustain, Ronin AOE/Disarm, Frostmancer control and Berserker time scaling
records.state_resource: Combat time, Frost, disarmed attacks, growing Attack, lifesteal and Revenge immunity
records.trigger: Repeated attacks/actives until Ronin and Berserker overtake incoming damage
records.scope: Four-hero compressed party
records.payoff: Berserker single-target scaling and Ronin AOE finish the fight
records.survival: Druid, crowd control, lifesteal and owner-specific anti-Revenge equipment
records.spatial_condition: Druid takes first contact while the three payoff/control heroes preserve protected uptime
records.payoff_owner: Ronin and Berserker; immunity belongs to their equipped owners
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Skip an impossible early elite, add AOE/control before the final ramp owner and restart only when the route falls irrecoverably behind.
records.counterplay: Boss actives, Stun, Disarm and insufficient early bodies can kill or reset ramp owners before settlement.
records.failure_explanation: Show time-to-first-cast, time-to-ramp, control uptime, Revenge received by source and which item prevented it.
records.transferability: Compressed population can create hybrid roles, but the final boss still needs a planned counter slot rather than generic more healing.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project's population and boss roster are different, and old C20 is no longer even Astronarch's fixed rule.
records.project_question: When population is temporarily constrained, which hybrid roles preserve choice without becoming mandatory all-purpose heroes?

records.version_scope: 1.2.x-1.5.3 guide periods with v1.4 interaction support
records.rule_support: Guides distinguish HP, Defense, Shield, several heal ownership formulas and Bleed/Burn/Poison/Piercing that bypass Defense and Shield; official v1.4 confirms Fallen intercept can trigger Bone-Spike Armor and Tower Shield multi-copy handling matters.
records.practical_support: Druid can turn attackers into ATK/SPD and ATK into Shield, Paladin turns Defense into adjacent Shield, Brawler turns Max HP into Shield/counter value, and a late Gladiator can use HP-scaling Giant's Clubs for damage.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The effective-HP equation is player-derived from a loading tooltip; exact final-version formulas are not independently published.
records.mechanism: Defense chassis and damage payoff are connected by explicit owner-bound converters rather than an implicit global tank bonus.
records.engine: Incoming attacks, Defense/HP scaling and equipment readers
records.state_resource: HP, effective mitigation, Shield, healing source, attacker count and owner stats
records.trigger: Being attacked, attacking, casting, shielding or equipping an HP/Defense reader
records.scope: One owner, adjacent allies or one generated Shield instance depending on source
records.payoff: Stored defensive investment becomes more uptime, retaliatory damage or a separate carry's settlement window
records.survival: Layered HP, Defense, Shield, heal, cleanse and immunity answer different damage packages
records.spatial_condition: Adjacent shield/intercept and frontline attacker ownership determine who converts the state
records.payoff_owner: The equipped reader or named hero, never the abstract team total
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Select a converter only after the run already owns the matching HP, Defense, Shield or attacker signal.
records.counterplay: Piercing and DOT bypass mitigation/shield, while unused pre-shield and backline focus waste the defensive engine.
records.failure_explanation: Separate raw HP, mitigated damage, shield absorbed, bypass damage, healing source and converter damage by owner.
records.transferability: This directly supports shield plus ranged-carry and defense-to-damage relic designs if ownership and bypass counters stay explicit.
records.incompatible_assumptions: No Astronarch formula, item or percentage becomes accepted project balance.
records.project_question: Should team defense feed one carry through a relic, the defender's own retaliation, or bounded thresholds, and what bypass package tests it?

records.version_scope: v1.3.3 with later 1.5.3 guide context
records.rule_support: v1.3.3 raised Frost cap from 5 to 10, halved per-stack effect, applied Frostmancer passive before active calculation and changed Avalanche to consume all Frost only at 10 stacks for target plus adjacent damage.
records.practical_support: Guides use Frostmancer/Tundra/Frozen defensive items as control and then assign damage to Pyromancer, Assassin or an Avalanche-like owner; a 2025 trio still separates Frost controller from Assassin payoff.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The later guide does not state patch/difficulty and does not establish current meta; maximum Frost effect remained unchanged rather than doubled.
records.mechanism: A low cap that was reached too easily became a wider buildup space with explicit threshold cashout.
records.engine: Frost-applying attacks, passive, global timer items and potions
records.state_resource: Zero-to-ten Frost stacks and per-stack slowdown/control value
records.trigger: Apply Frost; at ten stacks an eligible reader may consume all
records.scope: Enemy target with possible adjacent splash
records.payoff: Control grows gradually, then Avalanche/Frostmancer converts the completed state into burst or stun
records.survival: Slower enemies buy time for tanks and backline owners
records.spatial_condition: Adjacent enemies increase the cashout's group value
records.payoff_owner: The Frostmancer or equipped Avalanche attacker owns settlement; suppliers retain attribution
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: The higher cap requires more supplier/item investment before committing a consumer.
records.counterplay: Fast kills, dispersed enemies, status resistance or removing the payoff owner prevents full-cap settlement.
records.failure_explanation: Show stack source, current cap, stacks consumed, adjacent targets and whether the owner fired before the encounter ended.
records.transferability: A status cap should create build space and a readable payoff window, not merely stop numerical overflow.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has not accepted Frost, ten stacks or an Avalanche item.
records.project_question: Which elemental states should persist as control, and which should invite a visible full-stack cashout?

records.rule_support: Attack interval affects regular attacks and their procs, while active cadence depends on MP cost and gain; official patches separately changed animation bar reset and twice corrected the displayed Speed cap.
records.practical_support: Proc items such as Searing Edge favor speed, high-scaling actives favor Attack plus Orbs, and Lich Wraps/Symbiote target active cost; the 1.5.3 guide warns not to stack displayed attack speed below the cap.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The guide states a general 10 MP per second and the patches expose 0.3/0.5 display drift; a complete final cadence formula is unavailable.
records.mechanism: Regular attacks and active abilities have separate acceleration levers and must not be summarized as one speed number.
records.engine: Attack interval, animation timing, MP gain and active cost reduction
records.state_resource: Seconds per attack, MP, active progress and proc count
records.trigger: Attack animation start, regular hit or sufficient MP
records.scope: Individual hero and equipped attack/active effects
records.payoff: Players can deliberately accelerate status supply or active settlement without assuming both scale together
records.survival: Accurate cadence predicts whether a shield/heal/control cast arrives before the tank fails
records.spatial_condition: Only legal targets and surviving owners turn theoretical cadence into actual triggers
records.payoff_owner: The attacking or casting hero; each item proc remains attributed to its owner
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Stop buying speed at the actual cap and redirect upgrades toward Attack, MP or survival.
records.counterplay: Disarm, Stun, target loss and owner death suppress different cadence channels.
records.failure_explanation: Display real seconds, current MP, next active estimate, wasted cap and interrupted triggers.
records.transferability: Attack speed, cast cadence and tactical-command cooldown should remain separate authored clocks.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Astronarch's exact MP and animation constants do not apply to the project's simulation.
records.project_question: Which cadence channels need separate player-facing forecasts so an item never appears to accelerate the wrong action?

records.version_scope: v1.4.0 with 1.5.3 guide role context
records.rule_support: Fallen intercepts part of incoming damage for adjacent allies, can trigger on-hit defense items such as Bone-Spike Armor and slowly steals HP from non-adjacent allies.
records.practical_support: The official rationale says self/AOE healing can replace a dedicated healer, while the later guide treats Fallen as an off-tank/buffer whose value changes with Helm or tank/caster item sets.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The official announcement intentionally withholds active details and exact percentages; the guide rates Fallen subjectively.
records.mechanism: One hero creates a spatial bargain: protect adjacent allies, drain distant allies and convert intercepted hits into item triggers.
records.engine: Adjacency check, incoming allied damage and non-adjacent HP siphon
records.state_resource: Protected ally damage, Fallen HP, healing throughput and trigger count
records.trigger: Adjacent ally is hit or periodic non-adjacent siphon
records.scope: Fallen, adjacent protected allies and non-adjacent allies
records.payoff: Damage transfer activates retaliation/defense equipment and frees a roster slot from dedicated healing
records.survival: Self/AOE healing must offset intercepted damage and ally HP theft
records.spatial_condition: Adjacency chooses beneficiaries; non-adjacency chooses costs
records.payoff_owner: Fallen owns intercepted damage and triggered items; original ally remains the attack target
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Recruit Fallen only when party healing and formation can finance the interception pattern.
records.counterplay: AOE, concentrated burst on Fallen or forced displacement can turn the protection into accelerated self-destruction.
records.failure_explanation: Show original target, intercepted amount, Fallen trigger, distant-ally HP transfer and resulting death source.
records.transferability: Spatial protection can itself be an engine, but damage ownership and friendly costs must remain explicit.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has no accepted ally-health theft hero or Fallen equivalent.
records.project_question: Can a shield/guard hero create offense by legally owning intercepted hits without obscuring who was originally attacked?

records.version_scope: 2021-2024 guide routes across early full release
records.rule_support: Runs offer fights, elites, events, merchants, item upgrades, potions and Morale; v1.5 added item previews and lowered merchant prices.
records.practical_support: Guides prefer early fights when poor, events when stocked with Gold/Morale, merchants above a Gold threshold, route avoidance for known DOT/debuff enemies, limited losses through Morale and a reserve item/potion kit for elite and Boss tempo.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Lane and elite priorities differ by author and version; they are route heuristics, not guaranteed optimal paths.
records.mechanism: Known encounter packages and current resources determine whether to fight, shop, take an event, spend a potion or preserve a swap kit.
records.engine: Branching map, encounter preview, merchant, events and consumables
records.state_resource: Gold, Morale, potions, current items, upgrade tiers and boss plan
records.trigger: Map-node and precombat decisions
records.scope: Current act and whole run
records.payoff: The build reaches its core upgrades without taking every nominally rewarding fight
records.survival: Morale tolerates selected losses while potions and swap items cover burst, DOT or long fights
records.spatial_condition: Formation is retuned for split groups, adjacency disruption and backline threats before each battle
records.payoff_owner: Run owns route resources; equipped hero owns each temporary counter item
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Skip an impossible elite or buy/upgrade the current answer instead of hoarding for a speculative perfect event.
records.counterplay: Harder lanes and bosses punish a build that spends all counters on routine fights or follows one memorized route.
records.failure_explanation: Record previewed threat, skipped alternatives, Morale before/after, potion timing and unused reserve answers.
records.transferability: Tower routes should expose adaptation windows and make preserving a situational answer a real inventory cost.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has no accepted Morale or potion belt system.
records.project_question: Which tower rewards and previews let players carry one counter forward without making every encounter solvable by free swapping?

records.rule_support: Ancient items stop duplicating already owned Ancient items, and common/rare items reduce their reappearance chance each time seen; items remain equipped to individual heroes and can be upgraded.
records.practical_support: Guides prefer a two-star synergistic item over two one-stars, keep owner-specific boss swap kits and group available pieces into caster, DPS, tank and tempo packages rather than demand one exact recipe.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Reduced reappearance is not a full no-repeat rule and no public drop-weight table exists.
records.mechanism: Weak duplicate protection widens discovery while finite slots and owner-specific synergies preserve commitment.
records.engine: Item rewards, seen weighting, Ancient exclusion, merchant and upgrades
records.state_resource: Seen items, owned Ancient set, item slots, tier and Gold
records.trigger: Item reveal, equip, replace or upgrade
records.scope: Run pool and concrete hero owner
records.payoff: Players more often see new build bridges without being guaranteed a completed set
records.survival: Tank and counter kits compete with damage pieces for the same slots and upgrade budget
records.spatial_condition: Adjacency/attacker/target effects only function on a compatible owner and cell
records.payoff_owner: Equipped hero; run only owns the remaining offer distribution
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Promote the hero already matching a strong item signal, while retaining one counter kit if the final boss needs it.
records.counterplay: Slot pressure, wrong owner, missing upgrade and encounter-specific uselessness prevent a rare item from being universal power.
records.failure_explanation: Show item owner, tier, trigger count, inactive condition and what was replaced or left unequipped.
records.transferability: Offer protection can reduce dead repetition without silently completing a build or erasing item ownership.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has not accepted Astronarch rarity tiers, three slots or seen-weight formula.
records.project_question: How much duplicate protection preserves discovery while still requiring bridges and pivots?

records.rule_support: Three key items each have one acquisition opportunity per run; collecting all combines them into an item that replaces the normal final boss with Primarch, while selling the combined item yields substantial Gold.
records.practical_support: Earlier guides already route around a known final-boss counter kit and value exclusive event items, so keys add a visible choice between a different capability test and immediate economic acceleration.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The practical guides predate v1.6 and do not provide Primarch matchup statistics; they support the existing boss-preparation loop, not the new boss's exact abilities.
records.mechanism: One-time route pickups progressively commit the run to an alternate final exam but retain an explicit sell exit.
records.engine: Three unique key locations, combination and boss replacement
records.state_resource: Keys collected, missed opportunities, combined item and foregone Gold
records.trigger: Accept/skip each key, combine three or sell the result
records.scope: Whole run and final encounter
records.payoff: Alternate boss/achievement or a large economy conversion
records.survival: Players can decline the challenge when the current party lacks the necessary aggression
records.spatial_condition: Indirect; the chosen boss still tests the final formation and item ownership
records.payoff_owner: Run owns keys; the alternate boss flag belongs to the combined item
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: After missing a key, stop investing for Primarch; after combining, choose boss access or Gold based on actual build readiness.
records.counterplay: One missed key closes the route, while selling sacrifices the alternate encounter.
records.failure_explanation: Show key opportunities, accepted/missed state, sell value and the boss package selected before the final act.
records.transferability: Optional challenge routes benefit from progressive commitment, a clear abort value and a different build test.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has no accepted hidden boss or three-key quest.
records.project_question: Could tower branches visibly trade a harder capability exam against immediate build resources without becoming mandatory completion content?

records.version_scope: old C20 through v1.5.0
records.rule_support: v1.5 introduced four optional Omens usable independently with Corruption, replaced C20's effect and moved the old effect into an Omen.
records.practical_support: Three earlier guides show the old C20's two-to-four hero restriction fundamentally changed party composition, forced hybrid roles and added restart variance rather than merely scaling enemy numbers.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The official announcement does not state the new C20 effect, and guide claims about consistency are personal experience.
records.mechanism: A composition-warping rule was separated from the linear difficulty ladder into an independently selectable modifier.

records.state_resource: Unlocked modifiers, active Corruption and selected Omen combination
records.trigger: Pre-run difficulty configuration
records.scope: Whole run rules and roster capacity
records.payoff: Players can combine numerical/progression difficulty with a chosen rule-changing challenge
records.survival: Removing forced compression from C20 restores ordinary role coverage unless its Omen is deliberately chosen
records.spatial_condition: The old modifier reduced available formation bodies and adjacency options
records.payoff_owner: Run configuration owns modifiers; no hero owns the difficulty reward
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Select hybrid heroes only when the roster-compression Omen is active, not as the universal C20 answer.

records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has no accepted Corruption or Omen ladder.
records.project_question: Which future challenge modifiers alter build grammar enough that they must be optional and separately reported?

records.rule_support: v1.2.3 changed bar reset timing and moved displayed Speed cap to 0.3 because 0.2 was inaccurate; v1.5 later stated 0.3 was displayed while functional speed was 0.5 and made the tooltip stop at 0.5.
records.practical_support: Guides use attack interval to compare DPS and proc throughput and warn not to invest below the displayed cap, so the mismatch directly changed item-upgrade decisions.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The two patches describe different intermediate realities; this record preserves the sequence instead of declaring one timeless cap.
records.mechanism: A player-facing cap diverged from simulation after animation timing changes and required a later correction.

records.version_scope: v1.3.5 with v1.5.3 route context
records.rule_support: Interstellar Seller was changed to price sacrifices per item and offer either ATK/SPD or HP/DEF payment; the developer explicitly said this reduced the reason to delay upgrades while waiting for the event.
records.practical_support: Later routing advice treats the event as a deliberate Act 3 vitality/stat sacrifice and otherwise upgrades tank/DPS items along the run instead of universally hoarding unupgraded inventory.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No before/after pick-rate or win-rate statistics are available.

records.rule_support: v1.3.5 fixed Warlord's Burden damage when another hero held Life-giving Chamber and made cross-hero start effects resolve more beneficially; v1.4 fixed Tower Shield being reduced too much when multiple copies were equipped.
records.practical_support: Guides place multiple start-of-combat, shield and percentage-stat items on different owners and sometimes stack Tower Shields, so phase and owner order determine whether the written build works.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The patch gives examples rather than a complete ordering table; 'more beneficial' is not a deterministic tie specification.
records.mechanism: Cross-owner start effects and multiple copies produced outcomes inconsistent with item text until ordering and stacking were corrected.
records.engine: Start-of-combat phase, stable owner order and copy aggregation
records.state_resource: Pre/post-sacrifice HP, Shield contributions, owner stats and item copies

records.scope: All equipped start effects and repeated team items
records.payoff: The same loadout produces a stable, explainable initial state
records.survival: Correct shield and HP ordering prevents accidental opening deaths or over-reduction
records.spatial_condition: Adjacent start effects still require their formation links after global ordering resolves
records.payoff_owner: Each item retains its equipped owner and source attribution
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Players can compare a second copy or cross-owner combo only when the preview shows the resolved order.

records.version_scope: v1.2.3 with early full-release summon context
records.rule_support: v1.2.3 fixed Mother Rat continuing to spawn rats after she was defeated while existing rats remained.
records.practical_support: Guides use Ranger companion, Illusionist copies and disposable Fiend/turtle bodies specifically to buy finite time for a protected ramp owner, so generation lifetime changes the encounter's tempo budget.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Mother Rat is an enemy bug and the sources do not publish universal summon caps or cleanup order.
records.mechanism: Existing temporary units kept a defeated source's generation loop alive until the source-death guard was fixed.

records.state_resource: Source alive/defeated state, existing children and spawn timer
records.trigger: Source defeat and subsequent spawn tick

records.rule_support: Dungeon movement consumes Mana while fights provide Keene and free units; Jewelers buy, sell and reroll units, party/storage slots expand for Keene, and Witch's Maze IX adds harder routes and Magic Hammer rewards.
records.practical_support: The Maze IX route clears most profitable fights, avoids impossible Monster Spots, carries Mana recovery, delays ordinary rerolls and returns to shops only when enough pairs and Keene make a broad roll-down efficient.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact movement/over-capacity Mana formulas and reroll costs are guide-period rules, not a current official table.
records.mechanism: Exploration, roster holding and shop access share a Mana/Keene budget, so recruitment timing is also a route decision.
records.engine: Random floor, fights, Jeweler, traveling Jeweler and party/storage expansion
records.state_resource: Mana, Keene, open slots, held pairs, shop pool and distance to stairs
records.trigger: Move, fight, acquire/sell a unit, reroll or expand a slot
records.scope: Current floor and run roster
records.payoff: A timed roll-down converts broad held pairs into several upgrades and active symbols
records.survival: Mana recovery and selective encounter avoidance prevent economy routing from ending the run
records.spatial_condition: Map position and remaining path determine whether another shop visit is affordable
records.payoff_owner: Run owns economy and slots; upgraded units own stats/skills
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Expand slots before repeated rerolls, then hold multiple pairs rather than chase one named unit from the full pool.
records.counterplay: A difficult Monster Spot or low Mana can force an earlier spend or abandonment of a greedy route.
records.failure_explanation: Show Mana path cost, Keene spent, pairs held, reroll count and missed alternatives.
records.transferability: Recruitment and route resources should expose why holding flexibility delays immediate power.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has no accepted movement Mana, Jeweler or mass duplicate bench.
records.project_question: What run resource makes holding several future pivots meaningfully costly without turning navigation into bookkeeping?

records.rule_support: Units usually carry one color and one mark/symbol, each counted on an independent breakpoint table; exceptions can carry other combinations or random symbols, and official patches can reassign one unit's mark without changing its color identity.
records.practical_support: A player may use Reno's Orange/Fool to close both reliable skill activation and extra-action lines, while Topaz's Yellow/Tower is taken only for Shock and does not require completing Tower.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The beginner guide initially says 'usually' color/trait and a comment corrects that combinations can vary; no final official catalog schema is public.
records.mechanism: Two orthogonal tags create crossing routes where one unit can advance two engines or provide a disposable bridge on only one axis.
records.engine: Unit color contribution plus independent mark contribution
records.state_resource: Counts and active breakpoint levels on both axes
records.trigger: Acquire/upgrade a tagged unit or equip a tagged accessory
records.scope: Run-wide symbol state and whole party effects
records.payoff: One roster choice can close survival, cadence, damage or Gem support without enforcing a fixed faction package
records.survival: Defense colors/marks can cross offensive marks on the same bridge unit
records.spatial_condition: Unit skill and row still determine whether the bridge's body is worth keeping active
records.payoff_owner: Run owns activated symbol effects; concrete units retain skills and stats
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Choose a unit for one needed axis and treat its second tag as an option, not a requirement to complete another line.
records.counterplay: Boss rules can punish particular effect categories even when the tag count is high.
records.failure_explanation: Display which axis each source contributes, the exact breakpoint reached and whether its active body adds any useful skill.
records.transferability: Affinity and role/mechanic tags can cross freely if content includes multiple bridges and no payoff requires one closed six-name recipe.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project's exact affinity and role tags remain undecided; Vivid names and thresholds are not adopted.
records.project_question: Which two project tag axes create meaningful cross-products rather than duplicate team-wide stat bonuses?

records.rule_support: Three copies merge to silver-star and three silver-stars to gold-star; reaching silver permanently acquires that unit's symbols for the run even if the unit is sold.
records.practical_support: High-difficulty guides silver cheap Bronze bridges, sell them for Keene and roster space, retain several two-copy pairs before a roll-down and rarely pursue nine-copy gold-stars because the economy is better spent closing more symbols.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The exact gold-star cost calculation is guide-derived and versions changed upgraded-unit HP; symbol persistence is official enough to receive repeated tutorial improvements but no full state spec is public.

records.payoff_owner: Run build compiler owns the symbol effect
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A shop pivot is safe only when preview and compiled battle state share one authority.
records.counterplay: Not applicable as enemy counter; correctness guard preserves legitimate preparation.
records.failure_explanation: Show authoritative symbol delta and compiled effect before leaving recruitment.
