records.version_scope: v1.1.1-v1.1.5 launch guide
records.rule_support: Meta progression unlocks more Gems/units while random rewards and shops draw from available content; official patches adjusted rarity and reward access but do not confirm a dilution fix.
records.practical_support: One detailed Boss guide recommends not unlocking mutually exclusive Burn/Shock, heal and attack Gem families because unwanted unlocks obstruct collecting three copies of the planned tools; another guide values broad unit exposure, showing the tension is pool-specific rather than universally agreed.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This is one strongly opinionated guide that also uses reload manipulation; no drop table or official acknowledgement establishes population-wide behavior.
records.mechanism: Permanent content unlocks can reduce the probability of assembling a coherent run package and make progress feel punitive.
records.engine: Unlock catalog feeding random Gem/unit reward pools
records.state_resource: Unlocked content breadth and live copies needed for upgrades
records.trigger: Meta unlock followed by randomized offer generation
records.scope: Future runs and multiple reward pools
records.payoff: Specialization improves internal consistency but sacrifices discovery breadth
records.survival: Missing shields/heals because of pool dilution can make Boss counters unavailable
records.spatial_condition: Indirect; target-row Gems may be diluted by functionally wrong attack tools
records.payoff_owner: Meta profile owns unlock breadth; run owns current offers
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Avoid treating every unlock as strictly positive when it enters a shared random pool.
records.counterplay: Offer weighting, category slots, soft bans or unlock-aware guarantees can preserve new content without rewarding non-unlock.
records.failure_explanation: Report pool size, category, seen offers and whether required counter functions remained reachable.
records.transferability: Content progression must not make a smaller account strategically stronger through cleaner pools.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project's meta unlock and reward-pool contracts are not yet accepted.
records.project_question: How will new hero/item unlocks preserve counter availability instead of diluting every future run?

records.version_scope: 2023-07 to 2023-11 post-archive and Challenge updates
records.rule_support: Official updates expose the current Boss decks during character selection/battle and let Challenge Mode upload or fight completed Classic saves.
records.practical_support: A readable save lists distinct previous player builds at floors 15, 30, 45 and 60, while players describe later 75, 90 and 100 walls and a class lock intended to prevent simply mirroring the saved boss.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The exact Classic save/replace schedule and class-lock lifecycle have no complete official rules page; Challenge copying as a loophole is community interpretation.
records.mechanism: A successful player build becomes a future visible Boss package that a later carrier and skill graph must counter.
records.engine: Saved Boss deck, class availability and sequential floors
records.state_resource: Archived class, nine-card deck, star levels and remaining class options
records.trigger: Reach a saved Boss floor or load a completed-save Challenge
records.scope: Persistent Classic save and optional Challenge opponent
records.payoff: Past optimization creates a personalized future capability exam
records.survival: The new build must include enough defense/control to live through the old build's opening graph
records.spatial_condition: Saved ranged, melee, projectile and summon packages change contact distance and body access even without a formation grid
records.payoff_owner: The archived character/deck owns Boss behavior; the current character owns the counter build
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Players must preserve answers for prior builds instead of maximizing only the current floor's damage.
records.counterplay: Inspect exact Boss cards, identify trigger/body/range/damage layers and assemble a non-mirror answer.
records.failure_explanation: Show the archived deck, class, triggering card and layer that ended the current run.
records.transferability: Authored PvE can preserve capability packages and exact previews without copying player saves or class locks.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project does not use uploaded saves, asynchronous PvP or a single-character class ladder.
records.project_question: Could a tower reuse prior successful enemy packages as visible remixes while keeping every counter authored and deterministic?

records.version_scope: 2023-04-25 live major update through post-August community builds
records.rule_support: The major update gives Quick Mode all nine card slots from the start and lets a card carry up to three synergies without the old one-class-plus-one-element restriction.
records.practical_support: Players reuse a Bear/Shield recipe on Druid and Rogue, run non-Warrior variants of Warrior-oriented damage graphs and assemble complete Hunter/Shaman decks from cross-synergy cards.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Sources do not publish the complete shop eligibility table, so this record establishes broad cross-class assembly rather than claiming every card is always equally obtainable.
records.mechanism: The class supplies a carrier bias while nine ordered cards and multi-synergy tags define the actual build engine.
records.engine: Class passive plus nine card slots and one-to-three tags per card
records.state_resource: Open slots, card stars, synergy counts and carrier-specific bonuses
records.trigger: Buy, merge or replace a card and recalculate the skill/synergy graph
records.scope: One active character and its complete deck
records.payoff: A recipe can migrate between carriers while changing access, scaling or survivability
records.survival: Carrier choice determines whether the same cards gain enough defense, control or tempo
records.spatial_condition: Range, AOE and summon proxies still determine contact even though cards are not placed on a team board
records.payoff_owner: The character owns stats; each card owns its effect and tags; the compiled deck owns breakpoints
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Keep a functional early shell and replace whole card clusters when the final carrier/tag combination becomes reachable.
records.counterplay: A class lock or prior-Boss package can deny the easiest carrier without deleting the underlying recipe.
records.failure_explanation: Separate class bonus, card effect, star value and synergy threshold instead of reporting one power score.
records.transferability: Project heroes may bias a build family without being the only legal owner of that family.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project does not accept a single hero with nine unrestricted skill cards or three tags on every effect.
records.project_question: How much should a hero change access and efficiency without turning a build system into either a fixed kit or a classless card pile?

records.version_scope: 2023-02 community rules with 2023-05 and 2023-08 official ordering fixes
records.rule_support: Official patches later distinguish Treant alternating casts and repair wrong form ordering and failed multi-release triggers, confirming that cast sequencing is mechanically consequential.
records.practical_support: Players report active skills scanning left to right, with zero/short-cast cards starving active skills to their right; long cooldowns go left and the final spammer goes right, while passives do not consume the same queue.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This is not a complete current official ordering specification, and Cyclone-like duration behavior creates exceptions to simple cooldown reasoning.
records.mechanism: An ordered active-skill queue makes slot position a timing resource and can silently disable later cards.
records.engine: Left-to-right scan, cast time, cooldown, duration and passive exclusion
records.state_resource: Ready skills and the first legal active card
records.trigger: Character becomes able to cast
records.scope: One character's ordered card row
records.payoff: Intentional order lets several cooldown bands operate around one main skill
records.survival: Defensive or control cards must be placed where a spammer cannot starve them
records.spatial_condition: AOE duration and target contact can make a nominal cooldown effectively continuous
records.payoff_owner: The character cast scheduler owns selection; the chosen card owns its effect
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A newly bought short-cooldown card may be rejected or moved if it disables a more important effect.
records.counterplay: Interrupt, range denial or target invalidation can expose a graph that depended on one uninterrupted spammer.
records.failure_explanation: Show the scan order, first ready card, blocked cards and next legal cast time.
records.transferability: Any deterministic hero action priority must be inspectable and explain skipped legal-looking abilities.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Project heroes do not use a freely reordered nine-card cast row.
records.project_question: How will a selected hero explain which legal attack, heal or ability won the current priority decision?

records.version_scope: 2023-04-25 live major update
records.rule_support: Critical Casting triggers all connected active skills to its right, Hit Casting always triggers the skill on its right, and Trigger Sprite relocates eligible triggers while calculations keep the original character's attributes.
records.practical_support: Players build around one main active, use forms or trigger cards to bypass normal queue starvation, and combine Spell Totem/Trigger Sprite/Bestow with Shield/Loot Box cards.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The complete eligibility and simultaneous-resolution order remain unpublished; translation names vary between Trigger Sprite and Trigger Elf.
records.mechanism: Adjacent cards form directed edges, while a summoned proxy may change origin position without stealing stat ownership.
records.engine: Hit/crit trigger edge, right-side adjacency and capped Trigger Sprite
records.state_resource: Trigger event, eligible connected skills, proxy count and original attributes
records.trigger: Basic hit, critical hit, Loot Box or shield-break event
records.scope: Original character, connected cards and temporary proxy
records.payoff: One event deliberately fans into a bounded skill package
records.survival: Proxy position can keep the original damage owner away from contact
records.spatial_condition: Trigger Sprite changes cast origin but not source stats, so range and target coverage move separately from ownership
records.payoff_owner: Original character owns attributes; proxy owns origin; triggered card owns effect
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A trigger card is valuable only when adjacent eligible cards and enough trigger frequency already exist.
records.counterplay: Kill/disable the proxy, break adjacency by replacement or deny the initiating event.
records.failure_explanation: Log trigger source, edge, proxy origin, original stat owner and every rejected child.
records.transferability: Triggered equipment, relics or summons need explicit direction and source attribution.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has no accepted card adjacency or proxy-cast system.
records.project_question: If an ally or summon repeats another hero's effect, which parts inherit position, stats, tags and report ownership?

records.version_scope: 2023-10/11 community build after 2023-08 substantive patches
records.rule_support: Official rules define Hunter attack speed, Combat extra casts, Warrior AOE, multi-tag cards, Chaos width scaling/cap and the repaired Dragon Form trigger behavior used by the recipe.
records.practical_support: A full Hunter deck uses Dragon Form, Curse of Frailty, two Blade Storms, Power of Chaos, Attack Combo, Gambler and two Coins to reach seven named bond thresholds; the author separates additive within-prong bonuses from multiplicative cross-prong scaling.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Strength and exact multiplication are one expert's testing, not official statistics; the build needs two Legendary Coins and is explicitly weak before all nine slots close.
records.mechanism: Attack cadence launches duplicated AOE payoffs through several independently owned damage layers.
records.engine: Hunter attack speed, Dragon Form and two Blade Storm copies
records.state_resource: Nine slots, two Coins, Combat bonus hits, crit, Frailty and seven synergy thresholds
records.trigger: Dragon-form attack and Combat extra attack
records.scope: One Hunter and all contacted enemies
records.payoff: Blade Storm converts attack cadence and cross-prong scaling into AOE burst
records.survival: No dedicated sustain card; it relies on completing and firing burst before contact pressure wins
records.spatial_condition: AOE contact and attack range determine whether both Blade Storm copies acquire targets
records.payoff_owner: Hunter stats and Blade Storm own damage; Coins only supply tags
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Abort or keep an independent transition when two Coins and all nine slots cannot be assembled before the next saved Boss.
records.counterplay: An earlier floor wall, burst survival, range denial or class lock attacks its long non-functional formation window.
records.failure_explanation: Report missing bond thresholds, additive versus multiplicative layer and which main copy failed to trigger.
records.transferability: A single carry can read several team/build states only when the payoff owner and incomplete-build floor remain explicit.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project does not accept nine-card one-character builds, Legendary Coins or these exact synergies.
records.project_question: How many independent multipliers may feed one carry before the build becomes either unreadable or non-functional until perfect?

records.version_scope: 2023-01 pre-major-rework historical build
records.rule_support: Later official reworks confirm Nature/Shield, auras, attack speed, AOE and multi-tag ownership as separate channels and warn that the pre-April values changed materially.
records.practical_support: The historical nine-card Druid uses Bear Form, Battle Fury, Lone Wolf, Hunter/Nature/Shield Auras, Cursed Energy, Curse of Fragility and Enhanced Shield so Shield sustains the body and converts into Attack for cursed cleave basics.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This is a pre-rework all-Legendary single sample; later replies claim Rogue with Mirror Images/basic buffs beats it and can carry the same recipe better.
records.mechanism: Max Shield and replenishment form defensive state, Enhanced Shield converts the state to Attack, and Bear/basic cleave owns damage.
records.engine: Bear attack cadence, Hunter Aura and Shield Aura
records.state_resource: Health, Shield percentage, Attack conversion and curses
records.trigger: Shield regeneration and each basic attack
records.scope: One melee carrier and cleaved nearby enemies
records.payoff: Battle Fury basics cash out Shield-derived Attack through curse-amplified hits
records.survival: Nature and Shield Auras keep the same payoff body alive
records.spatial_condition: The carrier must reach melee/cleave contact; Mirror bodies can add control and effective targets
records.payoff_owner: Carrier basic attack owns damage; Enhanced Shield owns conversion; Auras own supply
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: The recipe can move from Druid to Rogue when carrier bonds or the next Boss make the alternative stronger.
records.counterplay: Rogue Mirror Images and basic-attack scaling add bodies/control and can defeat the original Druid version.
records.failure_explanation: Separate Shield generated, Attack gained, basic/cleave damage and curse amplification by source.
records.transferability: Shield can support offense through a named converter and one payoff owner rather than a global team damage grant.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Exact cards, values, all-Legendary completion and free cross-class transfer are not project rules.
records.project_question: Should a shield carry read current Shield, maximum Shield, Shield gained or Shield spent, and which reading creates the clearest counter?

records.version_scope: 2023-07 after Loot Box/Metamorphosis patch and before 2023-08 balance
records.rule_support: Official updates define Trigger Sprite, Shield/Loot Box rate limits, multi-synergy cards, Dragon Form fixes, Balance/Coin changes and curse trigger eligibility used by the two decks.
records.practical_support: One Shaman clear uses Timeshield, Coin, Spell Totem, Trigger Sprite, Bestow, Shield Aura, Shielding Battlecry, Loot Box and Shield Burst; another starts with Dual Cast Lightning and pivots to Dragon Form plus Agony/Fragility/Elements, two Curse Outbreaks, Enhanced Curse, Balance and Coin.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Both are all-Legendary personal-save outcomes; reported remaining Health is not a general win rate and August patches later changed several cards.
records.mechanism: A complete early Lightning shell is replaced by either a bounded Shield-loss trigger graph or a Dragon-driven curse cashout graph.
records.engine: Dual Cast Lightning transition, then Trigger Sprite/Bestow or Dragon Form
records.state_resource: Shield loss/cooldowns or stacked curses, plus card stars and tags
records.trigger: Shield break, proxy trigger or Dragon-form cast
records.scope: One Shaman carrier, temporary proxies and affected enemies
records.payoff: Loot Box/Shield Burst or duplicated Curse Outbreak owns final damage
records.survival: Timeshield/Shield Aura on one route; curse route relies on fast control/damage and reported high remaining Health
records.spatial_condition: Totem/Sprite origin and curse/AOE range determine target access
records.payoff_owner: Original Shaman attributes remain authoritative; proxies relocate effects; cashout cards own damage
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Use Lightning as a real early build, then replace the cluster only when curse or trigger pieces and stars are complete.
records.counterplay: Rate limits, proxy deletion, Shield denial, cleanse/range or a saved Boss that outscales the transition timing.
records.failure_explanation: Show old/new engine completeness and the exact source of Shield, curse, trigger and cashout.
records.transferability: A healthy pivot can move between two playable engines instead of carrying dead pieces until a nine-part combo appears.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has no card shop, all-Legendary deck or unrestricted Dragon/curse package.
records.project_question: Can each future build core name at least one independent transition shell that remains useful before the payoff appears?

records.version_scope: 2022-12 historical guide contrasted with 2023-04 to 2023-08 guards
records.rule_support: Official updates let triggers cast summon/buff skills, define proxy ownership and progressively cap Golems, Spirits, Plants and Loot Box frequency.
records.practical_support: The historical guide alternates pet and Bestow cards or gives Skeleton/Rat summons ranged skills plus Loot Box/Shield cards, producing a body wall that can keep melee curse/one-hit bosses away from the original caster.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Claims of thousands of pets and hundreds of triggers per second are author hyperbole/observation, not measured limits; later versions deliberately changed the graph.
records.mechanism: Temporary units inherit or cast connected skills, multiplying origins and creating physical access pressure in addition to damage.
records.engine: Summon source plus repeated Bestow/trigger edges
records.state_resource: Living summons, inherited effects, summon limits and available target space
records.trigger: Summon cast, inherited cast or summon death
records.scope: Original owner, temporary children and nearby enemies
records.payoff: Many origins generate projectiles/triggers and body-block a melee Boss
records.survival: Disposable bodies keep the ranged owner behind them
records.spatial_condition: Body density, push/contact and AOE coverage determine whether quantity protects or collapses
records.payoff_owner: Original character owns stats unless a rule transfers them; each summon owns position and lifetime
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: The chain consumes most card slots and should be abandoned when AOE or performance limits make quantity negative.
records.counterplay: Wide AOE/projectile bounce clears the wall; strong single-target melee is itself blocked by excessive bodies.
records.failure_explanation: Report summon source, child skill, inherited stats, living count, cap rejection and body-access result.
records.transferability: Temporary units may be spatial defense and trigger carriers only with explicit occupancy and ownership.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project's 18-cell ceiling forbids unbounded pet clouds, pushing stacks or invisible extra occupancy.
records.project_question: Which temporary-unit effects justify consuming a real cell, and how should overflow fail visibly?

records.version_scope: 2023-04-25 to 2023-04-28 major-update period
records.rule_support: The official update makes all elemental Golems share one summon limit, and a follow-up fixes Golem-death limit accounting.
records.practical_support: A player explains that Stonehenge and four elemental Golems visually suggest a mixed set, but the shared cap and leftmost replacement favor one Golem repeatedly recast and make Summon Fusion appear non-functional.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The claim that mono-Golem is best and Warlock is weak is one player's evaluation without usage data.
records.mechanism: A legal shared cap contradicts the content's apparent collect-several composition and compresses diversity.
records.engine: Four Golem cards, one shared limit and leftmost replacement behavior
records.state_resource: Current Golem count, types and cap
records.trigger: Cast another Golem or resolve Golem death/Fusion
records.scope: All Golem summons owned by one character
records.payoff: Mono-type recasting frees slots while retaining generic Golem-count value
records.survival: A stable replacement loop preserves the frontline but removes intended elemental variety
records.spatial_condition: Summoned frontline occupancy is shared even when elemental visuals differ
records.payoff_owner: Shared family cap owns legality; the leftmost card may own replacement identity
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Sell or skip extra Golem types when they consume slots without increasing legal presence.
records.counterplay: AOE and summon deletion remain answers, but do not repair misleading build affordance.
records.failure_explanation: Display family cap, type contribution and why a Fusion/recast was rejected.
records.transferability: Capacity rules must support the composition shape that content names and visuals promise.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Project temporary units use physical cells, not a hidden Golem family counter.
records.project_question: If several summon variants form a set, does the cap reward variety, specialization or neither?

records.rule_support: Carnivorous Plant cannot create itself on death and later cannot receive Warlock quantity bonuses; Soul Strike spirits attack once with a cap of two and can no longer have lifetime refreshed by Summon Fusion.
records.practical_support: The earlier guide intentionally chains pet deaths, Bestow and resurrection and reports severe quantity/performance pressure, showing why child eligibility and lifetime refresh matter to real builds.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No public profiler data or exact maximum total entity count was found.
records.mechanism: Death-generated children use explicit self-exclusion, quantity eligibility, lifetime and population caps to stop recursive growth.
records.engine: Summon death trigger, Plant/Soul child rules and Summon Fusion
records.state_resource: Living child count, child type, remaining lifetime and shared cap
records.trigger: Temporary unit dies, attacks once or receives a fusion attempt
records.scope: One summon family and its descendants
records.payoff: Death value remains buildable without infinite descendants or permanent short-lived damage bodies
records.survival: Temporary children can absorb contact only for their authored lifetime
records.spatial_condition: Every additional body increases crowding and AOE vulnerability even when under a logical cap
records.payoff_owner: Root skill owns lineage; child owns one attack/lifetime; family cap owns admission
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Invest in death triggers only when capped child value still justifies the card slots.
records.counterplay: AOE deletes children; self-exclusion prevents deaths from creating a self-sustaining board.
records.failure_explanation: Log root source, generation depth, cap/eligibility rejection and lifetime expiration.
records.transferability: Every death summon requires lineage, generation depth, occupancy and refresh policy before content authoring.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Project summons cannot exceed legal cells or keep battle alive after persistent heroes die.
records.project_question: Should any project summon create another summon, and if so what generation and lifetime rules make the chain finite?

records.rule_support: Metamorphosis was changed so every quality consumes only its own summons; Legendary no longer devours all summons, and its Health increase became fixed rather than scaling with consumed count.
records.practical_support: Historical summon recipes place several independently generated pet families and Bestow chains in one deck, where global consumption would erase other engines and make ownership unclear.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The patch states the new ownership rule but not the usage rate or exact prior dominance of global consumption.
records.mechanism: A sacrifice payoff consumes descendants from its own source rather than every friendly temporary unit.
records.engine: Metamorphosis and its authored summon lineage
records.state_resource: Owned living summons and fixed transformation Health
records.trigger: Enter Metamorphosis
records.scope: The form owner and only that source's summons
records.payoff: Consumed bodies become temporary Attack while unrelated summon engines remain intact
records.survival: Fixed maximum-Health gain prevents quantity from multiplying both defense and offense without bound
records.spatial_condition: Consumed bodies disappear from contact/occupancy while the transformed owner remains
records.payoff_owner: Metamorphosis owner receives Attack/Health; each summon lineage determines eligibility
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A sacrifice card is evaluated against the value of its own child package, not the whole board.
records.counterplay: Delete eligible summons before transformation or pressure the owner after it spends its body wall.
records.failure_explanation: List every consumed summon, its root source and the fixed versus per-body rewards.
records.transferability: Sacrifice effects should default to an explicit source family instead of silently consuming all temporary allies.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has no accepted global summon-devour form or free-form card lineage.
records.project_question: When a hero sacrifices temporary units, which source relationships define legal victims and who receives the conversion?

records.rule_support: Loot Box was barred from randomly casting Shield skills specifically to avoid infinite loops, then its Shield-loss trigger received a maximum of three activations per second and erroneous form triggering was fixed.
records.practical_support: Both the historical three-card Loot Box/Shield Burst/Shield Aura core and a later Shaman nine-card deck intentionally generate Shield, break it and cash out random/Shield damage through proxies.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The guide's hundreds-per-second claim predates the cap and is not measured; exact random skill weights are unavailable.
records.mechanism: Shield loss can drive a random-cast payoff only after removing self-replenishing children and enforcing a per-second cap.
records.engine: Shield Aura/Battlecry, Shield loss and Loot Box
records.state_resource: Current Shield, activations in the current second and eligible random skill pool
records.trigger: Lose all Shield
records.scope: One character and any proxy-triggered Loot Box
records.payoff: At most three bounded random casts per second plus explicit Shield Burst damage
records.survival: Shield generation still protects the owner without recursively regenerating through Loot Box
records.spatial_condition: Proxy origin may alter cast range, but the Shield owner remains the trigger source
records.payoff_owner: Shield owner creates the event; Loot Box owns random cast; child skill owns its effect
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A compact three-card engine remains useful, but extra trigger frequency has diminishing value at the cap.
records.counterplay: Avoid breaking Shield repeatedly, disable the owner/proxy or survive the bounded burst window.
records.failure_explanation: Show Shield depletion, activations used/capped, rejected Shield children and final cast owners.
records.transferability: Any trigger that can regenerate its own prerequisite needs eligibility exclusion and a visible rate limit.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Random Loot Boxes and Shield-loss command spam are not accepted project mechanics.
records.project_question: Which future relic/equipment triggers can recreate their own input, and where must recursion be cut?

records.version_scope: 2022-12 historical builds versus 2023-04-25 major rework
records.rule_support: The live major update separates Shield cap/damage blocking, Nature max Health, AOE/Combat/Arcane modifiers and life/shield-based Boss normalization into distinct channels.
records.practical_support: Historical builds use Shield as defense, Shield Burst/Defense Shield as damage, Enhanced Shield as Attack conversion, or Bestow Shield skills to summons; none requires Shield itself to be an element.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact pre/post values and card tags changed materially, so this record normalizes ownership rather than preserving a recipe as current balance.
records.mechanism: One defensive state can feed basic Attack, direct Shield damage, random triggers or temporary-unit survival through different converters.
records.engine: Shield generation from Aura, Battlecry or Nature/Shield synergy
records.state_resource: Current/max Shield, Shield lost and Shield-derived Attack
records.trigger: Gain Shield, lose all Shield, basic attack or explicit Shield skill cast
records.scope: Carrier, summoned recipients or contacted enemies depending on converter
records.payoff: Enhanced Shield/basic attack, Shield Burst or bounded Loot Box becomes the identifiable damage owner
records.survival: Unspent Shield blocks a capped share of incoming damage
records.spatial_condition: Melee cleave, proxy origin and AOE range distinguish otherwise similar Shield routes
records.payoff_owner: Shield source, converter and final attack remain separate owners
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Choose one payoff route and enough supply rather than stacking every Shield reader in one graph.
records.counterplay: Shield bypass, cleanse/disable, burst before regeneration or refusing repeated break events attack different variants.
records.failure_explanation: Report Shield generated/blocked/lost and damage credited to each reader separately.
records.transferability: Shield can stay an orthogonal chassis while ice, earth or another affinity changes supplier, control or payoff behavior.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Dungeon 100 card values and Shield synergies do not define project balance.
records.project_question: Which first-version Shield reader provides damage without making every shielded hero a universal carry?

records.version_scope: 2023-03-24 test concepts confirmed in 2023-04-25 live update
records.rule_support: Nine mixed-damage cards add a second element and trigger its synergy; live Fire reads triggering-skill damage with a five-per-second cap, Frost stacks taken damage, Lightning adds bounces and Chaos reads other active synergies.
records.practical_support: Historical Curse, one-hit, infinite-Lightning and fire-explosion recipes use different supplier/state/payoff chains and counter different target counts rather than sharing one generic elemental multiplier.
records.disagreement_or_limit: March was a test branch and April changed many values; the guide predates both and supports archetype use, not current numbers.
records.mechanism: Damage-type bridge cards let one hit activate a second elemental engine while each element reads a different event/state.
records.engine: Primary damage skill plus added-element bridge
records.state_resource: Triggering damage, Frost stacks, bounce count, Fire activations or active-synergy width
records.trigger: Deal the primary specified damage type
records.scope: Hit target, AOE neighbors or chained targets
records.payoff: Fire repeats bounded AOE, Frost amplifies later hits, Lightning reaches more bodies and Chaos rewards width
records.survival: No element automatically supplies survival; Shield/Nature or control cards remain separate commitments
records.spatial_condition: Target density, bounce availability and AOE range determine elemental value
records.payoff_owner: Bridge supplies the second trigger; each elemental synergy owns its own payoff
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Take a bridge when both its source damage and second payoff already have usable support.
records.counterplay: Single targets suppress bounce/AOE; cleanse/resistance or cap saturation attacks stack/trigger routes.
records.failure_explanation: Attribute base hit, added element, secondary trigger and capped/stacked payoff separately.
records.transferability: Affinities should modify distinct events and spatial conditions rather than repaint one damage formula.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has no accepted Fire/Frost/Lightning/Chaos roster or these breakpoints.
records.project_question: Which affinity bridges create real cross-system decisions without letting one hit activate every element?

records.version_scope: 2023-04-25 Quick Mode launch
records.rule_support: Quick Mode uses 30 floors, full-screen swarms, shorter battles, fixed five Gold per round, one interest per ten saved Gold capped at five, cheaper shop upgrades and all nine card slots unlocked at start.
records.practical_support: Players distinguish early complete Lightning shells from late nine-card/two-Coin graphs and report when a finished route cannot pass intermediate saved Bosses, showing that open capacity does not remove acquisition timing.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Quick economy cannot define Classic income, shop odds or Boss cadence; public sources do not give full rarity probabilities.
records.mechanism: Capacity is front-loaded while Gold saving, shop level and card-star completion remain competing tempo investments.
records.engine: Per-round Gold, capped interest and cheaper shop upgrades
records.state_resource: Gold, shop level, nine open slots, card pairs/copies and remaining floors
records.trigger: End preparation round or buy/merge/upgrade
records.scope: One 30-floor Quick run
records.payoff: Saving reaches a bounded economy plateau that funds higher-star completed graphs
records.survival: Spending early on a functional shell trades maximum future interest for immediate floor safety
records.spatial_condition: Full-screen swarm favors AOE/bounce and changes which incomplete build survives
records.payoff_owner: Run economy owns interest; each card owns star/effect; deck owns graph completeness
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Stop greed before an intermediate wall, or use a low-star transition and roll only when multiple final pieces are live outs.
records.counterplay: Swarm floors punish single-target greed; late saved Bosses punish a transition kept too long.
records.failure_explanation: Show interest gained/forgone, shop spend, missing pieces and floor capability mismatch.
records.transferability: Open roster capacity does not replace an explicit economy tension between immediate function and late build closure.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Project population, rewards and recruitment are unresolved and should not copy this 30-floor curve.
records.project_question: What bounded saving or upgrade decision creates tempo without importing PvP-style interest by default?

records.rule_support: Boss decks are inspectable during selection/battle, and Challenge Mode accepts completed Classic saves as opponents.
records.practical_support: Players say Classic locks the Boss's class to avoid exact mirror copying, while Challenge challengers may still select that class and reproduce the same deck, undermining the stated anti-mirror purpose.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The anti-mirror rationale and loophole are player analysis; no official response or frequency data was found.
records.mechanism: Exact enemy information supports deliberate counters, but inconsistent carrier restrictions can turn the answer into trivial cloning.
records.engine: Boss archive preview, class lock and Challenge save sharing
records.state_resource: Known enemy cards and legal current carriers
records.trigger: Select a class or enter a saved Challenge
records.scope: Classic progression versus external Challenge run
records.payoff: A player can plan a counter before committing the run
records.survival: Preview reveals whether burst, body wall, Shield or control is required
records.spatial_condition: Exact range/summon/projectile cards communicate contact conditions
records.payoff_owner: Preview owns information; mode rules own legal carrier choices
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Commit to a differentiated answer rather than reconstructing the identical Boss graph.
records.counterplay: Rule consistency must prevent trivial mirror abuse while preserving multiple legitimate answers.
records.failure_explanation: Explain unavailable carriers and whether the same restriction applies in every mode.
records.transferability: Enemy previews should reveal capabilities without prescribing one named answer or enabling an exact clone shortcut.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project uses authored single-player encounters, not shared player saves or class locks.
records.project_question: How much enemy build detail should a floor preview expose so counters are deliberate but discovery remains meaningful?

records.rule_support: Self-Boss fights first received more damage reduction to avoid instant kills, then the reduction was replaced by Life/Shield enhancement explicitly because fights could deal only one damage; life/shield-scaling attacks were normalized downward in Boss fights.
records.practical_support: Player saves show early and later saved builds creating very uneven walls, so a global Boss durability transform directly changes whether a counter fight bursts, stalls or remains solvable.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No before/after duration statistics or exact Boss scaling table is published.
records.mechanism: Boss durability moved from extreme damage reduction to larger readable pools, with special normalization for attacks that scale from those pools.
records.engine: Archived build converted into Boss Health/Shield scaling
records.state_resource: Boss maximum Life, Shield and incoming damage floor
records.trigger: Fight one's saved Boss
records.scope: Both sides in a self-Boss encounter
records.payoff: The original build identity remains while damage stays above a one-point stalemate
records.survival: Larger pools lengthen response windows without making mitigation opaque
records.spatial_condition: Longer time preserves room for range/contact counters rather than instant resolution
records.payoff_owner: Encounter modifier owns Boss durability; cards retain their normal damage ownership
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Players can evaluate whether more damage or a different counter is needed instead of facing an artificial floor.
records.counterplay: Health/Shield scaling remains answerable by damage type, sustain pressure and explicit pool-based normalization.
records.failure_explanation: Show base and Boss-modified pools, mitigation and any normalized max-pool damage separately.
records.transferability: Boss conversion should scale visible resources and preserve counter channels instead of applying near-total hidden reduction.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Project Bosses are authored enemies, not transformed copies of player characters.
records.project_question: How can elite/Boss durability increase without invalidating defense-to-offense builds or collapsing combat into minimum damage?

records.version_scope: 2022-12 guide observation and 2023-04-27 official warning
records.rule_support: The developer added a warning that acceleration may cause damage loss and later continued fixing pathfinding and multi-release behavior.
records.practical_support: The historical Infinite Lightning guide reports projectile position evaluated per frame and low refresh allowing shots to pass through enemies, making dense projectile builds both performance-heavy and result-sensitive.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The guide's frame explanation is a player hypothesis, and the official note does not enumerate all affected effects.
records.mechanism: Presentation/acceleration rate changes hit or trigger sampling and therefore combat outcome.
records.engine: Projectile travel, frame sampling, acceleration and trigger release
records.state_resource: Projectile positions, pending hits and simulation steps
records.trigger: Run combat at accelerated/low-render conditions
records.scope: Projectile, pathfinding and multi-release effects
records.payoff: None; speed convenience incorrectly changes realized damage
records.survival: Missed hits can turn an otherwise sufficient build into a false failure
records.spatial_condition: Fast projectiles crossing target bounds between evaluated positions cause the loss
records.payoff_owner: Simulation owns collision/event delivery; the skill should retain credit independent of speed
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Players should never need to build around a chosen observation speed.
records.counterplay: Not legitimate counterplay; fixed simulation stepping/swept hits must remove the discrepancy.
records.failure_explanation: Record simulation time, event creation and hit resolution independent of rendered frames.
records.transferability: Project x1/x2/x4 presentation must preserve deterministic ordering, outcomes and attribution.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Dungeon 100's speed implementation is not reused by the project.
records.project_question: Which automated replay tests will prove every supported speed produces the same digest?

records.version_scope: 2023-02-24 to 2023-04-25 test-to-live transition
records.rule_support: The developer moved unstable updates to beta for one-to-two months, then disclosed a broad card-code restructure with deleted cards, aura/bond/star changes, unlisted changes, many expected bugs and difficulty problems before the later live major update.
records.practical_support: Players already struggled to infer basic cast order and card starvation, so simultaneous rule, value and content replacement made comparison and migration especially fragile.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This establishes release/process instability and version discontinuity, not that every redesigned mechanic failed after launch.
records.mechanism: A large content-graph rewrite invalidated old builds and saves faster than rules, migration and QA could stabilize.
records.engine: Card code, removed effects, rewritten synergies and test/live branches
records.state_resource: Existing decks, saved Bosses, card ids/stars and current branch
records.trigger: Load an old save or follow an old build after the rework
records.scope: Whole build system and persistent saves
records.payoff: The later graph supports cross-element/multi-tag design, but only after explicit stabilization
records.survival: Difficulty and defensive assumptions drifted with the same rework
records.spatial_condition: Range/AOE/projectile rules were also changed, so old spatial expectations were unsafe
records.payoff_owner: Versioned ruleset owns compatibility; old save cannot silently mix eras
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Guides and saved decks require version labels; removed cards need migration or honest invalidation.
records.counterplay: Not enemy counterplay; staged rollout, compatibility tests and complete notes reduce false failures.
records.failure_explanation: Expose branch/version, migrated/removed card ids and rule deltas before loading combat.
records.transferability: System-wide build changes require explicit authority, migration and versioned test coverage rather than piecemeal hotfixing.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project does not reuse Dungeon 100 saves or card ids.
records.project_question: What build-state schema and migration policy will keep future hero/item/relic reworks inspectable?

records.rule_support: The final substantive patch fixed Dragon Form infinite added-damage stacking, pet bonuses while not transformed, Gold/Legend bonus errors and failed Deadly Rhythm/Time Shield triggers; earlier patches fixed Resurrection/Skeleton and Loot Box interactions.
records.practical_support: The post-Aug Hunter deck makes Dragon Form the cadence driver for two Blade Storms and several scaling layers, so a form-state or ownership error multiplies through the complete build rather than affecting one card.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No telemetry shows the prevalence or post-fix strength; the exact runtime ordering remains incomplete.
records.mechanism: A transformation rewrites attack/cast behavior and touches summons, buffs, Shield and quality tiers, creating a high-risk cross-system state boundary.
records.engine: Dragon Form active state and all-skills-on-attack behavior
records.state_resource: Form active flag, per-source damage stacks, pet bonuses and triggered buff eligibility
records.trigger: Enter/leave form, attack in form or resolve a connected trigger
records.scope: One transformed character and its entire card graph
records.payoff: Bounded form cadence launches legitimate connected skills without permanent or duplicate bonuses
records.survival: Time Shield and summon/resurrection interactions must follow the same form state
records.spatial_condition: All released skills still require valid origins, ranges and targets
records.payoff_owner: Form changes cadence; each child skill owns damage; state authority owns eligibility
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A form is a high-coupling core and should not be offered as a casual bridge without compatible cards.
records.counterplay: Downtime outside form, interrupting attack cadence and surviving its bounded window remain legitimate answers.
records.failure_explanation: Log form enter/exit, each inherited bonus, child cast and rejected cross-state trigger.
records.transferability: Rule-rewriting forms/relics need one authoritative state boundary and explicit interaction tests with every trigger family.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has no accepted all-skills-on-attack form or these card interactions.
records.project_question: Which future rule-rewriting relics are valuable enough to justify a complete interaction matrix and stricter coupling budget?

records.version_scope: 0.3.0 historical guide, 2022 formation discussion and 1.0.1 input update
records.rule_support: The campaign party uses fixed front, back, left and right slots around the King; official 1.0.1 exposes mouse, WASD/arrows and tank-control movement/rotation inputs.
records.practical_support: The Pacifist route continuously moves the whole party, keeps distance and loops enemies through persistent hooks or gates, while the formation thread treats non-cross layouts as a suggestion rather than an existing rule.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No complete official collision, target-reselection or rotation-update order is public, and the detailed slot guide is historical 0.3.0.
records.mechanism: A fixed relative cross is translated and rotated through continuous player control, changing contact, range and environmental overlap together.
records.engine: Player movement and rotation of the King-centered party
records.state_resource: Party center, facing, four relative slots, movement speed and nearby targets
records.trigger: Every movement or rotation input during campaign combat
records.scope: King plus all four slotted heroes
records.payoff: Choose which hero contacts first, preserve ranged distance or align the team with hazards and pickups
records.survival: Kiting and active hazard avoidance replace part of static frontline durability
records.spatial_condition: All hero positions remain relative to the moving center, so one input changes every range and collision relationship
records.payoff_owner: Player input owns party displacement; each hero retains its attacks, heals and effects
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Recruitment must account for whether a hero can function in one of four fixed relative slots.
records.counterplay: Slow, narrow safe zones, repeated dashes and forced corner objectives tax the same movement budget.
records.failure_explanation: Separate failure to move the center, wrong slot/facing, insufficient movement speed and a hero's own targeting failure.
records.transferability: Use explicit relative-slot ownership and range/contact capability tests, not continuous whole-party steering.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project uses prebattle deployment and limited tactical commands, not persistent twin-stick movement or rotation.
records.project_question: Which relative-slot bonuses remain readable when mapped onto a larger grid rather than a four-body cross?

records.version_scope: 0.3.0 historical forms/items with 0.4.6 and 1.0.1 slot-specific item changes
records.rule_support: Druid historically becomes Turtle in front, Wolf on a side and healer in back; many items read front/back/left/right, and later patches continue changing the slot where interaction items grant secondary stats.
records.practical_support: Players compare position-locked Druid healing against Cleric flexibility and identify slot bonuses as a constraint on proposed custom formations.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact forms and item values changed after 0.3.0; current complete item text is unavailable.
records.mechanism: Relative slot is an authored input to hero form and equipment effect rather than a cosmetic placement label.
records.engine: Assign a hero and its item package to one of four named slots
records.state_resource: Slot identity, active form, item owner and team-broadcast qualifier
records.trigger: Shop reassignment and battle start
records.scope: One holder plus any explicitly broadcast allies
records.payoff: Turn the same recruit into tank, damage or healing and close a role gap with slot-aware equipment
records.survival: Front Turtle or defensive front-slot items absorb contact while back-slot healing stays protected
records.spatial_condition: Front/back/opposite-side identity and the whole formation's facing must remain stable and visible
records.payoff_owner: Hero owns form actions; item holder owns local effect; the item source owns any team broadcast
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A flexible hero reduces replacement cost only if the needed slot is available and its items remain compatible.
records.counterplay: Forced movement, flank access or a boss that invalidates the required slot can disable the role package.
records.failure_explanation: Show active form, slot-derived modifiers, broadcast recipients and invalidated spatial conditions separately.
records.transferability: Preview position-driven role/equipment changes during deployment and preserve explicit ownership.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy four fixed slots or infer that arbitrary grid movement should continuously change class form.
records.project_question: Should a future position-dependent hero read row, adjacency or facing, and when is that choice locked?

records.version_scope: 0.3.0 historical rule cross-checked by later hero and item haste changes
records.rule_support: Haste affects attacks, healing and hourglass-marked skill cooldowns; official patches alter high-Haste firing, hero Haste duration and movement-speed-linked cadence.
records.practical_support: Healer comparisons require roughly enough Haste to maintain regeneration or direct-heal coverage, while damage teams use the same source to accelerate multihit or Burn application.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The public sources do not expose the complete current cooldown formula or caps.
records.mechanism: One cadence stat accelerates several action families, so its value depends on which owner converts additional actions into a payoff.
records.engine: Hero traits and equipment grant Haste
records.state_resource: Attack interval, heal interval, eligible skill cooldown and Haste duration
records.trigger: Each action timer advances while the Haste modifier is active
records.scope: Holder or explicitly broadcast party members
records.payoff: More attacks, heals or skill activations within the same encounter window
records.survival: Healing and control uptime can convert the same cadence investment into durability
records.spatial_condition: Extra actions matter only while legal targets remain in attack/heal/skill range
records.payoff_owner: Each accelerated actor owns its action; the Haste source owns only the enabling modifier
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Prefer Haste when several current actors have useful legal actions, not simply because it is a universal label.
records.counterplay: Disarm, slow, no legal target, forced displacement and short invulnerability windows waste accelerated cadence.
records.failure_explanation: Report Haste source, affected timer, legal-target downtime and actions gained rather than one aggregate speed score.
records.transferability: A shared cadence stat needs action-family eligibility, caps and owner-attributed realized uptime.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has no accepted universal Haste stat or Just King cooldown formula.
records.project_question: Should attack, heal and ability cadence share one stat, or require explicit converters to avoid universal best-in-slot scaling?

records.version_scope: 2025-10 to 2026-06 community party, with historical and official movement-scaling cross-checks
records.rule_support: Ronin's level-three multihit cadence is movement-speed-linked; official patches added and later reduced party movement speed around the skill.
records.practical_support: A named party uses Knight stun, Huntress movement speed and Bard Haste to let Ronin reach full movement speed and trigger many level-three hits; a reply substitutes Ranger for Huntress when a starting item already covers speed.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This is a small community sample without difficulty, complete items or win rate and does not establish current best play.
records.mechanism: Two support stats and a control window are converted into one melee owner's repeated multihit payoff.
records.engine: Huntress movement-speed buff, Bard Haste and Knight stun
records.state_resource: Ronin movement speed, attack count and level-three trigger progress
records.trigger: Ronin attacks and reaches the movement-linked level-three threshold
records.scope: Ronin payoff supported by four-hero party
records.payoff: Repeated Steel Storm multihits into controlled targets
records.survival: Knight absorbs contact and stuns; Bard supplies support, or Ranger wolves body-block in the alternate line
records.spatial_condition: The moving cross must maintain Ronin contact without exposing the support slots
records.payoff_owner: Ronin owns damage; Huntress/Bard own buffs; Knight owns stun
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Replace Huntress with Ranger only after another source already closes the movement-speed requirement.
records.counterplay: Slow, repeated boss dashes, untargetable phases and initial burst reduce contact or remove the carry.
records.failure_explanation: Separate missing speed, insufficient attack uptime, failed stun coverage and carry death.
records.transferability: Team-wide defensive or tempo support can feed one visible payoff owner through a named conversion rule.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not require continuous manual pursuit or adopt historical percentages.
records.project_question: What battle-visible threshold tells the player that a support stat has activated a carry's conversion payoff?

records.version_scope: 2022-08 Early Access build with 0.3.0 hero and ownership rules
records.rule_support: Knight provides tanking, AOE and stun; Cleric/Paladin provide differently owned healing; Imp applies stacking Burn and historically spreads it on death at level three.
records.practical_support: The named cross puts Knight front, two Clerics or Paladins on the sides and Imp back, prioritizing Imp flat damage/Haste and healer cooldown while placing aura items on the King.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The composition and values predate the 0.4 item/stat rework and are retained as a structural case, not current meta.
records.mechanism: A defensive shell preserves one backline status payoff long enough to stack and spread.
records.engine: Knight control plus two healer action loops
records.state_resource: Frontline Block/HP, healing cadence and Burn stacks
records.trigger: Knight contacts enemies, healers repair damage and Imp repeatedly attacks
records.scope: Four-hero cross and Burn targets
records.payoff: Imp single-target Burn accumulation and death-driven area spread
records.survival: Knight holds front while two healers cover one another or self-heal according to class
records.spatial_condition: Front initiates, side slots maintain coverage and back keeps the damage owner outside first contact
records.payoff_owner: Imp owns Burn; Knight owns control/AOE; each healer owns healing; aura source owns its modifier
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Choose Cleric for resurrection/burst recovery or Paladin for self-sustain and a tougher side/front line.
records.counterplay: Backline access, forced movement, anti-heal, cleanse or enemies that do not remain stacked break different parts of the line.
records.failure_explanation: Attribute frontline failure, missed heals, cleansed Burn and backline access separately.
records.transferability: A shield/heal chassis can support an elemental carry without becoming the same vertical trait system.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project does not use King-centered slots, historical Burn values or King aura inventory.
records.project_question: Which defensive chassis should remain compatible with multiple payoff owners without becoming mandatory?

records.version_scope: 2022-08 Early Access community build
records.rule_support: Archer historically fires three arrows, Hot Hands supplies Haste, Frenzy supplies percent damage and movement speed, and Rusher adds party movement speed.
records.practical_support: A named two-Archer/two-Berserker line upgrades one Archer, gives it flat-damage or flame-AOE equipment and relies on movement-speed kiting rather than a heavy tank.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The author calls kiting easy, but no difficulty, exact equipment roll or win-rate sample is available and later patches changed items.
records.mechanism: Flat damage and percent scaling multiply a multihit carry while party movement supplies survival.
records.engine: Hot Hands Haste, Frenzy kill stacks and Rusher movement speed
records.state_resource: Archer attack cadence, flat damage, Frenzy stacks and party movement speed
records.trigger: Archer fires, enemies die and Frenzy stacks accumulate
records.scope: Primary Archer plus party-wide trait effects
records.payoff: Rapid multi-arrow or flame-AOE damage from one upgraded Archer
records.survival: The whole party keeps distance through movement instead of relying on a durable front
records.spatial_condition: Open space and continuous player kiting are required to preserve ranged uptime
records.payoff_owner: One level-three Archer owns primary damage; trait sources own Haste/movement/damage modifiers
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Prioritize one Archer upgrade and leave support duplicates lower-level when resources are scarce.
records.counterplay: Slow, narrow safe zones, unavoidable telegraphs and ranged/backline threats invalidate movement-only defense.
records.failure_explanation: Show whether the failure came from missing upgrade/items, lost spacing or insufficient kill-stack ramp.
records.transferability: Team bonuses can feed one ranged carry, but survival must remain a distinct, counterable layer.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project cannot require real-time kiting as the baseline defense of a build.
records.project_question: What autonomous spacing behavior or limited command can express a kiting archetype without turning combat into direct control?

records.version_scope: 2022-08 Area 3 Hard single-run report
records.rule_support: Bard historically generates extra economy and Discord support while level-three Captain summons Forgotten Heroes; Haste affects both support and combat cadence.
records.practical_support: The recorded run starts with Chainmail, uses Frost Witch as an early bridge, saves Bard income for Wrath Crown, then wins with two level-three Bards, one level-one Bard and a level-three Captain.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This is one successful hard-mode run, and linked screenshots are not used to infer unwritten item values.
records.mechanism: An economic support body funds a late summon/support payoff and can remain under-upgraded when rerolls miss.
records.engine: Bard extra Gold and Haste items
records.state_resource: Gold, Bard/Captain levels, Discord uptime and Forgotten Hero bodies
records.trigger: Shop rewards fund Crown purchase; combat starts Captain summons and Bard support
records.scope: Three Bards, one Captain and temporary summons
records.payoff: Discord control/damage plus Forgotten Heroes clears waves while Haste sustains the party
records.survival: Starting armor, an early Frost Witch slow bridge and final slowing/Haste items
records.spatial_condition: Captain/summons require contact while Bards need protected relative slots and safe movement
records.payoff_owner: Captain owns summons; each Bard owns Discord/support; King-held Crown owns party Haste modifier
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Sell or replace Frost Witch after the final party closes; accept one level-one Bard instead of exhausting Gold on perfection.
records.counterplay: Early elites, summon-clearing AOE, burst into support slots and missing the expensive Crown strain the line.
records.failure_explanation: Separate economy miss, bridge failure, reroll miss, summon loss and support-slot death.
records.transferability: A bridge hero can have a complete early job and a clear replacement point without being a fake core.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has no accepted Bard economy, Crown or wave-start ghost army.
records.project_question: How should the offer UI identify a functional bridge and communicate the encounter that ends its usefulness?

records.version_scope: 0.3.0 through patch 1.1.0 guide, with 0.4.0 token-source rework
records.rule_support: Heroes are bought, moved and sold in the shop; same-synergy heroes or class tokens upgrade a hero to level three, and 0.4.0 moved token acquisition into MVP/SVP combat rewards while increasing costs.
records.practical_support: Guides use level-three milestones for unlocks and builds, while a 2025 discussion treats a full level-three party as standard before later sinks.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No complete current shop odds, duplicate count table or resale formula is public.

records.trigger: Buy, combine, feed token or sell a hero

records.payoff: Level-three skill and stronger base performance
records.survival: Early functional bodies or bridges keep the run alive before perfect upgrades
records.spatial_condition: An upgraded hero still needs a legal relative slot and compatible range/contact role
records.payoff_owner: Upgraded hero owns level and skill; reward system owns token generation
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Stop chasing all level-three copies when a functional slot or later resource sink has higher value.

records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has not accepted duplicate merging, class tokens or Just King's four-slot cap.

records.version_scope: 0.3.0 item taxonomy, 0.4.0 rework and patch 1.1.0 achievement guidance

records.version_scope: 0.5.2 Food guide, 1.0 hotfix teaching and 2025-04 community economy description
records.rule_support: Cook converts tokens into permanent stat food after node seven; later sources describe Smith token refinement and a Merchant that charges a token to reveal special items before a Gold purchase.

records.disagreement_or_limit: Smith/Merchant details are community-described and no current conversion table or optimal allocation data is published.

records.spatial_condition: Purchased stats/items still require a compatible owner and slot

records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has not accepted tokens, food, Smith refinement or paid item reveals.
