records.version_scope: 2022-08 Zone 3 discussion, cross-checked with 0.4.0 empowered Oxygen rule
records.rule_support: Zone 3 uses Oxygen and a boss with summons; later official Wicked difficulty explicitly reduces Oxygen as an empowered zone mechanic.
records.practical_support: Players recommend keeping O2 high, entering a corner just after the three-tentacle summon, clearing summons quickly and dodging red slowing projectiles; melee Deep unlock teams struggle to maintain both contact and oxygen.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The claim that phase-two minions also slow is tentative community recollection and not promoted to a firm rule.
records.mechanism: A shared movement budget must alternate between damage contact, summon clearing and corner-based oxygen recovery.
records.engine: Oxygen decay, corner refill, summon cadence and slowing projectiles
records.state_resource: O2, party movement speed, safe corner availability and summon count
records.trigger: Boss phase change, tentacle summon or low Oxygen
records.scope: Whole party and arena corners
records.payoff: Survive the environmental timer while preserving enough damage uptime to finish the boss
records.survival: Timed corner recovery and projectile avoidance
records.spatial_condition: Corners are both required recovery points and occupied danger zones after summons
records.payoff_owner: Encounter owns Oxygen/hazards; heroes own summon clear and boss damage
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Add movement, ranged reach or faster summon clear before committing to a melee-only unlock route.
records.counterplay: The player counters cadence by entering after summons; the boss counters greed through slow and forced travel.
records.failure_explanation: Show Oxygen loss, slow source, corner timing, summon damage and boss-contact downtime separately.
records.transferability: A boss can test resource routing and range/contact as separate capabilities with visible telegraphs.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not require manual corner running or copy an Oxygen meter into the project.
records.project_question: Which battlefield-object objectives can create a prebattle positioning test without demanding continuous steering?

records.version_scope: 2022-10 Early Access achievement route
records.rule_support: Deep hooks or Yokai gates can damage enemies independently of hero, item and King damage; Cultist tentacles require a commanded target to attack.
records.practical_support: The route buys a matching hero to activate the trait, then keeps heroes from dealing damage while continuously luring enemies through environmental objects.
records.disagreement_or_limit: It is a narrow achievement route and does not establish ordinary build strength; later comments mention additional methods without full rules.
records.mechanism: A composition supplies persistent battlefield objects while player movement becomes the targeting engine and the environment owns kills.
records.engine: Two-hero synergy creates hooks or repeating gates
records.state_resource: Object count/location, enemy path, party distance and hero attack eligibility
records.trigger: Enemy crosses an object while heroes remain unable or uncommanded to attack
records.scope: Arena objects and enemies that traverse them
records.payoff: Environment-only damage completes combat with zero hero/item/King damage
records.survival: Continuous kiting keeps the party outside enemy contact
records.spatial_condition: Player loops enemies through persistent objects and preserves a safe following distance
records.payoff_owner: Synergy/object source owns environmental damage; Cultist owns commands but not uncommanded tentacle attacks
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Buy a duplicate to activate the required environmental trait or restart when the shop misses.
records.counterplay: Fast enemies, insufficient open space or objects spawning off the pursuit path break the route.
records.failure_explanation: Damage report must distinguish hero, King, item, summon and battlefield-object sources.
records.transferability: Battlefield objects need explicit creator/root-owner attribution and enemy path interactions.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project should not make continuous manual luring the required activation method.
records.project_question: How can authored devices or terrain remain build-owned while autonomous movement makes their activation legible?

records.version_scope: 2023-04 Zone 4 community report with historical hero and achievement rules
records.rule_support: Zone 4 introduces melee Yokai heroes and a shadow-cloning boss interaction; Ronin and Oni depend on repeated close contact.
records.practical_support: Players report the boss repeatedly crossing the screen faster than melee units can maintain contact and say cloned Berserker/Bard effects can make the encounter substantially harder.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This is a two-player negative report with no official response or duration/win-rate statistics.
records.mechanism: Boss locomotion suppresses actual melee uptime while cloning can turn the player's own support package into an enemy amplifier.
records.engine: Repeated boss dash and shadow copy of party units
records.state_resource: Melee contact time, chase distance and copied hero effects
records.trigger: Boss dashes or creates a shadow copy
records.scope: Melee attackers and copied party package
records.payoff: Boss avoids damage and gains temporary access to the player's synergies
records.survival: Players can reportedly face-tank some passes, but that does not repair missing offensive contact
records.spatial_condition: Target crosses the arena faster than melee engagement can re-establish
records.payoff_owner: Boss owns dash/copy; melee hero retains attempted damage but loses realized uptime
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Bring ranged access, movement/contact control or avoid support units whose hostile copies create extreme pressure.
records.counterplay: Ranged damage, intercept windows and controlled copy selection can answer the exam if telegraphed.
records.failure_explanation: Report theoretical DPS separately from contact uptime and damage/effects produced by each hostile copy.
records.transferability: Boss previews should expose contact denial and copy behavior so roster adaptation is possible.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy the exact dash pattern or infer that the project's melee units share this pursuit behavior.
records.project_question: How will combat reports show that a melee core failed from zero contact rather than insufficient damage scaling?

records.version_scope: 2024-09 to 2024-12 community disagreement plus 1.0.2 difficulty update
records.rule_support: Bosses expose dodgeable attacks and build counters; 1.0.2 adds an optional enemy modifier with more Armor/Damage and faster Sudden Death while strengthening Zone 2 boss attacks.
records.practical_support: One player reports first-read instant-kill frustration and movement-speed pressure; replies cite an item that converts instant kills to one damage, 200-300 HP, 15 Armor, resurrection, Cleric and reaching level three before the boss.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The thread contains direct disagreement and cannot establish representative difficulty or universal fairness.
records.mechanism: Several valid defensive counters exist, but the run may still fail if the player cannot learn the capability exam before an irreversible boss loss.
records.engine: Boss telegraph, lethal effect and preboss build acquisition
records.state_resource: Player knowledge, movement, HP/Armor, resurrection and hero levels
records.trigger: First encounter with a lethal boss pattern
records.scope: Whole party and current run
records.payoff: A prepared build survives or avoids the lethal event
records.survival: Damage conversion, durable stats, resurrection and correct positioning are alternative defenses
records.spatial_condition: Safe-zone proximity and movement speed determine whether dodge remains available
records.payoff_owner: Boss owns telegraph/effect; each defensive item or hero owns its counter
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Spend before the boss on one of several visible answers rather than assuming generic power is sufficient.
records.counterplay: The encounter should preview the tested capability and allow more than one acquisition/spatial response.
records.failure_explanation: Name the lethal skill, available response time, mitigation owner and missing capability without erasing community disagreement.
records.transferability: Enemy previews and postcombat explanations must distinguish missing counter from unreadable first exposure.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project need not copy one-run-loss punishment or reflex-dodge gates.
records.project_question: What preview and early safe demonstration are required before a boss can fairly test a new lethal rule?

records.version_scope: Patch 1.0.0 Zone 5 with 1.1.0 achievement guide and later community boss note
records.rule_support: Dreek Coliseum assigns trophy/favor through fighting on red, blue or neutral ground; Mythic recruitment opens selectable Gods whose blessings include explicit tradeoffs.
records.practical_support: Achievement routes deliberately collect one side's trophies or remain neutral, while a later player reports the final God fight changing after one opponent dies.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The community note is frustration, not a complete phase specification; exact blessing values may have changed.
records.mechanism: Combat location simultaneously chooses encounter score, future blessing and which enemy side receives compensation.
records.engine: Left/right/center kills, trophies and selected Mythic God
records.state_resource: Side score, trophies, God slots and party-wide blessing state
records.trigger: Defeat an enemy on a side, end combat or recruit two/four Mythics
records.scope: Current Zone 5 run and both allied/enemy parties
records.payoff: Chosen God grants a build-shaping rule such as speed/risk or front-slot concentration
records.survival: Tradeoffs include half-health starts, healing cadence or reduced health/damage on non-front heroes
records.spatial_condition: Where the party fights determines score, and movement speed itself can become risk through extra damage taken
records.payoff_owner: Encounter owns trophies; selected God owns blessing; front hero owns concentrated stats
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Recruiting Mythics opens one or two God slots, while swapping a God costs a token.
records.counterplay: Enemy compensation and anti-draw rules prevent one-sided favor from being a free permanent buff.
records.failure_explanation: Show side kills, trophy result, active God, allied benefit and enemy compensation.
records.transferability: A floor rule can turn position into a visible run-level tradeoff rather than a hidden damage modifier.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has no accepted Gods, trophy sides or continuous arena steering.
records.project_question: Which future floor objectives can visibly trade formation safety for a chosen run reward?

records.version_scope: 1.1.0 Duels beta/live and 1.1.5 balance period
records.rule_support: Duels removes the King from combat, becomes fully automatic after battle starts, uses ten PvE/PvP rounds and applies mode-specific hero/item adjustments including a Duels-only backline-jump item.
records.practical_support: The live announcement reports more than 2,000 beta matches and 250 testers, then ongoing weekly balance/data-tool changes; those observations belong to Duels rather than campaign movement play.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No public mapping separates every Duels value from campaign, so later balance notes cannot silently define campaign numbers.
records.mechanism: The same hero/item identities participate in two modes with different control, ownership and balance rules.
records.engine: Mode selection and separate balance tables
records.state_resource: Campaign movement state versus Duels round/loss/rank state
records.trigger: Start campaign or Duels
records.scope: Entire ruleset and all hero/item evidence
records.payoff: Duels supports asynchronous autobattle competition without changing campaign's direct-control identity
records.survival: Duels baseline HP/Armor and loss budget are mode-specific
records.spatial_condition: Campaign moves a King-centered cross; Duels watches stored parties and may use mode-only backline access
records.payoff_owner: Mode authority owns stats and control contract; individual heroes retain effect ownership within that mode
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Ten-round Duels assembly cannot define campaign route/shop decisions.
records.counterplay: Counters and tier lists must name the mode and patch before being compared.
records.failure_explanation: Reports must store mode, patch and control contract alongside result.
records.transferability: Treat mode/version as mandatory evidence fields whenever content ids are reused under different rules.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project is a single-player tower autobattler and does not inherit Duels PvP rounds, ranks or passive control.
records.project_question: How will future difficulty or alternate modes avoid silently reusing incompatible balance evidence?

records.version_scope: 1.0.0 release to 1.0.0 hotfix
records.rule_support: Release Bravery Sigil amplified damage to near targets; the next hotfix fixed its damage amplify stacking infinitely, while 1.0.2 separately clarified item-before-hero damage ordering for Block breaking.
records.practical_support: Because equipment can broadcast or modify repeated attacks, an unguarded amplification can feed back through every additional hit rather than remaining one local stat error.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No occurrence rate, exact recursion trace or post-fix strength is published.
records.mechanism: A damage modifier re-enters its own eligibility path and accumulates without a bounded source or stack rule.
records.engine: Near-target damage event and Bravery Sigil amplification
records.state_resource: Amplification stacks, source id and current damage event lineage
records.trigger: Resolve amplified damage against a near target
records.scope: Item holder and affected damage events
records.payoff: Fixed version applies the authored bounded amplification once per eligible event
records.survival: None; the failure deletes encounter durability and counter windows
records.spatial_condition: Near-target qualification determines eligibility but must not create a new independent root event
records.payoff_owner: Sigil owns modifier; original actor/effect retains damage ownership
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A rule-rewriting damage item must be evaluated for recursion risk before becoming a core payoff.
records.counterplay: No legitimate counterplay exists against infinite amplification; lineage and stack guards are required.
records.failure_explanation: Log root event, applied modifier, recursion rejection and bounded stack count.
records.transferability: Every damage-to-damage conversion needs root ownership, re-entry eligibility and a hard bound.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project does not reuse the Sigil or its historical near-target value.
records.project_question: Which proposed relic conversions can emit new damage, and how will event lineage prevent self-amplification?

records.version_scope: Duels patches 1.1.5 to 1.1.13
records.rule_support: 1.1.5 increased Sharkmancer armor, shark damage, level-three hook damage/range; 1.1.13 then said it was overperforming by a lot and reduced attack cadence and shark damage.
records.practical_support: The role package combines self-heal, summon damage and long-range hook/control, so the buff strengthened several responsibility channels at once.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This is official Duels qualitative assessment without public pick/win rates and cannot define campaign strength.
records.mechanism: One hero compresses sustain, summon payoff, ranged access and control, so buffs to several axes create an outlier faster than a single-role unit.
records.engine: Basic attacks spawn/support shark and level-three hook reaches targets
records.state_resource: Attack interval, shark presence/damage, self-heal and hook range
records.trigger: Attack cadence, shark summon and hook cooldown
records.scope: Sharkmancer, pet and hooked target
records.payoff: Sustained damage and target access from one roster slot
records.survival: Armor and self-heal let the same slot remain active
records.spatial_condition: Long hook range repairs contact while pet adds another body
records.payoff_owner: Hero owns attack/hook; pet owns pet attack under summoner root attribution
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A slot-efficient multi-role unit reduces reasons to recruit separate tank, control or ranged coverage.
records.counterplay: Longer attack interval and lower pet damage restore response time but do not by themselves separate roles.
records.failure_explanation: Break results into hero, pet, heal and hook contribution rather than one score.
records.transferability: Audit role compression when one recruit solves survival, access and payoff simultaneously.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has no accepted Sharkmancer or Duels balance table.
records.project_question: How many distinct capability gaps may one functional hero close before it erases recruitment tradeoffs?

records.version_scope: Historical Bard/Captain trigger context and 1.2.0 hotfix
records.rule_support: The 1.2.0 hotfix fixed dead Bards obliterating enemies from the afterlife; historical rules include Bard Discord and Captain death/wave summon interactions.
records.practical_support: The three-Bard/Captain build multiplies Bard triggers and temporary bodies, making stale post-death eligibility capable of deciding entire waves.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The official note does not publish the exact stale callback, victim count or affected modes.
records.mechanism: A defeated actor retains a pending or subscribed offensive trigger and resolves it after losing action eligibility.
records.engine: Bard effect callback surviving death cleanup
records.state_resource: Alive flag, pending actions, subscriptions and source lineage
records.trigger: Bard dies while an offensive/support effect remains pending
records.scope: Dead Bard and affected enemies
records.payoff: None; fixed behavior cancels ineligible post-death damage
records.survival: Invalid afterlife damage bypasses normal defeat and wave-pressure rules
records.spatial_condition: Stale effects may retain old targets/positions after the source leaves the formation
records.payoff_owner: Dead source must lose eligibility while historical damage attribution remains inspectable
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Players should not value a support unit for an unintended death exploit.
records.counterplay: No legitimate enemy response exists; death cleanup must cancel or revalidate effects deterministically.
records.failure_explanation: Log death time, cancelled actions/subscriptions and any effect explicitly allowed to persist.
records.transferability: Death must atomically revoke navigation, targeting, action and trigger eligibility unless persistence is explicitly authored.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project does not reuse Bard Discord or Captain ghosts.
records.project_question: Which future statuses, summons or projectiles may legally persist after owner death, and who receives attribution?

records.version_scope: 0.4.0 save introduction, 2025-02 rollback and 1.4.0 separate-save overhaul
records.rule_support: 0.4.0 introduced run continue saves; a 2025 update was rolled back because save conversion could affect progression; 1.4.0 later introduced separate save support.
records.practical_support: The developer kept the new update on an open beta branch while restoring live to the prior version, prioritizing progression safety over forward-only rollout.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The conversion defect's technical root cause and affected save population are not public.
records.mechanism: A content/system update transforms persistent progression and is quarantined when conversion integrity cannot be guaranteed.
records.engine: Versioned save schema and migration
records.state_resource: Run state, unlocks, progression and source/target schema versions
records.trigger: Load an older save under the new update
records.scope: All persistent player progress
records.payoff: Safe migration preserves unlocks and enables the new version
records.survival: Rollback and beta isolation prevent irreversible progression loss
records.spatial_condition: None; formation/item ids still require stable serialization references
records.payoff_owner: Persistence layer owns migration; content ids own only their serialized definitions
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Roster, item-pool and upgrade state must not silently remap across versions.
records.counterplay: Not player counterplay; dry-run migration, backups, version gates and rollback are required.
records.failure_explanation: Expose schema version, migrated ids, rejected fields, backup and rollback status.
records.transferability: Build-system reworks require explicit save migrations and a reversible release path.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project does not share Just King's schema or unlock data.
records.project_question: Which roster/equipment/run facts require stable ids and migration tests before the first persistent build-system revision?

records.version_scope: 1.4.0 release, 2026-01 feedback review and 1.4.1 repair
records.rule_support: 1.4.0 overhauled tutorial, input and UI for new-player and mobile/Deck needs; the developer later said reception missed expectations, offered a legacy branch, then rebuilt navigation and added reduced UI scaling in 1.4.1.
records.practical_support: Official feedback identifies PC users seeing the redesign as too mobile-like or in-the-face and asks for recorded interaction sessions, while the repair uses platform-sensitive defaults.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No quantitative usability sample, completion funnel or platform split is published.
records.mechanism: A uniform high-density interface optimized for touch/readability reduces usable battlefield and information space on another platform.
records.engine: UI scaling, navigation graph and platform default
records.state_resource: Screen area, focus path, tooltip readability and battlefield visibility
records.trigger: Use shop, side panels or controller/keyboard navigation on PC, Deck or mobile
records.scope: Whole build/combat interface
records.payoff: Platform-appropriate density preserves both readable text and spatial context
records.survival: Legacy branch and reduced mode keep the game usable while repair continues
records.spatial_condition: Oversized panels reduce room to perceive formation and combat space
records.payoff_owner: UI system owns layout; content retains semantic source and slot information
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Shop and build decisions require compact comparison without hiding exact details.
records.counterplay: Not combat counterplay; platform testing and reversible settings address the failure.
records.failure_explanation: Measure task flow, focus traps, text size, panel occupancy and battlefield visibility by platform.
records.transferability: Dense build information should use platform-aware scale and progressive detail, with real input-path QA.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project does not reuse this UI or need one identical layout across all devices.
records.project_question: What compact first-glance build facts must remain visible while exact ownership and formulas stay available on demand?

records.version_scope: Official FAQ through 1.0.12, with Early Access and 1.0 progression separated
records.rule_support: Battles, events and releasing creatures provide experience; level-two and level-three evolution changes the creature; the level-three cap was removed at 1.0, while party and Box management provide recruitment and replacement surfaces.
records.practical_support: Players route through encounters, events, shops and camps while deciding whether to level an existing body, recruit a bridge or preserve a Box replacement.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The public material does not provide a complete current shop-odds table, Box capacity history or one official end-to-end manual.
records.mechanism: Route rewards feed a four-body party whose members can evolve, be released or be replaced from a Box.
records.engine: Region route plus battle, event, shop and camp rewards
records.state_resource: Party slots, Box candidates, experience, items and route opportunities
records.trigger: After encounters and at recruitment, camp or shop decisions
records.scope: Run roster and current four-creature team
records.payoff: Convert route resources into stronger forms or a better counter package
records.survival: Box replacements and defensive bridges preserve a run after a bad matchup
records.spatial_condition: The active party is ordered front to back; replacement changes first contact and adjacency wording
records.payoff_owner: Each evolved creature owns its active/passive effects; the route owns only opportunity delivery
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Choose between feeding the current core, releasing a creature for experience or keeping a functional replacement.
records.counterplay: Boss previews and known matchup constraints can make a lower-level counter more valuable than another level on the current core.
records.failure_explanation: Separate an under-levelled core, a missing counter role, a poor route and a bad front-order choice.
records.transferability: Preserve recruitment, upgrade and replacement as distinct opportunity costs in a tower run.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project does not have creature capture or a confirmed Box/reserve capacity and must not inherit one implicitly.
records.project_question: What reserve and experience rules make keeping a counter hero valuable without making replacement free?

records.version_scope: Early Access type challenge and evolution guide, cross-checked with 1.0 type additions
records.rule_support: Type counts grant threshold benefits and can gate alternate evolutions; units, evolutions, items and camp effects can contribute type coverage, while concrete attacks, shields and statuses remain separately owned effects.
records.practical_support: The three-Fire/three-Water/three-Grass challenge closes thresholds through innate types, an evolution, a primarily Water recruit and either an item or camp type bridge.
records.disagreement_or_limit: One proposed Shameleon step contains an explicit player assumption and is excluded from the hard rule; current complete type formulas are unavailable.
records.mechanism: Type width is a horizontal team and evolution condition, not the same thing as the vertical combat engine it supports.
records.engine: Type contributions from bodies, evolution branches, items and route modifications
records.state_resource: Count of each type and available bridge sources
records.trigger: A threshold closes or an evolution checks the current team type state
records.scope: Whole team for thresholds; one creature for the chosen evolution branch
records.payoff: Unlock a team bonus or a different creature form while retaining separate combat responsibilities
records.survival: Survival still comes from concrete shield, armor, healing, control or body sources rather than the type label alone
records.spatial_condition: Type width does not repair front-order, adjacency or target-access requirements
records.payoff_owner: Team rule owns threshold activation; each creature owns its attack, status, shield or summon payoff
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A bridge recruit or item can close a threshold without becoming the final damage owner and can later be replaced if another source preserves the count.
records.counterplay: Enemy packages can attack the actual mechanism—cleanse, burst, multihit punishment or backline access—without requiring an element-locked answer.
records.failure_explanation: Report whether the type threshold failed, the combat engine failed or the payoff owner could not act.
records.transferability: Let an ice shield and an earth shield share a Shield system while contributing different affinity bridges or reactions.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not make every affinity a self-contained engine, survival package and payoff or copy Kādomon's exact type roster.
records.project_question: Which project tags are horizontal bridge conditions, and which named mechanics remain the actual engine and payoff?

records.version_scope: Early Access FAQ and community guide updated through 2025-05-19, with recipe-level version limits
records.rule_support: A level-three creature holding a specific item must gain additional experience to Hyper Evolve; separate alternate evolutions can require type thresholds such as Air four, Ice three or mixed Physical and Fire counts.
records.practical_support: The maintained guide functions as a player-facing recipe table and shows that team width and an equipped item can both change the next form rather than merely add stats.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The guide is not an official complete database and does not provide an independent version tag for every recipe.
records.mechanism: Horizontal team state and an item commitment unlock a vertical form rewrite.
records.engine: Reach level three, satisfy a type or item condition and gain another experience event
records.state_resource: Level, experience, held item and current team type counts
records.trigger: Evolution check after gaining experience
records.scope: One creature, with team-wide type prerequisites where specified
records.payoff: A new form with changed active/passive identity
records.survival: The route must keep the incomplete form alive while reserving the required item and team width
records.spatial_condition: The evolved form still occupies one ordered party slot and can change front/back suitability
records.payoff_owner: The evolved creature owns the rewritten ability package; the item/type state is the unlock condition
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Holding a recipe item or bridge type competes with immediate combat strength and roster flexibility.
records.counterplay: A route or Boss that demands an immediate counter can force abandonment of the delayed Hyper recipe.
records.failure_explanation: Expose which requirement is missing—level, item, experience event or type threshold—instead of silently failing evolution.
records.transferability: Use a small number of visible rule-rewrite upgrades where team state changes a core's active or passive.
records.incompatible_assumptions: A hidden recipe for every roster unit creates guide dependence, irreversible traps and excessive migration cost.
records.project_question: Which few heroes merit a visible horizontal-to-vertical upgrade branch, and how is the preview shown before commitment?

records.version_scope: 2023 Demo Ascension historical build, not current 1.0 balance
records.rule_support: Poison can be applied across enemies, shield and Strength can be granted to a chosen ally, and ordered front position determines who absorbs pressure first.
records.practical_support: The reported Beryl plus Snake plus Water starter line uses Snake for AOE Poison, Beryl as the tank and Poison cashout, Water starter for Beryl Shield/Strength and unicorn or front Bear as the fourth charge/support body.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This is one player reaching Ascension page fourteen in the Demo period; it cannot establish current optimality or 1.0 values.
records.mechanism: A status supplier and defensive support concentrate Poison cashout, survival and added Strength into one front payoff owner.
records.engine: Snake AOE Poison plus repeated Beryl Poison application
records.state_resource: Poison stacks, Beryl Shield and Strength, and charge support
records.trigger: Snake applies Poison and Beryl triggers all Poison on its target
records.scope: Enemy group for status; Beryl for the main defensive and damage conversion
records.payoff: Beryl converts accumulated Poison into decisive damage while remaining the protected tank
records.survival: Water starter Shield and optional Bear-first ordering keep Beryl active
records.spatial_condition: Beryl is front unless Bear is recruited, in which case Bear moves first and buffs Beryl behind it
records.payoff_owner: Beryl owns the primary cashout; Snake owns Poison production; Water starter or Bear owns the support effect
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Use question-mark nodes to recruit Beryl early; choose unicorn or Bear based on whether charge or front absorption is missing.
records.counterplay: Cleanse, burst before Poison ramps, status resistance and hit-count retaliation can break the line.
records.failure_explanation: Show Poison supplied, Poison cashed out, Shield received and front damage absorbed by source.
records.transferability: A shield team can deal damage by routing a shared defensive/status engine into one explicit core rather than buffing every member equally.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has no accepted Beryl, Poison formula, Water starter or Demo Ascension economy.
records.project_question: Which shield or status source supports one carry, and what prevents the same support from making every body a payoff?

records.version_scope: Early Access 0.3.x challenge route
records.rule_support: Units can contribute multiple types, evolution can change type coverage and items or camp effects can add a missing type.
records.practical_support: Snose, Baleam and Shiftyke begin at two Grass, three Fire and one Water; evolving Shiftyke to Sewindler and adding a primarily Water unit reaches three Fire, three Water and two Grass, with Spare Button or a camp type addition closing Grass three.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The suggested Shameleon enemy-type step is conditional speculation and is not counted as a verified rule.
records.mechanism: Four distinct acquisition channels can close a team threshold without requiring four final natural-type bodies.
records.engine: Innate types plus evolution, item and camp bridges
records.state_resource: Four roster slots, type counts and one bridge opportunity
records.trigger: Recruit, evolve, equip or modify a type at camp
records.scope: Whole team threshold graph
records.payoff: Close three simultaneous type thresholds or a challenge condition
records.survival: The source does not establish that threshold closure supplies adequate defense; concrete skills remain required
records.spatial_condition: Front order and target wording remain independent of the completed type graph
records.payoff_owner: Team rule owns the thresholds; creature skills retain their own owners
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Choose the least costly bridge among a unit slot, an item slot, a camp modification or an evolution branch.
records.counterplay: A narrow bridge can become a liability when a Boss demands cleanse, burst or a different front body.
records.failure_explanation: Display both the missing type count and the functional role sacrificed to close it.
records.transferability: Provide several bridge channels so elemental width is a decision rather than a forced fixed roster.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy the exact three-by-three challenge or allow unlimited tags on one hero.
records.project_question: How many bridge channels can close a trait threshold before the threshold stops constraining the build?

records.version_scope: Early Access 0.3.0 launch and 0.3.2 nerf
records.rule_support: Gnocking copied or benefited from player buffs; 0.3.2 changed the interaction to copy enemy effects once and removed its Crown.
records.practical_support: Players reported that passive automatic buff teams could not choose to withhold their engine, while others succeeded with Rocorm, Toxic, Pupulsion, Grubuddy, Shock or other packages whose value exceeded or bypassed the copied buffs.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Community opinion split between a legitimate capability exam and a diversity-suppressing wall; no pick/win statistics exist.
records.mechanism: A Boss reflects an automatic player engine that cannot be disabled after combat begins.
records.engine: Boss reads and copies incoming player buff effects
records.state_resource: Player buff package, Boss copied effects and available debuff replacements
records.trigger: Player automatic buffs resolve during the Boss fight
records.scope: Boss and the buffing player team
records.payoff: The intended exam rewards debuffs or asymmetrically valuable buffs
records.survival: Slow, Poison, Shock or a superior self-scaling tank reduces the mirrored offense
records.spatial_condition: Front order still determines who receives the copied or amplified pressure
records.payoff_owner: Boss owns its copy; each player source retains ownership of the original buff
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: The counter must be recruited or equipped before combat because automatic passives cannot be withheld on demand.
records.counterplay: Use debuffs, poison, shock, extreme slow or a buff owner that extracts more value than the Boss.
records.failure_explanation: Preview copied effects and report original source versus Boss copy so the reversal is attributable.
records.transferability: A counter-Boss must respect the control freedoms of an autobattler and provide a visible precombat adaptation window.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy a deckbuilder counter that assumes the player can simply stop casting a passive engine midbattle.
records.project_question: Which automatic engines can a Boss invert without invalidating a whole run, and what replacement window is guaranteed?

records.version_scope: Early Access 0.3.0 launch counter package before the 0.3.2 Gnocking nerf
records.rule_support: Summons and items can generate Poison triggers, Poison can feed a Shield-gaining unit and Gnocking's copy behavior was limited in 0.3.2.
records.practical_support: One concrete counter combines Poison, minion summons, Poison-on-summon items and a creature that gains Shield whenever Poison is applied; alternatives include Snose attack reduction, four Earth plus Thorn and Shock.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The thread does not identify every unit and item name or provide a win rate; it is a structural counter package rather than a fixed current list.
records.mechanism: Temporary bodies generate status events that simultaneously damage the Boss and fund a defensive payoff owner.
records.engine: Summon creation plus Poison-on-summon item triggers
records.state_resource: Summon count, Poison stacks and converted Shield
records.trigger: A minion enters and applies Poison
records.scope: Summoned body, poisoned Boss and the Poison-to-Shield owner
records.payoff: Poison deals damage while repeated application creates survival
records.survival: Minion occupancy and Poison-to-Shield conversion buy time without feeding a large conventional buff package
records.spatial_condition: Summons require space and the front body must protect the conversion owner
records.payoff_owner: Summon/item root owns Poison production; the designated creature owns Shield; Poison state owns delayed damage attribution
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Assemble a status/summon bridge before the Boss or pivot to Snose, Shock or Thorn if the conversion owner is missing.
records.counterplay: Summon clearing, Poison cleanse, trigger caps and fast burst can stop the loop.
records.failure_explanation: Report summon origin, Poison source, converted Shield and any capped trigger separately.
records.transferability: Cross a summon engine with a status and a defensive conversion while preserving one named payoff owner and recursion guards.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project has no accepted poison-on-summon item, and temporary units cannot exceed physical occupancy or keep battle alive alone.
records.project_question: Can temporary bodies feed a shield core without making body count and trigger count scale quadratically?

records.version_scope: Early Access 0.3.0 launch final Boss only
records.rule_support: The launch-era final Boss summoned creatures released during the run and creatures in the Box; Box creatures received experience, and party/Box manipulation was still being repaired in 0.4.0.
records.practical_support: Players responded by avoiding new recruits after World two or emptying the Box before the Boss, turning collection and reserve development into liabilities.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This historical encounter is not the later Portal Boss and community posts do not establish every summon scaling formula.
records.mechanism: A Boss reads accumulated reserve and released-roster history as enemy power.
records.engine: Run history and Box roster converted into Boss summons
records.state_resource: Released creatures, Box bodies, their levels and experience
records.trigger: Enter the final Boss phases
records.scope: Entire run recruitment history
records.payoff: Thematic confrontation with prior choices, but at the cost of discouraging collection
records.survival: Players reduce risk by deleting or never acquiring optional bodies
records.spatial_condition: Extra enemy summons create occupancy and target-pressure consequences
records.payoff_owner: Boss encounter owns the conversion; prior player bodies become hostile instances
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Optimal preparation can become anti-recruitment and pre-Boss reserve liquidation.
records.counterplay: Empty the Box, stop recruiting or use sufficiently strong decay/summon/defensive scaling.
records.failure_explanation: Expose exactly which reserve or released body was reproduced and at what retained strength.
records.transferability: Run-history Bosses may echo player choices only when the preview and answer do not punish normal experimentation.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not make reserve heroes, collection or discarded experiments silently strengthen the final Boss.
records.project_question: How can a Boss reference prior roster choices without making keeping functional replacements a trap?

records.version_scope: 0.5-era report through confirmed 1.0 persistence of the Portal gimmick
records.rule_support: Portal hits reduce a random teammate's maximum health; the developer identified the retaliation as intended and the negative or stale display as a bug, while 1.0.1 repaired related evolution and combat-position presentation.
records.practical_support: Players using many small or random multihits reported unseen repeated reductions that appeared as an abrupt whole-team drop to one maximum health between phases.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The exact retaliation value and portal tuning vary by report; the visible-state defect and intended Boss rule must remain separate.
records.mechanism: Every hit on a target object spends a hidden team maximum-health budget, making hit count a negative resource.
records.engine: Portal on-hit retaliation
records.state_resource: Number of hits, random ally selection and each ally's maximum health
records.trigger: Each portal hit
records.scope: Hit portal and one random player creature per retaliation
records.payoff: Boss pressure rewards fewer stronger hits or rapid portal removal
records.survival: High health, armor, replacement bodies or healing-max-health rewards extend the budget
records.spatial_condition: The portal must be targetable; random ally scope obscures which ordered body is being depleted
records.payoff_owner: Portal owns retaliation; each attack source owns its hit count; affected ally owns the reduced maximum health state
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Replace a multihit package or hold reserve bodies before the fight when the preview exposes the rule.
records.counterplay: Rush down, one-shot portals, use special-focused damage or prepare durable/replacement units.
records.failure_explanation: Show every maximum-health reduction at the moment it occurs and attribute it to the triggering hit source.
records.transferability: Bosses may invert multihit only with a visible per-hit cost, trigger budget and precombat adaptation window.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not hide persistent maximum-health loss behind stale health bars or apply it randomly without source attribution.
records.project_question: What on-board marker and report line make a per-hit retaliation budget understandable before it destroys the formation?

records.version_scope: 1.0 and post-1.0 community counter discussion through 2026-04
records.rule_support: Attacks and damage taken feed Energy under the 1.0.7 rule, while the Portal penalizes repeated hits and can be answered by faster removal or reserve replacement.
records.practical_support: Reported answers include high HP/Armor, special spam, Lightning plus Poison, an elite reward that grants health on special use, and enough Strength to break a portal in one hit; random triple-hit effects are called out as bad matches.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This is a low-sample community answer without verified current numbers or comparative success rates.
records.mechanism: Several orthogonal counter packages answer the same per-hit retaliation through durability, cadence conversion or fewer larger hits.
records.engine: Pre-Boss selection of health, armor, special cadence, status or Strength burst
records.state_resource: Maximum health, armor, Energy, special frequency and hit count
records.trigger: Portal phase begins and the player attacks
records.scope: Whole active team with one main portal breaker or special engine
records.payoff: Destroy the portal before maximum-health attrition becomes terminal
records.survival: Durability or health-on-special offsets the retaliation budget
records.spatial_condition: The chosen breaker must be able to target the portal from its ordered position
records.payoff_owner: Strength carry or special engine owns portal damage; defensive supports own survival
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Elite-route rewards and Box replacements create a pre-Boss pivot window.
records.counterplay: The Boss punishes rain or random multihit packages that cannot control hit count.
records.failure_explanation: Compare portal hits taken, maximum health lost, special casts and breaker damage rather than one total score.
records.transferability: Design Boss exams with multiple answer families so defense, cadence and burst builds can each adapt differently.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project does not inherit Kādomon's elite reward, Lightning, Poison or Portal numbers.
records.project_question: For each Boss capability exam, which three materially different response families remain available in ordinary run offers?

records.version_scope: Early Access 0.4.x developer-led discussion
records.rule_support: Speed controls attack timing while Energy controls special timing; later official patches continued to change Energy acquisition and battle status presentation.
records.practical_support: Players considered Speed a core build axis and linked it to Air and Frost, but found lower-is-better Speed and Energy values counterintuitive and combat hard to parse between battlefield actions and portrait bars.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Suggestions for higher-is-better values, a timeline or action spotlight were proposals, not confirmed implemented rules.
records.mechanism: Two cadence statistics use an inverse direction while their actions and bars are displayed on separate visual layers.
records.engine: Speed-driven attacks and Energy-driven special actions
records.state_resource: Time to next attack, Energy threshold and queued action
records.trigger: A cadence timer or Energy requirement completes
records.scope: Each creature and the global action sequence
records.payoff: Faster attacks or specials enable cadence-focused builds
records.survival: Players need enough warning to understand whether healing, shielding or control will act before incoming damage
records.spatial_condition: Action spotlight must connect the portrait resource to the creature acting in the ordered battle line
records.payoff_owner: The acting creature owns the attack or special; the UI owns prediction and attribution
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A speed item or recruit is evaluable only when the player can compare its actual time-to-action consequence.
records.counterplay: Slow, speed manipulation and action interruption need a visible timeline consequence.
records.failure_explanation: Show the next actor, action type, resource source and interruption rather than only moving bars.
records.transferability: Use one value direction and connect cadence resources to an inspectable next-action forecast.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not adopt a full turn queue if the project's real-time simultaneous rules cannot honestly support one.
records.project_question: What minimal next-action indicator explains real-time attack, heal and skill cadence without pretending combat is turn based?

records.rule_support: 1.0.7 removed passive Energy gain, granted ten Energy on attacks and fifty percent of damage taken as Energy; 1.0.9 excluded triggered attacks and lethal damage from Energy and allowed sufficient gains to fund consecutive Supers; 1.0.12 fixed self-damage Energy errors.
records.practical_support: Attack cadence, tanking, self-damage and triggered attacks therefore represent different Energy engines and cannot be treated as one generic action event.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact unit thresholds and balance values remain version-specific; the sources do not publish the full scheduler.
records.mechanism: Energy accrual is rewritten from passive time to qualified attack and damage events with explicit exclusions.
records.engine: Normal attacks and eligible incoming damage
records.state_resource: Energy, attack provenance, incoming damage and Super cost
records.trigger: Perform a normal attack or survive eligible damage
records.scope: Acting or damaged creature
records.payoff: One or multiple Super casts when enough Energy is accumulated
records.survival: Damage-fed Energy gives durable front bodies faster access to defensive or offensive Supers
records.spatial_condition: Front order changes who takes damage and therefore which creature accelerates its Super
records.payoff_owner: The qualifying attacker or damaged creature owns Energy; triggered child attacks retain their root but do not gain Energy
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A tank, fast attacker or self-damage unit now values Energy support differently after the rewrite.
records.counterplay: Burst that kills without granting terminal Energy and denial of normal attacks limit Super acceleration.
records.failure_explanation: Log each Energy gain or rejection with event type and source eligibility.
records.transferability: Define Energy eligibility separately for basic attacks, triggered attacks, damage taken, self-damage and lethal events.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy the ten/fifty-percent values or permit passive, triggered and self-damage events to double-dip by default.
records.project_question: Which exact combat events may generate a future shared or personal resource, and which derived events are explicitly ineligible?

records.version_scope: Early Access 0.3.2
records.rule_support: 0.3.2 lowered the per-battle effect-trigger limit to fifty and cancelled queued damage from creatures that had fainted; later patches continued to fix infinite targets and rapid-trigger ownership.
records.practical_support: Status, summon, passive and item chains can create more scheduled events than their visible bodies suggest, so a dead source and a live recursion chain require separate guards.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The official notes do not specify whether every effect family shared the same counter or the complete queue order.
records.mechanism: A global trigger budget stops infinite chains while death cleanup invalidates already queued source-dependent damage.
records.engine: Nested passive, status, item and summon triggers
records.state_resource: Per-battle trigger count, action queue, source alive state and root lineage
records.trigger: Any effect recursively schedules another effect or its source faints before resolution
records.scope: Whole battle queue and each root effect chain
records.payoff: Valid finite chains resolve while infinite or stale actions stop deterministically
records.survival: Enemies and allies avoid being killed by actions whose source no longer has legal eligibility
records.spatial_condition: Queued targets and source positions must be revalidated when a body leaves the ordered formation
records.payoff_owner: Root effect owner retains attribution; fainted sources lose action eligibility unless persistence is explicit
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Players should not value a build for an unintended infinite or post-death damage exploit.
records.counterplay: Legitimate counterplay is restored by finite cadence, death and target invalidation.
records.failure_explanation: Report cap exhaustion, cancelled stale actions and the root effect that consumed the budget.
records.transferability: Use per-root budgets and death revalidation in addition to any global emergency cap.
records.incompatible_assumptions: A silent global fifty-trigger cutoff would truncate legitimate high-population builds without explaining which chain failed.
records.project_question: Which trigger families need local budgets, and what battle-wide emergency ceiling preserves determinism without hiding valid output?

records.version_scope: Early Access 0.4.0 and 1.0.9–1.0.12
records.rule_support: 0.4.0 fixed a Tainee and Ice Club infinite loop; 1.0.9–1.0.12 fixed infinite Super targeting, rapid-damage, passive, target, self-damage and enemy-Super ownership defects.
records.practical_support: The repeated fixes show that a numerical trigger cap alone does not define child eligibility, self-recursion, target count, resource gain or source ownership.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Patch notes name symptoms rather than publishing a common technical root cause.
records.mechanism: Different recursive failures arise from eligibility, ownership, targeting and resource feedback even when all appear as too many effects.
records.engine: Items, passives, Supers, self-damage and rapid multi-target effects
records.state_resource: Root owner, child marker, eligible targets, Energy and recursion depth
records.trigger: An effect invokes another effect that can re-enter its parent pathway
records.scope: One root chain and every generated child event
records.payoff: Only authored finite combinations repeat
records.survival: Invalid rapid chains no longer delete a team before a legal response window
records.spatial_condition: Target-set expansion must remain bounded by real living bodies and legal positions
records.payoff_owner: Every generated event preserves root and immediate source; enemy-owned Supers cannot credit the player
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Balance should evaluate a legal combo, not an exploit created by ambiguous child eligibility.
records.counterplay: Rate limits, target limits, non-reentrant flags and resource exclusions restore finite response windows.
records.failure_explanation: Expose the guard that stopped a chain and retain its original owner for combat reports.
records.transferability: Specify root owner, child eligibility, shared cap, self-recursion, lifetime and per-time rate as separate contracts.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not treat all recursion failures as one balance number or solve them only with a universal cooldown.
records.project_question: Which generated attacks, summons and status ticks may themselves trigger the source effect, and how is that rule shown?

records.version_scope: Early Access 0.4.0 and post-launch item fixes
records.rule_support: 0.4.0 enabled item removal while fixing all-party release progression locks, in-battle party/Box drag freezes, enemy-team editing, shop item duplication and route skipping; 1.0.10 and later patches continued to repair item duplication and ownership effects.
records.practical_support: Roster and equipment operations span inventory, active team, Box, combat phase and route state, so partial mutation can create duplication or a run with no legal continuation.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The official notes do not expose transaction boundaries or save implementation details.
records.mechanism: A multi-surface drag, release or equip operation must validate all dependent states before committing once.
records.engine: Party/Box transfers, item equip/unequip, release and route progression
records.state_resource: Creature identity, slot, item ownership, phase, rewards and next-node eligibility
records.trigger: Player mutates roster or item state
records.scope: Active party, reserve, inventory and run route
records.payoff: A legal replacement or equipment change commits without duplication or softlock
records.survival: Phase gates prevent combat-time edits from invalidating current actions and occupancy
records.spatial_condition: Moving the front body changes ordered targeting and must not leave duplicate or missing occupants
records.payoff_owner: Roster authority owns body location; inventory owns item location; battle snapshot owns current combat participants
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Replacement remains a meaningful choice only when sale/release rewards and item recovery commit consistently.
records.counterplay: Not combat counterplay; preflight, atomic commit and rollback prevent invalid state.
records.failure_explanation: Return a localized rejection reason without consuming the creature, item or route action.
records.transferability: Treat roster replacement and equipment movement as validated transactions with explicit phase authority.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not allow live combat drag operations unless the project's battle contract explicitly authorizes and resolves them.
records.project_question: Which roster and equipment mutations are preparation-only, and what exact preflight keeps failed moves non-consuming?

records.version_scope: 2023 Demo historical observation only
records.rule_support: Front bodies absorb attacks, Thorns retaliates and Shield sustains the defender; Poison provides a damage route that need not feed the same direct-hit loop.
records.practical_support: A Demo-period post describes Wormonger growing Thorns and Shield under front focus, making weak or frequent direct attacks harmful and motivating Poison or fewer stronger hits.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This is an old single-thread complaint with no official balance confirmation or population data and cannot establish an era-wide Earth meta.
records.mechanism: Attacking a front defender repeatedly increases both its survival and retaliation, turning hit count into a liability.
records.engine: Front focus feeding Shield and Thorns
records.state_resource: Incoming hit count, Shield and retaliatory damage
records.trigger: The front defender is attacked
records.scope: Front defender and each direct attacker
records.payoff: The defender survives while attackers damage themselves
records.survival: Shield grows from the same pressure that would normally wear a tank down
records.spatial_condition: Front placement is essential because it concentrates target selection
records.payoff_owner: Wormonger owns defensive growth and Thorns; each attacker owns its triggering hit
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A player facing the package needs a low-hit finisher, Poison or another indirect bridge rather than more small attackers.
records.counterplay: Poison, fewer larger hits, shield break or target bypass.
records.failure_explanation: Show Shield gained and Thorns returned per incoming source so the negative feedback is visible.
records.transferability: Retaliation can make attack frequency a Boss or defender counter-axis, but it requires explicit per-hit feedback and caps.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not infer current balance, copy Wormonger or make every shield tank scale from unlimited enemy hits.
records.project_question: Which defensive payoff may legitimately grow when hit, and what prevents multihit builds from becoming globally invalid?

records.version_scope: Prologue and Early Access player experience before 1.0
records.rule_support: Healing, spikes, swarm, vampiric sustain, Poison, Shield and summon bodies can be combined as separate defensive and damage channels.
records.practical_support: One long-form player report describes heal/spike/swarm, vamp/swarm and poison/swarm as reliable defensive lines while pure damage required narrow support and balanced teams lost late through insufficient specialization.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This is one player's historical experience; the publisher only replied that 1.0 added content and rewards and did not confirm the balance diagnosis.
records.mechanism: Several sustain engines can share swarm occupancy while different payoffs decide how the stall converts into victory.
records.engine: Healing, lifesteal, Shield or summons extending combat
records.state_resource: Effective health, summon bodies, Poison or spike retaliation
records.trigger: Repeated attacks, heals, summons and status ticks
records.scope: Whole team with one selected damage conversion
records.payoff: Poison, spikes or vampiric damage wins after the survival engine stabilizes
records.survival: Defense is the primary engine rather than a passive stat bundle
records.spatial_condition: Front tanks and summon bodies protect the actual payoff owner
records.payoff_owner: Poison source, spike defender or vampiric attacker owns damage; swarm and heal sources own survival support
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A balanced early team should later specialize into one defensive conversion rather than remain mediocre in every channel.
records.counterplay: Burst, anti-heal, cleanse, indirect damage or summon clearing can attack different variants.
records.failure_explanation: Separate time bought by defense from damage produced by the chosen conversion.
records.transferability: Shield and health systems need explicit offensive conversion options such as one carry scaling from team extra health or defense.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not treat the report as proof that offense is universally weak or import all stall families at once.
records.project_question: Which one or two rare conversions let a defensive chassis win without giving every shield source free team-wide offense?

records.version_scope: Early Access FAQ and guide updated through 2025-05-16
records.rule_support: A Misprint must reach a rest event or be extracted through the run to unlock permanently; failure before extraction loses it, and seeded routes can be used to hunt rare variants.
records.practical_support: The guide recommends mapping encounter/shop opportunities and repeated seed or restart routes to maximize rare-color sightings rather than to solve combat roles.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Odds and seed behavior are guide-maintained collection evidence, not a combat balance source.
records.mechanism: A rare cosmetic collection state creates run extraction risk and repeatable seed-hunting behavior.
records.engine: Low-probability appearance plus rest-event extraction
records.state_resource: Encounter count, seed, rare variant and extraction opportunity
records.trigger: Find a Misprint and either reach extraction or fail the run
records.scope: Account collection and the current rare body
records.payoff: Permanent alternate appearance
records.survival: Combat survival protects a collection find rather than the build engine itself
records.spatial_condition: None beyond carrying the body in the run roster
records.payoff_owner: Account collection owns the unlock; the creature's combat mechanics are unchanged
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: The rare appearance can pressure the player to buy or keep a mechanically unsuitable body until extraction.
records.counterplay: Not enemy counterplay; route planning and safe extraction reduce loss risk.
records.failure_explanation: Clearly distinguish cosmetic collection loss from combat-build failure.
records.transferability: Use the case to separate collection/meta goals from combat-system research and authority.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project should not add capture, rare-color odds, seed farming or permanent collectible loss to justify its first combat content.
records.project_question: Which future meta rewards can remain optional without distorting hero recruitment and build evaluation?

records.version_scope: Early Access level-three ceiling versus 1.0 uncapped progression
records.rule_support: The Early Access loop centered on evolutions through level three and Hyper conditions, while 1.0 removed the level-three cap and immediately patched evolution and position-display defects.
records.practical_support: A capped form-completion economy and an uncapped post-form stat progression create different reasons to keep feeding the same body versus replacing it.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The official launch post does not provide a complete post-level-three scaling curve or current optimal feed policy.
records.mechanism: Removing the level cap changes a completed evolution from a terminal investment into an indefinitely extensible carry.
records.engine: Continued experience after final normal evolution
records.state_resource: Level, experience and opportunity cost of feeding alternatives
records.trigger: Gain experience beyond level three
records.scope: One chosen carry and the roster options it displaces
records.payoff: Greater continued power from the established body
records.survival: Overlevelling a core can stabilize the run but leaves less experience for counters and replacements
records.spatial_condition: The overlevelled body still needs a legal front/back role and target access
records.payoff_owner: The repeatedly levelled creature owns the vertical payoff
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: The player must compare another level on the core with developing a Box counter or bridge.
records.counterplay: Boss mechanics that invert the core's hit count, buffs or position can expose overconcentration.
records.failure_explanation: Show level investment separately from form, item and team-threshold contributions.
records.transferability: If vertical progression can continue after a hero's kit is complete, preserve reasons to invest in functional replacements.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not assume uncapped hero levels or use them to erase roster replacement decisions in this project.
records.project_question: Where should vertical hero investment stop yielding efficient power so a new functional recruit remains competitive?

records.version_scope: Early Access 0.5.0 through 1.0.11
records.rule_support: 0.5.0 added Keeper and starter selection with a unique relic and varied region Bosses per run; 1.0 added Ascension and completion systems, and 1.0.11 added another Keeper, random Keeper and more starter choices.
records.practical_support: Run-start identity and relic alter the opening option set, while variable Bosses prevent one fixed route answer from covering every run.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No public selection or win-rate data establishes whether Keeper relics or Boss variance are balanced.
records.mechanism: A chosen start package and a variable Boss sequence jointly define the initial build bias and future counter demands.
records.engine: Keeper, unique relic, starter options and seeded/variable region Bosses
records.state_resource: Starting identity, relic rule, starter roster and known upcoming Boss package
records.trigger: Run creation and region generation
records.scope: Whole run
records.payoff: Distinct openings and replayable counter routes
records.survival: A flexible starter or relic can cover early weakness while future Boss previews guide replacement
records.spatial_condition: Starter ordering and Boss target rules still determine who receives pressure
records.payoff_owner: Keeper/relic owns run-level rule changes; each creature owns its combat action
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: The opening bias must leave room to recruit a different answer when the generated Boss sequence demands it.
records.counterplay: Variable Boss packages test whether the build has retained adaptation capacity instead of forcing one solved opening.
records.failure_explanation: Separate start-package bias, later recruitment choices and Boss-specific mismatch.
records.transferability: A run relic can bias a chassis while visible enemy packages create later pivot pressure.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project's starting hero does not own run-wide rules merely because it was selected first; relics remain separate run-level content.
records.project_question: Which run-start choices may bias offers without making the starting hero an irreplaceable commander category?

records.version_scope: 0.5.0 design-clarity admission through 1.0.7–1.0.12 presentation fixes and 2026 newcomer report
records.rule_support: The developer acknowledged broader clarity and experience problems in 0.5.0; later patches added type icons, optional battle status text and corrected type grants and next-battle effect wording.
records.practical_support: A 2026 newcomer still asked how types are added, how multiple synergies are built and whether 'ally in front' or 'all Kādomon ahead' refers to one neighbor, all allies or both teams.
records.disagreement_or_limit: One newcomer report does not measure tutorial failure rate, and the community answer is not a complete official targeting specification.
records.mechanism: Type acquisition, threshold progress and positional target scope are split across icons, text and battle state without one explicit source/recipient grammar.
records.engine: Type-grant effects and front/ahead target selectors
records.state_resource: Current types, threshold counts, ordered positions and pending next-battle effects
records.trigger: Inspect, recruit, add a type or resolve a positional effect
records.scope: One creature, adjacent ally, all creatures ahead or whole team depending on wording
records.payoff: Correctly forecast whether a bridge or positional effect closes the intended build
records.survival: Players can protect the correct front or support body only when recipient scope is unambiguous
records.spatial_condition: Front neighbor, all allied bodies ahead and all bodies ahead on both teams are materially different selectors
records.payoff_owner: Effect source owns the action; each recipient owns the resulting state; UI owns preview clarity
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A type bridge or support recruit can be evaluated before purchase only when source, scope and threshold change are previewed.
records.counterplay: Enemy previews must use the same selector language so formation changes are a reliable answer.
records.failure_explanation: Highlight affected cells or portraits and list added/removed type or status with its source.
records.transferability: Use consistent source-arrow-recipient wording and preview exact threshold deltas and positional scope.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not rely on color-only type icons or vague front/ahead text where a grid has multiple valid directions.
records.project_question: Which compact spatial and source indicators let players predict an effect before committing a hero, item or formation cell?

records.version_scope: 2025 Playtest/Demo asynchronous modes versus 2026-02 live friend lobbies
records.rule_support: Casual/Ranked use uploaded player-team snapshots matched by round/win/loss, with MMR added for Ranked; friend lobbies are a later real-time longest-survivor mode.
records.practical_support: Ranked preview supports a preparation pivot against a saved formation, while live elimination follows a different match lifecycle.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The Playtest explanation predates release; current retention, deduplication and exact matchmaking formulas are unpublished.
records.mechanism: Saved formations form an asynchronous opponent pool distinct from live multiplayer.
records.engine: Team upload, snapshot selection and mode-specific matchmaking
records.state_resource: Round, wins, losses, MMR and saved formation
records.trigger: Start Casual/Ranked combat or join a friend lobby
records.scope: Opponent selection and match lifecycle
records.payoff: Asynchronous variety or live group competition
records.survival: Mode rules determine run continuation or live elimination
records.spatial_condition: The saved snapshot preserves its 3x3 formation

records.version_scope: 1.2.0 launch feedback through 1.3.0 rework
records.rule_support: Version 1.3 reduced same-unit upgrade requirements from three copies to two; the client allows a full team to buy only when the purchase immediately creates a legal merge.
records.practical_support: Early review and discussion report that three-copy upgrading occupied two or three of five positions, restricted unit variety and made buy-sell supports harder to operate; later feedback says the 1.3 change removed that exact pressure.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The reports do not establish whether two copies became optimally tuned or whether reserve space would have solved other constraints.
records.mechanism: Upgrade recipes compete with combat diversity when duplicate ingredients occupy active slots rather than a separate reserve.

records.payoff_owner: Merged unit owns combined stats; roster pays ingredient occupancy
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Hold duplicates toward a merge or sell/replace them to restore functional variety and a cycling slot.
records.counterplay: Lower ingredient count, reserve capacity or merge-preview rules reduce dead occupancy.
records.failure_explanation: Preview whether a purchase merges, needs a slot or is illegal before gold is committed.
records.transferability: Upgrade recipes must price temporary population loss as deliberately as their currency cost.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not import active-slot-only upgrading into a project that may use a reserve or roster layer.
records.project_question: Where should upgrade ingredients live so vertical investment does not erase horizontal team play?

records.version_scope: 1.3.0 tempo rework
records.rule_support: Version 1.3 changed rerolls from two gold to one, grants two free first-round rerolls, prevents Health loss in the first three rounds, reduces the win target from fifteen to ten and lowers merge requirements.
records.practical_support: The pre-1.3 review describes expensive rerolls and roster-space setup friction, supplying the practical problem context for the official tempo package.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The patch gives changes, not quantified retention or balance outcomes; the first three battles still occur and can affect wins or income.
records.mechanism: Cheaper search and temporary loss protection create a bounded window to find an engine before defeats consume run health.
records.engine: Opening rerolls, life-loss gate and shorter victory target
records.state_resource: Gold, free rerolls, round index, five Health and accumulated wins

records.survival: Early losses do not reduce Health

records.payoff_owner: Player owns protection window; recruited units own resulting board power
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Spend free/cheap searches to assemble a pair or support before normal life loss begins.
records.counterplay: Protection expires at a clear round boundary and does not remove later opportunity costs.
records.failure_explanation: State that a loss was protected and show when normal damage resumes.
records.transferability: Enemy capability exams should expose counter tools before the punishment window closes.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy exact rounds or wins without matching this project's tower length and recovery rules.
records.project_question: How many floors of warning and acquisition access should precede the first hard counter exam?

records.version_scope: 1.2.0 announcement versus 1.3.0 client and 2023 practice
records.rule_support: The 1.2 announcement describes fixed level-scaled enemy-team retaliation, while the 1.3 client instead makes a hit Thorns unit attack Level random enemies using its own Attack.
records.practical_support: A 2023 player placed a 50/50 Thorns first against a 45/50 opposing front Thorns and reports the 50-Attack retaliation clearing the full enemy team in one round.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The exact migration is undocumented, and one battle cannot establish general strength; 1.2 and 1.3 formulas must remain separate.
records.mechanism: Frontline durability increases the number of received-hit triggers while owned Attack scales each random multi-target retaliation.

records.payoff_owner: The struck Thorns owns trigger, damage stat and durability
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Invest permanent Attack and Health into the front Thorns rather than distribute all growth evenly.
records.counterplay: Separate trigger frequency, target count, damage scale and durability; public practice does not close an external counter.
records.failure_explanation: Report source Thorns, received hit, versioned formula, selected targets and resulting damage.
records.transferability: Retaliation is a valid shield-system payoff only when its owner and independent tuning knobs remain visible.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not combine the 1.2 fixed team damage with the 1.3 Attack-based random-target rule.
records.project_question: Which unit or relic should own retaliation when team durability is the engine but one carrier owns damage?

records.version_scope: 2023 post-1.3 community reports
records.rule_support: The 1.3 client gives Thorns a self-contained WhenHit-to-Attack conversion with target count scaling by Level.
records.practical_support: One reviewer says four of five observed games contained Thorn spam and felt forced to play Thorn or an anti-Thorn build; a separate player reports an extreme 50/50 front-Thorns outcome.
records.disagreement_or_limit: There are no pick-rate, win-rate or matchmaking-pool statistics, and the anti-Thorn composition is unnamed; this is community pressure evidence, not an objective dominance rate.
records.mechanism: A durable self-owned retaliation package can compress the environment when the visible counter package is narrower than the build itself.
records.engine: Repeated frontline Thorns triggers across one or more copies
records.state_resource: Thorns count, capped stats, matchup pool and access to an unspecified counter

records.failure_explanation: Label the observed archetype and missing response rather than presenting one anecdote as a population statistic.
records.transferability: A defense-to-offense archetype needs authored enemy counters and adaptation access, not only a numeric cap.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not claim 80-percent adoption, universal dominance or a named counter from this sample.
records.project_question: What enemy packages punish repeated retaliation carriers without invalidating ordinary shield teams?

records.version_scope: 1.2.0 additions verified against 1.3.0 linear client
