records.practical_support: Official patch history repeatedly fixes target side, redirect removal and front-summon alignment, showing these relative selectors materially affect execution even without a published meta formation guide.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No practical source provides a complete Magician or summon build, and summon interaction with the nominal five-unit cap is unresolved.

records.version_scope: 1.2.0 ordering report and developer reply, reworked in 1.3.0
records.rule_support: The developer confirms that old Samurai dealt damage equal to the front enemy's Health and Paladin healing could resolve during Samurai's death sequence; 1.3 changes Samurai to always kill the front enemy.
records.practical_support: A player observed a high-Health level-three Druid survive at one Health because Paladin healed after the equal-Health damage was applied.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This is one historical interaction; it proves a semantic distinction between lethal damage and forced death, not that either policy is universally preferable.
records.mechanism: An interleaved heal can rescue a target from numerically lethal damage, while an explicit kill operation closes that intervention window.
records.engine: Samurai attack, death event and Paladin heal

records.payoff_owner: Samurai owns execution; Paladin owns heal; front target owns Health
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Composition can only rely on the rescue in the historical rule set; 1.3 removes it.
records.counterplay: Specify whether an effect deals damage, sets Health, marks lethal or forces death and which reactions can interrupt.
records.failure_explanation: Render ordered events and state transitions rather than only final Health.
records.transferability: Deterministic autobattle needs typed lethal semantics and an inspectable reaction stack.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not let generic healing silently override an effect authored as unavoidable execution.
records.project_question: Which death, revive, shield and heal reactions can legally intervene between lethal damage and removal?

records.version_scope: 1.3.0 client with independent 2023 and 2024 reports
records.rule_support: Paladin heals every turn, and the public 1.3 client exposes manual stop/speed controls but no obvious turn cap, healing decay, overtime damage or automatic-draw rule.
records.practical_support: Two players independently report frontlines whose healing exceeded incoming damage and produced endless combat, including a final battle at 9/10 wins that blocked run completion.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The reports lack complete teams and logs, and hidden server timeouts cannot be ruled out; absence is limited to publicly visible client guards.
records.mechanism: Sustain above opposing damage creates a zero-progress state when combat has no bounded termination policy.

records.spatial_condition: Mutually sustaining front units remain first living targets indefinitely
records.payoff_owner: Healer owns recovery; front unit owns Health; battle controller must own termination
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: No in-combat recruitment pivot exists once an asynchronous battle starts.
records.counterplay: Detect repeated states or no-progress windows, then apply previewed overtime, draw or deterministic resolution.
records.failure_explanation: Report the repeating state, elapsed turns and termination rule instead of appearing frozen.
records.transferability: Every healing/shield system requires an explicit anti-stalemate owner and attributed resolution.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not claim the original server has no hidden timeout or copy manual Stop as the solution.
records.project_question: Should tower battles use no-progress detection, escalating pressure or bounded turn counts, and how is the result explained?

records.version_scope: launch beta reports and 1.3.0 opponent-pool fix
records.rule_support: Version 1.3 explicitly stopped matching a player against their own team in the asynchronous cloud-opponent system.
records.practical_support: Launch-period review and discussion both describe seeing the player's own or suspiciously identical submitted team when the cloud pool was sparse.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The sources do not quantify pool size, repeat frequency, general matchmaking quality or later server availability.
records.mechanism: Uploaded team snapshots need identity exclusion before similarity matching so the opponent pool does not feed the player's own state back as an enemy.

records.transferability: Authored single-player ghosts or comparison simulations still need provenance, identity and fallback rules.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not import cloud PvP or infer population decline from isolated self-matches.

records.version_scope: Contract launch practice through 2025 updates
records.rule_support: Characters, equipment and candidate battles share one three-choice panel; gold rerolls all three offer types, while an unaffordable result can be locked for later.
records.practical_support: Players use the panel to search for easier or higher-reward enemies, elite recruits and build pieces, and report early turns where several desired offer types appear but cannot all be purchased.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact reroll prices, offer weights and current Book-level probability tables were not published.
records.mechanism: A single reroll action simultaneously changes roster, equipment and opponent opportunities, coupling economy and route choice.

records.version_scope: Contract launch through 2025-07 public patches

records.practical_support: The 300+ guide maxes Ranger, melee and Priest contract trees while assigning one Shield, four damage weapons and three supports; another review records profession-specific versus whole-team Contract choices.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Current threshold values and every weapon/set contribution are unavailable; launch percentages cannot define later patches.
records.mechanism: Role identity comes from equipped weapon while separate armor pieces fund a breakpoint tree that chooses vertical class power or horizontal team support.

records.spatial_condition: Weapon attack profiles distinguish near, front, furthest and support targets

records.version_scope: Contract launch, March transaction fixes and June one-click follow-up
records.rule_support: Three identical same-quality items merge into a higher-quality copy; three different same-quality items can be reforged into a random higher-quality item. March fixed equipment disappearing during reforge dragging, and June added one-click synthesis.
records.practical_support: Players describe repeatedly unequipping, merging, replacing and reforging items as the main long-run labor, while warning that unidentified set pieces can be accidentally consumed.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No complete probability or salvage table establishes reforge expected value, and one-click synthesis behavior for equipped/special items is undocumented.
records.mechanism: Deterministic vertical merging and random conversion share scarce ingredients, so item identity and transaction atomicity matter as much as material value.
records.engine: Three-copy synthesis, three-item reforge and inventory transfer

records.survival: Upgraded defensive items improve protection, but accidental consumption removes it
records.spatial_condition: Not battlefield spatial; equipment location between hero, bag and forge is transactional state
records.payoff_owner: Output item owns stats; hero owns equipped state; forge owns transformation
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Keep rare set ingredients, deterministically merge a core item, or sacrifice three off-plan items for a random pivot.
records.counterplay: Preview all consumed ids, protected/special status, output class and rollback on invalid transfer.
records.failure_explanation: Show inputs, prior owners, materials, output and why an item was ineligible or consumed.
records.transferability: Equipment crafting needs atomic ownership transfer, lock markers and deterministic-versus-random paths with different opportunity costs.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not auto-consume equipped or unique build pieces without explicit confirmation and provenance.
records.project_question: How should duplicate gear, salvage and random conversion coexist without turning build management into repetitive risk?

records.version_scope: 2025-04-23 historical guide with later supply changes separated
records.rule_support: Magicbook upgrades increase accessible recruit/equipment quality, Grimoire health and other rewards; after the May rework they also expand Treasure Synergy energy and enable Red+1 shop offers after Shop Level 11.
records.practical_support: The guide deliberately fields only four or five characters, rushes Book 4, then replaces placeholders with starred elite characters; reviewers independently treat Book level as the central supply curve.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact upgrade prices and modern elite odds are missing, and the guide predates May's energy and infinite-growth rework.
records.mechanism: A shared run-level upgrade trades immediate full-team strength for future offer quality, survivability and build capacity.
records.engine: Magicbook level and shop-quality gates

records.survival: Book upgrades increase Grimoire health while a smaller transition team risks combat

records.version_scope: Contract launch through 2025-05 infinite-level rework

records.disagreement_or_limit: Launch reviews complained the experience pool and costs were not displayed; current curves, passive milestones and replacement refunds are unknown.

records.version_scope: historical 2025-04-23 pre-rework Endless build

records.rule_support: Shield, healing, Cleanse, lifesteal, energy and double-cast are separately owned effects; official Weakness can reduce healing and apply Healing Block at maximum stacks.

records.project_question: How can displacement plus control enable an elemental area build without forming an uninterruptible loop?

records.version_scope: 2025-04-25 status and Contract rework
records.rule_support: Weakness caps at ten and reduces physical/magic damage and healing before applying Healing Block; Poison and Burn allow unbounded layers with separate attribute/duration caps; Armor Melt caps at ten; Rogue Contract can add, settle or double Burn/Poison.
records.practical_support: Endless players distinguish Freeze control, Poison setup, Cleanse/immunity and burst, while a long review explains that missing stack, duration and trigger feedback makes those combinations impossible to verify.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No current maintained database resolves every status duration, source eligibility or resistance interaction beyond the selected patch.
records.mechanism: Statuses have different stack, duration and payoff semantics; Contract nodes propagate or immediately settle them rather than treating all elements as one affinity bonus.
records.engine: Burn/Poison suppliers, Weakness/Armor Melt amplifiers, Rogue Contract and Cleanse
records.state_resource: Stacks, duration, stat-reduction cap, Healing Block and source identity
records.trigger: Normal attack, skill, timed Contract pulse or threshold
records.scope: Target, nearby units, random enemies or all enemies by effect
records.payoff: DOT, reduced stats/healing, increased damage taken and immediate abnormal-damage settlement
records.survival: Cleanse/immunity and Wind Shield interrupt the chain
records.spatial_condition: Some effects spread to target surroundings while others select random or all enemies
records.payoff_owner: Applying item/weapon owns source; status owns state; Contract owns propagation/detonation
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Choose suppliers and payoff items before committing Contract points to status amplification.
records.counterplay: Cleanse, immunity, Healing Block reversal, stack caps and timed windows answer different states.
records.failure_explanation: Display stack source, duration refresh, cap, propagation and immediate settlement separately.
records.transferability: Element systems should define supplier, persistent state, payoff and cleanse owner instead of granting generic team damage.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy infinite raw stack counts or mix Poison, Burn, Frost and armor reduction into one counter rule.
records.project_question: Which statuses persist, propagate, detonate or cleanse, and which hero owns each step?

records.version_scope: launch Treasure Linkage to 2025-05-18 Synergy 2.0
records.rule_support: Contract launch added treasure linkage set effects; Synergy 2.0 replaced/expanded this with 20 freely distributable starting energy, increasing through Magicbook upgrades to 175, and optimized trigger/range rules.
records.practical_support: The historical guide activates a treasure synergy for Health and damage by distributing required items across heroes, while players otherwise prioritize Contract, Book and equipment simultaneously.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No public complete energy-cost table or before/after strategy source establishes current optimal allocations.
records.mechanism: Cross-item rule packages consume a separate expandable capacity budget, preventing every discovered treasure synergy from activating at once.
records.engine: Treasure ownership, set relations and Synergy energy allocation
records.state_resource: 20-to-175 energy, equipped treasures, unlocked effects and Magicbook level
records.trigger: Equip required treasure set and allocate sufficient energy
records.scope: Carrier, nearby allies or team according to synergy
records.payoff: Conditional stats, shielding, status or damage effects
records.survival: Defensive synergies compete with offensive effects for the same capacity
records.spatial_condition: Some treasures can be spread across heroes; effect ranges were explicitly optimized
records.payoff_owner: Treasure holders own pieces; Synergy node owns combined rule; Book owns capacity growth
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Upgrade Book for capacity or spend immediate resources on units/equipment; reallocate energy when the build changes.
records.counterplay: Cap total active rules and expose required pieces, energy cost, range and inactive reason.
records.failure_explanation: Show missing item, insufficient energy, range failure or disabled synergy.
records.transferability: Relic combinations can use a separate visible budget rather than stacking every global modifier without cost.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not tie all relic capacity to one universally optimal Book upgrade or import 175 as a project value.
records.project_question: Should relic combinations consume shared capacity, individual slots or mutually exclusive activation choices?

records.version_scope: April capped Endless before 2025-05-18 growth revamp
records.rule_support: May removed character-level and red-equipment enhancement caps, allowed orange materials to enhance red gear, added Red+1 shop offers after Shop Level 11 and enabled standard Endless weapon swaps every 90 stages.
records.practical_support: Before the rework, players reported equipment flattening around stage 120 and runs stalling around 160–165 while enemies continued scaling; later players still report steep enemy multipliers and costly progression.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Individual stage walls vary by build and mode; cap removal does not prove the new infinite scaling curve is healthy.
records.mechanism: An endless enemy curve cannot continue after player upgrade channels hard-cap; removing caps restores progress but can replace a wall with repetitive inflation.
records.engine: Character level, gear enhancement, shop quality and enemy stage scaling
records.state_resource: Stage, item tier, enhancement level, materials, character level and enemy multiplier
records.trigger: Advance beyond prior player-growth ceiling
records.scope: Whole Endless run
records.payoff: Continued player scaling and a late weapon pivot window
records.survival: More Health/defense growth can answer later burst only if costs track enemy escalation
records.spatial_condition: Enemy package, not only numeric stage, determines whether backline or frontline fails
records.payoff_owner: Character/gear own growth; mode controller owns enemy curve and pivot schedule
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Use orange materials and high-level shops to extend core gear; every 90 stages permits weapon reselection.
records.counterplay: Use finite meaningful milestones and enemy capability exams rather than endless multiplicative numbers.
records.failure_explanation: Identify capped channel, unaffordable enhancement, enemy capability or raw scaling mismatch.
records.transferability: Tower progression needs synchronized player ceilings, enemy exams and late pivot access.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not import infinite character/gear scaling or hundreds of stages as content depth.
records.project_question: Where should a finite tower end before growth becomes repetitive inflation, and what remains upgradeable near the finale?

records.version_scope: Contract launch through 2025-06 Boss-set event update
records.rule_support: Fate/hero/Blacksmith events can award, duplicate, exchange or complete special armor; June added a Boss-set event at stage 100 and every 50 stages thereafter.
records.practical_support: The guide targets Requiem Knight from an event then uses Blacksmith Karl to clone or make the missing half; Challenge players call high-tier duplication/set completion far stronger than random reforge.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Event weights, duplicate limits and current special-set pools are unpublished; community value judgments are not drop-rate statistics.
records.mechanism: Rare build-defining sets use events for the first piece and a later duplication/completion service, forming a directed acquisition chain outside the shop.
records.engine: Special event reward, Blacksmith duplication and set completion
records.state_resource: Event availability, owned set half, item quality, exchange inputs and stage schedule
records.trigger: Select event, offer two items or reach Boss-set milestone
records.scope: One special set or duplicated item
records.payoff: Complete a powerful set and its Contract contribution
records.survival: Defensive special sets can supply shield, cleanse or delayed death
records.spatial_condition: Set effect remains on its equipped hero even when Contract broadcasts team-wide
records.payoff_owner: Event owns acquisition; Blacksmith owns transform; equipped hero/set owns effect
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Preserve two exchange items and a valuable first set piece instead of reforging them; pivot when event reveals a stronger line.
records.counterplay: Preview possible rewards, offer pity/completion routes and avoid making one rare event mandatory.
records.failure_explanation: Show whether a set is shop-excluded, event-only, missing one piece or waiting for the scheduled milestone.
records.transferability: Directed event completion can rescue a partial build without making ordinary rerolls deterministic.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not require an unpreviewed rare Blacksmith event for every viable late build.
records.project_question: Which rare equipment packages need a guaranteed completion path after the player commits to the first piece?

records.version_scope: 2025 launch through June weapon update
records.rule_support: Weapons explicitly target nearest, front, furthest, random or surrounding units; Taunt, grouping, knockback and control immunity alter access, and official patches repaired long-range targeting and monsters moving behind player characters.
records.practical_support: Endless builds respond to mass Rangers killing healers, Skeleton Shield reflection, 35–40-unit groups, perma-freeze and intermittent immunity by changing shield, Cleanse, target count, grouping or damage source.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Public text does not define the exact eight-unit formation topology or deterministic tie-breaks; one reviewer felt positioning beyond range was weak.
records.mechanism: Formation value comes from target selectors and displacement/control rules even when exact grid geometry is undocumented.
records.engine: Weapon target policy, Taunt, grouping, knockback and immunity
records.state_resource: Front/back role, range, target count, current Taunt, enemy density and immunity window
records.trigger: Acquire target, cast grouping/knockback or lose current target
records.scope: Nearest/front/furthest/area recipients
records.payoff: Direct damage/control toward the intended enemy package
records.survival: Taunt and protection keep backline owners alive; knockback immunity preserves formation
records.spatial_condition: Mass Rangers bypass normal front pressure; grouped mobs enable area payoff; reflection punishes repeated hits
records.payoff_owner: Weapon owns target rule; controller/displacer owns movement state; hero owns formation slot
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Add Cleanse, a different target profile or extra multi-target carry when the previewed enemy package demands it.
records.counterplay: Preview access rule, reflection, immunity and density before battle and allow at least one replacement window.
records.failure_explanation: Show why a target was chosen, moved, taunted, immune or reflected damage.
records.transferability: Authored enemy packages can turn targeting and formation into clear exams without copying the original unknown grid.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not infer exact adjacency or deterministic ordering from screenshots and community outcome reports.
records.project_question: Which enemy packages test front protection, backline access, grouping, reflection and control immunity on the square board?

records.version_scope: launch readability complaints and April/July report fixes
records.rule_support: Official updates added in-battle character details and repaired attribute, damage-taken, Boss text and passive-description mismatches.
records.practical_support: A 120-hour reviewer reports missing enemy Health/shield bars, status icons/stacks, damage type/source, duration, stacking, trigger and multihit semantics, making it unclear whether combinations function.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The review predates some fixes, while later patches do not demonstrate that every attribution gap was closed.
records.mechanism: Dense equipment/status systems become untestable when results show only colored numbers instead of owner, source, target, state and trigger chain.
records.engine: HUD, Codex, combat details and settlement report
records.state_resource: Health, shield, status stacks/duration, damage type, attack count and effect source
records.trigger: Attack, skill, status change, shield change or battle end
records.scope: Each actor/event and aggregate report
records.payoff: Player can confirm a build, diagnose failure and compare replacements
records.survival: Visible shield and prevented/healed damage explains defensive value
records.spatial_condition: Target reason and range/position must accompany damage source
records.payoff_owner: Effect source owns event; target owns resulting state; report aggregates without erasing attribution
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Reliable attribution lets the player decide which hero, weapon or set to replace rather than reroll blindly.
records.counterplay: Expose enemy status, immunity, reflection and target selection with the same grammar.
records.failure_explanation: List ordered source → effect → target → mitigation/state/result events plus totals.
records.transferability: Build-heavy autobattle requires shield, status, multihit and conversion attribution as a core system, not optional polish.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not rely on color alone or one aggregate damage number to explain multi-owner builds.
records.project_question: Which event fields must appear in the battle report so shield and element builds can be independently verified?

records.version_scope: launch inventory workflow to 2025-06-27 one-click synthesis
records.rule_support: The June update explicitly attributes the new one-click synthesis feature to player feedback.
records.practical_support: Multiple reviews describe long Endless runs dominated by unequipping, merging, swapping, reforging and hovering unidentified set pieces, with repeated clicks rather than new decisions.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The update does not publish usage data or define whether all special/equipped items are safely excluded.
records.mechanism: A deterministic known merge should be batchable once the player has protected exceptions; repeated manual execution adds labor, not strategy.
records.engine: Eligible-item scan and one-click synthesis
records.state_resource: Duplicate ids, quality, equipped/locked/special flags and inventory capacity
records.trigger: Player invokes batch synthesis
records.scope: All safe deterministic merges
records.payoff: Reduce repetitive inventory operations while preserving build decisions
records.survival: Locked defensive/core items remain untouched
records.spatial_condition: Not battlefield spatial; item location and owner are eligibility constraints
records.payoff_owner: Player owns confirmation; merge system owns batch transaction; output keeps provenance
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Automate settled upgrades so attention remains on route, replacement and counter choices.
records.counterplay: Allow preview, exclusion, lock and undo/rollback on failure.
records.failure_explanation: Show every merge, skipped protected item and resulting free capacity.
records.transferability: Automate repeated deterministic maintenance after the strategic choice has already been made.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not automate random reforge or consume uncertain set pieces as if they were deterministic cleanup.
records.project_question: Which inventory actions are real build choices and which should become safe batch operations?

records.version_scope: 2025-03 prelaunch fixes through 2025-07 regressions
records.rule_support: Official patches fixed passives active at level one, pre/post-purchase effect changes, unapplied upgrade stats, talents leaking across saves, description/effect mismatches, unintended Ranger Contract effects and a broken Destiny Start trait.
records.practical_support: Players report missing passive translations, unclear activation and the inability to verify whether effects work, while a July thread independently reported Destiny and reward breakage before the official fix.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The public notes list symptoms rather than one root cause, and the latest patch does not guarantee all start-state or localization defects are gone.
records.mechanism: Passives and starting modifiers must derive from one authoritative state across preview, purchase, battle and save boundaries.
records.engine: Passive unlock/evaluation, Contract threshold and start-mode initialization
records.state_resource: Character level, purchased state, selected start, save id and localized description
records.trigger: Preview recruit, purchase, level up, load save or start run
records.scope: Character passive, team Contract and run modifier
records.payoff: Consistent intended stats and triggers
records.survival: Defensive starts/passives must not silently fail or leak between runs
records.spatial_condition: Combat-only passives may hide prep-phase values but must state that boundary
records.payoff_owner: Character/start mode owns effect; save/run owns lifetime; UI reflects authority
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Preview and purchased behavior must agree so a recruit or start choice remains valid.
records.counterplay: Validate on phase transitions and reset all run-scoped state on new save/run.
records.failure_explanation: State inactive reason: level, combat-only phase, missing Contract, failed initialization or version mismatch.
records.transferability: Resource-authored passives need authoritative phase/lifetime rules and regression tests across preview, purchase and save load.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not duplicate effect logic between tooltip, shop preview and battle implementation.
records.project_question: How will passive, trait and relic state stay identical across preview, roster, battle and save restoration?

records.version_scope: 2025-06-27 Workshop/leaderboard release
records.rule_support: Workshop lets players create/apply custom weapons without coding, but Workshop weapons are explicitly ineligible for Endless and Challenge leaderboard rankings.
records.practical_support: Existing guides and discussions compare authored weapon/build progression and high-stage results, making the separation necessary for interpretable rankings.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The announcement does not define custom-weapon access in normal runs, achievements, saves or shared build reports beyond leaderboard exclusion.
records.mechanism: Rule-editing custom content can coexist with solo experimentation only when verified progression and comparative records exclude it by provenance.
records.engine: Workshop weapon loading plus leaderboard eligibility check
records.state_resource: Weapon origin, mod state, run mode, achievement and leaderboard flag
records.trigger: Start/load run, equip custom weapon or submit score
records.scope: Run validity and external ranking
records.payoff: Creative custom builds without contaminating authored comparisons
records.survival: Not a defensive layer; integrity protects meaning of progression evidence
records.spatial_condition: Custom target/range rules may alter formation assumptions and must retain provenance
records.payoff_owner: Creator owns custom definition; run owns mod set; leaderboard owns eligibility policy
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Custom weapons may alter shop pools and build access, so their origin must remain visible in every offer/report.
records.counterplay: Hash content set, label modded runs and block incompatible submissions deterministically.
records.failure_explanation: Show which custom dependency made a run ineligible rather than silently rejecting it.
records.transferability: Modded rule content needs provenance and mode boundaries before it can coexist with balance evidence.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not treat Workshop builds as evidence for the authored game's balance or allow them into comparable records.
records.project_question: If content mods arrive later, which run rewards, saves and comparisons remain valid?

records.version_scope: launch Endless observations through 2026 post-public-patch review
records.rule_support: Official rules provide Healing Block, reflection-related shields, immunity/control, infinite gear/level scaling and periodic weapon reselection as distinct axes.
records.practical_support: Across periods, players report mass Rangers, reflection, huge groups and perma-freeze pushing shields/Cleanse/AOE/control, while a 2026 review says mandatory Healing Block and enemy multipliers invalidate healing and narrow viable late lines.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No pick/win-rate data proves universal convergence, and reports span different versions/modes; current exact balance is unknown.
records.mechanism: Many nominal build axes collapse when late enemies simultaneously demand burst survival, backline protection, Cleanse, multi-target throughput and anti-heal/anti-reflection answers.
records.engine: Enemy capability packages and player build axes
records.state_resource: Shield uptime, Cleanse, target count, status immunity, healing, gear access and replacement cost
records.trigger: Cross late Endless capability wall
records.scope: Whole eight-person composition
records.payoff: A small package of carries plus mandatory defensive answers continues progression
records.survival: Layered shields and delayed death outperform pure healing under burst/Healing Block reports
records.spatial_condition: Backline access, crowd size and reflection change which formation/weapon survives
records.payoff_owner: Enemy package owns exam; each player component must own one answer rather than one universal unit owning all
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Late recruits become expensive and special pieces event-dependent, so periodic weapon swap may be too narrow to rebuild a failed composition.
records.counterplay: Distribute exams across floors, preview them early and offer bridge items/replacement windows for multiple valid responses.
records.failure_explanation: Identify missing capability, not merely higher enemy level or lower total power.
records.transferability: A rich system needs authored enemies that test axes separately before combining them, or apparent variety becomes a checklist.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not present community frustration as measured dominance or solve convergence with infinite stat growth.
records.project_question: Which late-tower floors test shield, cleanse, targeting, control and sustain independently before a combined final exam?

records.version_scope: public Demo release through latest accessed patch 0.5.7 on 2026-09-01
records.rule_support: Leyline announced the standalone public Demo, then published a continuous 0.5.1.718–0.5.7 patch line; the maintained wiki identifies its extracted shipped-data snapshot as 0.5.6 build ff633149.
records.practical_support: The 0.5.2 Endless guide and later discussions operate in different points of that line, so their builds require patch-specific corrections rather than being merged as current rules.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The main App remains TBA, the wiki is not official and stops at 0.5.6, and 0.5.7 does not restate the complete rules table.
records.mechanism: Bind every rule and build to a public Demo version before comparing performance or transferring design lessons.
records.engine: Official release/patch chain plus maintained shipped-data snapshot
records.state_resource: App identity, build id, patch date and source access date
records.trigger: Use a rule, numerical value or practical build claim
records.scope: Whole dossier and evidence corpus
records.payoff: Avoid mixing launch, 0.5.2, 0.5.6 and 0.5.7 behavior
records.survival: Not a combat layer; version hygiene protects analytical validity
records.spatial_condition: Targeting evidence is specifically 0.5.6 unless later patch text changes it
records.payoff_owner: Official notes own declared changes; wiki owns its snapshot interpretation; practice sources own observed builds
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Re-evaluate old shop/build advice whenever a relevant patch changes costs, classes or effects.
records.counterplay: Require explicit version scope and downgrade any older recommendation contradicted by a later patch.
records.failure_explanation: Identify source date, mapped build and the later rule that invalidates an old conclusion.
records.transferability: Keep version ids on balance data, build examples and failure reports from the start.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not describe Demo 0.5.7 as the unreleased main game's final design.
records.project_question: Which content and balance fields need version provenance so later patches do not silently rewrite design evidence?

records.version_scope: 0.5.2–0.5.6 economy, with no declared 0.5.7 table change
records.rule_support: Regular shops offer three heroes, two items and one relic with one 25% discount; reroll starts at one Shard and rises, Freeze carries offers while affecting pity, heroes/items sell for 66%, relics cannot be sold, and Auction House rerolls start higher and cannot Freeze.
records.practical_support: Red Rift players use common items as bridge power/small banks and delay the Key until the last viable shop, while a long review describes pre-ranked purchases and expensive Auction pivots locking direction.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Hidden weights come from the maintained data snapshot; player sources do not quantify optimal roll counts or prove the economy is universally too restrictive.
records.mechanism: Escalating rerolls, discounted mixed offers, partial sellback and non-sellable relics create different commitment levels in one shop.
records.engine: Shard income, mixed offers, reroll escalation, Freeze/pity and sellback
records.state_resource: Shards, current roll cost, frozen offers, pity state, owned pieces and future shop count
records.trigger: Enter shop, buy, freeze, reroll or sell
records.scope: Current run economy and roster
records.payoff: Acquire immediate strength or preserve a reachable future build
records.survival: Bridge items and early heroes reduce losses while the final package is incomplete
records.spatial_condition: Purchased heroes still require scarce active/reserve slots
records.payoff_owner: Player owns currency choice; offer owns discount; item/hero owns purchased value; relic is irreversible
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Use discounted bridges and sellable items early, but demand stronger evidence before committing to a non-sellable relic or costly Auction reroll.
records.counterplay: Visible remaining shops, pity impact and resale values keep a miss from appearing arbitrary.
records.failure_explanation: Show cumulative reroll cost, frozen-pity change, resale loss and unavailable future window.
records.transferability: Different resale/lock rules can make temporary equipment, heroes and global relics carry distinct commitment weights.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy hidden pity tables or exact 66% resale without testing the project's run length.
records.project_question: How should temporary gear, recruit replacement and irreversible relics communicate their different pivot costs?

records.version_scope: Demo 0.5.5–0.5.6 rank/class rules
records.rule_support: Heroes progress C→B→A→S; B chooses among three fixed specializations, while A/S offers draw from active class pools and dual-class heroes split that modifier pool.
records.practical_support: Players describe buying pre-ranked heroes as powerful but direction-locking because specialization, subsequent offers and sunk Shards constrain later replacements.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No public complete offer-weight table or current class win rates establish the best specialization strategy.
records.mechanism: An upgrade changes both current ability and the distribution of future build offers, creating path dependence.
records.engine: Rank-up, fixed B specialization and class-filtered A/S modifiers
records.state_resource: Hero rank, active class tags, modifier pool, Shards and already equipped resources
records.trigger: Promote a hero or buy a pre-ranked hero
records.scope: One hero and its future modifier offers
records.payoff: Access a coherent class-specific engine or bridge into a second class
records.survival: Defensive specializations can stabilize immediately but may narrow later damage options
records.spatial_condition: Class choice changes role/targeting priorities and whether the hero occupies frontline, backline or reserve
records.payoff_owner: Hero owns rank; specialization owns new class/rule; later modifier owns its payoff
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: The first useful promotion may define the carry; replacing it means repaying rank and equipment investment.
records.counterplay: Preview future pool changes and offer a limited respec/replacement route before late commitment.
records.failure_explanation: Show whether a desired modifier was outside the active class pool or diluted by dual class.
records.transferability: Class-bending is meaningful when it changes future option space, not only a tag count.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not import Guildrun's four ranks or random modifier pool into a fixed authored hero tree.
records.project_question: Should a hero's first specialization alter later equipment/relic offers, and how is that future cost previewed?

records.version_scope: Demo 0.5.5–0.5.6 active-board/reserve rules
records.rule_support: The active team expands from three to five while roster capacity reaches six; specific Backup modifiers allow the reserve hero to provide a defined effect from outside the active board.
records.practical_support: Mystic players move Fiona or Grace into Backup to retain shield/stat utility while fielding a higher-rank active hero; another player reports that reserve investment can be difficult to recover.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Sources do not publish every reserve interaction, buff eligibility or replacement edge case, and Fiona's strength is disputed.
records.mechanism: A reserve slot can own a narrowly authored support payoff but still consumes recruitment and upgrade investment.
records.engine: Roster capacity plus Backup modifier
records.state_resource: Five active slots, one reserve slot, hero rank, equipment and Backup effect
records.trigger: Combat begins or a qualifying active action occurs while the owner is in reserve
records.scope: Named ally/team effect from one reserve owner
records.payoff: Preserve a support conversion without occupying an active combat slot
records.survival: Backup shield/heal/stat support can protect active units while the owner avoids battlefield danger
records.spatial_condition: Reserve owner has no active grid position; effect must define how it selects recipients
records.payoff_owner: Reserve hero owns Backup; active recipient owns resulting stat/state
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Move an early stabilizer to reserve only when the retained effect justifies sunk rank/equipment and the active replacement adds more value.
records.counterplay: Limit reserve stacking and expose whether effects stop on replacement, defeat or owner removal.
records.failure_explanation: Show inactive reason: wrong position, missing Backup modifier, invalid recipient or roster removal.
records.transferability: Bench passives can create roster depth if ownership and opportunity cost remain explicit.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not let every benched hero broadcast full abilities or ignore its upgrade cost.
records.project_question: Which support effects may operate from reserve, and what active-slot or resource tradeoff prevents a second invisible team?

records.version_scope: Demo 0.5.6 targeting snapshot with 0.5.7 target/source fixes
records.rule_support: Normal target ordering uses distance, class priority, log2(current HP)+Defense/100 and a deterministic GUID tie-break; selection and pathfinding are separate, and an already locked projectile may continue tracking a target that gains Stealth.
records.practical_support: Players answer teleport, furthest pull/stun/poison, random snipe and AOE with reverse formation, all-front deployment, left/right ordering, backline access and aggro sharing.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The exact extracted formula is not an official player-facing contract, and community reports do not measure every enemy selector or visual radius.
records.mechanism: A deterministic target score plus special enemy selectors turns formation into counterplay, but only if lock/reselection/path states are visible.
records.engine: Target sorter, special selector, pathfinder and projectile lock
records.state_resource: Distance, class, current HP, Defense, GUID, reachability, Stealth and current lock
records.trigger: Acquire/lose target, move, teleport, launch projectile or enter Stealth
records.scope: One attacker, candidate targets and path
records.payoff: Predictable focus fire or a deliberately exceptional enemy attack
records.survival: Repositioning and aggro sharing keep vulnerable owners alive
records.spatial_condition: Reverse/all-front/left-right layouts answer furthest, teleport and AOE rules differently
records.payoff_owner: Selector owns target; pathfinder owns movement; projectile owns retained lock; target owns Stealth state
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Reserve swap or recruit backline access when positioning alone cannot answer the selector.
records.counterplay: Preview special selector and show target line/lock before combat where possible.
records.failure_explanation: Report target candidates, winning rule, path failure, lock persistence and Stealth interaction.
records.transferability: Separate selection, reachability and projectile tracking into inspectable deterministic stages.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not require players to calculate GUID tie-breaks or copy the exact score into the project's moving grid.
records.project_question: What target intent and lock information must be visible before an independent tactical command changes position?

records.version_scope: launch Red Rift guide corrected through 0.5.4
records.rule_support: Red Rift combines limited-loss/class/shop mission rules; 0.5.2 raised the first-shop budget to 30 Shards, while 0.5.4 gave the Act 2 Boss 50% Frost resistance.
records.practical_support: The guide prioritizes survival, then mission completion, then end-build; it buys two heroes, reaches B rank early, uses common items as bridges/banks, fields tank+DPS+sustain or tank+two DPS+team shield/heal, and delays the Key until the last viable shop.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The guide predates later Frost/Funke changes and deliberately avoids a fixed hero/item list, so it supports route principles rather than a current best composition.
records.mechanism: A constrained challenge route rewards solving the next mission with liquid bridges before committing to a final build.
records.engine: Mission objectives, loss budget, shop schedule, 30-Shard opener and Key purchase
records.state_resource: Shards, lives, class requirements, common items, rank and remaining shops
records.trigger: Enter shop, inspect next mission or reach final Key window
records.scope: Whole Red Rift run
records.payoff: Complete mandatory objectives without sacrificing terminal combat power
records.survival: Tank plus sustain/teamwide shield protects the limited-loss budget
records.spatial_condition: Tank/frontline and damage/support positions adapt to each encounter and Boss
records.payoff_owner: Current tank/carry/support own combat roles; Key owns access cost; route owns timing pressure
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Buy immediate two-hero structure, rank a viable core, bank through sellable items and purchase Key only after required combat shopping.

records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy old Frost advice, exact 30 Shards or Red Rift mission tables as project balance.

records.practical_support: The Endless guide uses Aria, Gustav, Pollen and optionally Ming around Kai and values Mana Regen/high-frequency shielding over a single large shield; Mystic players independently discuss Grace/Gustav shield-mana support.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The core guide is 0.5.2 and community Mystic strength is disputed; later fixes prove the structure existed but not its 0.5.7 tier.

records.version_scope: 0.5.2 Endless build with later 0.5.5 control context

records.version_scope: 0.5.2 Endless build corrected by 0.5.6 targeting/counter notes

records.version_scope: Endless stunlock reports through 0.5.5–0.5.6 resistance behavior
records.rule_support: 0.5.5 introduced stacking Stun Resistance and cast-time immunity to stop indefinite control, with subsequent text/interaction correction continuing in later patches.
records.practical_support: A launch-period Red Rift review identifies stunlock as a formation/encounter failure that can prevent invested units from acting.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The review predates the fix and no post-patch control-uptime statistics prove final tuning; not every control effect is documented.
records.mechanism: Repeated hard control grants growing resistance and protects committed casts, ensuring eventual action without deleting control as a build axis.
records.engine: Stun application, resistance stack and casting immunity

records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Players may still recruit resistance/cleanse, but it is not the only route out of an infinite lock.

records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not grant unconditional permanent immunity after one Stun or allow chained controllers to reset resistance.
records.project_question: What resistance accumulation and decay preserves control builds while guaranteeing heroes eventually execute a command?

records.version_scope: 0.5.1–0.5.5 balance telemetry and specialization revisions
records.rule_support: Official patches repeatedly redistribute relic/specialization power; 0.5.5 reports Duelist Outbreak Banner nearly ten percentage points above other banners and reworks it, while earlier notes address specialization convergence.
records.practical_support: The rank system makes these modifiers path-defining rather than isolated stat items, so an overperforming banner can collapse multiple hero branches into the same choice.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Only selected internal differences are published; there is no complete dataset, sample size or mode-stratified table for independent causal analysis.
records.mechanism: Use outcome data to detect a rule modifier that erases sibling choices, then change its structure rather than only hiding the number.

records.state_resource: Selection, mode, rank, effect structure and measured win difference
records.trigger: Telemetry shows one option materially separating from peers
records.scope: Duelist specialization and comparable banners
records.payoff: Restore meaningful horizontal modifier choice
records.survival: Avoid one modifier becoming the universal defensive/offensive package
records.spatial_condition: Banner effects may alter which positions/owners benefit; exact current geometry is not public
records.payoff_owner: Banner owns rule; hero/class owns eligibility; analytics owns comparison
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A rework changes the value of prior rank commitments, so patches should provide preview/respec or clear version boundaries.
records.counterplay: Inspect by mode, rank and owner before generalizing a headline win gap.
records.failure_explanation: Publish what behavior was overperforming and what structural choice the rework restores.
records.transferability: Balance data is most useful when tied to a choice-collapse hypothesis and followed by an interpretable rework.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not treat the quoted difference as universal or copy a banner without its dataset/context.
records.project_question: Which first-version relic/class choices need telemetry fields that can reveal choice collapse rather than only average win rate?

records.version_scope: 0.5.1–0.5.2 meta-resource and rewind fixes
records.rule_support: 0.5.2 grants two Boss Tokens on reaching each Boss as a stated temporary solution, while the 0.5.1–0.5.2 chain fixes Emergency Rewind recharge incorrectly accumulating Shards and a result-screen softlock.
records.practical_support: Mode progression makes Boss access, restart/rewind and Shard economy share a run boundary; duplicated rewards or a locked result screen directly alter subsequent build purchasing.

records.version_scope: 0.5.4–0.5.7 combat-event integrity fixes
records.rule_support: 0.5.4 guarded automatic-attack effects from recursively triggering each other; 0.5.5 repaired same-frame damage/death, resurrection state and aggro; 0.5.7 continued DoT/immunity/crit/on-damage ordering fixes.
records.practical_support: High-frequency Shield, Assassin, Poison and Stall builds all multiply event count, so corrupted recursion or death ordering changes both output and apparent counterplay.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Patch notes enumerate symptoms but do not publish the complete event queue, recursion depth or deterministic ordering contract.
records.mechanism: Every generated attack/damage/death event needs source lineage, re-entry guards and an atomic death/retarget boundary.
records.engine: Combat event queue, source tags, recursion guard, death resolver and target reacquisition

records.scope: All affected actors and pending targets
records.payoff: Deterministic finite resolution with correct source ownership
records.survival: Immunity/resurrection apply at defined points and cannot be bypassed by event race
records.spatial_condition: Death/teleport/revival changes occupancy and requires path/target revalidation
records.payoff_owner: Original source owns lineage; generated effect owns child event; resolver owns ordering; targeter owns reacquisition
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Build evaluation remains stable because extra-trigger pieces cannot create hidden infinite value.
records.counterplay: Cap/reject prohibited re-entry and expose immunity, cancellation and target changes.
records.failure_explanation: Trace ordered parent→child events, guard rejection, lethal grouping, resurrection and retarget.
records.transferability: Typed event lineage and recursion/death guards are prerequisites for rich relic and status combinations.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not allow generated automatic attacks to count as fresh roots unless explicitly authored.
records.project_question: Which triggers may generate attacks or damage, and what lineage rule prevents a relic pair from recursively feeding itself?
