records.version_scope: Demo 1.5.5 through full 2.0.9 perimeter display
records.rule_support: Trigger direction/linkage and backpack shape determine activation; 2.0.9 adds an explicit track-perimeter display.
records.practical_support: Independent reviews explain that the ball runs around the connected bag perimeter: expanding capacity lengthens a loop and lets time-based enemies act more often, while a compact route triggers fewer items more frequently.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The current cells-to-seconds formula, multiple disconnected-region rule and loop-speed cap are not published.
records.mechanism: Backpack perimeter is both capacity and a shared attack-speed budget.
records.engine: Movable bag cells, trigger ball and perimeter track
records.state_resource: Connected perimeter length, ball speed, loop count, item count and enemy action time
records.trigger: Ball reaches an item point or completes a loop
records.scope: All active items attached to the selected route
records.payoff: Trade more effect owners for slower global cadence or fewer owners for faster repetition
records.survival: Longer paths expose the player to more timed enemy actions before defensive triggers repeat
records.spatial_condition: Only the outer track of the ball's connected bag region defines travel; starting point affects opening order
records.payoff_owner: Bag layout owns path; ball owns cadence; each item owns its triggered effect
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Buy/attach more bag space only when the new owner adds more value than the frequency lost by the whole loop.
records.counterplay: Enemy timing, fatigue and item seal punish oversized low-throughput routes.
records.failure_explanation: Display perimeter, estimated loop time, active points and enemy actions per loop.
records.transferability: Treat spatial expansion as a rate cost, not a free increase in slots.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy a yellow orbit ball or assume every project equipment slot shares one literal track.
records.project_question: Which roster/equipment-space expansion should reduce cadence or create another visible opportunity cost?

records.version_scope: full version 2.0.1-period player clear
records.rule_support: Item placement can guarantee a linked weapon's critical trigger, while another weapon can read current gold as critical-damage bonus.
records.practical_support: A player links 贪欲之刃 to 聚焦仪, then stops buying/rerolling to preserve about 2000 gold and reports 2000% critical-damage scaling; another review independently confirms guaranteed-crit plus permanent-growth combinations.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The complete defensive backpack and current 2.4.2 values are absent; one clear does not establish meta dominance.
records.mechanism: A positional guarantee converts an unreliable gold-scaling weapon into a deterministic carry while each shop spend directly reduces damage.
records.engine: 聚焦仪 guaranteed-crit star link plus 贪欲之刃 gold reader
records.state_resource: Current gold, critical guarantee, critical damage, adjacency and trigger cadence
records.trigger: Linked blade activates at the focus device's star position
records.scope: One weapon carry
records.payoff: Deterministic critical hit amplified by unspent gold
records.survival: Unspecified in the source; remaining internal space must solve Armor/heal rather than assuming offense is defense
records.spatial_condition: Blade trigger point reaches perimeter and occupies a valid star neighbor of the focus device
records.payoff_owner: Blade owns damage; focus device owns crit guarantee; player economy owns gold state
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Do not hoard before the guarantee arrives; after it arrives, every purchase/reroll is an explicit damage tradeoff.
records.counterplay: Physical immunity, item seal, low survivability and forced spending suppress the carry.
records.failure_explanation: Show current gold contribution, crit source, failed adjacency and post-mitigation damage.
records.transferability: A team-resource-to-carry conversion becomes interesting when the resource remains spendable and the reader occupies a scarce slot/position.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not import 1 gold = 1% or let all carries read the same team resource for free.
records.project_question: If one shooter reads team excess Health/Defense, what competing use and positional/equipment cost prevents automatic scaling?

records.version_scope: full version 2.0.1-period practical item chain
records.rule_support: 斯巴达战盔 is described as an Iron Mask craft endpoint with four side star positions; adjacent weapon triggers grant Armor and Strength, with lost-Health scaling, while loop-based Thorns was separately nerfed in 2.0.1.
records.practical_support: The review places active weapons around the internal Helmet so their perimeter triggers repeatedly feed both survival and weapon damage.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No current official English item table or full backpack screenshot text verifies exact 2.4.2 numbers; the Thorns patch is a related defense-output correction, not proof this Helmet was nerfed.
records.mechanism: An internal reader converts neighboring weapon events into Armor and an offensive buff without taking final damage ownership from the weapons.
records.engine: Four adjacent active weapons feeding an internal Spartan Helmet
records.state_resource: Star occupancy, trigger count, Armor, Strength, lost-Health ratio and loop time
records.trigger: Combat starts or a star-adjacent weapon activates
records.scope: Helmet owner and linked weapons
records.payoff: Strength raises linked weapon damage while repeated triggers compound output
records.survival: Armor absorbs damage and lost-Health scaling can accelerate recovery, but needs a safe activation window
records.spatial_condition: Helmet uses interior cells; four weapons must touch its stars and expose their own trigger points to the outer route
records.payoff_owner: Helmet owns Armor/Strength conversion; each weapon owns its damage
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Commit to the Iron Mask craft only when enough compatible active weapons and interior space exist.
records.counterplay: Physical immunity, positive-status clearing, item seal, slow perimeter or burst before Armor buildup attack different layers.
records.failure_explanation: Report which linked weapon fired, resulting Armor/Strength, lost-Health multiplier and damage owner.
records.transferability: A shield/armor system can support offense by feeding an explicit carry buff while defense remains defensive.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not make Armor itself universally deal damage or let one item cover every adjacent owner without a geometry/trigger cost.
records.project_question: Which defensive equipment can read ally actions and empower one or more carries without becoming a self-contained tank-carry?

records.version_scope: Demo 1.5.9 item package plus full 2.3.x route practice
records.rule_support: Beast Echo Totem can retrigger creatures, Beast Pact Seal counts creature triggers and at ten activates star-position creatures, and Heartnest heals per orbit for each unique creature; later patches repair creature conversion/loop interactions.
records.practical_support: The developer confirms Hunter guarantees Dragon Tamer, while a player reports dragon-egg hatch delay often forces a pivot before the creature line becomes ready.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The core item text is Demo-era and current values/pool odds are unknown; no complete screenshot or win-rate sample establishes current strength.
records.mechanism: Horizontal creature variety supplies per-loop sustain while repeated creature events cross a threshold that retriggers a selected payoff owner.
records.engine: Hunter route, creature triggers, Beast Echo Totem and Beast Pact Seal
records.state_resource: Creature count/types, ten-trigger counter, retrigger chance, egg progress, loop time and Health
records.trigger: Creature activates, counter reaches ten or ball completes an orbit
records.scope: Star-linked creatures and hero Health
records.payoff: Selected creature effects repeat; each creature retains its own output ownership
records.survival: Heartnest heals each loop according to unique creature variety
records.spatial_condition: Pact stars select retrigger owners; active creature points still need track access while Heartnest reads the whole loop
records.payoff_owner: Creature owns effect; Echo owns chance; Pact owns threshold/selection; Heartnest owns healing
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Hunter lowers route variance, but abandon or bridge if the egg cannot hatch before an already functional build occupies its space.
records.counterplay: Long hatch, slow route, item seal, positive-stack removal and recursion guards limit the chain.
records.failure_explanation: Show hatch progress, creature tags, event count, threshold recipient and loop-heal source.
records.transferability: Summon/creature builds need an entry window, explicit count ownership, payoff selection and non-recursive retrigger guard.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not guarantee the route for every hero or let converted creature tags replay old triggers.
records.project_question: How late may a summon engine arrive before its guaranteed event becomes a trap rather than a viable pivot?

records.version_scope: full version 2.3.x community/developer explanation
records.rule_support: The developer states Medium is an item type, bows qualify, and Metronome triggers itself extra times according to Mediums at its star positions; official patches later fix trigger stack overflow and chain loops.
records.practical_support: Players pair repeated neutral triggers with Omen Badge/Strength, while an independent review describes multi-trigger items feeding adjacent damage buffs and a bag that pays gold per activation.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Omen/Strength suggestions are small-community examples and no exact complete backpack or adoption data is supplied.
records.mechanism: A zero-base-damage cadence item becomes valuable through external readers, but generated events must preserve lineage and refuse recursive re-entry.
records.engine: Metronome self-trigger count plus star-linked Mediums and adjacent reader
records.state_resource: Medium tags, extra-trigger count, Strength, reader state, gold and event depth
records.trigger: Metronome point activates and creates additional self activations
records.scope: Metronome and linked readers
records.payoff: Reader converts frequency into damage, status or economy
records.survival: Not inherent; a sustain reader or separate defense must consume additional space
records.spatial_condition: Star positions count qualifying Mediums while Metronome itself needs route access
records.payoff_owner: Metronome owns cadence; Omen/adjacent item owns payoff; generated event retains parent source
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Choose reader before filling stars with Mediums; frequency without a payoff is empty activity.
records.counterplay: Item seal, slow perimeter, trigger caps and recursion guard reduce event volume.
records.failure_explanation: Separate raw activation count, reader activations, rejected recursion and realized output.
records.transferability: High-frequency engines should be reusable chassis whose value depends on a separately owned reader.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not equate trigger count with damage or let extra triggers create fresh root events.
records.project_question: Which relics may read repeated ally actions, and how does the event model prevent two readers from feeding each other forever?

records.version_scope: Demo 1.5.10 authored Ranger arsenal with full-version Boss counter context
records.rule_support: Ranger recipes create Heal Block, multi-status arrows, a ten-projectile decaying bow and an arrow applying Burn/Frost by trigger count; a Challenge bans duplicate backpack items.
records.practical_support: The hidden-Boss guide requires answers across physical/magic/status immunity, and one successful Adventurer settlement contains physical, magic, Poison, crit, Frost, healing and Armor rather than one damage axis.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No player source provides a complete Ranger layout using all named recipes; this is an authored module and counter-validation, not a claimed current optimal build.
records.mechanism: A class-specific craft tree packages cadence and multiple statuses, while no-duplicate and multi-immunity exams force horizontal coverage.
records.engine: Ranger base arrows/bows combined through explicit recipes
records.state_resource: Components, craft branch, projectile count/decay, Heal Block, Poison, Burn and Frost
records.trigger: Craft components or activate resulting projectile/arrow
records.scope: Ranger item pool and enemy targets
records.payoff: Repeated projectiles and layered status/control coverage
records.survival: Not supplied by the weapon module; separate Armor/heal space remains required
records.spatial_condition: Resulting active points need perimeter access; craft consolidation can free cells for readers/defense
records.payoff_owner: Crafted bow/arrow owns projectile/status; components cease to be separate owners after craft
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Choose a craft branch based on available components and previewed enemy immunity instead of merging every higher rarity item.
records.counterplay: Physical, magic or status immunity and cleanse each suppress only the relevant branch.
records.failure_explanation: Show component path, resulting damage type/status, decay and enemy resistance.
records.transferability: Equipment trees can offer horizontal counter tools, but upgrades must preview any lost damage type or trigger.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not infer a full Ranger meta build or copy ten projectiles as a balance target.
records.project_question: Which equipment branches add missing anti-heal, control or damage type without replacing the carry's entire engine?

records.version_scope: full 2.0.x shop/craft workflow
records.rule_support: Battles feed loot/shop acquisition, Relic Shop guarantees a free refresh after 2.0.2, and 2.0.5 adds a craft tree plus character-specific Training Mode pool preview.
records.practical_support: Players buy/reroll components, combine them into new items and warn that a higher craft can change rather than inherit the parent's buff/debuff function; long runs allow repeated pursuit of a narrow recipe.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Shop tier/rarity odds, reroll price curve and exact component inheritance are not publicly documented.
records.mechanism: Crafting compresses components and changes semantics, so the decision is a pivot rather than an automatic vertical upgrade.
records.engine: Post-battle loot, shop/reroll, event supply and recipe tree
records.state_resource: Gold, components, bag cells, current effects, character pool and remaining floors
records.trigger: Buy/drop required components and claim craft output
records.scope: One item chain and surrounding backpack
records.payoff: Stronger or more specialized effect plus possible space compression
records.survival: A craft may remove a defensive/buff function, so pre-merge survival must be re-evaluated
records.spatial_condition: New item shape, stars and trigger points can invalidate the old layout
records.payoff_owner: Parents own pre-craft effects; output becomes the new owner; craft tree owns preview
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Hold/merge/sell based on current role and enemy exam, not rarity alone; rerolling for one recipe spends both gold and floor opportunities.
records.counterplay: Preview lost tags/targets/types and keep bridge items or an undo/lock before irreversible craft.
records.failure_explanation: Show recipe, consumed owners, changed semantics/shape and missing future component.
records.transferability: Equipment upgrades must expose semantic and spatial diffs before commitment.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not assume crafted items inherit all affixes or that more rarity is always stronger for the current build.
records.project_question: How will the item UI compare old and crafted trigger, owner, shape, damage type and team role?

records.version_scope: 2.0.3 phase split through 2.3.x player diagnosis
records.rule_support: 2.0.3 introduces separate always/default and non-combat relic pages; 2.0.5 adds Battle/Non-Combat tags, and 2.0.4 fixes gold-spend effects based on relic-bar placement.
records.practical_support: A player reports Gold Dart not responding to spend-gold relics; the developer identifies that a combat trigger must be placed in the combat relic slot, after which the player accepts the diagnosis.
records.disagreement_or_limit: One example does not establish every relic's phase or whether invalid placements are currently blocked/warned.
records.mechanism: The same relic/economy event behaves differently by phase-specific slot, making location part of effect ownership.
records.engine: Combat and non-combat relic bars plus phase filter
records.state_resource: Relic tag, bar, combat phase, gold-spend event and active/inactive state
records.trigger: Spend gold during combat or outside combat
records.scope: Placed relic and its legal phase
records.payoff: Correctly timed rule modifier without leaking across phases
records.survival: Defensive relics must remain active only in their declared phase
records.spatial_condition: Relic bar placement, not backpack adjacency, is the relevant location
records.payoff_owner: Relic owns effect; bar/phase owns eligibility; gold event owns source
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Moving a relic between bars changes build behavior without selling it, so previews must update before battle.
records.counterplay: Warn or reject a placement that can never receive its required event.
records.failure_explanation: Display inactive reason: wrong phase/bar, missing event, cooldown or target.
records.transferability: Global relics need explicit phase, owner and lifetime, especially when they read economy during combat.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not allow legally slotted but permanently inert relics without visible diagnosis.
records.project_question: Which relic effects operate in preparation, combat or both, and how does the UI prevent wrong-phase placement?

records.version_scope: full 2.0.x–2.2.5 hidden route and player counters
records.rule_support: Collect four Runes before floor 30, defeat the floor-30 Boss for Dungeon Core, then use Ancient Ruins to fight three sequential forms immune to physical, magic and status respectively.
records.practical_support: A Thorns/interrupt player reaches the exam without a viable alternative and dies after long fatigue, while an Adventurer clear reports meaningful physical, magic, Poison, crit, healing, Frost and Armor contributions.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Players disagree whether a unique final three-axis exam is fair; exact current preview, boss numbers and the clear's item layout are unavailable.
records.mechanism: A multi-phase boss tests distinct payoff axes and sustain, but complete immunity turns a specialized owner off unless the route teaches and supplies a bridge.
records.engine: Rune/Core route plus three ordered immunity phases
records.state_resource: Physical/magic/status output, Armor/healing, phase Health and fatigue loops
records.trigger: Summon Ancient Watcher and transition forms
records.scope: Whole backpack across three forms
records.payoff: A mixed build transfers damage ownership between axes and survives all forms
records.survival: Armor/healing must cover long phases where one payoff owner is inactive
records.spatial_condition: Item seal/trigger denial can temporarily disable parts of the bag; layout alone cannot bypass immunity
records.payoff_owner: Each damage source owns one axis; Boss form owns immunity; route owns advance requirement
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Four-Runes route should telegraph the required axes early and offer a final shop/event to add a secondary owner.
records.counterplay: Use resistance/phase mechanics and visible alternatives rather than surprise deletion of the only built axis.
records.failure_explanation: Show phase immunity, suppressed sources, surviving alternate owner and missing preview/opportunity.
records.transferability: Final enemies may combine earlier tests only after each counter has been taught and remains acquirable.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy three complete immunities or require every project build to cover every damage type.
records.project_question: How can a final boss test shield, element and physical owners without making focused archetypes invalid by definition?

records.version_scope: full 2.2.x Endless around floor 147
records.rule_support: The released game advertises mechanic-driven enemies and increasing difficulties, while practical reports distinguish timed enemy actions from player loop cadence.
records.practical_support: A 66-hour player reports billion-HP main enemies with unscaled small summons and random combinations of cleanse, regeneration and multi-hit that can hard-counter without enough preview; other reviews report enemy-answer compression.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No seed, full enemy data, trait weight or performance statistics prove prevalence; summon scaling may have changed after 2.2.x.
records.mechanism: Random enemy capability stacks can turn a reposition/counter decision into hidden luck when scaling and preview are inconsistent.
records.engine: Enemy base scaling, summon scaling and random skill/passive package
records.state_resource: Enemy HP, summon HP, cleanse, regeneration, hit count, player cadence and preview
records.trigger: Generate/enter an Endless encounter
records.scope: Enemy group and player backpack response
records.payoff: A readable enemy exam that rewards a counter adjustment
records.survival: Player defense must answer multi-hit/regeneration without relying on hidden future traits
records.spatial_condition: Preview determines whether reorganizing trigger order/owner is meaningful before auto-combat
records.payoff_owner: Enemy base owns stats; trait owns capability; summon owns separate scaling; encounter owns combination
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Provide a shop/rearrangement window with known enemy package and retain low-tier utility tools.
records.counterplay: Cap incompatible trait combinations, align summon scaling and expose cleanse/immunity/heal before commitment.
records.failure_explanation: Separate raw HP, summon mismatch, random trait combination and unavailable counter.
records.transferability: Enemy modifiers need authored compatibility rules and pre-battle visibility, not unrestricted random stacking.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not infer exact floor-147 values or claim all enemies feel identical from anecdotes.
records.project_question: Which elite modifiers may combine, and what preview/reward makes a hard package a tactical exam instead of a surprise?

records.version_scope: full 2.0.2 pre-change experience to 2.0.4 rule
records.rule_support: 2.0.4 changes Life Erosion from losing one max HP whenever any item triggers to losing one whenever the trigger ball completes a loop.
records.practical_support: A floor-99 player reports old Life Erosion offered alongside magic immunity and enemy-max-HP death retaliation, leaving all three nearly fatal to the current build; frequency reviews explain why per-item punishment scales with bag density.
records.disagreement_or_limit: One three-choice outcome does not establish pool-wide dead-choice frequency, and 2.0.4 only repairs one calamity.
records.mechanism: A global penalty should read a build-neutral cadence unit such as loop count rather than multiply by every item's trigger density.
records.engine: Endless Calamity choice and Life Erosion counter
records.state_resource: Max HP, item trigger count, loop count, damage axes and chosen calamities
records.trigger: Item activates before 2.0.4; ball completes loop after 2.0.4
records.scope: Player max Health across Endless
records.payoff: Preserve Calamity pressure without uniquely deleting high-frequency builds
records.survival: Max-Health loss remains serious but is paced by shared loop cadence
records.spatial_condition: Larger perimeter slows loops, making geometry interact transparently with the normalized penalty
records.payoff_owner: Mode owns calamity; loop owns cadence; individual items no longer each own extra punishment
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Before selection, forecast each option against current damage/survival and permit a veto/reroll when all three invalidate the build.
records.counterplay: Use caps, normalized counters and mutually compatible choice generation.
records.failure_explanation: Preview projected max-HP loss per loop and identify which current axis an alternative disables.
records.transferability: Negative modifiers must normalize against the intended resource unit so fast engines are not penalized quadratically.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy max-HP loss or assume three random curses always contain a fair option.
records.project_question: What unit—cast, second, round or battle—should global hazards read so shield, summon and rapid-fire builds face comparable pressure?

records.version_scope: launch fatigue/long fights through current 2.4.2 surrender
records.rule_support: Combat applies late-loop pressure/fatigue and 2.4.2 moves Surrender appearance from 50 to 20 loops while making it always available in Blood Battle.
records.practical_support: One player reports a 45-minute floor-150 fight; the developer warns 10x can alter trigger calculation and recommends build adjustment/surrender, while a modded floor-1001 stalemate prompted a developer-accepted request for reliable surrender.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Extreme floor/time reports are individual and one run was modded; they support an exit invariant, not authored balance or average performance.
records.mechanism: Rules escalate late-loop pressure while UI guarantees a deterministic exit; simulation speed cannot substitute for termination.
records.engine: Loop counter, fatigue pressure and Surrender state
records.state_resource: Loops, elapsed time, enemy/player healing/damage, trigger calculation and run save
records.trigger: Combat exceeds threshold or enters Blood Battle
records.scope: Current battle/run
records.payoff: End an unwinnable or non-terminating combat without corrupting progress
records.survival: Fatigue prevents indefinite pure sustain, but cannot be the only recovery from a deadlocked modded state
records.spatial_condition: Oversized slow-perimeter builds reach fewer productive triggers before pressure grows
records.payoff_owner: Combat controller owns fatigue/termination; player owns surrender intent; simulation owns speed
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A surrender should clearly state run consequence and enable a new build attempt rather than forcing process termination.
records.counterplay: Use bounded healing/control, escalating pressure and always-reachable exit in every custom mode.
records.failure_explanation: Show loop/time threshold, why damage cannot progress and exact surrender outcome.
records.transferability: Every battle needs both a systemic anti-loop rule and an unconditional user exit.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not infer that 10x is safe or import 20 loops as the project's timeout.
records.project_question: When does the project declare stalemate, accelerate resolution or allow retreat without losing unrelated run state?

records.version_scope: full 2.0.x–2.4.x progression/endless
records.rule_support: The developer confirms Ascension is unlocked sequentially and current Endless grants no additional reward; achievements/hidden route focus on the first 30 floors and selected Endless milestones.
records.practical_support: Players describe ordinary builds completing around floor 20–25, then the more demanding Endless adding calamities, scaling and required pieces without equivalent progression purpose.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Reward preference is subjective and achievement hunters do have goals; no retention data shows the mismatch causes churn.
records.mechanism: The mode with the most build adaptation can become optional dead time when meta rewards end where the build merely finishes.
records.engine: Thirty-floor clear, sequential Ascension and optional Endless
records.state_resource: Progression points, unlocks, floor, completed recipe and calamity stack
records.trigger: Clear floor 30, continue Endless or finish an Ascension tier
records.scope: Run/meta progression
records.payoff: Align ongoing decisions with an explicit objective/reward rather than pure number extension
records.survival: Endless survival has meaning only if the mode declares its score/challenge purpose
records.spatial_condition: Completed bag layout may stop changing even while numerical floors continue
records.payoff_owner: Base mode owns unlock reward; Endless owns challenge; mod debug is outside authored progression
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Add late horizontal upgrades/counters or end the run once meaningful pivot space is exhausted.
records.counterplay: Use score, optional milestones or finite ending without making meta power mandatory for all players.
records.failure_explanation: Show what floor rewards, what Endless changes and whether further progress is cosmetic, score or unlock.
records.transferability: Run length should match the horizon over which the player still makes build decisions.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not require infinite mode rewards or copy sequential Ascension grind.
records.project_question: At which tower floor is the first build complete, and what distinct decisions justify every remaining floor?

records.version_scope: full 2.0.x–2.3.x shop/endless practice
records.rule_support: Shop/relic supply supports rerolls and 2.0.2 guarantees one free Relic Shop refresh, but no public probability table explains late pools.
records.practical_support: One long review says many rerolls let players force a few overpowered recipes, another reports spending 1.8 million gold without one target relic and receives developer confirmation that specific Endless relic odds are very low; deep players report some pieces becoming near-required.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No odds, mode-stratified item statistics or complete build sheets prove exact dominance; 1.8 million and 'top 5%' are anecdotes/rhetoric, not distribution estimates.
records.mechanism: A broad random pool can simultaneously allow routine forcing of common strong lines and make one rare required connector practically unreachable.
records.engine: Shop tier/pool, reroll, free relic refresh and recipe dependencies
records.state_resource: Gold, reroll count, rarity, character pool, target relic and remaining floors
records.trigger: Search repeatedly for a build-defining item/relic
records.scope: Run supply and final build
records.payoff: Reach a coherent line without deterministic sameness or impossible connector hunting
records.survival: Missing a defensive/cleanse connector can make late enemy packages unwinnable
records.spatial_condition: Even acquired items must fit/route; supply availability precedes spatial optimization
records.payoff_owner: Shop owns offer distribution; recipe/relic owns build connection; player owns spend decision
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Publish pools/pity and provide substitute connectors; define a latest-safe stop instead of infinite reroll.
records.counterplay: Use function-level redundancy, targeted rewards and rarity floors that retain basic utility.
records.failure_explanation: Distinguish bad pool odds, exhausted currency, unavailable tier/class and over-forced preference.
records.transferability: A rich item system needs several accessible converters for each required function, not one rare keystone.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not infer an exact probability or balance tier from isolated reviews.
records.project_question: How many interchangeable shield/element/payoff connectors must the first-version reward pool contain to keep pivots real?

records.version_scope: Demo 1.5.5 through full 2.0.9 UX chain
records.rule_support: Updates add run output/status overview, draggable-benefit marking, trigger-ball tutorial, craft tree, battle-log search and perimeter display.
records.practical_support: Players describe simultaneously arranging movable bag cells and item cells over a large late grid, and needing to reason about route length, trigger points, adjacency and combo owners.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Feature additions reveal information needs but do not prove usability is solved; no user test or accessibility study is public.
records.mechanism: Different views answer distinct questions: legal link, affected owner, future craft, loop cost and realized event chain.
records.engine: Drag overlay, tutorial, craft tree, perimeter display, data overview and searchable log
records.state_resource: Item shape/point/star/tag, bag perimeter, recipe, source/target and output totals
records.trigger: Drag, inspect, craft, start battle or review result
records.scope: Preparation and post-battle analysis
records.payoff: Player can predict and verify a complex spatial build without memorizing hidden relations
records.survival: Armor/heal recipients and trigger frequency remain visible before lethal tests
records.spatial_condition: Overlay must distinguish outer active points, inner passive readers, disconnected cells and new craft shape
records.payoff_owner: UI reflects authoritative item/event data; it does not own mechanics
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Preview how a purchase/craft changes perimeter, links and outputs before spending.
records.counterplay: Enemy immunity/traits need the same inspectability as player links.
records.failure_explanation: Show inactive point, wrong tag/phase, missing recipe, added perimeter and source chain.
records.transferability: A build UI needs prediction, attribution and history views; one tooltip cannot carry all three.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not hide precise behavior behind color-only arrows or require reading a full combat log for basic legality.
records.project_question: What preparation overlays and battle-report drill-down let players validate shield/element/reader ownership at a glance?

records.version_scope: full 2.0.2–2.0.3 damage/report fixes
records.rule_support: Patches fix Poison omission from Total Damage, Shadowkill triggers missing from logs, player-hit source text, and Burn not being blocked by Armor/physical immunity even though Burn is physical damage.
records.practical_support: A hidden-Boss clear breaks settlement into physical, magic, Poison, crit, healing, Frost and Armor, while the three-phase guide makes correct damage category decisive.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The current full damage pipeline and whether status damage can crit are not published; settlement totals do not expose the complete item layout.
records.mechanism: Damage simulation and report must share one authoritative type/source so immunity, Armor and totals cannot disagree.
records.engine: Typed damage event, mitigation/immunity resolver and report aggregation
records.state_resource: Source item, physical/magic/Poison/Burn type, crit, Armor, immunity and final damage
records.trigger: Item/status deals damage or combat settles
records.scope: One event, target and aggregate run report

records.version_scope: Demo 0.2.x through 0.3.4 practice
records.rule_support: A 3x3 slot summons the matching unit from horizontal, vertical or diagonal three-symbol lines; one nudge per wave can move a near result, while repeated spins in the wave become more expensive and kills replenish spin gold.
records.practical_support: Players use nudge and slot-adjustment Cores as limited corrections but still report waves where no useful unit appears.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact reel weights, multi-line order, jackpot, nudge direction and pity are unpublished; one review's wording cannot establish every edge case.
records.mechanism: Recruitment is a spatial result-line problem with one low-frequency correction and an escalating per-wave retry cost.
records.engine: 3x3 reels, paylines, spin action, one nudge and kill income
records.state_resource: Visible symbols, remaining nudge, current spin price, gold, wave and desired unit

records.survival: Missing several lines reduces bodies and upgrades before the next enemy wave

records.counterplay: Enemy tempo and limited gold shorten retries; nudge only rescues some near-lines.
records.failure_explanation: Show reel result, valid paylines, nudge delta, spin cost, payout and summoned unit.

records.version_scope: Demo 0.2.0 through 0.3.4 player reports
records.rule_support: Runs allow repeated spins, limited nudge/Core correction, two losses and permanent upgrades that improve hearts, army size, rerolls and rarity access.
records.practical_support: Multiple players report early waves with no units and repeated restarts or grinding easy mode, while a post-overhaul player says economy/Core planning usually salvages bad starts.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Sentiment and frequency conflict; no seed-level failure rate or before/after statistics establish how often control succeeds.
records.mechanism: Persistent power and run corrections can insure variance, but they should not be prerequisites for a viable opening.
records.engine: Spin distribution, nudge/Core correction, final-roll fallback, two-life rule and meta upgrades
records.state_resource: Early units, retries, lives, meta unlocks, wave strength and restart time
records.trigger: Several early spins miss or first battle is lost
records.scope: Opening stabilization and between-run progression
records.payoff: Recover a weak start through visible insurance rather than mandatory repetition
records.survival: Extra hearts/units reduce elimination risk but do not supply a coherent role package
records.spatial_condition: Missing recruitment lines leaves roster/formation empty regardless of battlefield skill
records.payoff_owner: Slot owns variance; correction tool owns mitigation; meta tree owns long-horizon insurance
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Offer bounded pity/direct supply before the first lethal exam; let players abandon a failed line without lengthy dead play.
records.counterplay: Escalating wave and advancing after loss can remove the adaptation window before corrective resources arrive.
records.failure_explanation: Show roll history, available corrections, pity progress, army deficit and enemy escalation.
records.transferability: Use meta progression to widen future choices, not to make baseline recruitment statistically playable.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not infer that RNG is solved or broken for all players from reviews.
records.project_question: What opening guarantee preserves random team discovery while preventing two empty reward cycles from deciding the run?

records.version_scope: Demo launch to official 0.2.0
records.rule_support: Official 0.2.0 removes the wave preparation timer so spinning, reading traits, organizing units and planning are untimed.
records.practical_support: Launch-period players say the timer expired while inspecting random passives/units and added stress to a single-player planning phase.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The patch does not publish telemetry or prove every player disliked time pressure.
records.mechanism: A PvE preparation phase needs time proportional to the number of random traits, absorption and formation decisions it asks players to inspect.
records.engine: Wave-preparation timer and manual Start Battle action
records.state_resource: Remaining time, unread offers/traits, spins and pending organization
records.trigger: Enter preparation between waves
records.scope: Pre-combat planning UI
records.payoff: Let players finish meaningful decisions before deterministic combat starts
records.survival: Enough planning time prevents accidental empty/unorganized formations
records.spatial_condition: Dragging/positioning and reading 3x3 outcomes occur without forced timeout
records.payoff_owner: Player owns start timing; game owns optional pacing aids
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Remove mandatory countdown but preserve fast-confirm controls for experienced players.
records.counterplay: None; this is accessibility/agency rather than enemy power.
records.failure_explanation: If auto-start exists, show explicit cause and pending decisions rather than silently beginning.
records.transferability: Single-player autobattler preparation should be untimed unless time pressure is an explicit mode rule.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not infer combat should be pausable or remove all tempo from run structure.
records.project_question: Which tactical-command and equipment decisions require unlimited preparation, and which modes may deliberately constrain it?

records.version_scope: Demo 0.2.0 plan through 0.3.1 post-overhaul repair
records.rule_support: Random trait options receive a major 0.2.5 overhaul; Core activation is fixed in 0.2.7, the system is almost entirely rebuilt/replaced in 0.3.0, then activation is repaired again in 0.3.1.
records.practical_support: Pre-overhaul players describe Core odds changes as too weak or hard to feel, whereas 0.3.0-period players report impactful active/passive modifiers and discard flexibility.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No old-to-new mapping, adoption or power statistics isolate which changes caused improved perception.
records.mechanism: A run modifier must visibly change decisions and activation, not merely add small invisible odds to an already random supply loop.
records.engine: Trait offer generator and active/passive Core system
records.state_resource: Core pool, activation phase, effect strength, discard slot, trait option and player perception
records.trigger: Core/trait offer, activation or overhaul migration
records.scope: Whole run rule layer and inherited unit traits
records.payoff: Distinct build directions and legible control over slot/army behavior
records.survival: Defensive/odds Cores can stabilize a run only if activation and magnitude are visible
records.spatial_condition: Some effects change payline odds or unit behavior but do not merge slot and battlefield geometry
records.payoff_owner: Core owns run rule; trait owns unit effect; UI owns preview; patch owns migration
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Replace/discard a Core when its direction no longer matches roster instead of stacking every modifier.
records.counterplay: Pool dilution and hidden activation make offers feel inert; explicit before/after odds and proc reports restore trust.
records.failure_explanation: Show Core phase, trigger, affected symbols/units, rejected activation and measured effect.
records.transferability: Relics/augments should create qualitatively different routes and report their actual owner/trigger.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not import unnamed Core effects or claim the overhaul solved all balance issues.
records.project_question: Which first-version relics genuinely alter build grammar rather than add another small stat percentage?

records.version_scope: Demo 0.2.7 Core capacity through 0.3.4 roster reports
records.rule_support: Holding more than eight Cores once froze selection, absorb interactions could consume units, and 0.3.0 added explicit unit locks; a current community report describes a unit trait that does not count toward an eight-unit display cap.
records.practical_support: Players report drag/absorb ambiguity and roster counts appearing inconsistent when an exception trait is active.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The population exception lacks developer confirmation/name, and Core capacity is not the same system as army population; they remain separate safety cases.
records.mechanism: Every capacity-limited collection needs overflow rules, visible exceptions and irreversible-action protection.
records.engine: Core selection list, army population counter, absorb mode and unit lock
records.state_resource: Core count, population cap/exception, selected material, locked flag and overflow state
records.trigger: Receive Core beyond capacity, exceed population or drag/absorb unit
records.scope: Core inventory and army roster
records.payoff: Resolve overflow and sacrifice deliberately without softlock or accidental loss
records.survival: Protecting a critical tank/healer from absorption preserves the build
records.spatial_condition: Roster display must distinguish occupied and exempt slots; battlefield position cannot imply sacrifice selection
records.payoff_owner: Collection owns capacity; trait owns exception; player owns sacrifice; lock owns protection
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: When full, compare replacement/absorption/discard before accepting another owner.
records.counterplay: Not enemy counterplay; UI ambiguity is the failure pressure.
records.failure_explanation: Show count formula, exempt unit/Core, overflow choice and blocked sacrifice reason.
records.transferability: Bench, relic and active-roster capacity require explicit overflow transactions and locks.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not infer the unconfirmed trait's name/rule or merge Core and unit caps.
records.project_question: How will active roster, reserve and relic capacity show exemptions and prevent accidental consumption of build-critical owners?

records.version_scope: Demo 0.2.5–0.3.3 stability chain
records.rule_support: Official updates repair missing save creation, black screen, crash/blue-screen reports, memory leak, frame drop, freeze and audio/background issues, while 0.3.0 adds mid-run save.
records.practical_support: Long Demo runs include repeated waves, promotion and meta decisions whose loss makes performance failure a run-integrity failure rather than cosmetic inconvenience.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Patch notes group symptoms without a public root-cause analysis, hardware matrix or persistence schema.
records.mechanism: Long-run games need resumable snapshots and bounded resource/event state before content complexity grows.
records.engine: Mid-run save, device/runtime lifecycle and performance monitoring
records.state_resource: Run wave, roster, traits, Cores, items, currencies, RNG state, save and active device
records.trigger: Save/continue, background/audio change, prolonged play or device-specific failure
records.scope: Entire run and host process
records.payoff: Resume the same legal build without data loss or system-level instability
records.survival: Not a combat statistic; preserving the run protects accumulated player decisions
records.spatial_condition: Roster positions and selection/lock state must survive restore exactly
records.payoff_owner: Run snapshot owns state; content definitions own versions; platform layer owns resource cleanup
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Persist offers, spin/reroll prices and committed absorption atomically so reload cannot reroll outcomes.
records.counterplay: Use versioned snapshots, deterministic RNG, leak tests and safe recovery rather than disabling saves.
records.failure_explanation: Report save version, last committed wave/action, recovery state and performance fault context.
records.transferability: Tower runs need mid-run persistence and performance budgets as architecture contracts, not late QoL.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not infer the exact technical cause of blue-screen/freezes or copy Demo save behavior.
records.project_question: Which preparation and battle transitions are atomic save points, and how is deterministic offer/combat state restored?

records.version_scope: Demo 0.3.2 result fix to 0.3.4 real-time display
records.rule_support: 0.3.2 fixes damage not appearing on the result screen; 0.3.4 updates damage values in real time during battle to improve combat readability.
records.practical_support: Players compare Deadeye, Mage, Cavalry and inherited traits as payoff owners, making source-level contribution necessary for evaluating absorption and formation decisions.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Official notes do not state whether values include summon, Core, trait, mitigation, overkill or parent-source attribution.
records.mechanism: Live feedback and settlement must derive from the same event lineage so a player can validate a chosen owner.
records.engine: Resolved damage events, live value display and result aggregation
records.state_resource: Unit, inherited trait, Core/item proc, target, raw/final damage, mitigation and time
records.trigger: Attack/skill/trait deals damage or wave settles
records.scope: One event, owner and aggregate battle result
records.payoff: Explain which promoted/infused owner actually converted the build into damage
records.survival: Damage view should pair with incoming damage/healing/control to explain why a carry stayed active
records.spatial_condition: Target/path position remains part of why an owner had or lacked uptime
records.payoff_owner: Unit or generated summon owns damage; source trait/Core/item keeps parent attribution; report only aggregates
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Use contribution evidence to stop feeding an ineffective carry or replace a dead item/Core.
records.counterplay: Show target reason, blocked/mitigated amount and control downtime, not only rising headline damage.
records.failure_explanation: Trace source→parent trait/Core→target→mitigation→final amount in live and result views.
records.transferability: Battle reports should support build debugging and sacrifice decisions, not merely display total damage.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not claim 0.3.4 already exposes full lineage or recompute totals separately from simulation.
records.project_question: How will inherited effects, summons and team-stat converters remain attributable to both source and final damage owner?

records.version_scope: Demo 0.3.2–0.3.4 current practice
records.rule_support: Shop, unit rarity, class items and absorption are separate acquisition/commitment layers whose offers do not automatically match the current roster.
records.practical_support: A 0.3.4 player reports common +5% Attack/HP items are cheap/easy to max, a no-shop run felt similar, Mage/Champion are too rare to justify tailored items, and rare units are usually not worth consuming until round 20+; others report irrelevant class offers.
records.disagreement_or_limit: These are individual observations without item/unit odds, run seeds or statistics; no universal balance ranking is claimed.
records.mechanism: A specialized reward is dead when its target rarity/class and the safe sacrifice window do not overlap in the run horizon.
records.engine: Random shop, class item pool, unit rarity unlock and irreversible absorption
records.state_resource: Shop currency, item rarity/stacks, current classes, rare unit, passive value and remaining rounds
records.trigger: Roll item/rare unit or consider absorbing it
records.scope: Current roster and late-run build
records.payoff: Provide relevant upgrades and meaningful high-rarity inheritance before the build is already finished
records.survival: Cheap broad Health items may outperform inaccessible specialized survival
records.spatial_condition: Population pressure creates desire to absorb, but formation may still need the rare body
records.payoff_owner: Item owns stat/effect; eligible unit owns benefit; rare unit owns body/trait alternative; shop owns availability
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Buy broad bridge items early; consume rare bodies only when roster roles are covered and enough time remains to exploit the trait.
records.counterplay: Targeted shop filters, function substitutes, sell/lock and rarity-aware pity reduce timing dead zones.
records.failure_explanation: Show why offer lacks owner, expected remaining access window and body-versus-trait comparison.
records.transferability: Reward pools need temporal compatibility among target, converter and remaining encounters, not just theoretical synergy.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not infer exact item tiers or that the shop is objectively useless.
records.project_question: How will first-version equipment offers guarantee that a shield/element converter appears while a compatible owner can still pivot?

records.version_scope: Demo 0.3.4 developer-confirmed open bug
records.rule_support: The developer confirms golden-symbol +1 rarity cannot output a rarity not yet unlocked by meta progression and acknowledges a bug where a nudge-created golden win failed to apply the bonus.
records.practical_support: A player reproduces normal golden wins and a nudge-assisted win yielding only a basic unit, then tests the absence of rare output against current unlock state.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The promised fix has no later patch on the access date, and exact rarity probabilities remain unknown.
records.mechanism: A transformed payline event must preserve its parent modifiers while respecting a separately owned unlock ceiling.
records.engine: Golden-symbol Core/relic, nudge-generated win, rarity bonus and meta unlock gate
records.state_resource: Winning line, nudge flag, +1 rarity modifier, unlocked maximum rarity and spawned unit
records.trigger: Nudge completes a golden-symbol payline
records.scope: One recruitment event
records.payoff: Apply the run modifier exactly once without bypassing account progression
records.survival: Higher-quality recruit may stabilize the next wave; no direct defensive rule
records.spatial_condition: Payline geometry creates the event; rarity cap resolves after line/modifier ownership
records.payoff_owner: Golden effect owns +1 modifier; nudge owns line transformation; meta tree owns rarity ceiling; spawned unit owns result
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Do not invest in golden-line control expecting locked rarity; unlock ceiling or choose a modifier with immediate value.
records.counterplay: Not enemy counterplay; deterministic event tracing and cap preview prevent false expectations.
records.failure_explanation: Log base line result, nudge parent, rarity modifier, cap clamp and final spawn.
records.transferability: Offer transformations, relic bonuses and meta unlocks need an explicit deterministic resolution order.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not assume the bug is fixed or infer odds beyond the confirmed cap.
records.project_question: In what order do rerolls, guaranteed upgrades, rarity caps and pity resolve, and how is each clamp shown to the player?

records.version_scope: 2026-08-18 public Playtest through 2026-09-03 live release; official v1.0.13 versus MPIGDB v1.0.15 dataset remains separate
records.rule_support: The public Playtest ended with a reset, the full free game launched on 27 August with three difficulties, official notes name v1.0.13, and the developer calls the game server-based; MPIGDB separately labels a checked campaign dataset v1.0.15.
records.practical_support: Guides and reviews all concern the first live week and should not be mixed with the reset Playtest or unreleased Hell/Inferno data.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No official node maps v1.0.15 to a dated patch, so the maintained dataset is not silently promoted to the official live version.
records.mechanism: A live service research record must separate public build, client-data snapshot and server-authoritative behavior.
records.engine: Steam release/update channel, server validation and maintained client-table extraction
records.state_resource: Account progress, client version, server state, released difficulty and dataset revision
records.trigger: Launch, update, reconnect or compare a rule claim
records.scope: Whole account and research version map
records.payoff: Keep build and balance claims tied to the period that actually exposed them
records.survival: No direct combat effect; version separation prevents false defensive formulas
records.spatial_condition: No formation claim can be inherited from screenshots or another version
records.payoff_owner: Official channel owns release labels; server owns accepted state; maintained wiki owns only its extracted snapshot
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Recheck official notes before spending on a route whose values came from a later dataset.
records.counterplay: When versions cannot be mapped, downgrade strength and preserve both labels.
records.failure_explanation: Show client version, server rejection and source snapshot independently.
records.transferability: Version every balance-sensitive build and keep server state distinct from visible client animation.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not infer that v1.0.15 was publicly patched on a specific date or that Playtest progress persisted.
records.project_question: Which content-version and save-schema labels must appear in combat reports so a build result remains reproducible after balance changes?

records.version_scope: early live release through 2026-09-03
records.rule_support: The party has one fixed slot for each of Knight, Warrior, Assassin, Archer and Mage; unlock costs are 1,500, 7,000, 20,000 and 50,000 Coin after the starting Knight.
records.practical_support: Three independent guides prioritize new classes and active-skill slots before most small stat nodes because a new body and action change early combat discretely.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The guides differ on exactly how straight to path toward an unlock and do not prove every nearby stat node is weak.
records.mechanism: A fixed party can still create recruitment pressure when each new role and skill slot competes with permanent stat spending.
records.engine: Rally Orb unlock nodes and active-skill-slot nodes
records.state_resource: Coin, unlocked classes, active slots, nearby path cost and current stage stability
records.trigger: Earn Coin and choose the next Orb Circuit node
records.scope: Account progression and five-class party
records.payoff: Add a new role or action rather than only increasing an existing number
records.survival: Knight recovery plus additional bodies reduce early collapse
records.spatial_condition: One class slot per hero; no bench or replacement formation was found
records.payoff_owner: Unlock node owns access; class owns its skills; player owns Coin allocation
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Warrior then Assassin form the early bridge; Archer/Mage wait until their larger path cost is affordable.
records.counterplay: Overcommitting to unlock paths can delay immediate survival, while scattering Coin into tiny nodes can delay role completion.
records.failure_explanation: Preview total path cost, new role/skill slots and the current combat deficit each route solves.
records.transferability: Horizontal role access and vertical stat growth should have visible, comparable opportunity costs.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not import a shop, reroll, bench or trait breakpoint that this fixed-party game does not expose.
records.project_question: How will the first tower run compare recruiting a new hero with deepening one existing hero without making either always correct?

records.version_scope: MPIGDB accessed 2026-09-03; duration behavior corrected 2026-08-31
records.rule_support: Knight owns party Recovery and an HP-scaled party Shield; Warrior owns party Attack and Reflect buffs; Assassin owns party Attack/Movement Speed plus attacks and Stun; Archer owns Drained, Ice Dragon and Poison; Mage owns elemental attacks and Ice Lake defense reduction/root.
records.practical_support: A long review criticizes role/passive allocation because the sole party heal and shield sit on Knight while damage and support ownership are distributed across fixed classes.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The review's class rankings are subjective; the owner map and durations come from database and official fixes.
records.mechanism: Team defense, team buffs, control and final damage remain separate owned actions even when all five heroes are mandatory.
records.engine: Per-class active loadouts and timed buffs/debuffs
records.state_resource: Four equipped slots per class, cooldown, duration, HP reader, target and element
records.trigger: A class skill comes off cooldown and resolves on its target set
records.scope: Party and enemy group
records.payoff: Compose sustain, amplification, control and damage without erasing attribution
records.survival: Knight Recovery/Shield, Warrior Reflect and Archer Drained buy uptime
records.spatial_condition: Each skill has its own range, target and maximum-target count
records.payoff_owner: Casting class owns the skill; affected ally owns resulting attack events; report retains the buff source
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Unlock and level the owner whose missing function currently blocks progress.
records.counterplay: Buff expiry, range failure, burst damage and resistance can break different parts of the chain.
records.failure_explanation: Show cast, target set, applied duration, expiry, source and downstream damage contribution.
records.transferability: A team-wide modifier should never overwrite the identity of the final damage or shield owner.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not call every cold skill a shield or every defensive class a damage converter.
records.project_question: Which hero, equipment or relic owns each party-wide stat change and how will downstream combat events retain that lineage?

records.version_scope: guide updated 2026-09-02 with accessed client-table values
records.rule_support: Archer Summon Ice Dragon and Mage Frozen Anger are Cold multi-target skills; Mage Ice Lake reduces Defense and prevents movement, while range/area/element stats exist on passives and socket-context gear.
records.practical_support: DS-CAN reports strong damage after filling gear and maxing Ice Dragon plus Elemental Damage/Skill Range on Archer, and Frozen Anger plus Elemental Damage/Skill Range/Skill Area on Mage.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No current DPS, enemy resistance table or manual-position rule establishes universal strength.
records.mechanism: Two fixed ranged owners share an elemental amplifier while keeping separate cooldown, range, area and target budgets.
records.engine: Cold actives plus elemental/range/area passives and compatible gear sockets
records.state_resource: Archer/Mage skill levels, Elemental Damage, Skill Range, Skill Area, cooldown and socket capacity
records.trigger: Ice Dragon, Frozen Anger or Ice Lake resolves in range
records.scope: Up to each skill's target cap or area
records.payoff: Archer and Mage deliver Cold damage; Ice Lake can increase physical/elemental follow-up by reducing Defense
records.survival: Knight Recovery/Shield and Drained create time for long-cooldown ranged skills
records.spatial_condition: Range, area, target cap and movement restriction are the verified spatial controls; manual formation is unresolved
records.payoff_owner: Each caster owns its damage; support classes own buffs; gear/gem owns the stat modifier
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Unlock all classes and fill basic gear first; pivot away if the stage resists Cold or the backline cannot cast consistently.
records.counterplay: Cold resistance, burst on the frontline, range failure and long cooldowns attack different dependencies.
records.failure_explanation: Report damage by skill/owner, targets missed by range, resisted amount and support uptime.
records.transferability: An element route should bind multiple owners through a shared amplifier without collapsing their individual timing and space.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not invent Freeze/Shatter, an Ice Shield or automatic Cold-resistance penetration.
records.project_question: Should an element route require two complementary owners and a support chassis, or can one relic compress all three functions into one carry?

records.version_scope: first live week, including a post-duration-fix Nightmare 1-9 video description
records.rule_support: Assassin owns both Dodge and Life Steal passive slots; each has a client-derived final 9% cap, with currently reachable levels gated by class hero level.
records.practical_support: Guides prioritize Assassin offensive gear and Life Steal; a Nightmare 1-9 video description moves Knight defensive gear to Assassin, while a review reports maxing global/Assassin Dodge and Life Steal as a luck-dependent clear route.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The review is second-hand community observation, no formula proves independence or skill applicability, and no clear rate makes this a guaranteed solution.
records.mechanism: Concentrated damage can become self-sustain when the same owner avoids hits and converts landed damage back into HP.
records.engine: Assassin damage/attack cadence, Dodge passive, Life Steal passive and transferred defensive gear
records.state_resource: Attack, hit frequency, HP, Defense, Dodge, Life Steal, equipment and passive points
records.trigger: Assassin attacks or receives an incoming hit
records.scope: One Assassin carry with party support
records.payoff: The Assassin owns damage, tanking and healing instead of splitting them across fixed roles
records.survival: Dodge prevents some damage; Life Steal and gear recover/absorb the rest
records.spatial_condition: Melee uptime and target access are required; no verified manual formation control exists
records.payoff_owner: Assassin owns damage and self-sustain; Knight still owns any Recovery/Shield cast; gear owns transferred stats
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Unlock Assassin at 7,000 Coin, verify contribution in the meter, then bind scarce gear; pivot to Knight/team resistance or ranged owners if burst prevents attacks.
records.counterplay: Elemental burst, control, miss/target denial and anti-sustain break the loop before Life Steal pays back.
records.failure_explanation: Show avoided hits, incoming element, time without targets, damage dealt and healing actually returned.
records.transferability: A defense-to-output route can be indirect through uptime and self-heal; it need not pretend Defense itself is damage.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not claim all attacks can be dodged, all skill damage lifesteals, or Assassin is the only viable current hero.
records.project_question: What explicit enemy package tests a dodge/lifesteal carry without invalidating every other defense route?

records.version_scope: early live release through 2026-08-31 automation update
records.rule_support: Coin/EXP settle on stage clear, and Automatic Challenge now retreats one stage and turns off after ten consecutive losses.
records.practical_support: Independent guides tell players to disable repeat challenge and farm a stable earlier stage rather than spend time repeatedly failing the frontier.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact best stage depends on clear time, chest weights, difficulty and account bonuses; no universal farming ranking is claimed.
records.mechanism: An idle game needs a clear adaptation window between frontier testing and reliable resource production.
records.engine: Stage selection, repeat/Automatic Challenge, clear settlement and offline progression
records.state_resource: Current stage, loss streak, clear time, Coin/EXP/chests and next upgrade cost
records.trigger: Current frontier stops clearing reliably
records.scope: Campaign progression loop
records.payoff: Convert time into resources on a stable stage, then re-attempt after a meaningful upgrade
records.survival: Avoid repeated wipe states that produce no useful progression
records.spatial_condition: No formation change is required; stage/enemy package is the pivot axis
records.payoff_owner: Stage clear owns settlement; automation owns retry/retreat; player owns stage choice
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Fall back one or more stages, target the missing gear/resource, then challenge again.
records.counterplay: A stable Coin stage may have zero chance for the needed gear grade, so reward category must also be checked.
records.failure_explanation: Show loss streak, last cleared stage, expected rewards and which required drop has zero weight.
records.transferability: Auto-progression should fail into a productive fallback, not an invisible infinite-loss loop.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not assume the immediately previous stage is always optimal or that failed combat grants full rewards.
records.project_question: When a tower floor fails, should fallback be automatic, player-authored, or offered as a forecasted farming choice?

records.version_scope: MPIGDB campaign data accessed 2026-09-03, with v1.0.15 recheck noted on progression page
records.rule_support: A field drop is chest acquisition multiplied by reward-category weight and then subpool weight; early chest rows can assign zero weight to higher grades.
records.practical_support: A Hard 3-5 player reports long farming without usable gear, class-locked drops and material bottlenecks, consistent with multiple independent supply gates rather than one generic drop rate.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Client weights do not prove server rolls or the review's perceived frequency; only the structural zero is retained.
records.mechanism: Time cannot solve an unavailable reward: zero pool weight is a progression gate, not bad luck.
records.engine: Chest acquisition roll, category table, item subpool and grade weight
records.state_resource: Stage, difficulty, chest type, category weight, subpool weight and desired item owner
records.trigger: Enemy/chest clear requests a reward
records.scope: One reward transaction and long-run farming plan
records.payoff: Choose a stage that can actually produce the needed class/grade/slot
records.survival: Appropriate gear can close a tank or carry deficit only if it exists in the current pool
records.spatial_condition: Equipment slot need is independent of battlefield range
records.payoff_owner: Chest owns acquisition; table owns category/grade; gear class/slot owns eligibility
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Move to a stage with nonzero target weight or invest in crafting/synthesis instead of extending impossible farming.
records.counterplay: Pool preview, target filters and pity only help if they explicitly override the zero-weight gate.
records.failure_explanation: Display every factor and call out zero probability before the player idles.
records.transferability: Reward UI must distinguish low chance from impossible acquisition.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not multiply partial numbers into an exact item chance when a subpool or server modifier is unknown.
records.project_question: Which first-version rewards can be temporarily impossible, and how will the tower surface that gate before a run starts?

records.version_scope: accessed MPIGDB gear/gem tables and 2026-08-31 enchant patch
records.rule_support: Each class has twelve gear slots; grade controls option, engraving, enchant and gem capacity, and the same gem maps to different stats in Weapon, Armor and Accessory contexts.
records.practical_support: Elemental damage, resistance, Dodge and Skill Range therefore compete through concrete owner/slot choices rather than one unrestricted upgrade pool.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The loadout planner omits final displayed damage/HP and no optimal socket allocation is published.
records.mechanism: An upgrade component gains meaning from the receiving slot, so offense, defense and spatial reach can be mutually exclusive uses of one drop.
records.engine: Class gear loadout, grade capacity and socket-context stat mapping
records.state_resource: Twelve slots, grade, option slots, engravings, enchants, sockets and eligible class
records.trigger: Equip, socket, engrave or enchant an item
records.scope: One class loadout and account inventory
records.payoff: Create targeted damage/range/resistance/Dodge packages
records.survival: Armor-context resistance or Dodge competes with offensive and utility socket uses
records.spatial_condition: Accessory-context Skill Range can change whether an ability finds targets
records.payoff_owner: Gear owns base/options; gem owns one context-specific effect; wearer owns resulting combat stat
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Preserve flexible gear until the carry/survival owner is known; replace a socket package when the stage changes damage type.

records.version_scope: Nightmare-era live release; Hell/Inferno client rows not publicly selectable on access date

records.version_scope: first live week

records.version_scope: Nightmare in the first live week; comments straddle the 2026-08-31 duration fix

records.version_scope: bugged launch balance through 2026-09-02 acknowledged retune plan

records.version_scope: launch rule through 2026-08-31 risk reduction
records.rule_support: Enchanting can destroy gear; failure destruction was reduced from 100% to 50%, and synthesis wording was clarified so the attempt after ten accumulated failures is guaranteed.
records.practical_support: Players avoid investing in rare bound gear because drop, bind and destruction risks combine, while nine-piece synthesis and facility levels already consume inventory/time.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Player-reported streaks do not establish hidden rates, and the official note does not remove destruction.
records.mechanism: A risky upgrade changes build agency when replacement supply and tradeability are also constrained.
records.engine: Enchant success, destroy roll, synthesis failure counter and bound equipment
records.state_resource: Gear owner/grade, enchant slots, success chance, destroy chance, failure count and replacement supply

records.payoff: Gain a specialized stat/effect or advance grade
records.survival: Losing a tank/carry item can collapse the active build immediately
records.spatial_condition: Destroyed range/resistance gear can invalidate cast or survival positioning indirectly
records.payoff_owner: Gear owns upgrade; Mage Tower/Blacksmith owns transaction; pity counter owns only synthesis guarantee
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Test on replaceable gear, lock core items and compare expected replacement time before committing.
records.counterplay: Protection materials, deterministic thresholds and recoverable downgrade can preserve commitment without total loss.
records.failure_explanation: Display success, destroy chance, protected state, pity count and exact item lost/gained.
records.transferability: Irreversible item systems need visible safeguards proportional to acquisition time and build dependence.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not import marketplace incentives or infer that 50% destroy chance equals 50% total loss per attempt.
records.project_question: Should first-version equipment ever be destroyed, or can commitment pressure come from slot binding and scarce transfer instead?

records.version_scope: 2026-08-31 live update
records.rule_support: Automatic Challenge retreats one stage and disables after ten consecutive losses; it also stops and retreats when Act Boss chest storage fills.
records.practical_support: Before the guard, guides explicitly tell players to turn repeat off and choose a stable stage because repeated failures waste productive farm time.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Sources do not define whether all failure causes share one counter or the exact reward state at interruption.

records.version_scope: Playtest through first live week

records.practical_support: Guides/reviews report visible combat continuing during maintenance or connection loss while Coin/EXP/chests fail to commit, making apparent idle time diverge from accepted progress.

records.version_scope: first live week

records.disagreement_or_limit: No complete server drop table or measured frequency establishes how often each mismatch occurs.

records.version_scope: community reproduction on 2026-08-30 before accessed later updates
records.rule_support: A campaign stage separates field wave, stage boss and clear settlement; official updates also adjust automatic stopping and stage-clear logs.
records.practical_support: A player reports that buying wave reduction and revisiting an easy stage can clear the wave before the boss spawns, leaving progress at 90% with a concrete reproduction path.
records.disagreement_or_limit: There is no developer root-cause or fix confirmation, so this remains a historical community negative case.

records.version_scope: source-backed early live mechanics; project inference remains exploratory
records.rule_support: Knight Shield reads Knight HP and protects all allies; Cold skills, Elemental Damage, specific resistance, party-wide stats and Assassin sustain are owned by different skills, slots and classes.
records.practical_support: One guide pairs Knight sustain with Archer/Mage Cold output, while another clear description moves defense from Knight to Assassin; defense can buy uptime for a different owner or be concentrated without becoming damage itself.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The original game provides no defense-to-damage relic, Ice Shield, Earth Shield or team-stat-to-carry conversion formula.

records.version_scope: launch final stage with Patch 1.1 damage outlet noted separately
