records.transferability: A roster can express quantity through reinforcement cadence without spawning hundreds of concurrent entities.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not map 500 produced units to 500 occupied battlefield slots or copy an unpublished curve.
records.project_question: Could tower reinforcements use a visible production/cadence threshold while preserving explicit population and performance caps?

records.version_scope: EA layout practice; topology remains relevant but v1.1.4 flow fixes make exact rates historical
records.rule_support: Written guides describe 4/s internal bridge/tunnel flow, 2/s endpoints, eight Canvas requiring 4/s, and named multi-stage recipes whose upstream and downstream cadence must be balanced.
records.practical_support: Players report downstream starvation despite apparently sufficient labels and trade larger efficient layouts against compact bridge-limited schematics and Ink Engine footprint.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact rates are historical and image geometry is not interpreted; current flow after multiple fixes lacks an official formula sheet.
records.mechanism: A build's effective output is the minimum local flow across extraction, transport, endpoint, Canvas and synthesis stages, paid for with finite cells.
records.engine: Motif/Ink sources, transport lanes, endpoints, Canvas and combiners
records.state_resource: Per-stage rate, backlog, starvation, footprint and rebuild time
records.trigger: Several consumers share a lane or a multi-stage recipe introduces a slower segment
records.scope: One production chain and dependent Hero/Spell lines
records.payoff: Higher stable export rate or a smaller layout at accepted throughput loss
records.survival: Starved frontline production reduces later battle uptime
records.spatial_condition: Crossings, bridges, inputs, outputs, mergers and recipe lanes occupy authored factory space
records.payoff_owner: Each production line owns its output; the bottleneck stage owns the limiting rate
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Choose compact, expandable or high-throughput topology according to map cells, current recipe and time remaining.
records.counterplay: Resource color/shape mismatch and new recipes can invalidate a tightly packed layout.
records.failure_explanation: Expose requested, supplied, transported, consumed and exported rates at every stage.
records.transferability: Build space can live in an item/factory graph as long as throughput and ownership stay diagnosable.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy real-time conveyor work or historical device values into a non-factory autobattler.
records.project_question: Can equipment/relic slots represent a lighter-weight throughput graph without demanding factory micromanagement?

records.version_scope: formal release v1.0 Ascension 9 practice
records.rule_support: Hero upgrades form multi-input synthesis chains, while Statue replicas introduced in 1.0 can supply synthesis without entering battle or consuming the original low-tier deployment line.
records.practical_support: A player completed Ascension 9 on the third attempt using Pikemen→Horses→Light Cavalry→Knight, optional Shieldbearer→Heavy Infantry and only opportunistic Archer; another completion used Mages→Shields→Horses.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The thread is a small self-selected sample and predates later 1.1 balance; no seed, win rate or complete factory image is available.
records.mechanism: A low-tier throughput line survives as early deployment and synthesis input while cavalry upgrades become the late Boss payoff and shield infantry preserves uptime.
records.engine: Continuous recipes, Canvas/divider/transport lines and optional Statue synthesis bridge
records.state_resource: Per-line produced count, recipe order, Mana, Motif/Ink, Research, footprint and battle timing
records.trigger: Horse and Light Cavalry recipes become available without collapsing the current defense
records.scope: Pikemen/Horse/Cavalry/Knight line plus optional shield/ranged modules
records.payoff: Knight/cavalry Boss damage, engagement speed and edge pressure
records.survival: Shieldbearer/Heavy Infantry and retained low-tier deployment protect the transition
records.spatial_condition: Factory lanes must reserve upstream split, high-tier inputs and Portal overflow; battlefield placement is not manually controlled
records.payoff_owner: Knight/cavalry owns terminal damage; each retained line owns its own cadence; Statue owns synthesis-only supply
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Open with efficient Pikemen/basic output, retain it until recipes/resources support the chain, and add ranged output only when offered cheaply.
records.counterplay: Ascension 9 first-Boss pressure, Naga, missing recipes/resources and factory footprint can end the run before the payoff arrives.
records.failure_explanation: Distinguish early-line collapse, missing recipe, synthesis starvation and insufficient late Boss damage.
records.transferability: Vertical upgrades need an explicit bridge so advancing one owner does not erase the survival/economy that enables it.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not treat the path as a guaranteed 1.1 win or import exact production counts.
records.project_question: Which project units/items can bridge a defensive early line into a late carry without making either stage disposable?

records.version_scope: 1.1-era 2026 Ascension 9 community practice
records.rule_support: Hero lines deploy automatically according to production cadence, allowing one status-supplying line and many basic/Horse attackers to coexist.
records.practical_support: A current player recommends Thief or Ninja for Bleed plus many basic Units or Horses for repeated hits and a first-map buffer, explicitly adapting to available resources and layout.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Shield bypass, added-damage ownership and the full Bleed stack/cleanse/immunity rule are supported only by this player discussion, not an official current formula.
records.mechanism: A low-footprint status supplier marks enemies and a high-cadence swarm supplies many reader hits while cheap bodies buy the time needed for repeated triggers.
records.engine: Thief/Ninja Bleed line plus basic Unit/Horse production lines
records.state_resource: Bleed state, deployment intervals, attack count, enemy Shield, Motif/Ink and footprint
records.trigger: Bleed is applied and later attackers hit the marked enemy
records.scope: Marked enemy and all qualifying attacking units
records.payoff: Repeated status-linked damage across many hits
records.survival: Basic Units/Horses form the buffer; Bleed itself is not the frontline
records.spatial_condition: Short inexpensive lines fit the first map; battlefield formation is automatic
records.payoff_owner: Thief/Ninja owns supply lineage, each hitter owns the read event, and final damage attribution remains unresolved
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Keep multiple basic lines until a viable status recipe and matching resources appear; remain on Horses/basic throughput if they do not.
records.counterplay: Early burst, production mismatch and any unverified status resistance/cleanse can break the chain before hit volume ramps.
records.failure_explanation: Report status application uptime, reader hits, absorbed versus bypassed Shield and final source lineage separately.
records.transferability: An element/status system should specify supplier, persistent state, readers and payoff owner rather than treating a tag as a build.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy Shield bypass, stack count or immunity rules without stronger evidence.
records.project_question: Which project statuses reward many attackers, and how should supplier versus reader damage appear in reports?

records.version_scope: 2024 Demo/EA structure with formal-release role corroboration; current strength unresolved
records.rule_support: Historical sources show frequent Shieldbearer deployment forming a wall while Mages appear behind it for area lightning; formal-release practice still separates Mages, Shields and Horses by combat role.
records.practical_support: EA players describe Mage as too fragile alone and pair it with a shield wall; a 1.0 Ascension completion uses Mage for general enemies, Shields for survival and Horses for Boss damage.
records.disagreement_or_limit: v1.0 comprehensively rebalanced Heroes, so this supports module ownership and uptime, not current Mage/Shieldbearer tier strength.
records.mechanism: A high-cadence shield line absorbs engagement pressure so a separate ranged/AOE owner can complete more attacks.
records.engine: Shieldbearer production cadence plus Mage/Horse output lines
records.state_resource: Frontline uptime, deploy interval, enemy pressure and ranged cast/attack opportunities
records.trigger: Shield units intercept enemies before they reach fragile payoff owners or the portal
records.scope: Frontline survival supporting separate Mage/Horse damage
records.payoff: More area-clear or Boss-damage actions by the actual damage owner
records.survival: Shieldbearer owns the defensive wall and replacement cadence
records.spatial_condition: Production layout determines cadence; no reliable manual battle formation is evidenced
records.payoff_owner: Shieldbearer owns mitigation; Mage/Horse owns damage; no defense-to-damage converter exists in the cited original rules
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Add enough shield throughput to stop collapse, then invest marginal production in the damage axis demanded by the next enemy.
records.counterplay: Backline access, burst, anti-shield or a Boss damage check can bypass pure uptime investment.
records.failure_explanation: Separate damage prevented, uptime gained and attacks/casts completed by the protected owner.
records.transferability: A shield archetype can deal damage indirectly by enabling a carry without needing innate shield-scaling attacks.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not infer team Defense-to-AP/Attack conversion or current hero rankings from this module.
records.project_question: Should the project support both pure uptime shields and slot-costly relic/equipment converters into one carry's output?

records.version_scope: v1.0 introduction and formal-release practice
records.rule_support: Choosing a Hero Upgrade grants its Statue; the Statue creates replicas at the base Hero production speed, replicas are synthesis-only, and removal requires a Pickaxe.
records.practical_support: Players route Statue replicas with priority into a combiner while normal low-tier output overflows to the Portal, preserving both high-tier input and low-tier battle cadence; placement timing and low output remain costs.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact inserter priority, current Research modifiers and late-run Statue efficiency are not published as a complete formula.
records.mechanism: A dedicated noncombat replica decouples high-tier recipe consumption from the original low-tier line's combat deployment state.
records.engine: Upgrade reward spawning a fixed Statue/Tablet producer
records.state_resource: Replica rate, normal-line output, combiner demand, Portal overflow, footprint and Pickaxe
records.trigger: An upgrade is chosen and the Statue is placed and connected
records.scope: One Hero/Spell lineage and its downstream recipe
records.payoff: Enable vertical synthesis without erasing the predecessor's ability/cadence contribution
records.survival: The normal predecessor line can continue supplying battlefield bodies
records.spatial_condition: Fixed placement and priority/overflow routing consume scarce factory cells
records.payoff_owner: Statue owns synthesis-only supply; normal line owns deployment; high-tier line owns final payoff
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Use the bridge only when recipe timing and space justify it; otherwise retain the established line and Pickaxe flexibility.
records.counterplay: Late placement, low replica rate, missing side inputs or trapped footprint can make the bridge too slow.
records.failure_explanation: Show replica versus normal products, their destinations, unmet combiner inputs and lost Portal export.
records.transferability: Upgrade systems can provide a bridge token that preserves predecessor ownership during vertical transitions.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not treat replicas as free battle units or a universal no-cost upgrade.
records.project_question: Could evolution consume a synthesis-only proxy or reserve slot rather than deleting a still-needed low-tier unit?

records.version_scope: v1.0 route/shop/research rules with 1.0-era practice
records.rule_support: The Incursion Route Shop spends Carat on items and was added to answer a missing Carat sink and pure-RNG frustration; 1.0 also changed Research reroll currency and Relic choices.
records.practical_support: Players describe route, recipe, Motif/Ink, Research and map-expansion offers jointly determining whether a chain is producible; an Arcane opener reroll can collapse into fixed Underground Utilization/Inserters starts.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No complete current offer probabilities, Shop inventory or 1.1 meta statistics are available; a popular opener is not proved unique.
records.mechanism: Route nodes and draft offers create path-dependent production options, while Carat/Keen/reroll tools buy bounded correction rather than guaranteeing a build.
records.engine: Route selection, Hero/upgrade/Research/Relic offers, Shop and reroll currencies
records.state_resource: Carat, Keen, consumables, recipes, Research, map resources and upcoming node information
records.trigger: A route or reward offer is presented
records.scope: Current run's producible build space and future nodes
records.payoff: Convert uncertainty into an adaptable recipe/research plan
records.survival: Early defensive options may be prioritized when the first Boss window is near
records.spatial_condition: Map expansion and available Motif/Ink positions constrain the offered recipe's real value
records.payoff_owner: Each offer owns a rule/resource change; Shop/reroll owns correction cost; chosen line owns battle payoff
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Pay to reroll only when an offer cannot connect to resources, prerequisites or a viable survival/payoff path.
records.counterplay: Dead rewards, missing prerequisites and fixed no-cost opening rerolls undermine adaptive choice.
records.failure_explanation: Mark unavailable inputs/prerequisites before selection and show reroll cost plus remaining correction options.
records.transferability: Random build offers need visible feasibility and paid recovery, while recovery itself needs opportunity cost.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy currencies, route cadence or claim that one Research opener is mandatory.
records.project_question: How should tower rewards preview build compatibility and let players recover from an offered-but-unusable unit/item?

records.version_scope: formal release v1.0 community practice
records.rule_support: The formal-release Research/economy system supports alternate factory technologies and level rewards, while unused map resources otherwise retain spatial and routing cost.
records.practical_support: A detailed community route uses Shredder/Recycle to turn unwanted Motif into early XP/levels and partial reclaimed material, clearing dead resources while competing with Ink Engine/production Research and factory space.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The cited 10–16% reclaim and level-six-before-wave-one examples are player-period observations, not current fixed formulas or proof of strongest Research.
records.mechanism: A secondary line converts unusable inputs into progression and partial reusable supply, turning a failed resource match into a costly pivot.
records.engine: Shredder/Recycle Research and transport line
records.state_resource: Unused Motif, reclaimed material, XP/levels, Mana, Research slot and footprint
records.trigger: A map resource cannot feed the chosen recipes efficiently
records.scope: Current factory economy and level progression
records.payoff: Recover part of sunk map value and accelerate choice/Mana thresholds
records.survival: Earlier levels may add capacity before combat, but recycling does not directly defend
records.spatial_condition: Recycler routing consumes the same cells needed by production lines
records.payoff_owner: Recycle system owns conversion; level system owns rewards; later Hero line owns resulting battle output
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Recycle only dead/excess inputs and abandon or shrink the line when direct production becomes more valuable.
records.counterplay: Low reclaim, late setup and footprint pressure can make recycling worse than leaving a resource unused.
records.failure_explanation: Display material in, material recovered, XP gained, footprint/time cost and foregone production.
records.transferability: Salvage can turn unusable draft resources into a bounded pivot instead of forcing a restart.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not import the author's `most op` label or historical percentages as current balance.
records.project_question: Should unwanted tower rewards sell, recycle into reroll value, or remain commitment costs—and how visible is the exchange rate?

records.version_scope: formal release 1.0 through 1.1 current long-form practice
records.rule_support: Production and battle alternate around timers/Mana, while 1.1 adds broader Box Select editing but does not publish a complete Focus/Free Control time-authority specification.
records.practical_support: Two long reviews report that Focus output may not count or grow Mana and that Free Control/pause permits no-cost editing; one describes disconnecting a belt to accumulate output before restoring it.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The exact current intended behavior and reproducibility after v1.1.4 are unresolved; the workaround is not treated as developer intent.
records.mechanism: Different subsystems disagree on whether paused/focused time advances production credit, Mana, inventory and build cost, creating storage exploits or lost output.
records.engine: Production timer, Focus Time, Free Control/pause, transport buffers and Portal counter
records.state_resource: Elapsed build time, Mana, in-flight products, stored backlog and credited exports
records.trigger: Player enters Focus/Free Control, pauses flow, edits, then resumes
records.scope: Whole production phase and subsequent battle state
records.payoff: Extra planning access, or unintended inventory/time advantage
records.survival: Banked or lost deployments change the next defense wave
records.spatial_condition: Belts/buffers can store physical products while the authoritative counter is paused
records.payoff_owner: Run clock owns elapsed time; factory owns movement; Portal owns credit; UI must reconcile them
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Pause/edit affordance should have one declared cost and atomic resume behavior.
records.counterplay: Cap buffers, freeze every dependent clock consistently, or explicitly charge planning time/resources.
records.failure_explanation: Show which clocks/resources are frozen, which continue and why a product was not credited.
records.transferability: Independent tactical pause needs a single time authority across simulation, cooldowns, resources and settlement.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not claim the reported exploit remains universal after the latest patch.
records.project_question: What exactly advances during tower planning pause, hero command slow-time and menu inspection?

records.version_scope: formal release v1.0 Ascension 9 with historical Naga context
records.rule_support: v1.0 reworked Ascension, EX stages, Bosses and knockback behavior; the earlier Naga nerf explicitly states that only particular Heroes answered it reliably.
records.practical_support: Ascension 9 players report severe first-Boss pressure, extra mini-boss/enemy scaling and dependence on available resources/recipes, with cavalry or Bleed-swarm routes failing when their transition arrives too late.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Forum outcomes are self-selected and do not provide win rates; historical Naga tuning is not the current exact Boss package.
records.mechanism: A difficulty tier combines early tempo, survivability, single-target Boss damage, crowd handling and production-RNG pressure, so one aggregate power score cannot explain failure.
records.engine: Ascension modifiers, Boss/mini-boss composition, route timing and production constraints
records.state_resource: Enemy HP/speed/count, first-Boss deadline, available recipes/resources and current line cadence
records.trigger: The run reaches an early wave/Boss before the intended chain is online
records.scope: Whole run and its current counter coverage
records.payoff: Reward builds that cover tempo, frontline, area clear and Boss damage at different stages
records.survival: Extra enemies and early elites test replacement/frontline cadence
records.spatial_condition: Factory footprint and route expansion determine how many counter axes can coexist
records.payoff_owner: Each Hero/status line owns one response; Ascension package owns the exam
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Use a cheap first-map line, inspect upcoming threats, and delay high-tier commitment if inputs or survival are missing.
records.counterplay: Offer readable windows for shield bypass, single-target burst, AOE, sustained frontline and control resistance.
records.failure_explanation: Attribute defeat to timing, missing counter axis, production bottleneck or insufficient payoff rather than only `Ascension too hard`.
records.transferability: Enemy packages should test distinct build links with enough preview and pivot time.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not convert anecdotal attempts into a difficulty probability or reuse historical Naga values.
records.project_question: Which tower floors separately test frontline uptime, backline access, swarm clear, Boss damage and control dependence?

records.version_scope: v1.0.0 rework
records.rule_support: v1.0 broadened initial knockback applicability but made enemies gain resistance each time they are knocked back until they become immune.
records.practical_support: Cavalry is used for engagement and edge pressure in practical routes, so repeated displacement can create tempo but cannot remain a permanent control lock.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The public note gives no resistance stages, decay timer, Boss exceptions or exact per-hit values.
records.mechanism: Each successful knockback writes target-local resistance, preserving early utility while bounding recursive or permanent control.
records.engine: Knockback events and per-enemy resistance state
records.state_resource: Knockback count/resistance stage, displacement distance and immunity
records.trigger: An enemy is displaced repeatedly
records.scope: Individual enemy across the current battle
records.payoff: Temporary spacing, retargeting or extra attack time without infinite lock
records.survival: Distance delays contact with the portal/frontline
records.spatial_condition: Value depends on enemy position, available retreat distance and battlefield edge
records.payoff_owner: Displacing unit owns the control event; enemy owns accumulating resistance
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Do not overinvest in displacement when the next Boss will reach immunity before damage is sufficient.
records.counterplay: Resistance, immunity and limited space attack control without deleting its opening value.
records.failure_explanation: Display current resistance stage, applied distance and reason for partial/failed knockback.
records.transferability: Diminishing resistance is a readable recursion guard for hard control.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not invent the number of stages, decay or universal immunity policy.
records.project_question: Which project controls accumulate resistance per target, and how will the player see that progression before a Boss ignores them?

records.version_scope: EA balance history to v1.0 Burn rewrite
records.rule_support: EA patches nerfed several Burn sources, while v1.0 changed Burn into a stackable status whose layer count drives damage over time.
records.practical_support: A formal-release review discusses Dragon Burn cap and slow tick cadence as a build constraint, showing that source rate, cap and tick timing remain separate levers.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Player-observed cap/tick details lack an official current formula, and EA source strength cannot be carried into 1.1.
records.mechanism: Burn sources add a persistent counted state whose tick cadence and cap govern realized damage independently from application frequency.
records.engine: Burn-applying Hero/Spell and target status stack
records.state_resource: Stack count, cap, duration, tick interval and target life expectancy
records.trigger: A Burn source hits/applies and the DOT tick resolves
records.scope: Each affected enemy
records.payoff: Damage over time that can reward sustained application
records.survival: No inherent defense; frontline uptime may be needed for stacks to mature
records.spatial_condition: Target access and survival duration determine whether ticks occur
records.payoff_owner: Source owns application lineage; status owns stored stacks; tick event owns final damage
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Invest in more sources only while additional applications improve stack uptime before targets die or cap.
records.counterplay: Short fights, cleanse/resistance if present, cap and slow ticks can suppress payoff.
records.failure_explanation: Report applications, rejected over-cap stacks, uptime, ticks and source-attributed damage.
records.transferability: Elemental DOT needs explicit supplier, stack policy, cadence, cap and final owner.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not import EA values or unverified current cap/cleanse rules.
records.project_question: Should project elemental DOT scale through more stacks, faster ticks, detonation readers or mutually exclusive ownership?

records.version_scope: EA v0.8.7-v0.8.10, superseded in strength by v1.0
records.rule_support: Official EA patches reworked D/C Warriors, reduced Human power, raised Archer/Mage/production values, then nerfed Mythic units that broadly exceeded Warriors and fixed an abnormally strong Frost Laser configuration; v1.0 later rebalanced all Heroes.
records.practical_support: EA players independently report ranged dominance and poor payoff from resource/space-heavy high tiers, matching the need for role and recipe-cost rework without establishing exact causality.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Community complaints are not population data, and the official notes do not prove that one complaint caused each change; current 1.1 rankings remain unresolved.
records.mechanism: Unit power must repay production time, consumed predecessors, side resources and footprint, not merely occupy a higher nominal tier.
records.engine: Hero family stats, production speed, recipe costs and ability configuration
records.state_resource: Tier, damage/role output, production cadence, side inputs and consumed low-tier value
records.trigger: A family or high-tier recipe under/overperforms its total opportunity cost
records.scope: Warrior, Human, Archer/Mage and Mythic families
records.payoff: Restore distinguishable roles and credible vertical investment
records.survival: Warrior/Human adjustments affect the frontline component separately from ranged payoff
records.spatial_condition: Complex high tiers require more production equipment and cells
records.payoff_owner: Hero family owns combat role; recipe owns acquisition cost; patch owns rebalance
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Compare marginal battle value against lost low-tier cadence and new recipe footprint before upgrading.
records.counterplay: Keep multiple viable role routes instead of one ranged family answering every enemy.
records.failure_explanation: Show recipe opportunity cost and per-owner battle contribution, not tier labels alone.
records.transferability: Vertical rarity/tier must pay for all resources and ownership displaced by the upgrade.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not treat EA complaints or patch direction as current rankings or exact multipliers.
records.project_question: How will project upgrades show the predecessor value they consume and the new counter coverage they buy?

records.version_scope: EA v0.10.2, before v1.0 Boss/Ascension rework
records.rule_support: The developer explicitly nerfed Naga because it was much harder unless the player used particular Heroes; v1.0 later reworked Bosses and Ascension.
records.practical_support: Historical role guidance shows Hero families differed in Boss, swarm and survival function, explaining why a narrow enemy gate could invalidate many production routes.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The official note does not name the privileged Heroes or before/after values, and the current Naga package is not established.
records.mechanism: A Boss becomes a build lock when its decisive mechanic has only a few valid owners and the acquisition path cannot reliably pivot before contact.
records.engine: Naga rules interacting with Hero family capabilities
records.state_resource: Available counter Heroes, recipe access, production cadence and Boss deadline
records.trigger: The route reaches Naga without one of the narrow effective answers
records.scope: One Boss encounter and run viability
records.payoff: After nerf, broaden the set of viable strategies
records.survival: Boss pressure can overwhelm lines that otherwise survive regular waves
records.spatial_condition: Factory rebuild time/space limits late counter substitution
records.payoff_owner: Boss owns the exam; specific Hero line owns the response
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Preview the counter need early enough to acquire and produce an alternative line.
records.counterplay: Use several independently obtainable answers or weaken the gate while retaining its identity.
records.failure_explanation: Name the failed capability rather than implying the player's whole build was numerically weak.
records.transferability: Counter encounters need route-visible answer breadth and a real adaptation window.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not reconstruct the old Naga mechanic or current answer list from the short patch note.
records.project_question: How many viable owners should answer each elite/Boss mechanic, and how early are those owners offered?

records.version_scope: EA v0.9 flow overhaul through formal release and v1.1.4 fixes
records.rule_support: Official updates repeatedly changed/fixed Mixer, Ink Engine, Inserter, portal flow, speed behavior and Ink Coating deployment-speed display across 0.9, 1.0 and 1.1.4.
records.practical_support: Players report downstream starvation despite displayed transport capacity and uncredited Focus output, showing that local labels can disagree with end-to-end production state.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The incidents span versions and are not one persistent bug; no current full device-rate table or deterministic reproduction is public.
records.mechanism: A rate-driven build becomes unreadable when displayed local speed omits endpoint, batching, delay, counting or downstream ownership that limits realized output.
records.engine: Motif/Ink flow, Mixer/Canvas/transport devices, Portal credit and UI labels
records.state_resource: Displayed rate, effective rate, input/output latency, backlog, threshold credit and deploy interval
records.trigger: Speed changes, focus/pause, shared transport or conversion causes local and final rates to diverge
records.scope: Factory chain, Portal count and battle deployment display
records.payoff: Trustworthy optimization and diagnosis
records.survival: Incorrect cadence estimates can leave the next battle under-defended
records.spatial_condition: The failing segment may be an endpoint/crossing rather than the visually longest lane
records.payoff_owner: Each device owns local flow; Portal owns credit; Hero line owns deployment; UI owns their lineage
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Rebuild or research only after the interface identifies the actual limiting stage.
records.counterplay: Validation should cover speed multipliers, pause/focus, empty/full buffers and mixed Ink paths.
records.failure_explanation: Show end-to-end throughput, limiting stage, dropped/delayed products and why displayed deploy speed differs.
records.transferability: Any cadence/charge build needs telemetry that follows source→conversion→owner→effect.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not merge all historical fixes into one current defect or infer current rates.
records.project_question: What per-owner diagnostic chain will connect resource gain, skill cadence, summon deployment and battle output?

records.version_scope: EA v0.10.2 performance work and v1.0 battle/production safeguards
records.rule_support: v0.10.2 reports roughly halved Endless battle load, and v1.0 optimizes battle/Ink processing while suppressing excessive deployment of some Heroes/Spells when combat is already overwhelmingly favorable.
records.practical_support: Formal-release practice drives very high production counts to reduce deployment intervals, creating pressure to preserve progression credit without materializing every possible entity/effect.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The public notes do not give the suppression trigger, affected owners, entity cap or whether skipped deployments retain all secondary effects.
records.mechanism: The system preserves production/cadence progression but limits redundant battle materialization once outcome pressure and entity volume cross a guard.
records.engine: Hero/Spell deployment scheduler and battle-performance guard
records.state_resource: Produced count, requested deploy rate, live entities/effects, battle advantage and suppressed events
records.trigger: Deployment demand is high while the battle is already decisively favorable
records.scope: Selected Hero/Spell deployments in the current battle
records.payoff: Maintain responsiveness and readability without erasing factory growth
records.survival: Guard should not suppress needed defenders when the battle is contested
records.spatial_condition: Dense battlefield occupancy/effects create CPU and visual load
records.payoff_owner: Production line owns earned cadence; scheduler owns materialization; report owns suppressed-event visibility
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Players should not need to avoid a valid high-throughput build solely for performance.
records.counterplay: Use deterministic caps, pooling/aggregation and hysteresis so the guard cannot oscillate or alter close fights.
records.failure_explanation: Report requested, spawned, aggregated and suppressed deployments plus the guard reason.
records.transferability: Summon/reinforcement systems need explicit population, rate and visual-load safeguards.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not infer the exact algorithm or claim production itself is nerfed.
records.project_question: How can project summons and reinforcements preserve build payoff while bounding entity count and proc recursion?

records.version_scope: v1.0 report expansion through v1.1.4 display fixes
records.rule_support: v1.0 added Minion Master direct-attack damage to reports and fixed range, miss and Spell/Relic effect-area text; v1.1.4 fixed Ink Coating's battle-deploy-speed display.

records.version_scope: Garg update 2026-04-13 and v1.011 through v1.032

records.practical_support: Adam practice depends on enemy corpses remaining available long enough to seed a reanimated frontline, so loot consumption and reanimation can contend for the same state.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The public corpus does not reveal corpse eviction order, exact caps or Vulture-versus-reanimation priority.
records.mechanism: A corpse is a finite state consumed by competing readers under both gameplay and runtime throughput limits.
records.engine: Corpse creation, Vulture loot reader, Adam reanimation reader and corpse cleanup/entity controller
records.state_resource: Live corpse count, age/source, reader eligibility, consumption budget and object cap
records.trigger: Enemy death, reader scan, cap pressure or cleanup tick
records.scope: Current battlefield corpse pool
records.payoff: Loot, reanimated body or cleanup/performance relief
records.survival: Reanimation may supply frontline bodies; premature consumption can remove that survival path
records.spatial_condition: Vulture reads nearby corpses and entity density affects clustering/performance
records.payoff_owner: Corpse retains source; each reader owns consumption request; controller owns arbitration/cleanup
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Choosing a corpse-loot item can compete with a corpse-reanimation plan and should be visible before purchase.
records.counterplay: Corpse denial, decay, reader rate caps and deterministic priority constrain loops.
records.failure_explanation: Report created, expired, capped and consumed corpses plus the winning reader.
records.transferability: Treat corpses as transactional resources with one-writer arbitration and bounded readers.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not infer exact cap numbers or allow one corpse to silently pay multiple terminal rewards.
records.project_question: What deterministic priority resolves project corpse loot, revival, explosion and cleanup requests?

records.version_scope: formal release through v1.015+ economy/readability period
records.rule_support: Top-tier unit progress feeds Oaths/tags; rarity expansion adds specialized units to the offer pool, while The Many cannot use upgrades/Oaths and Garg uses a distinct Champion rule.
records.practical_support: Players identify pool dilution and reroll cost as the price of opening higher-rarity builds; Banish trims unusable percentage/stat options or unwanted branches.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No current odds table, complete Banish pricing function or universal best rarity timing is public.
records.mechanism: Opening new build owners enlarges the pool; Oath payoff and Banish correction must repay the lower probability of finishing existing lines.
records.engine: Rarity unlock, offer pool, reroll, Banish, three-copy tiering and Oath/tag progress
records.state_resource: Unlocked units/items, pool size, current pairs/tiers, reroll/Banish cost and Oath progress
records.trigger: Rarity purchase, offer generation, Banish or Tier-3 completion
records.scope: Run recruitment/item economy and trait layer
records.payoff: Access specialized builds and Oath effects
records.survival: Premature pool expansion can delay a needed frontline/defense upgrade
records.spatial_condition: Indirect; new roles still require target access and squad coverage
records.payoff_owner: Pool owns availability; unit line owns tier; Oath owns breakpoint; Banish owns correction
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Expand only when new owners answer a known need or current lines are sufficiently stable.
records.counterplay: Threat pressure and limited reroll budget punish over-broad pools.
records.failure_explanation: Show how unlocks changed odds, what Banish removed and which Oath progress was abandoned.
records.transferability: Unlock breadth needs priced correction and visible dilution, especially when traits require vertical copies.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy Oaths, rarity costs or treat Banish as a free permanent solution.
records.project_question: How will project recruitment expose the opportunity cost of adding a new hero family or trait bridge to the offer pool?

records.version_scope: launch Armor confusion, 2026-05-01 Evasion overhaul and v1.026+ Thorns period
records.rule_support: The developer confirms stale Armor text, later replaces Dodge scaling with Evasion, and v1.026 fixes non-functional Thorns/Riposte; community rule discussion places Thorns after final damage.
records.practical_support: Players distinguish Armor+healing uptime from death economy and observe that Dodge prevents a Thorns event while Armor-reduced final damage also reduces its input.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The player-derived Armor formula and Thorns order lack a complete official current equation/event table; no current build-rate data exists.
records.mechanism: Armor, Evasion and retaliation are separate defensive axes whose event order changes both survival and output.
records.engine: Armor mitigation, Evasion avoidance, Thorns/Riposte trigger and healing
records.state_resource: Incoming hit, mitigated final damage, avoided-hit flag, retaliation coefficient and effective Health
records.trigger: Attack resolution after avoidance and mitigation
records.scope: Defender and attacker
records.payoff: Reduced damage, healing efficiency and eligible retaliation
records.survival: Armor multiplies effective healing/Health; Evasion can negate hits entirely
records.spatial_condition: Requires an attacker to hit a retaliation owner; ranged/untargeted events may differ
records.payoff_owner: Defender owns mitigation; Evasion owns cancellation; Thorns reader owns retaliation event
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Invest only when the chosen defensive axis also fits expected hit size/frequency and payoff readers.
records.counterplay: Large hits, attack denial, avoidance, non-contact damage and backline access attack different axes.
records.failure_explanation: Show raw hit, avoided/mitigated amount, final damage and accepted/rejected retaliation.
records.transferability: Defense-to-offense needs a declared calculation point; pre-mitigation and post-mitigation readers produce different builds.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not import the player formula, old Dodge values or assume Thorns is currently strong because it was fixed.
records.project_question: Should project retaliation read attempted damage, prevented damage, final damage or a capped defense stat?

records.version_scope: formal release through v1.032
records.rule_support: Official patches fix Thorns/Riposte and multiple Burn/Plague/Rot/Freeze/reanimated achievement attribution problems, while v1.032 fixes a Chilled/Frozen stack crash.
records.practical_support: Guides build around repeated status application, Crit readers and Rot reanimation, so missed accounting or stack failure can make a functioning engine appear ineffective.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The corpus does not expose every stack cap, cleanse/resistance rule, tick order or current numerical formula.
records.mechanism: Status application, stack storage, threshold conversion, tick/trigger and achievement/report credit must retain one source lineage under bounded stack guards.
records.engine: Burn, Plague, Rot, Freeze/Chilled and reanimation event pipelines
records.state_resource: Applications, accepted/rejected stacks, source, cap, duration, ticks, conversion and credited outcome
records.trigger: Status application, tick, threshold, target death or reanimation
records.scope: Target state, source unit/item and report/achievement system
records.payoff: Damage, control, reanimation or progression credit
records.survival: Freeze/root may buy uptime while Rot/Burn/Plague mature
records.spatial_condition: Application depends on target access and clustered AOE may multiply event volume
records.payoff_owner: Supplier owns application; status owns stacks; reader owns conversion; report retains lineage
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Add more suppliers only while stacks/ticks/readers are not capped or wasted.
records.counterplay: Resistance, cleanse, short fights, cap, immunity and source removal limit payoff.
records.failure_explanation: Report application, rejection, stack conversion, tick, crash guard and credited owner separately.
records.transferability: Status systems require deterministic stack caps, conversion order and source-attributed reports.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not invent current formulas or interpret achievement fixes as balance changes.
records.project_question: What shared status event schema will let project DOT, control and corpse conversion reuse lineage without recursive overcounting?

records.version_scope: v1.026 through post-v1.032 current reviews
records.rule_support: Player control is limited to Skull movement, Rally and a character ability, while official performance work acknowledges high enemy counts, clustering and object pressure.
records.practical_support: Separate reviews report autonomous units spreading into isolated deaths or clustering into AOE, plus difficulty distinguishing Skull/allies/enemies/projectiles and detecting an imminent full wipe.
records.disagreement_or_limit: These are individual experiences, not measured failure rates; settings, unit mix and encounter may change severity.
records.mechanism: When agents self-position, the system owns enough formation intelligence and feedback to prevent unavoidable density failures.
records.engine: Unit AI, Rally, enemy AOE/cleave, visual layers and low-unit warning
records.state_resource: Unit positions/density, command eligibility, AOE telegraph, living count and source colors/shapes
records.trigger: Target selection, Rally, enemy AOE windup or living-count threshold
records.scope: Battlefield formation and player attention
records.payoff: Readable autonomous combat with a timely reposition decision
records.survival: Spread mitigates AOE but risks isolation; clustering protects focus fire but risks synchronized death
records.spatial_condition: Local density, range, pathing and access are the central variables
records.payoff_owner: AI owns default movement; player owns limited command; enemy owns telegraph; UI owns identification/warning
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Roster roles cannot compensate for a counter that the available command cannot express.
records.counterplay: Offer explicit regroup/spread/guard commands or enemy telegraphs with sufficient reaction time.
records.failure_explanation: Identify whether loss came from AI pathing, ignored command, AOE overlap, target access or unreadable source.
records.transferability: Autobattle agency requires commands that map to actual counters and non-color visual ownership cues.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not claim Skull Horde has fixed formation cells or that every player experiences unusable AI.
records.project_question: Which project tactical command answers density/AOE without becoming full RTS micromanagement?

records.version_scope: formal release through v1.032 source-backed event structure
records.rule_support: The game exposes death-currency readers, on-death status effects, death-effect target priority, corpse readers, reanimation, respawn and overheal-created summons as distinct event owners.
records.practical_support: The Many deliberately repeats Petard/death events for currency and statuses, while Adam and Vulture require corpse state after death; this creates observable ordering/recursion pressure.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No complete official event-order table proves the exact sequence among every reader, corpse consumer and respawn request.
records.mechanism: One death transitions through event emission, bounded readers, corpse creation/consumption and return without letting child events recursively duplicate terminal rewards.
records.engine: Death dispatcher, Charon/items, status readers, corpse controller, reanimation and respawn scheduler
records.state_resource: Death source/cause, reader budget, corpse id/state, currency, status events, summon requests and respawn ticket
records.trigger: A friendly/enemy unit reaches death settlement
records.scope: One deterministic death transaction and resulting children
records.payoff: Multiple build interactions with traceable ownership and bounded work
records.survival: Respawn/reanimation may restore bodies but cannot erase full-wipe timing
records.spatial_condition: Corpse location and nearby readers affect eligibility
records.payoff_owner: Dead unit/cause owns root event; each reader owns one child; corpse/respawn controllers own terminal state
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Combining death readers should consume item/relic opportunity and disclose shared caps.
records.counterplay: Corpse removal, reader cooldowns, per-event caps and recursion depth constrain loops.
records.failure_explanation: Trace root death, accepted/rejected readers, corpse disposition, currency and returned body.
records.transferability: Use transaction ids and deterministic reader ordering for sacrifice/corpse systems.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not assert the inferred ordering is Skull Horde's undocumented exact implementation.
records.project_question: What project-wide event budget and transaction lineage prevent one sacrifice from recursively spawning currency, corpses and units forever?

records.version_scope: source-backed formal-release structures; project converter remains exploratory
records.rule_support: Garg can concentrate survivability on chained frontline or damage on ranged recipients; Armor/healing, elemental/status readers and Blood Feast conversion modules remain separately owned.
records.practical_support: Successful/advised lines use durable units to bridge respawn time for mage/gunner/status payoff, or choose explicit healing/overheal readers; no source silently converts all team defense into one carry's damage.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The user's proposed team bonus-Health/Defense conversion and Ice/Earth shield taxonomy belong to project discussion, not Skull Horde rules.
records.mechanism: Defense buys uptime until a named item/relic/ability explicitly reads it and grants bounded output to a specified recipient.
records.engine: Frontline mitigation/healing, element/status supplier, explicit converter and carry
records.state_resource: Bonus Health/Defense/Shield, absorbed/healed amount, element/status, recipient, slot cost, cap and refresh
records.trigger: Hit/heal/status resolution or converter recalculation
records.scope: Team defense versus one carry or qualifying readers
records.payoff: Longer action time or explicit converted damage without erasing defensive identity
records.survival: Defense remains useful even when no conversion module is equipped
records.spatial_condition: Protected recipient still needs target access; chain distance/AI affects uptime
records.payoff_owner: Defender owns mitigation; supplier owns status; converter owns mapping; carry owns final attack
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Choose pure defense, death/status engine or slot-costly carry conversion based on enemy package.
records.counterplay: Shield break, anti-heal, burst, backline access, cleanse/resistance and conversion cap attack different links.
records.failure_explanation: Report defense source, uptime, converter input/cap, status reads and final damage owner separately.
records.transferability: Ice Shield and Earth Shield may share Shield semantics while element, supplier, reader, recipient and counter stay orthogonal.
records.incompatible_assumptions: This evidence authorizes no project item, relic, formula, element roster or first-version content.
records.project_question: Which project relic/equipment owns defense-to-output conversion, and what read scope, recipient, slot cost, cap, refresh and counters keep it a real build choice?

records.version_scope: formal release 1.0 through latest explicit main-branch hotfix 1.2.1; modes kept separate
records.rule_support: The game left Early Access at 1.0, removed the Demo while preserving Demo/EA saves, and exposes Standard, Elite, One-Man Army and co-op variants with different progression or control rules.
records.practical_support: The current Guide ties Elite access to a Standard boss clear and requires a Merc to be recruited before another co-op player can control it.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No current official prose states the exact solo Merc cap; five-player co-op is a control-seat statement, not a safe cap inference.
records.mechanism: Release, mode and control variants are explicit evidence dimensions rather than one blended ruleset.
records.engine: Operation-type selection, unlock state and co-op join state
records.state_resource: Version, mode, Standard clear, recruited Mercs and controller seats
records.trigger: Selecting an Operation or another player joining
records.scope: Run rules and control ownership
records.payoff: Comparable evidence without importing historical or co-op behavior into solo balance
records.survival: Mode-specific risk and extraction remain attached to their own rules
records.spatial_condition: Co-op control begins only for a Merc already present on the battlefield
records.payoff_owner: Mode owns modifiers; Commander/Merc owner changes only where the selected mode says so
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Clear Standard before pursuing Elite resources; recruit a Merc before exposing its co-op seat.
records.counterplay: Higher-risk modes and altered control contracts require separate balance checks.
records.failure_explanation: Label the active mode/version before attributing a loss or build outcome.
records.transferability: Version and mode tags should be mandatory in build evidence and combat reports.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy One-Man Army, free movement or co-op direct control into the project's solo autobattle contract.
records.project_question: Which project challenge variants may alter control or recruitment without contaminating baseline balance evidence?

records.version_scope: Guide updated for 1.0, cross-checked with 1.0/1.2 and current/late-EA reviews
records.rule_support: Operations chain combat stages, increasing Danger and objectives that award Mercs, XP/SP, Gear, loot, powerups or extraction.
records.practical_support: A detailed review observes branch-node missions carrying squad levels/upgrades forward and recommends early Merc recruitment for immediate power.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact node generation and reward rates changed repeatedly; the review does not establish a universal current opening.
records.mechanism: Spatial objectives convert exposure time into mutually competing recruitment, growth, loot and safe-exit rewards.
records.engine: Timed objectives, enemy drops, stage succession and Danger
records.state_resource: Dogtags, XP, SP, Blood Diamonds, Components, Gear, recruited Mercs and extraction eligibility
records.trigger: Capture an objective, clear a stage, defeat a boss or choose Retreat
records.scope: Current Operation and retained meta rewards
records.payoff: Grow the squad, secure loot or preserve long-run Merc bonuses
records.survival: Med-kits, Gear, Mercs and a timely extraction prevent total resource loss
records.spatial_condition: Commander must travel to and hold/capture objectives while the Merc squad fights around that route
records.payoff_owner: Each objective owns its reward; Merc/Commander upgrades remain with their declared recipient
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Choose between a Beacon, growth/loot objective, deeper Danger and safe extraction based on current squad readiness.
records.counterplay: Enemy pressure, end-stage barrage and objective timing punish greedy routing.
records.failure_explanation: Separate route greed, insufficient squad growth, missed extraction and combat failure.
records.transferability: Tower nodes can price recruitment, build power and safe cash-out against the same escalating risk.
records.incompatible_assumptions: The project does not need real-time POI running or an extraction shooter map.
records.project_question: How should tower rewards show the trade between one more build node and preserving accumulated run value?

records.version_scope: EA control philosophy through 1.0 Guide and 1.2 behavior fixes
records.rule_support: The player directly moves, dashes, aims and fires as Commander while each Merc owns independent movement, targeting and attack behavior.
records.practical_support: Developer and player accounts agree that Commander movement/positioning and active abilities indirectly steer Mercs that otherwise follow and auto-fire.
records.disagreement_or_limit: A current short review understates Commander Weapon activity; co-op can directly hand a Merc to another player and is excluded here.
records.mechanism: Autonomous combatants are influenced through leader position and bounded signals rather than per-unit micro.
records.engine: Merc AI plus Commander movement, facing, Mark and active Weapon
records.state_resource: Commander position/direction, Merc target state, movement pattern and command effects
records.trigger: Movement, a Weapon effect, target availability or AI replan
records.scope: Commander and eligible Mercs
records.payoff: Indirect focus, path clearing and survival without full RTS control
records.survival: Dash/space control rescues the Commander while Merc AI maintains output
records.spatial_condition: Merc range, path, facing and distance from Commander determine whether influence succeeds
records.payoff_owner: Commander owns input; Merc owns movement/target/attack; command effect owns any override
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Recruit Merc patterns that remain controllable under the selected Weapon and map package.
records.counterplay: Fast flanks, range, obstacles, AOE and AI/path defects can invalidate the indirect signal.
records.failure_explanation: Report whether the command was ineligible, the Merc ignored it, lacked range/path or chose another target.
records.transferability: Use explicit command eligibility and autonomous owner boundaries for tactical commands.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not import continuous twin-stick movement, manual aim skill or an irreplaceable Commander category.
records.project_question: Which limited project commands should override targeting, regrouping or protection, and which units are eligible?

records.version_scope: 0.9.11 owner separation through 1.0 Guide and post-1.2 structural review
records.rule_support: Feature, Characteristic and Talent Traits have different scopes; Dash, Weapon and Trait are distinct; Gear may modify Commander/squad or own a standalone rule.
records.practical_support: Current review describes Mercs as primary damage owners while Commander supplies buffs/effects, matching the Guide's separate owner categories.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No complete current per-item table proves every Gear recipient; unspecified group wording from 2023 cannot be generalized to all items.
records.mechanism: Build pieces compose only when supplier, reader, recipient and final payoff owner are explicit.
records.engine: Trait slot, Commander Weapon, Merc behavior and Gear rule
records.state_resource: Feature/Characteristic/Talent scope, stats, marks, Gear slots and Merc upgrades

records.payoff: Control, stat modification, healing or Merc-owned damage
records.survival: Defensive Gear/Trait effects can buy uptime without owning final damage

records.payoff_owner: Each Trait/Gear/Weapon/Merc retains its declared scope and event lineage

records.version_scope: current Guide with 0.15 specialization/synergy structure and historical pool practice
records.rule_support: Mercs come from Beacons, receive regular upgrades plus mutually exclusive SP specializations, and can roll Merc-pair synergy upgrades; Bunker options reroll or exclude pool entries.
records.practical_support: Players identify unlock-pool dilution and pressure to fish for a narrow Merc/Gear combination; official exclusion tools preserve some correction without removing randomness.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The negative specialization review predates 0.11/0.15 reworks and supplies no names; it is lifecycle evidence, not a current tier list.
records.mechanism: Adding content expands build possibility and pool dilution; reroll/exclusion prices correction while specialization creates commitment.
records.engine: Beacon/Gear offers, unlock pool, reroll, exclusion, regular levels and SP specialization
records.state_resource: Unlocked Mercs/Gear/upgrades, SP, reroll currency, chosen path and synergy eligibility
records.trigger: Offer generation, level-up, stage break or Bunker upgrade
records.scope: Run offer pools and individual Merc growth
records.payoff: Reach a coherent squad while retaining bounded adaptation
records.survival: Early recruitment and a viable defensive path bridge incomplete synergy
records.spatial_condition: A recruited Merc's movement/target pattern must fit the current squad route
records.payoff_owner: Pool owns availability; Merc owns specialization; pair upgrade owns synergy; Gear owns its own rule

records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not invent current pair lists, odds, exclusion counts or reroll prices.
records.project_question: How will project recruitment expose pool growth, path commitment and an affordable correction window?

records.version_scope: historical launch-EA build; later sources preserve structure but not current strength
records.rule_support: Priest supplies a moving aura, Stim Pack is a Gear healing option, and safe extraction preserves loot plus qualifying Merc Survivor Bonus while death removes most rewards.
records.practical_support: A player explicitly separates deep runs with an early Priest from early ejection without her and prefers stacking Priest with Stim Pack; the developer validates the healing logic.
records.disagreement_or_limit: This complete build is from 2023 EA; Armor, Priest movement, Gear, loot and progression changed, so it is not a 1.2 meta claim.
records.mechanism: Reliable repeat healing converts Commander Health from a one-way clock into a resource that can purchase deeper reward exposure.
records.engine: Early Priest recruitment plus stackable Stim Pack healing and Commander movement
records.state_resource: Commander Health, healing uptime, Gear slot, Danger, loot, extraction eligibility and Survivor Bonus
records.trigger: Take damage, enter aura/heal cadence, clear another stage or choose Retreat
records.scope: Commander survival and whole Operation reward exposure
records.payoff: More stages, later rare loot and preserved Merc starting upgrades
records.survival: Priest aura and Stim Pack, optionally reinforced by separately owned Armor/Shield
records.spatial_condition: Commander must remain in useful aura coverage while routing objectives and avoiding encirclement
records.payoff_owner: Priest/Stim Pack own healing; Commander owns Health; other Mercs/Weapon own damage; extraction owns settlement
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Take Priest in the first Beacon window or use another healing source; historically eject early when sustain fails to appear.

records.failure_explanation: Separate sustain absence, positioning loss, insufficient damage and missed safe extraction.
records.transferability: A defense build may pay through preserved resources and carry uptime while another owner deals damage.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy the old optimal timing, current strength, exact healing values or Commander hierarchy.
records.project_question: Can a project shield/sustain route earn value through protected carry actions and safer tower rewards without receiving free damage?

records.disagreement_or_limit: No current practical source supplies a named full Mark squad or exact mark priority/duration formula.

records.survival: Rapidly removing a key threat reduces incoming pressure
records.spatial_condition: Merc must be within its own range and able to execute its movement/attack pattern

records.version_scope: 0.9.9-0.11 Shield behavior; current 1.2 strength not asserted
records.rule_support: Riot/Defender Shield blocks projectiles/enemies, while later Riot contact adds Commander knockback; angle, hit invulnerability and heavy-projectile force limit coverage.
records.practical_support: Players found both a no-hit defensive use and near-default long blocking; the developer rejected an extra defense-point counter burden and favored natural knockback plus alternative tactics.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Challenge hitboxes and the OP report are historical individual observations, not a current formula or usage statistic.
records.mechanism: A directional Shield grants uptime but exposes angle, displacement and state-transition counters instead of becoming unconditional immunity.
records.engine: Shield collision/arc, projectile/enemy contact and knockback
records.state_resource: Covered direction, contact type, heavy-projectile force, enemy hit-invulnerability and position
records.trigger: Projectile/enemy intersects the Shield or approaches around its edge
records.scope: Commander and incoming contacts
records.payoff: Prevent hits and clear a path
records.survival: Blocked contacts preserve Health; one-hit Crusader Shield is a separate source
records.spatial_condition: Facing, angle, gap between Commander/Shield and knockback displacement determine protection
records.payoff_owner: Shield owns block; projectile/enemy owns force/path; Commander owns displaced position
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Take Shield for projectile-heavy fronts, or pivot to tanking, kiting/control and offense when angles/swarm/knockback dominate.
records.counterplay: Flanks, encirclement, heavy knockback, brief enemy invulnerability and DPS checks bypass or outvalue blocking.
records.failure_explanation: Show covered arc, bypass angle, blocked hit, displacement and any invulnerability-state interaction.

records.version_scope: formal 1.0 trigger bugs through 1.1 event-wording correction
records.rule_support: 1.1 distinguishes acquired from recruited and expands affected triggers to alternate acquisition; earlier fixes cover dismissed Echo Elemental, triple effects, Twin Elevation and Sacrificial Shade.
records.practical_support: Recruit/dismiss cycling and triple timing are core economy actions, while a long-running review reports lost transfer or upgrade resolution when Sacrificial Shade removes an unexpected target.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The player's proposed internal target-order explanation is unverified and one official fix does not prove all later upgrade cases are resolved.
records.mechanism: Obtain, recruit, dismiss, upgrade, remove, death and summon are separate events whose readers must not share accidental aliases.
records.engine: Acquisition resolver, shop recruitment, generated Gods, dismiss/remove, triple upgrade and trigger queue
records.state_resource: Source path, original owner, target selection, copy count, acquired abilities and pending event
records.trigger: Acquire, recruit, dismiss, triple, remove or die
records.scope: The named God, its target and eligible event readers
records.payoff: Predictable economy/scaling without lost, doubled or phantom triggers
records.survival: Correct transfer/removal prevents a build from deleting its own protected carry unexpectedly
records.spatial_condition: Target and slot are resolved before movement/removal changes formation
records.payoff_owner: Acquisition path owns event type; effect owns transfer; target owns received state; report keeps provenance
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Commit a cycle/upgrade only when its event type and target are visible.
records.counterplay: Event exclusions and one-shot consumption limit recursion without silently suppressing legal effects.
records.failure_explanation: Log acquisition path, selected target, transfer amount, removal and downstream triggers.
records.transferability: Use distinct gameplay events and preserve lineage through upgrades and generated content.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not equate sacrifice with death or infer a global sacrifice resource.
records.project_question: Which project verbs need separate event ids despite similar player-facing language?

records.version_scope: formal 1.0 Guide and launch practice; no 1.1 usage claim
records.rule_support: Egyptian death/summon pieces create bodies and Anubis/Sekhmet read deaths; Moiralith fields poison/reflect units followed by a large summon.
records.practical_support: A player gives Set(s), Hathor(s), one Sekhmet and one Anubis as a working poison answer because expendable summons clear lethal front units while scaling attack.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The Guide warns summon strategies are generally poor against single-target Azathoth; exact stats and post-1.1 success rate are unknown.
records.mechanism: Disposable bodies convert instant-kill counters into controlled death events that feed a separate damage owner.
records.engine: Egyptian summoners, death events, Sekhmet/Anubis readers and ordered attacks
records.state_resource: Available bodies, death count, Anubis attack, formation order, tier and remaining Boss summon
records.trigger: A summoned God dies or a death reader resolves
records.scope: Egyptian board and named death readers
records.payoff: Clear poison/reflect screens and retain enough scaled output for the final summon
records.survival: Small bodies absorb lethal effects so the main reader/carry survives
records.spatial_condition: Summoners/readers are ordered so expendable units die before the final owner must act
records.payoff_owner: Summoner owns body; body owns death; reader owns growth; surviving attacker owns final damage
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Use low-tier Egypt as transition, add the named readers, and borrow cleave/First Strike when the poison package demands it.
records.counterplay: Single-target combat scaling, seven-hit thresholds, backline damage and missing readers punish the line.
records.failure_explanation: Separate insufficient bodies, reader death, wrong order and failure to answer the final summon.
records.transferability: Summons need body budget, death ownership and an explicit enemy package that rewards them.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not treat all Egyptian Gods as summoners or claim this is a current meta composition.
records.project_question: Which project enemy packages should reward disposable bodies without making summon spam universal?

records.version_scope: formal launch developer example and 1.0 Guide; key pieces not directly listed in 1.1 changes
records.rule_support: Nezha can trigger Osiris at combat start; Osiris/Ptah repeat death effects and Ra/other Egyptian suppliers grow later bodies.
records.practical_support: The developer and Guide independently describe Nezha+Osiris+Ra/Ptah, optional Tezcatlipoca/copies and first-position plus taunt as a multi-trigger snowball.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No source provides a stable trigger-count formula, offer rate or 1.1 win rate; order fixes show historical resolver dependence.
records.mechanism: A bridge unit advances another faction's trigger schedule before normal attacks begin.
records.engine: Nezha combat-start trigger, Egyptian death suppliers, Osiris/Ptah replay and Ra buff
records.state_resource: Named pieces, copies, formation order, taunt, death effects and pending start triggers
records.trigger: Combat starts and the chosen death/replay effect resolves
records.scope: Named trigger chain and affected Egyptian Gods
records.payoff: Multiple early buff applications before the enemy can dismantle the scaling engine
records.survival: Taunt and first-position planning preserve the replay chain

records.payoff_owner: Nezha owns acceleration; Osiris/Ptah own replay; Ra owns buff; recipient owns final action

records.failure_explanation: Report each start trigger, replay owner, recipient and interruption point.

records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not infer infinite replay or copy this exact mythological package.
