records.version_scope: formal 1.0 developer example and Guide; no 1.1 current-meta claim
records.rule_support: Mesopotamian Gods read unspent Essence, Marduk supplies a combat buff and Aztec Tepeyollotl preserves its own combat buffs permanently.
records.practical_support: The developer and Guide describe assembling Marduk+Tepeyollotl early enough to compound one carry, while economy evidence frames the cost as sacrificing current purchases/tiering.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact Marduk scaling and survival threshold are omitted; later Essence recursion overflow does not prove this two-piece line is itself infinite or current best.
records.mechanism: A shared unspent currency is converted to temporary combat power and then captured by a single permanent-state reader.
records.engine: Divine Essence retention, Marduk combat buff and Tepeyollotl permanence
records.state_resource: Unspent Essence, temporary buff, permanent stats, assembly turn and survival margin
records.trigger: Combat start/end and Tepeyollotl's permanence resolution
records.scope: One protected carry with a cross-mythology supplier
records.payoff: Compounding single-owner attack/defense capable of carrying multiple fights
records.survival: The carry must live through the conversion; taunt or protection supplies uptime only
records.spatial_condition: Protect Tepeyollotl from cleave, poison and rightmost/backline counters
records.payoff_owner: Economy owns currency; Marduk owns temporary buff; Tepeyollotl owns permanence and final attacks
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Compare spending for tempo against saving for conversion; abandon the combo if either piece arrives after the compounding window.
records.counterplay: Poison, reflect, highest-Attack debuff, multi-hit thresholds and missed assembly attack the single core.
records.failure_explanation: Separate insufficient saved Essence, late supplier, failed permanence and carry removal.
records.transferability: A resource-to-output converter needs a named owner, timing window and forgone-spend cost.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not make all saved currency a generic team stat or copy unbounded compounding.
records.project_question: Which project economy converters can create a carry without erasing the need to spend for survival?

records.version_scope: formal Guide and 1.1 Cthulhu-targeted Heimdall change
records.rule_support: Norse Gods gain value from taking damage; Heimdall/Baldur/Loki can damage allies, Odin and other readers convert those events into buffs, and 1.1 changes Heimdall to allies only for the Cthulhu matchup.
records.practical_support: The Guide recommends deliberate late-game damage triggers plus Odin, Skadi for early scaling and Thor against one large enemy, but warns players to count procs against Cthulhu.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The exact same-timestamp loop order is unpublished and one Loki/Odin wipe was not reproduced; no current full lineup is established.
records.mechanism: A defensive loss event becomes output only through a named supplier-reader chain with threshold-aware rate limits.
records.engine: Friendly damage suppliers, damage events, Odin/Skadi/Thor readers and formation
records.state_resource: Health/defense, damage-event count, accumulated buffs, attack order and Cthulhu counter
records.trigger: An ally survives damage or a self-damage effect resolves
records.scope: Damaged ally, Norse readers or explicitly affected army
records.payoff: Team scaling or concentrated single-target damage
records.survival: Defense/healing must keep recipients alive long enough for readers to pay off
records.spatial_condition: Formation controls which unit receives enemy and friendly damage first
records.payoff_owner: Supplier owns friendly damage; event owns count; reader owns buff; attacker owns final output
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Add deliberate damage suppliers only after enough survival and readers exist.
records.counterplay: Burst, poison, seven-hit counters and event-order truncation punish excess proc density.
records.failure_explanation: Show supplier, recipient survival, reader trigger count and any threshold counter advanced.
records.transferability: Defense-to-offense should be an explicit event reader, not an implicit property of Shield or Health.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not infer that all damage taken, Shield loss or healing automatically grants attack.
records.project_question: Which project defensive events may be read for offense, at what rate and by whom?

records.version_scope: formal 1.0 Guide through official 1.1 nerf and post-1.1 player criticism
records.rule_support: Japanese suppliers grant Spiritual Power that scales other Japanese abilities; 1.1 states the mythology was far stronger and more consistent, then moves tiers and narrows several SP/stat effects.
records.practical_support: The Guide recommends early SP, high-tier cores and continued SP cycling, while post-patch reviewers still prefer Japanese or ranged answers against several hard counters.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Post-1.1 player rankings are individual observations and do not prove the official nerf failed or give current usage rates.
records.mechanism: A shared faction resource multiplies many readers and therefore couples supply density, tier access and consistency.
records.engine: SP suppliers, Japanese readers, Pantheon tiers and recruitment cycling
records.state_resource: Spiritual Power, available Japanese Gods, reader count, tier and run tempo
records.trigger: Acquire an SP supplier or a Japanese ability reads current SP
records.scope: Eligible Japanese abilities rather than every unit
records.payoff: High and consistent scaling across multiple owners
records.survival: Early SP power helps preserve run shields while reaching high-tier readers
records.spatial_condition: Individual readers still require legal formation and target access
records.payoff_owner: Supplier owns SP; each God owns its read; final actor owns damage/control
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Pivot after an early SP/core signal; stop rolling when tier and reader density cannot repay the pool cost.
records.counterplay: Tier delay, pool denial, direct damage and mythology-specific nerfs break the shared resource chain.
records.failure_explanation: Report SP supply, active readers, tier timing and which nerf changed the expected output.
records.transferability: Faction resources need supply/read ratios, tier windows and consistency controls.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy Japanese theme or treat post-patch opinion as a current tier statistic.
records.project_question: How many suppliers and readers should a project faction resource support before it becomes self-compounding?

records.version_scope: Guide, early developer economy rationale and formal shield-display fix
records.rule_support: Run shields absorb campaign losses and enable greedier tiering, while Ethereal Shield and Aegis/Sacred Barrier are combat or relic protection with separately fixed display state.
records.practical_support: The developer argues that more run shields would trivialize early power-leveling, while a launch reviewer reports that one lost shield sharply constrains further greed.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The exact current number/source of run and combat shields is not documented here; similarly named protection cannot be added together without an owner.
records.mechanism: Meta loss tolerance and per-combat mitigation are different resources even when both are represented as shields.
records.engine: Run-loss shield, combat Ethereal Shield, Relic/Blessing protection and display
records.state_resource: Remaining run failures, combat barrier layers, source, duration and display state
records.trigger: Lose a fight, receive a barrier, absorb a hit or render shield UI
records.scope: Run progression versus a named combat recipient
records.payoff: Economic greed or combat uptime through separately priced safety
records.survival: Both preserve continuation but at different phases and against different failure types
records.spatial_condition: Combat barriers still depend on target/order; run shields have no battlefield position
records.payoff_owner: Mode owns run shield; effect owns combat barrier; recipient owns protected state
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Spend run tolerance on tier greed only when the next enemy and recovery path justify it.
records.counterplay: A lost round consumes run tolerance; poison/direct damage or barrier removal attack combat protection.
records.failure_explanation: Name whether the failed layer was run life, barrier generation, display or target coverage.
records.transferability: Use different ids and UI for campaign lives and combat shields.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not treat every shield as one stack or as automatic damage conversion.
records.project_question: Which project safety resources belong to the run layer versus the battle layer?

records.version_scope: Next Fest Blessing introduction through 1.0 compatibility fixes and 1.1 Relic/Blessing rebalance
records.rule_support: Blessings add tiered run modifiers; Relics can alter mythology/pool/economy or grant standalone rules, and official updates remove incompatible offers, add eight Relics and rebalance multiple tiers/effects.
records.practical_support: Players distinguish pool-correction, event-doubling and economy Relics from weak flat bonuses, and report buy/sell busywork when a rule rewards every recruitment action.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No complete current Relic/Blessing table or offer odds exist; forum rankings do not establish universal value.
records.mechanism: A run modifier is a slot/offer owner that rewrites eligibility, event cadence or resource conversion rather than merely adding stats.
records.engine: Relic selection, Blessing tiers, pool filter, mythology substitution and event multipliers
records.state_resource: Selected modifier, tier, eligible mythologies, excluded conflicts, trigger count and Essence
records.trigger: Run start, Blessing milestone, acquisition, recruitment or end recruitment
records.scope: Run, army, eligible mythology, named God or event family as written
records.payoff: New build access, corrected odds, multiplied events or economy
records.survival: Defensive Relics can buy uptime but compete with scaling and pool correction
records.spatial_condition: Rule rewrites may change who can be fielded but do not erase formation constraints
records.payoff_owner: Relic/Blessing owns rewrite; source event retains lineage; God owns resulting action
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Select a rewrite only when its reachable pool and trigger family match the current core.
records.counterplay: Eligibility filters, mutual exclusions, caps and enemy packages prevent dead or universal modifiers.
records.failure_explanation: Show modifier owner, eligible sources, excluded conflict and actual proc count.
records.transferability: Relic pools need compatibility validation and visible opportunity cost.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy exact Relics, tiers or assume every modifier is team-wide.
records.project_question: How will project relics declare rule scope and reject mutually destructive combinations?

records.version_scope: formal 1.0 fixes with post-1.1 community overflow and transfer reports
records.rule_support: Official fixes cover Primordial Echo order, Fury/First Strike interleaving, Anu/Tezcatlipoca modifier integration, dismissed Echo Elemental and Sacrificial Shade resolution.
records.practical_support: Players later report unresolved transfer targeting, an opaque Loki/Odin feedback loop and Essence recursion exceeding numeric range, showing distinct targeting, ordering and overflow risks.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Community cases lack internal logs; the Loki case is unreproduced and no public post-1.1 patch confirms current Sacrificial Shade or overflow status.
records.mechanism: Automatic effect chains need deterministic target snapshots, queue priority, recursion guards and saturating numeric behavior.
records.engine: Target selector, event queue, replay/multiplier, removal/transfer transaction and numeric accumulator
records.state_resource: Pending triggers, selected target, source lineage, recursion depth, current/max value and overflow state
records.trigger: Simultaneous damage, First Strike/Fury, remove-and-transfer, end recruitment or Essence carryover
records.scope: One transaction and all downstream readers
records.payoff: Reliable combo execution without lost state, phantom interleaving or wrapped values
records.survival: Correct transaction order prevents accidental team deletion or skipped defensive response
records.spatial_condition: Target slot/order is snapshotted before removal and summon change formation
records.payoff_owner: Effect owns transaction; resolver owns order/guard; recipient owns committed state
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Do not encourage recursive builds until preview shows caps and legal targets.
records.counterplay: Caps, once-per-event guards, exclusion sets and saturating values bound multiplicative chains.
records.failure_explanation: Log target snapshot, queue order, recursion depth, accepted/rejected repeats and overflow clamp.

records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not assert the game's internal cause or current bug status from player symptoms.
records.project_question: Which project event chains require recursion budgets or saturating arithmetic from day one?

records.version_scope: formal 1.0 Guide with launch and post-1.1 counter-practice
records.rule_support: Horror campaigns expose distinct Cleave, combat scaling, death/summon, poison/reflect, direct-damage, attack-debuff and mixed-wave packages, with the final Boss known from run start.
records.practical_support: Players use weak cleave soaks, right-side sniping, disposable summons, First Strike, Ethereal Shield, direct damage and fewer units as package-specific answers, but report missing key counters after commit.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The Guide claims broad access through borrowing, while reviews report hard counter dependence; no offer-weighted clear rates resolve the disagreement.
records.mechanism: An enemy package attacks one or more build links and is fair only when its required response is previewed before the pivot window closes.
records.engine: Campaign roster, next-wave preview, final-Boss preview and formation counter rules
records.state_resource: Known enemy effects, available counters, remaining recruitment turns, formation slots and run shields
records.trigger: Choose a Horror, preview the next wave or reach a package breakpoint
records.scope: Whole run plan and current formation
records.payoff: Replace blind stat racing with targeted adaptation
records.survival: Different packages require bodies, defense, barriers, healing or reduced proc density
records.spatial_condition: Cleave, taunt, rightmost/backline, First Strike and summon order are primary counters
records.payoff_owner: Enemy owns test; preview owns information; counter unit owns response; carry owns finish
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Reserve a slot/Essence budget for the known package and pivot before the missing answer becomes unobtainable.
records.counterplay: Counter availability and multiple valid response classes prevent a puzzle from collapsing to one card.
records.failure_explanation: Name the tested link, preview timing, available answers and why the selected response failed.
records.transferability: Build enemy packages around explicit links and adaptation windows.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy exact Horrors or treat individual frustration as a measured impossibility.
records.project_question: How early must each tower enemy-package counter be previewed relative to recruitment lock-in?

records.version_scope: formal Guide, 1.0 counter fix and 1.1 Norse matchup adjustment
records.rule_support: Cthulhu kills the opposing army after taking seven damage instances, heals surviving fighters for part of damage and pairs with attack debuffs; 1.0 fixes counter reset and 1.1 changes Heimdall specifically to help Norse.
records.practical_support: The Guide advises counting procs, using fewer Gods or heavier single hits, while players note Nian Spellcast can delay damage until one large payoff.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact healing/debuff values and all counter reset timings are not generalized beyond the sourced Guide/patch wording.
records.mechanism: A low-damage Boss converts proc density into a lethal resource race and reverses the value of multi-hit engines.
records.engine: Damage-instance counter, reset/animation, healing environment and attack debuffs
records.state_resource: Damage instances, remaining threshold, hit size, army count and in-combat Attack
records.trigger: Cthulhu takes damage and the counter reaches seven
records.scope: Boss threshold and whole opposing army
records.payoff: Rewards low-frequency high-impact output and deliberate unit-count reduction
records.survival: Keeping units alive is irrelevant if the damage-instance threshold fires first
records.spatial_condition: Formation controls which few Gods survive long enough to deliver large hits
records.payoff_owner: Each attacker owns an instance; Boss owns counter/clear; report owns remaining threshold
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Reduce incidental attackers or pivot to Spellcast/single-hit scaling before the final fight.
records.counterplay: In-combat Attack gain, fewer bodies and one-shot capable carries avoid feeding the threshold.
records.failure_explanation: Show which sources advanced the counter and why the seventh instance resolved.
records.transferability: Bosses can counter cadence rather than raw damage, but must expose the counter clearly.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy instant army kill without readable threshold and multiple response paths.
records.project_question: Which project bosses should test hit cadence, and how will the report attribute every counted hit?

records.version_scope: launch Guide/practice through 2026 post-1.1 reviews
records.rule_support: The Guide says to play offered strength, wait for key pieces before committing and pivot into strong cross-mythology opportunities.
records.practical_support: One high-playtime reviewer values forced improvisation, while another reports repeated Boss losses after the pool stops supplying a committed deck beyond its pivot window.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The opposite experiences may reflect difficulty, seed, skill or build choice; no pool odds, run logs or population data isolate causality.
records.mechanism: Build variety depends on reachable bridges and recovery timing, not only the theoretical number of combinations.
records.engine: Random mythology set, tiered Pantheon offers, reroll, freeze, discover and bridge Gods
records.state_resource: Current core, available tags, key pieces, remaining turns, Essence and run shields
records.trigger: A strong core/bridge appears, a tier unlocks or repeated misses consume the pivot window
records.scope: Roster plan and economy
records.payoff: Adaptation that preserves current value while opening a counter-ready end state
records.survival: Temporary tempo units prevent a pivot from dying before it pays back
records.spatial_condition: A bridge must fit army/bench and formation needs, not only ability text
records.payoff_owner: Pool owns availability; player owns commit; bridge owns cross-system read; carry owns payoff
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Use multi-signal commitment and define a latest safe abandonment point.
records.counterplay: Pool correction, tagless tempo and transferable equipment reduce forced dead runs.
records.failure_explanation: Distinguish a bad commit, unavailable bridge, late tier, insufficient correction and enemy counter.
records.transferability: Measure practical reachability and pivot recovery, not catalogue breadth alone.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not claim either forcing or improvisation is universally optimal.
records.project_question: What project offers preserve a viable fallback after a specialized core fails to appear?

records.version_scope: Demo ladder-loss debate through formal Casual QoL and 1.1 offer observation
records.rule_support: The developer split experimentation from Ladder consistency pressure, formal QoL unlocks Casual difficulty from the start, and Ladder retains outcome-linked progression.
records.practical_support: Reviewers describe Ladder demotion and short runs, while a 1.1 player observes the next mythology/Relic set remains fixed until a result changes it and Casual can use Star Chart.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The exact current set-refresh and tie rules are not officially documented; one review's tie observation is not promoted to a rule.
records.mechanism: Competitive consistency and build experimentation require different loss contracts even in a single-player game.
records.engine: Ladder rank, Casual difficulty, outcome state, unlock-all option and run seed/offer set
records.state_resource: Highest difficulty, current rank, selected Horror, locked offers and experimental goal
records.trigger: Win, lose, restart or switch modes
records.scope: Meta progression rather than combat resolution
records.payoff: A place to test builds without devaluing ranked consistency
records.survival: Short runs lower time loss but do not replace explicit experimentation safety
records.spatial_condition: None beyond the selected combat formation; this is a meta contract
records.payoff_owner: Mode owns rank/loss; seed owns offers; player owns experimentation choice
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Use Casual to learn a new engine and Ladder only when the build's fallback/counter plan is understood.
records.counterplay: Separate records, selectable unlocked difficulty and clear seed semantics reduce punishment ambiguity.
records.failure_explanation: State whether the loss changed rank, offer set, unlock or only the current run.
records.transferability: Separate learning and mastery modes when failure costs would suppress experimentation.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy demotion or hidden seed-lock behavior into baseline project runs.
records.project_question: How can the project reward mastery without discouraging first-time build experiments?

records.version_scope: official 1.1 Infinity introduction with post-1.1 2025–2026 observations
records.rule_support: 1.1 adds post-clear Infinity with rising difficulty and new Relics, but publishes no round curve, numeric cap or recursion guard.
records.practical_support: One player reports difficulty ending most builds within two or three rounds, while others describe Anu/end-recruitment multiplication driving Essence or stats into wraparound values.
records.disagreement_or_limit: These are different builds and dates; no official follow-up proves frequency, exact limits, persistence or current bug status.
records.mechanism: Endless mode must coordinate enemy escalation, player compounding, numeric saturation and anti-stalemate rules.
records.engine: Infinity round scaling, Essence carryover, end-recruitment multipliers, stat growth and numeric storage
records.state_resource: Round, enemy power, player stats, Essence, recursion count, cap and overflow state
records.trigger: Continue after a clear, end recruitment or multiply carried state
records.scope: Post-clear run and all persistent numeric owners
records.payoff: Extended expression of a completed build without immediate wall or technical wraparound
records.survival: Enemy escalation should test the build before arithmetic invalidates its state
records.spatial_condition: Formation remains relevant only while scaling does not overwhelm all counters
records.payoff_owner: Infinity owns escalation; each effect owns growth; numeric layer owns cap/overflow policy
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Offer new counter decisions rather than only multiplying both sides until one overflows.
records.counterplay: Diminishing returns, hard caps, recursion budgets and anti-stalemate enemies bound growth.
records.failure_explanation: Report round scaling, capped sources, overflow prevention and the first failed build link.
records.transferability: Endless systems require explicit number policy and matched progression curves.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not infer current bugs, exact integer types or adopt unbounded exponential loops.
records.project_question: What project caps and escalation schedule preserve meaningful late-run decisions?

records.version_scope: Demo and formal launch complaints, official 1.0 fixes, 1.1 rebalance and later reviews
records.rule_support: 1.1 officially identifies Japanese dominance, buffs underperforming mythologies and adjusts Gods, Relics and Blessings after formal trigger/pool fixes.
records.practical_support: Players across versions report large faction/relic gaps, hard poison/reflect checks, late missing cores and Sacrificial Shade failures, while other high-playtime reviews still value improvisation and short recovery.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No statistics establish post-1.1 faction strength, bug incidence or whether difficulty complaints arise from balance, reachability or knowledge.
records.mechanism: A theoretical build library fails in practice when core reachability, counter availability, payoff timing and resolver integrity diverge.
records.engine: Faction pool, tier curve, Relic/Blessing offers, enemy packages, pivot window and effect resolver
records.state_resource: Available cores, bridge count, counter coverage, run shields, payoff turn and known defects
records.trigger: Balance patch, pool miss, Boss gate or non-resolving effect
records.scope: Whole build ecosystem and player diagnosis
records.payoff: Multiple reachable ways to answer each package without erasing faction identity
records.survival: Tempo, run tolerance and defensive links provide time to assemble rather than guarantee success
records.spatial_condition: Ranged/backline/cleave/poison answers must remain positionally meaningful
records.payoff_owner: Patch owns rule change; pool owns reachability; build owns output; report owns failure attribution
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Balance should evaluate complete routes and fallback windows, not isolated maximum stats.
records.counterplay: Bridge pieces, pool correction, multiple counter classes and resolver tests reduce non-games.
records.failure_explanation: Separate balance gap, unlucky pool, late commitment, hard counter and execution defect.
records.transferability: Validate systems through reachable builds against enemy packages and lifecycle regressions.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not convert community tier lists into current facts or copy any concrete content.
records.project_question: Which project test matrix jointly measures build reachability, counter coverage and payoff timing?

records.version_scope: EA v1.6/v1.16/v1.20, formal v2.0.0/v2.0.10 and current v2.1–v2.1.2 nodes
records.rule_support: Official nodes establish two Rune Circle redesigns, formal v2.0.0 and a v2.1 rebuild of Runes, Artifacts, skills and professions.
records.practical_support: Guides and discussions span these eras and repeatedly require old build instructions to be retained only as historical structures.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The public latest hotfix is v2.1.2, but no complete current data table or usage statistics map every effect after the rebuild.
records.mechanism: A build claim remains valid only across the version nodes that preserve its engine, reader and ownership chain.
records.engine: Official release and rework timeline plus source publication dates
records.state_resource: Observed version, season, changed systems and superseded claims
records.trigger: A Rune, Artifact, skill, class or acquisition rule is replaced or rebalanced
records.scope: All guides, formulas and build-strength claims
records.payoff: Retain transferable structure without presenting obsolete execution as current meta
records.survival: Version labels prevent a player from relying on a removed defensive or growth link
records.spatial_condition: Formation advice is versioned separately from underlying unit and item changes
records.payoff_owner: Official patch owns rule state; each secondary source owns its observed-period claim

records.transferability: Build research needs explicit lifecycle nodes instead of one timeless tier list.

records.version_scope: formal v2.0 loop cross-checked by maintained pages and 2026 reviews
records.rule_support: The game manages an expanding roster of up to ten independently equipped dwarves whose professions, equipment, Runes, Artifacts and Formation shape automatic combat.
records.practical_support: Independent reviews describe repeated roster/equipment decisions and preparation as the primary agency rather than direct attack control.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Current offer odds, full prices, target logic and exact expansion schedule and scaling are not reproduced here.
records.mechanism: A capped, progressively expanded roster becomes a build through independently owned equipment and team-level Formation rules.
records.engine: Roster expansion up to ten active slots, professions, equipment, Runes, Artifacts, Tavern and Formation
records.state_resource: Dwarf identity, gear slots, growth, role, formation requirement and replacement cost
records.trigger: Recruit, replace, equip, upgrade, select Formation or enter battle
records.scope: One dwarf, the currently unlocked active squad, capped at ten, and the current run
records.payoff: Role-specialized automatic combat with meaningful pre-battle ownership
records.survival: Tank, healer and protection owners buy uptime for separate damage owners
records.spatial_condition: Front/back placement, targeting and Formation threshold determine whether the equipped role executes
records.payoff_owner: Dwarf owns mutable growth; item/Rune/Artifact owns rule; Formation owns team modifier; attacker owns damage
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Compare a veteran's accumulated state against a recruit's profession and future growth before replacing.
records.counterplay: Boss resistances, targeting and displacement can invalidate a role even when its raw equipment is strong.
records.failure_explanation: Attribute failure to roster role, owner mismatch, formation, target access or insufficient growth rather than generic power.
records.transferability: Keep unit, item, team-rule and final-output owners separate in a roster autobattler.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy the ten-unit cap or expansion schedule, professions or exact equipment packages into the project.
records.project_question: Which project preparation surfaces expose unit owner, team rule and final damage owner at a glance?

records.version_scope: v1.6 replacement, v1.16 second redesign, v2.0 expansion and v2.1 supersession

records.version_scope: v2.0.x Forge Demon practice and maintained v2.0.10-like data; historical after v2.1

records.version_scope: v2.0.10 maintained rules and developer/community clarification

records.practical_support: Players actively calculate Block sources and Thorns interactions, exposing the need to distinguish chance, prevented value and retaliation owner.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact current source values after v2.1 are not generalized from the older database/thread.

records.engine: Block chance/cap, incoming hit, prevented-damage result and Vengeance reader
records.state_resource: Block chance, cap, qualifying attack, prevented damage, Frozen state and reader cooldown/rules

records.spatial_condition: Frontline exposure supplies attempts while target/range determines retaliation reach

records.version_scope: v2.0.10-like Scarab Brooch rules with v2.0 practice and pre-v2.1 growth observations

records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact current proc chance/value after v2.1 and whether overheal contributes are not asserted.

records.spatial_condition: Healing/propagation range and recipient placement determine who enters the window

records.version_scope: formal v1.0.0.2-v1.0.0.5, Chaos launch and August 2024 practice
records.rule_support: One character may have at most eight owned summons active; Chaos fixed summon bond eligibility and an infinite-unit acquisition case, while some units summon on death.
records.practical_support: Players use Bard/Light Elf summons as backline decoys, yet a long-play review argues the available summoners were too sparse to support a dedicated summon/ice-card route.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No full current summon roster, duration, occupancy or inheritance table is public.
records.mechanism: Per-owner summon cap, board occupancy, bond eligibility and supplier density jointly determine whether a summon system becomes a build.
records.engine: Summoner, spawn event, per-owner count, active body, bond eligibility and death/decoy role
records.state_resource: Owner id, active summon count, available cells/rows, inherited effects and supplier availability
records.trigger: Skill/death creates a summon while owner count is below eight
records.scope: One summoner's temporary bodies plus team targeting space
records.payoff: Extra bodies, distraction or inherited combat contribution
records.survival: Summons may absorb backline pressure but are not permanent roster Health
records.spatial_condition: Spawned bodies consume target/space attention and can shield rear rows
records.payoff_owner: Summoner owns cap; summon owns body/death; bond owns eligibility; target system owns aggro
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Verify multiple accessible suppliers and support readers before committing to a summon-only route.
records.counterplay: AOE, anti-summon targeting, cap pressure, spawn denial and bond exclusion bound the system.
records.failure_explanation: Report owner count, blocked spawn reason, placement, inherited bonds and target impact.
records.transferability: A population guard is necessary but cannot substitute for sufficient build supply.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy cap eight or assume every temporary body counts as a roster slot.
records.project_question: What summon supplier density, occupancy and inheritance rules make a viable but bounded project route?

records.version_scope: historical v1.0.0.9 converter through November 2024 defense reworks
records.rule_support: Stone Defense explicitly reads owned physical/magic Defense into damage, while Holy Prayer invulnerability, Guardian team damage reduction and Shield suppliers were changed as separate effects.
records.practical_support: Players distinguish nine-Stone retaliation, thick Shield/healing walls, death-fight invulnerability and ranged burst as different ways to survive or finish.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Community shorthand such as nine-shield does not prove that Shield itself is the Stone converter input.
records.mechanism: Health, Shield, damage reduction, invulnerability and Defense remain separate survival states; only a named reader converts one into output.
records.engine: Survival supplier, state owner, hit/threshold reader, converter and final damage event
records.state_resource: Health, Shield amount, Defense, damage reduction, invulnerability duration, Guard and lineage
records.trigger: Gain state, receive a hit, cross Guard threshold or start a protection window
records.scope: Declared wearer/team and affected enemy area
records.payoff: Defensive uptime or bounded defense-derived retaliation without implicit universal conversion
records.survival: Each defensive layer remains independently targetable and reportable
records.spatial_condition: Contact and nearby range matter for Stone retaliation; backline Shield does not inherit that output
records.payoff_owner: Supplier owns state; Stone owns conversion; protected carry owns its own attacks
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A defense-output route consumes bond/transfer/card slots that compete with a separate ranged finisher.
records.counterplay: Range, true damage, anti-heal, defense break, burst before protection and cap rules attack different layers.
records.failure_explanation: List each survival source, converter eligibility, trigger count and final output owner.
records.transferability: Defense-to-offense should be authored as a visible bridge, not a hidden property of Shield.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not collapse Shield, Defense, invulnerability and damage reduction or give their sum to any carry by default.
records.project_question: Which project relic or equipment explicitly bridges team defense to a named damage owner?

records.version_scope: March-November 2024 rule and practice slices
records.rule_support: Official rules distinguish bleeding physical, lightning/fire/poison magic, true damage, Frozen supply and status-linked readers; June fixes show these effects can resolve incorrectly.
records.practical_support: The Cold Touch route deliberately supplies Frozen before Shatter, while players use true damage and grievous wounds against shield/heal packages rather than treating all damage as one axis.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Current resistance formulas, stack duration and every card's final scope are unpublished.
records.mechanism: Affinity/damage type, applied status and payoff reader are orthogonal axes joined only by explicit effects.
records.engine: Damage source/type, status supplier, target state, reader and resistance/cleanse
records.state_resource: Frozen, bleed or mark state; damage type; stack/source; duration; target resistance
records.trigger: Apply status, attack, cast reader or satisfy a named threshold
records.scope: Declared targets and sources only
records.payoff: Control, true/magic/physical damage, defense break or a later detonation
records.survival: Shield/Defense mitigate according to their own rules and do not become an element
records.spatial_condition: Range, target cluster and target access govern supply/read coverage
records.payoff_owner: Supplier owns status; reader owns conversion; attacker/card owns final event
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Invest in a status reader only when suppliers, target access and counter coverage are reachable.
records.counterplay: Cleanse, immunity, resistance, spacing and source removal address different links.
records.failure_explanation: Report source, type, applied state, resisted/cleansed amount and reader result.
records.transferability: Elements should be event chains rather than color labels on generic damage.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not name an Ice Shield to imply Frozen supply or infer true damage from a tooltip mismatch.
records.project_question: Which project element/status chains have distinct supply, read, cleanse and resistance owners?

records.version_scope: Chaos launch and v1.0.1.5 hotfix with later DLC practice
records.rule_support: Chaos ties selectable Chaos value to difficulty/opportunity, adds Chaos currency, corrupted gear, enemy recruitment and enslaved Bosses; two days later prices/difficulty fell and rewards rose.
records.practical_support: Players report needing zero-cost cards, nine-Archer or nine-Stone routes for DLC walls and describe hidden-Boss access/recruitment as reachability problems rather than mere listed content.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No run statistics establish whether the first rebalance fully fixed the risk/reward curve.
records.mechanism: A difficulty scalar becomes a build system only when its exclusive currency, offers and Boss gates remain reachable within the same risk budget.
records.engine: Chaos value, Chaos currency, corrupted equipment, enslaved Boss offer, prices and encounter scaling
records.state_resource: Chosen risk, currency earned, offer refresh cost, acquired enemy/Boss and survival margin
records.trigger: Raise/lower Chaos, win encounter, shop/refresh or reach the final gate
records.scope: Chaos run and its exclusive pool
records.payoff: Higher-risk access to distinct units/equipment rather than only larger numbers
records.survival: Extra resources must arrive early enough to fund counters before difficulty spikes
records.spatial_condition: Enemy/Boss additions still consume roles and battlefield positions
records.payoff_owner: Mode owns risk/reward; shop owns offers; enslaved unit owns combat effect
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Preview final Chaos gate and allow a feasible switch between unit, gear and Boss acquisition.
records.counterplay: Price pressure, encounter spike and incompatible exclusive pieces keep risk meaningful.
records.failure_explanation: Separate insufficient Chaos, missed currency, expensive refresh, bad encounter match and build execution.
records.transferability: Risk modes need jointly tuned difficulty, acquisition cost and distinct payoff.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy Chaos values or infer that more exclusive content guarantees depth.
records.project_question: How will project difficulty modifiers fund counter access rather than only inflate enemy stats?

records.version_scope: formal launch through current rules and 2026 card practice
records.rule_support: Followers equip items, relics apply broader rules, cards have quality/sockets/cost and Mercenary sacrifice once incorrectly removed equipment; reforge and card-course limits are separately owned.
records.practical_support: Current players prioritize cost-reduction relics and specific gem combinations, while current reviews describe three follower equipment slots and exclusive equipment rewrites.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No complete current item/relic/card table or stacking order is published.
records.mechanism: Items, relics, card gems and unit passives modify different owners and transaction phases despite all appearing as build rewards.
records.engine: Follower equipment slot, team/run relic, card socket/gem, reforge and sacrifice/merge transaction
records.state_resource: Item owner, slot, quality, socket, effect source, equipped state and transaction boundary
records.trigger: Equip, socket, reforge, sacrifice, merge or cast
records.scope: Wearer, team/run, card or qualifying target as declared
records.payoff: Composable rules with auditable ownership and opportunity cost
records.survival: Defensive item/relic can buy time without owning card or carry damage
records.spatial_condition: Wearer placement and card scope determine realization
records.payoff_owner: Unit owns equipment state; relic owns run rule; gem owns card rewrite; effect source owns output
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Reserve scarce slots only after the build's reader and mode source are credible.
records.counterplay: Disarm/owner death, slot pressure, mode exclusion and transaction loss attack different assets.
records.failure_explanation: Show pre/post owner, effect source, slot, socket and any loss during transfer/sacrifice.
records.transferability: Build surfaces need explicit ownership and transaction receipts.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not treat every reward as a global passive or copy exact slot counts.
records.project_question: Which project rewards belong to hero, team, run, tactical command or meta account?

records.version_scope: Chaos/Decottini-era reports through current structure
records.rule_support: Official systems offer rerolls, quality/bond filters, town upgrades and adjusted Chaos prices but publish no complete pity or exclusion model.
records.practical_support: Players use occupation filters and cheap town merges to reach carries, yet report unlocked/locked pool pollution, hard bond thresholds, rare relic misses and explicit component-heavy build costs.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Individual frustration and successful high-hour routes do not establish an objective failure rate.
records.mechanism: A listed synergy becomes a practical build only when unit, transfer, item, card/gem and Boss deadlines align within the economy.
records.engine: Shop pool, reroll, level odds, Mercenary filter, route rewards, relic/card pools and deadline
records.state_resource: Gold/silver, missing links, remaining fights, current owner investment and fallback pieces
records.trigger: Repeated miss, filter/refresh, level-up, irreversible transfer or Boss approach
records.scope: Whole acquisition plan
records.payoff: Reach a coherent engine or credible fallback without deterministic forcing
records.survival: Bridge units/cards keep the run alive while the final reader is absent
records.spatial_condition: A reached unit still needs a legal role and target access
records.payoff_owner: Pool owns availability; player owns commit; transfer owns lock; build owns payoff
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Use multi-signal commitment and declare the latest safe pivot when key modifiers fail to appear.
records.counterplay: Pity, filtering, bridge pieces and transparent source tables reduce dead rerolls without guaranteeing exact builds.
records.failure_explanation: Separate bad offers, wrong level, pool pollution, late pivot, locked transfer and execution loss.
records.transferability: Evaluate build reachability across all required component types.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not claim the shop cheats or make every route forceable.
records.project_question: What project pool correction keeps shield/element bridges reachable while preserving uncertainty?

records.version_scope: formal launch through June 2024 Decottini fixes
records.rule_support: Official notes fixed failed casts, sacrifice equipment loss, freeze-card hangs, Cold Touch no-damage and Shattered Wound healing; players separately reported undisclosed status and scope mismatches.
records.practical_support: These defects break complete builds at input, transaction, status, target-scope and payoff-resolution layers rather than through balance alone.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Some community tooltip reports have no official resolution, so their current state is unknown.
records.mechanism: Every build link requires deterministic event ownership, valid targets, transaction safety and a visible failure reason.
records.engine: Input queue, mana transaction, card resolver, status store, target scope, equipment transaction and report UI
records.state_resource: Queued action, paid cost, source/target, status, owner, pre/post equipment and error reason
records.trigger: Cast, sacrifice, apply status, resolve damage/heal or change owner
records.scope: One event chain and affected owners
records.payoff: Correct, attributable combat and progression results
records.survival: Defensive casts must resolve before lethal damage under a declared ordering rule
records.spatial_condition: Target validity and area are rechecked at resolution
records.payoff_owner: Root action owns descendants; each modifier retains source lineage; transaction owns state change
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Do not punish a strategic commitment for an unreported resolver or persistence defect.
records.counterplay: Legal immunity/invalid target is distinct from silent failure or wrong effect type.
records.failure_explanation: Display cost, queue order, actual target/scope, applied state, final event and error category.
records.transferability: Determinism requires reporting and transaction tests, not only fixed RNG.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not reinterpret historical bugs as intended mechanics or assume all were fixed.
records.project_question: Which project event-chain assertions and combat-report fields catch silent build-link failures?

records.version_scope: launch-era Endless through 2025 mode observations
records.rule_support: Official patches repeatedly adjusted early Endless difficulty, added curses and scaling Dominion Flags after floor 80.
records.practical_support: Historical builds reached 183-340 and one high-hour account reports a floor-600 completion cap; later players report Adventure card/gem engines absent from Endless, forcing roster-centric scaling.
records.disagreement_or_limit: These periods differ and no current official floor curve, cap or build distribution is public.
records.mechanism: Long-run scaling tests whether damage, survival, counter access, input burden and component availability remain diverse across floors.
records.engine: Floor curve, curse/flag package, mode pool, permanent growth, unit/card scaling and end condition
records.state_resource: Floor, damage type, mitigation, carry growth, available suppliers, input rate and remaining counters
records.trigger: Cross floor thresholds, meet Boss package or lose access to a required scaling link
records.scope: Endless run and its mature build ecosystem
records.payoff: Sustain multiple long-run identities until a declared endpoint
records.survival: Shield/heal/decoys buy time but cannot replace escalating output and counter coverage
records.spatial_condition: Backline access and flag carriers remain relevant even at high raw stats
records.payoff_owner: Mode owns escalation/cap; build sources own growth; player/unit/card owns output
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Offer sidegrades and counters before floor packages invalidate an irreversible build.
records.counterplay: Damage-type flags, energy execute, anti-sustain, backline access and explicit caps prevent one-axis scaling.
records.failure_explanation: Report floor package, missing legal source, first failed link, input bottleneck and cap/end state.
records.transferability: Endless design needs explicit endpoint, mode pool and convergence monitoring.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy floor 600 or merge launch and 2025 scaling.
records.project_question: How will project tower depth preserve build diversity without turning one loop or permanent stat into the sole answer?

records.version_scope: cross-version structure bounded by current low-cost practice and post-November Cold Touch evidence
records.rule_support: Stone Defense explicitly converts Defense after hit thresholds, while Shield, damage reduction, invulnerability, Frozen and card cost/return remain separately authored rules.
records.practical_support: Current card loops, post-rework Cold Touch and historical Stone/Archer answers use distinct suppliers, readers, survival shells and final output owners.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The sources do not contain the proposed project-wide bonus-Health/Defense-to-carry formula or prove any one route is current meta.
records.mechanism: Defense, element/status and tactical-card axes stay independent until a named bridge reads one state and grants a bounded payoff to a declared owner.
records.engine: State supplier, reader/converter, recipient, item/relic/card owner, slot/cost and final event
records.state_resource: Health/Shield/Defense, Frozen/status, card cost, source lineage, cap, duration and recipient
records.trigger: Receive hits, apply/read status, cast a command or satisfy an explicit bridge event
records.scope: Declared wearer, team aggregate, one carry, card or qualifying source set
records.payoff: Multiple system identities plus controlled cross-axis builds
records.survival: Defense continues to buy uptime and remains counterable separately from damage
records.spatial_condition: Contact, formation, target access and effect range determine whether a bridge realizes value
records.payoff_owner: Supplier owns state; converter owns read; recipient/card owns granted output; attacker owns final damage
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Spend a scarce slot/transfer/card path only when supply, legal mode, recipient and counter window are credible.
records.counterplay: Shield break, defense break, status immunity/cleanse, backline access, mana denial and caps target different links.
records.failure_explanation: Show supplier totals, converter eligibility, mode legality, recipient gain and final damage attribution.
records.transferability: This supports separate shield and element systems with explicit equipment/relic bridges between them.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not redefine Shield by Ice/Earth labels, grant all team Defense to any shooter or reproduce an unbounded card loop.
records.project_question: Which first project bridges connect defense, element and carry output while preserving distinct counters and ownership?

records.version_scope: 2021-06 Early Access through 74.16 and the 2023-05-01 shutdown
records.rule_support: Official posts establish an Early Access launch, a 2022 roadmap that still treated public launch as future, a planned 2023 expansion, the last substantive 74.13 rule node and shutdown on 2023-05-01.
records.practical_support: The surviving historical archive permits period-specific build reconstruction but no current live meta.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No formal-release announcement or released Spooky Forest node was found; shutdown states only that there was no path forward and supplies no mechanical or commercial cause.
records.mechanism: Every build and rule is bounded by an Early Access patch window and a terminated service state.
records.engine: Official release, roadmap, patch, expansion-plan and shutdown timeline
records.state_resource: App identity, patch number, publication date, release label and server state
records.trigger: Launch, balance patch, announced content plan or shutdown
records.scope: All rules, builds, statistics and retrospective claims
records.payoff: Preserve historical mechanics without presenting planned or post-shutdown material as live content
records.survival: Version mapping prevents reliance on components removed before a build could execute
records.spatial_condition: Formation advice remains valid only where the relevant character and resolver rules coexist
records.payoff_owner: Official patch owns rule state; historical source owns only its observed period
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Revalidate every shop, hero, treasure and unit link at each patch boundary.
records.counterplay: Later official changes supersede older execution while leaving lifecycle evidence intact.
records.failure_explanation: Name the exact patch window and distinguish removed content, unshipped plans and server closure.
records.transferability: Research and combat reports need explicit version and availability boundaries.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not infer a formal launch, released expansion, current meta or shutdown cause.
records.project_question: How will project build records preserve rule-version and content-availability history?

records.version_scope: 2021 EA core loop with post-71.20 pool correction
records.rule_support: Historical rules document alternating Shop and Brawl phases, gold-funded purchases and rerolls, XP-driven levels, three-copy upgrades and same-level treasure choices with a three-treasure limit.
records.practical_support: The guide and long review describe locking offers, balancing levels against tempo, positioning seven characters and choosing when to pursue triples.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Early shared-pool copy counts are obsolete after 71.20 and exact late-EA odds are not reconstructed.
records.mechanism: One non-banking turn budget competes among bodies, spells, rerolls, XP and duplicate upgrades that open treasure choices.
records.engine: Shop offers, gold, reroll, lock, XP, triple upgrade and treasure cap
records.state_resource: Current gold, level, offer set, locked cards, pairs, board slots and treasure slots
records.trigger: Enter Shop, buy, reroll, lock, gain XP or complete three copies
records.scope: One player turn, roster and treasure inventory
records.payoff: Convert constrained offers into immediate tempo or a higher-ceiling engine
records.survival: Buying present stats preserves health while greedier XP and triple chases delay power
records.spatial_condition: A purchased character still needs one of seven legal combat positions
records.payoff_owner: Shop owns offers; unit owns upgrade; treasure owns persistent modifier; player owns spending
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Compare XP, rerolls, spells and a contested pair against the strongest affordable board each turn.
records.counterplay: Tempo pressure punishes speculative rerolls and delayed levels.
records.failure_explanation: Separate offer miss, overspending, missed upgrade, capped treasure and poor placement.
records.transferability: Recruitment currencies should expose immediate-strength versus engine opportunity cost.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy the old shared pool, exact prices or treasure count into the project.
records.project_question: Which project rewards compete directly with recruitment and when may offers be locked?

records.version_scope: 2021-2022 formation practice with 71.20 resolver refactor
records.rule_support: The archive describes seven positions, front/back ordering and start-of-brawl timing, while 71.20 officially revised simultaneous deaths, summons and vacancy handling.
records.practical_support: PVDDR explains first-attacker probability, slots 1-4 versus 5-7, protection, intentional empty slots and Copycat-specific placement costs.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The pre-71.20 timing page is historical and expert heuristics are not a complete resolver specification.
records.mechanism: A small ordered board makes attack access, protected readers, death timing and vacant cells explicit build resources.
records.engine: Seven slots, front/back rows, random first player, attack order and event queue
records.state_resource: Slot index, living unit, legal target, protected backline, empty cell and pending trigger
records.trigger: Start Brawl, choose first side, attack, die or summon
records.scope: One combat board and ordered event chain
records.payoff: Trade early activation against survival and reserve space for triggered effects
records.survival: Backline and sacrificial front slots protect delayed payoff owners
records.spatial_condition: Front four attack before protected rear three when legal; deliberate vacancies change adjacency and trigger access
records.payoff_owner: Unit owns attack/death trigger; slot owns access/order; resolver owns event sequencing
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A seventh body may be worse than an empty trigger lane, so board strength and occupancy are not identical.
records.counterplay: Backline damage, transformation and opposing order disrupt protected readers.
records.failure_explanation: Show initiative, slot order, target choice, death order, vacancy and canceled trigger.
records.transferability: Formation should alter event access and occupancy, not merely grant passive stats.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not import random initiative or this exact 4+3 board into deterministic project combat.
records.project_question: Which deterministic project ordering rules make sacrificial and protected slots equally legible?

records.version_scope: EA launch through 2022 roadmap-era rules
records.rule_support: The game separates a chosen Hero power, recruited characters, one-per-turn spell access, upgrades and treasures across Shop and Brawl phases.
records.practical_support: The hero guide treats Hero choice as a commitment that changes which engines are practical rather than making every offered unit equally valuable.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No complete final database or pick/win statistics establishes hero balance.
records.mechanism: A build joins several owners whose effects persist at different scopes and phases.
records.engine: Hero power, character card, spell, upgrade and treasure
records.state_resource: Hero rule, owned roster, spell entitlement, upgraded state and treasure slots
records.trigger: Choose Hero, buy character/spell, upgrade or enter combat
records.scope: Hero account, one unit, one Shop turn, team or combat event as declared
records.payoff: Layered build identity without treating every modifier as a unit stat
records.survival: Hero and treasure may buy setup time while units remain the bodies at risk
records.spatial_condition: Only characters occupy formation slots; Hero/spell/treasure effects require declared targets
records.payoff_owner: Each Hero, unit, spell and treasure retains its own effect lineage
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Hero direction informs purchases but should not justify forcing missing components indefinitely.

records.failure_explanation: Attribute each result to Hero, card, treasure, spell or placement.
records.transferability: Keep hero, equipment/relic, unit and tactical-command owners distinct.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy SBB Hero powers or PvP selection structure.
records.project_question: Which project systems modify offer space, team rules or individual heroes, and how are they labelled?

records.version_scope: post-61.1 through late-2022 historical archive
records.rule_support: Peter Pants stays at level 3 and converts each three XP into Shop-character growth; Merlin's Hat reduces Shop spell cost, Crystal Ball chains targeted spells, and Spell Weaver permanently gains attack when a spell is cast.
records.practical_support: Period guides combine early level-2/3 triples with Hat/Ball spell economy and a protected ranged Spell Weaver payoff.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No usage or win-rate data proves this was the unique late-EA best build, and Aon is not a normal Peter Shop component because Peter does not reach level 5.
records.mechanism: Fixed-level Shop scaling and spell-cost rewrites convert a normally temporary Shop budget into permanent backline attack growth.
records.engine: Peter XP conversion, Merlin's Hat discount, Crystal Ball replacement and Spell Weaver cast reader
records.state_resource: XP, Shop buffs, gold, spell entitlement, targeted-spell chain and permanent attack
records.trigger: Gain each three XP, buy/cast a qualifying spell or refresh the spell offer
records.scope: Peter's Shop, current turn spell chain and one/few carry units
records.payoff: Repeated affordable spells plus persistent ranged damage growth
records.survival: Growing low-level bodies and frontline purchases buy time for the backline reader
records.spatial_condition: Spell Weaver normally occupies a protected rear slot while frontline bodies absorb attacks
records.payoff_owner: Peter owns Shop growth; treasures own economy rewrites; Spell Weaver owns attack gain and attacks
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Use cheap pairs/upgrades to reach Hat/Ball, then compare each spell chain against buying or rerolling for board strength.
records.counterplay: Early tempo, missing Crystal Ball, exhausted gold and direct backline damage break distinct links.
records.failure_explanation: Report fixed-level growth, treasure reachability, spell eligibility/cost and the carry's survival.
records.transferability: A defensive shell can support a separate carry when a named relic/equipment bridge owns conversion.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not treat every spell as free, combine unreachable level-5 pieces or copy exact discounts.
records.project_question: Can project relics create an auditable temporary-resource-to-permanent-carry loop with a cap?

records.version_scope: 61.1 nerf through 71.20-71.25 community debate and late-EA observation

records.disagreement_or_limit: The sources demonstrate controversy and a reachability window, not a final tier ranking or representative prevalence.
records.mechanism: A high-ceiling engine remains conditional on treasure access, early board tempo and eligible repeatable inputs.
records.engine: Low-level treasure search, spell chain, healing/output payoff and opponent tempo
records.state_resource: Pairs, upgrades, treasure offer, gold, health, current board and missing engine link
records.trigger: Miss Crystal Ball, over-reroll, reach a damage round or receive an eligibility nerf
records.scope: Peter HatBall route and its observed patch window
records.payoff: Strong repeat casting only after several acquisition gates
records.survival: Early board strength must cover the time spent chasing engine treasures
records.spatial_condition: Backline payoff still needs protection after the economic engine assembles
records.payoff_owner: Treasure owns rewrite; carry owns output; balance patch owns removed interaction
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Do not force Mage until Hat/Ball and a credible carry appear; retain a tempo fallback.

records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not call the route universally dominant or restore nerfed The End access.
records.project_question: What project signals authorize commitment to a relic-dependent conversion build?

records.version_scope: 67.4-and-later Good Boy text with 2022 positioning practice
records.rule_support: Copycat triggers Last Breaths of characters behind it when attacking; Good Boy's post-67.4 Last Breath grants its stats to other Good characters only.
records.practical_support: PVDDR explains the trade between Copycat in slot 1 reading one rear unit and slot 2 reading two while risking death, while Good Boy often wants slot 1 to die early.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Pre-67.4 self-feedback footage or discussion is obsolete and no final-era win rate exists.
records.mechanism: An attack-trigger proxy reads a protected death effect, which transfers one source's stats to explicitly eligible allied recipients.
records.engine: Copycat attack trigger, rear Good Boy Last Breath and Good-recipient roster
records.state_resource: Slot, attack opportunity, Good Boy stats, alignment eligibility and surviving recipients
records.trigger: Copycat attacks or Good Boy dies
records.scope: Behind Copycat for trigger; other Good characters for stat grant
records.payoff: Repeat or accelerate a large team stat transfer
records.survival: Copycat must attack before dying while recipients survive long enough to use the grant
records.spatial_condition: Slot 1 offers faster access but one rear reader; slot 2 offers two readers but more exposure
records.payoff_owner: Copycat owns proxy trigger; Good Boy owns supplied stats; each other Good unit owns received stats
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Reserve aligned recipients and choose between Copycat space or a direct Good Boy death layout.
records.counterplay: Transform, targeted spell, backline access and initiative can remove supplier or proxy before resolution.
records.failure_explanation: Show attack opportunity, rear links, supplier death, eligible recipients and excluded self.
records.transferability: Proxy triggers require explicit source, recipient and no-self-feedback rules.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not let Good Boy buff itself or combine mutually exclusive slot plans for free.
records.project_question: Should project trigger proxies duplicate an effect, accelerate it or consume it once?

records.version_scope: pre-67.4 complaint and immediate post-67.4 observation
records.rule_support: 67.4 added 'other' to Good Boy specifically to stop self-reinforcing Copycat, Trophy Hunter and Phoenix Feather lines; Magic Sword affects slot 1 and Echowood reads team stat gains as a recipient.
records.practical_support: Players describe the old loop's limited targeting answers and, after the patch, a large drop in visible Copyboy play while naming Medusa, Cupid, Pigomorph and Smite as answers.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Tournament absence in one discussion is not proof the build ceased to exist, and Magic Sword slot 1 cannot simultaneously grant Copycat a costless two-rear layout.

records.version_scope: 338 logged TLD-era runs dated 2021-03-25 to 2021-10-28
records.rule_support: The `Filter Gabriot Imported DLC Sheet` records dates, clan pairs, Shards, Banner units, cards, Champion paths, Artifacts, seeds, videos and a victory flag for 338 logged runs: 311 TRUE and 27 FALSE.
records.practical_support: Three row-checked TRUE seeds establish that the Fire Light III, Corruptor III + Bog Chrysalis and Aggressive Edible III + Husk Hermit component chains each closed successfully at least once; guides and discussions still disagree on ease and reachability.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The catalog lacks a representative sampling frame, disclosed record-selection rule and game-wide population denominator, so its 311/27 split cannot support overall win rate, pick rate, relative strength or causality.
records.mechanism: A detailed curated catalog can prove specific outcomes occurred while remaining unsuitable for frequency or comparative-power inference.

records.failure_explanation: State the observed TRUE/FALSE counts and the missing sampling frame, selection rule and population denominator.

records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not rank clans or estimate prevalence from this 338-run catalog.

records.disagreement_or_limit: The 2023 guide only cross-checks continued historical discussion; it is removed/incompatible and does not establish current strength.

records.version_scope: 2019 mobile economy line with 2022/2025 capstone identity checks
records.rule_support: Goblin/Mech historically supplied armor/regen, Devastator owns Delayed Action Bomb, and the later patch confirms that named owner still has separately tuned damage/cooldown.
records.practical_support: The line rerolls low levels for cheap three-stars, stops around round 17, banks and levels 9/10 for Devastator, optionally bridging Mage or Assassin/Dragon; missing Devastator is an explicit terminal risk.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Exact roll rounds and trait values are 2019-only; current Legendary availability uses newer rules.

records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not let early defense guarantee a late payoff without a reachable owner.
records.project_question: What project signal tells players that a capstone search is no longer rational?

records.version_scope: 2019 item practice through 2025 holder rules
records.rule_support: Blade Mail converts received damage into holder retaliation, Guardian Shield grants nearby Armor when activated, Demon Gloves converts holder damage to pure and Twin Fangs selects same-name secondary targets.
records.practical_support: Redaxe Chief taunt plus Blade Mail, Water Spirit's concentrated item package and modern holder-bound effects all name the supplier, holder, trigger and final action.
records.disagreement_or_limit: These mechanics come from different eras and are structural examples, not one legal current loadout.

records.version_scope: 2025-05 Ancestor update
records.rule_support: Ancestor[2] makes each Ancestor steal 50+2% of the nearest enemy's max HP every five seconds and heal itself; Ancestor[4] grants every ally an effect that, whenever that ally's total healing received exceeds 100, deals equal pure damage to nearby enemies, capped at 300 per instance with a stated five-second cooldown.
records.practical_support: This is a defense/sustain-to-output bridge implemented as an effect on each ally with local nearby targets, not evidence of one team-shared healing pool.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The official text does not define how total healing received accumulates or resets, nor whether the five-second cooldown is team-global, per-unit or owned elsewhere; older sources only contextualize explicit converters.
records.mechanism: Each ally receives a local healing-received reader that can schedule capped pure damage around that ally when the stated threshold is exceeded.
records.engine: Ancestor[2] self-healing suppliers plus Ancestor[4] ally-local readers
records.state_resource: Per-ally total healing received, threshold greater than 100, per-instance cap 300, stated five-second cooldown with unresolved owner, and nearby enemies
records.trigger: An individual ally's total healing received exceeds 100
records.scope: Every ally receives the effect; damage originates around that ally and affects nearby enemies
records.payoff: Pure damage equal to that ally's qualifying total healing received, subject to the per-instance cap
records.survival: Ancestor[2] self-healing and other healing still restore the affected units
records.spatial_condition: Ancestor[2] reads the nearest enemy; Ancestor[4] damages enemies near the ally whose reader triggers
records.payoff_owner: Ancestor synergy grants the effect; each affected ally supplies the local read/origin, while cooldown storage ownership remains unresolved
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Four-trait investment needs enough healing across useful allies without assuming their reads pool together.
records.counterplay: Healing reduction, burst before a local read, spacing from a healed ally and pressure during the stated cooldown attack different links.
records.failure_explanation: Report the affected ally, its healing-received value, threshold result, per-instance cap, nearby targets and cooldown state while marking cooldown owner/accumulation reset unresolved.
records.transferability: Project healing converters must choose local versus shared accumulation, reset semantics, cooldown owner, cap and target origin explicitly.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not collapse all allied healing into one team ledger or assume every heal immediately damages every enemy.
records.project_question: Will project converters read effective or attempted healing, accumulate or evaluate per event, and store cooldown per ally or globally?

records.version_scope: S20 2022 with 2025 pool-rewrite boundary
records.rule_support: S20 Soul Clan[2] turns two grids into Soul Springs; each piece placed on a Soul Spring receives 18% of the total Max HP and ATK of deployed Soul Clan pieces, and a contributor's corresponding bonus share disappears when it dies.
records.practical_support: It is a team-stat-to-designated-cells structure with up to two beneficiaries; a player may reserve one Spring for a main carry, but single-recipient concentration is a strategy rather than the base rule.
records.disagreement_or_limit: It does not read arbitrary allies, Defense or permanent totals; Extended/Public pool rules around S20 were later removed.
records.mechanism: Two designated battlefield cells each aggregate eligible live contributors into their current occupant, allowing zero, one or two beneficiaries.
records.engine: Soul Clan supplier set plus two Soul Spring readers
records.state_resource: Eligible live Max HP/ATK, 18% ratio, two designated cells and zero-to-two occupants
records.trigger: Battle state changes or a contributing Soul Clan dies
records.scope: Deployed Soul Clan totals to each occupant of the two Soul Spring cells
records.payoff: Bonus Max HP and ATK on up to two occupants
records.survival: Contributor death dynamically removes its corresponding share
records.spatial_condition: A beneficiary must occupy one of the two Soul Spring cells
records.payoff_owner: Contributors supply stats; each Spring converts; each occupant owns its resulting attacks
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Spend roster slots on suppliers only while one or both chosen occupants justify them.
records.counterplay: Kill contributors, displace or deny either occupant, or focus the beneficiary using the stronger carry role.
records.failure_explanation: Show ineligible supplier, dead contributor, empty or wrong Spring, and which of the two occupants received each bonus.
records.transferability: This models team stats feeding designated slots; concentrating one slot on a carry is optional strategy, while the source rule supports up to two recipients with dynamic invalidation.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy the 18% value, collapse two Springs into one, or permit self-amplifying arbitrary team Defense.
records.project_question: Should a project team-stat relic support one chosen recipient or multiple designated recipients, and should recipients be excluded from the supplier set?

records.disagreement_or_limit: Civet battle-start copies and Cave graveyard returns are separate mechanisms and do not inherit Insectoid rules.

records.version_scope: 2020 Water Shaman before 2021-03 rework
records.rule_support: The developer says old Shaman[4] nearly lacked counterplay against a single core and was overly random; the replacement transforms dead Shaman into cost+1/+2 units after 2.5 seconds, inherits HP percentage but not item/synergy, and can only be interrupted by death.
records.practical_support: The official 2020 Water Shaman build is therefore a pre-rework artifact; new opponents can attack the transformation window and transformed target selection.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The developer diagnosis explains the motivation but does not prove the replacement is perfectly balanced.

records.spatial_condition: Replacement occupies the transaction's board context; exact collision arbitration is not inferred
records.payoff_owner: Shaman synergy owns transform; new unit owns later actions

records.version_scope: 2021-08 Cave Prodigy

records.practical_support: The effect needs a valuable prior death, a legal nearby cell and protection for the caster; multiple same-name dead units remain separate graveyard entries.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Tie order among equal sale-cost candidates and inheritance fields beyond the stated exclusions remain unresolved.

records.version_scope: S16 2022 through 2025 fear rate limit
records.rule_support: Martialist converts part of non-pure immediate damage into five-second pure DOT that cannot kill; Egersis[6] extends death four seconds with action/target restrictions; Kira's Wrath self-damages but cannot kill; Night Demon Fear has a six-second internal cooldown.

records.disagreement_or_limit: These mechanics span versions and are a guard taxonomy, not one concurrent composition.
