records.version_scope: 2019 historical builds plus 2021-2025 converter rules
records.rule_support: Knight mitigation, Evil Knight's named shield-break damage, Mage resistance debuff, Marine resistance, pure damage, Ancestor's ally-local healing-received reader and Fear use separate states; only named rules convert healing, holder damage or shield break into output.
records.practical_support: Knight+Glacier wins through protected carries, Mage through spell owners, and Ancestor through capped ally-local readers; none proves a universal Ice/Earth Shield, a shared team healing ledger or free Defense-to-Attack formula.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Ice Shield, Earth Shield and team bonus-Defense conversion are project design questions; Ancestor accumulation/reset and cooldown ownership are not specified by the source.
records.mechanism: Survival, affinity/status and payoff conversion are independent axes until an explicit bridge connects them.
records.engine: Defense supplier plus optional typed reader/converter
records.state_resource: Shield/mitigation, named break event, damage school, status, per-ally healing read, recipient, cap, cooldown and slot
records.trigger: Gain, mitigate, break, read or convert a named state
records.scope: Holder, group, ally-local reader or explicitly designated recipient
records.payoff: Survival or separately authored damage
records.survival: Defense remains useful even when no converter is present
records.spatial_condition: Nearby enemies, designated cells and AOE shape constrain value
records.payoff_owner: Supplier, converter, recipient and final attacker remain distinct; Ancestor cooldown owner is unresolved
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A converter consumes trait, item, relic, cell or unit opportunity.
records.counterplay: Pure damage, cleanse, healing reduction, backline access, displacement and cap/cooldown pressure.
records.failure_explanation: Show eligible source value, reader, recipient, cap, cooldown, target and final owner, preserving unresolved ownership where the source is silent.
records.transferability: Project can share shield lifecycle across affinities without collapsing elemental rules.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not grant arbitrary team defense as uncapped free carry damage or merge local healing reads into a global pool.
records.project_question: Should the proposed team-defense converter read bonus-only values, exclude itself and snapshot at combat start?

records.version_scope: 2019 item/build practice through 2025 rule rewrites
records.rule_support: Items attach to holders, Water Spirit owns its spell, Soul Clan suppliers feed the occupants of two designated Soul Spring cells, Ancestor grants every ally a local healing-received reader with nearby damage origin, and PVE packages alter spatial validity.
records.practical_support: The retained builds fail through different broken links: no copies, wrong economy phase, wrong holder, missing Mana/capstone, no legal cell, dead supplier, resistance or bad formation.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Internal simultaneous-event ordering beyond documented death and cell guards remains unresolved; Ancestor accumulation/reset semantics and five-second cooldown ownership are also not specified.
records.mechanism: Supplier, state, reader, converter, recipient, target and final event form a reportable lineage.
records.engine: Typed event ancestry
records.state_resource: Source id, version, holder, eligible contributor, local versus shared state, cell, cooldown owner, cap and target
records.trigger: Recruitment decision or combat event succeeds/rejects
records.scope: Run report and combat log
records.payoff: Explain why a build produced or failed to produce output
records.survival: Readable failure supports adaptation instead of blind rerolling
records.spatial_condition: Formation, radius, facing, both designated Soul Spring cells, vacancy and each Ancestor reader's local origin are recorded
records.payoff_owner: Final attacker/caster/summon owns damage while supplier/converter attribution is retained; unresolved cooldown ownership stays explicit
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Use reports to distinguish bad luck from an invalid or overcommitted line.
records.counterplay: Opponents can target supplier, reader, either Soul Spring recipient, local healed ally, resource, space or cadence separately.
records.failure_explanation: Emit missing/blocked/exhausted/cooldown/no-target/no-cell/dead-owner/version-mismatch reasons, including which Soul Spring occupant or ally-local reader was affected.
records.transferability: Project systems need event lineage across shields, elements, summons, items and relics.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not aggregate all damage under the trait/relic that amplified it or collapse ally-local healing reads into one team pool.
records.project_question: What is the minimum lineage retained in project battle reports without overwhelming players?

records.version_scope: 2025-12 Demo through 2026-07 formal release
records.rule_support: Developer-marked replies establish a short Demo period with XP/rank and layered base-stat progression; the complete formation post explicitly labels itself DEMO version, while the only formal-release review is dated after the July launch.
records.practical_support: The six-member reverse-placement build is usable only as a March 2026 Demo case; the current review supports a broad gold/level/skill-tree loop but no current formation.
records.disagreement_or_limit: There is no public patch chain, current guide or client verification linking the Demo build to formal release.
records.mechanism: Release boundaries limit how far a practical build may travel across versions.
records.engine: Dated source and product-state resolver
records.state_resource: Demo/full-release state, source date, build details and current corroboration
records.trigger: Apply a historical build to a current design claim
records.scope: Research corpus and build labels
records.payoff: Version-correct retention without inventing current meta
records.survival: The historical mechanism remains analyzable inside its Demo period
records.spatial_condition: The two-row formation is retained only for the Demo
records.payoff_owner: Developer posts own stated rules; player owns the build observation; researcher owns the version boundary
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Do not spend current-design confidence on an unverified formal-release roster.
records.counterplay: Require a current rules or practical source before promoting the build.
records.failure_explanation: Report Demo-only, missing current corroboration and unsupported field rather than silently blending periods.
records.transferability: Every project build example should carry product/version scope.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Formal release does not retroactively validate a Demo strategy.
records.project_question: Which historical mechanics remain useful after their exact balance context expires?

records.rule_support: The developer distinguishes base stats from final calculated stats and names character rank, character upgrades and stat upgrades as contributing layers; a +2 base value can be multiplied into a much larger final difference.
records.practical_support: Players who compare the displayed +2/+5 directly with a 70+ final stat can undervalue the rank choice or misunderstand a small visible change after upgrades.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No complete formula, operation order, rounding, cap or formal-release value table is published; +20/+40/+80 are examples.
records.mechanism: A base-stat modifier is amplified by separate progression multipliers before final combat use.
records.engine: Rank reward plus stat/character upgrade layers
records.state_resource: Base HP/Attack, rank, character upgrade, stat upgrade and final calculated stat
records.trigger: Gain a rank base-stat reward or purchase an upgrade
records.scope: One character and one named stat
records.payoff: Larger final HP or Attack than the face-value base increment
records.survival: Base HP follows the same layered distinction where selected
records.spatial_condition: No spatial condition is established for the stat calculation
records.payoff_owner: The character owns final stat; each progression layer owns its modifier
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Gold and time spent on character/stat upgrades amplify base rewards but create a bottleneck when upgrade branches cap.
records.counterplay: Scaling pressure can be answered only after the target and formula are visible; no enemy stat counter is documented.
records.failure_explanation: Show base change, each multiplier layer and final delta separately.
records.transferability: Project converters must name base, bonus or final input and snapshot timing.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not read +2 base Attack as flat +2 final Attack or infer multiplicative order.
records.project_question: Will project items read base, bonus-only or final Health/Defense, and how will the UI preview the result?

records.version_scope: 2026-03 Demo, single-player build report
records.rule_support: The public Demo exposes six positions across front/back rows, character progression and matchups where Cleric/Archer placement changes combat duration.
records.practical_support: Possessed deploys Warrior, Cleric and Sharpshooter in back; Twin-axe Healer, Archer and Basic Mage in front; three units attack the dangerous enemy back row while durable back-row occupants absorb its pressure.
records.disagreement_or_limit: BIS, unit rankings, exact target AI and the three-Healer/three-Thief limit come from one player at about level 80 and are not formal-release statistics.
records.mechanism: Threat-direction scouting reverses conventional role placement and concentrates reachable damage on the dangerous row.
records.engine: Enemy back-row threat observation plus three back-row attackers
records.state_resource: Six slots, row, HP/Defense, target reach, rank and upgrade investment
records.trigger: Enemy dangerous back row attacks the player's back row
records.scope: One six-member Demo formation
records.payoff: Basic Mage, Sharpshooter and Archer remove dangerous rear targets before low-threat front bodies
records.survival: Warrior, Cleric and Sharpshooter occupy the pressured back row; the valuable Twin-axe Healer is moved forward
records.spatial_condition: Back: Warrior/Cleric/Sharpshooter; front: Twin-axe Healer/Archer/Basic Mage
records.payoff_owner: Each attacker owns its damage; healer and durable members own sustain, not converted offense
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Six-slot opportunity cost favors Warrior over Tank and drops Lance Mage when front-row targets have low value; exact recruitment rules are unavailable.
records.counterplay: A healer front line plus Thief back line, insufficient back-row reach or long sustain can break the route.
records.failure_explanation: Show target row, incoming source, time-to-kill, healing offset and which slot/role failed.
records.transferability: Threat direction can make a robust unit protect a nominal back line without changing its class identity.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not encode tank=front or treat this one lineup as current optimal play.
records.project_question: Which enemy packages should visibly reward reversing front/back responsibility?

records.practical_support: A durable Warrior can be more valuable in back and a high-value healer can move front when enemy access reverses the ordinary threat map.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The rank-position effects were explicitly examples/ideas, not verified final effects; the complete target algorithm is unavailable.

records.engine: Row/column state plus explicit reader

records.version_scope: 2025-12 to 2026-03 Demo with 2026-07 current review contrast
records.rule_support: The developer says the Demo was designed for roughly 30-40 minutes and had a limited upgrade tree; the formal version's sole review reports continued gold, level and skill-tree progression.
records.practical_support: Two Demo players report all content unlocking in 10-15 minutes or stats exhausting around three hours, with one long-idle run reaching six level-20 heroes and about stage 81 before upgrade costs bottlenecked.
records.disagreement_or_limit: These are two unusually long Demo samples and one formal-release review, not retention, pacing or economy statistics; the 5x80-stage plan could change.
records.mechanism: Finite authored unlocks and an escalating upgrade curve create a content horizon distinct from numerical idling.
records.engine: Gold income plus character/stat upgrades and rank XP
records.state_resource: Gold, upgrade cost, level, rank, stage and remaining upgrade nodes
records.trigger: Continue idling beyond the authored Demo horizon
records.scope: Demo account progression
records.payoff: Higher stats and temporary additional stage reach
records.survival: Healing and stronger characters were planned to extend later progress
records.spatial_condition: No economy-specific spatial condition is documented
records.payoff_owner: Player account owns currency/progression; each character owns upgrades
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Stop treating capped Demo farming as representative of full progression; no reset or alternative spending route is documented.
records.counterplay: Escalating costs and enemy sets slow progress, but exact curves are unavailable.
records.failure_explanation: Separate content exhausted, upgrade branch capped, cost bottleneck and combat composition failure.
records.transferability: A run should expose whether the player lacks content access, resources or combat structure.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not call a 30-minute Demo's three-hour plateau formal-release failure.
records.project_question: How will project progression distinguish build failure from an intentionally closed content horizon?

records.rule_support: A developer reply identifies back-to-main as an escape from long combat and says speeds above x4 became unstable; x4 itself required a stability patch.
records.practical_support: The reported 1-7 Orc+healer versus Cleric-front/Archer-back matchup resolves only after an obnoxiously long wait, while another player reports a higher-stage formation limit near level 80.
records.disagreement_or_limit: There is no automatic overtime, draw, timeout or formal-release persistence rule; the developer expected more adventurers to remove the early edge case within minutes.
records.mechanism: Manual exit bounds a sustain stalemate when simulation speed cannot safely increase without limit.
records.engine: Damage/healing balance plus observation-speed control
records.state_resource: Combat duration, healing throughput, target access, speed tier and simulation stability
records.trigger: Neither side closes the fight in an acceptable observation window
records.scope: One Demo combat
records.payoff: Player can abandon the unresolved fight without requiring unstable higher speed
records.survival: Healing and durable placement prolong both sides
records.spatial_condition: Cleric front/Archer back versus Orc/healer is the observed arrangement
records.payoff_owner: Combatants own damage/healing; speed control owns presentation; exit owns termination request
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Unlock more adventurers or change formation rather than farming one stalled matchup indefinitely.
records.counterplay: Add reachable burst, reduce sustain, retarget the healer or exit; only the exit is developer-confirmed.
records.failure_explanation: Report duration, effective damage versus healing, unreachable priority target and exit outcome.
records.transferability: Project speed tiers need deterministic validation and a separate anti-stalemate policy.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not solve simulation stability by adding unlimited speed or invent an overtime rule.
records.project_question: Which timeout/anti-stalemate rule should end a project battle while preserving failure attribution?

records.version_scope: Same-project historical reconstruction: official components dated 2023-12 and a player direction dated 2024-11; exact version continuity unknown
records.rule_support: Official patches establish Crit and Dodge passives, the Dagger tree, Ninja's four-purchases-per-round permanent Crit gain, Thrust damage on critical attacks and four Thrust skills.
records.practical_support: A later player summarizes an approach as a Payday 2-style dodge plus crit direction, while another confirms the product is a single-character autobattler.
records.disagreement_or_limit: No player source lists the complete Ninja/Thrust loadout, timing or matchup, and no source proves the 2023-12 components remained together in 2024-11; this is a bounded cross-date reconstruction from the same project, not a same-version guide or current 1.0.2 build.
records.mechanism: A shop purchase threshold accumulates permanent Crit, which can feed a critical-attack damage reader while Dodge can buy additional attack uptime if the cross-date components coexist.
records.engine: Ninja four-purchase passive plus Dagger/Thrust critical-attack triggers, combined cautiously with the later dodge-plus-crit direction
records.state_resource: Gold, per-round successful purchase count, permanent Crit, Dodge, Dagger/Thrust and skill slots; shop odds, slot count and cross-date continuity are unknown
records.trigger: Complete the fourth successful purchase in a round, then make an attack that critically strikes
records.scope: One player-controlled combat character in the same project's historical Web materials
records.payoff: More frequent critical attacks and Thrust damage events if the documented historical components coexist
records.survival: Dodge supplies the later player's survival direction but is not converted into damage
records.spatial_condition: No squad formation is evidenced; the same single character carries the documented Dagger/Thrust/skill choices, while exact slot structure is unknown
records.payoff_owner: The single combat character owns Crit, attacks and Thrust damage; Ninja passive owns the purchase-count reader
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: The documented economic condition is Gold for four successful purchases in one round; shop odds, item types, timing, alternative route and 2024 continuity are unavailable.
records.counterplay: No reliable enemy anti-crit, accuracy, dodge bypass or pressure package is documented.
records.failure_explanation: Separate insufficient Gold, fewer than four successful purchases, a missing Crit/Thrust link, insufficient Dodge survival and unknown version continuity; no enemy-specific failure is evidenced.
records.transferability: A survival axis can support a separate damage reader without making defense intrinsically offensive.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not copy the class, values or exploit, assume cross-date coexistence, or present this reconstruction as a current Steam build.
records.project_question: Which project cadence builds should couple an economic accumulator to a separately owned attack trigger and survival supplier?

records.version_scope: 2023-11 to 2023-12 Web prototype
records.rule_support: Official patches rebalance one-star weapon effects and multiple five-star weapon/armor effects, while a player reports that one- and three-star upgrade rewards remain permanent even when the equipment is not worn.
records.practical_support: The player recommends refining multiple equipment pieces and explains that +3 Weapon/Armor Tree raises the number of equipment upgrades the character may own.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The persistent-off-equipment rule is one player's historical observation; no complete item table, later confirmation, reset rule or current-version check is available.
records.mechanism: Milestone rewards persist outside the currently equipped item, turning multiple equipment trees into a portfolio bounded by upgrade capacity.
records.engine: Equipment refinement stars, persistent milestone rewards and Weapon/Armor Tree capacity
records.state_resource: Owned upgrades, current holder item, one-/three-/five-star milestones, tree capacity and investment cost
records.trigger: Refine equipment to a milestone, equip or unequip it, or expand the eligible upgrade count
records.scope: Single character's historical equipment progression
records.payoff: Accumulate persistent bonuses from more than the currently worn weapon or armor
records.survival: Armor milestones can supply durability while weapon milestones supply output, but exact effects vary by item
records.spatial_condition: No board placement; opportunity cost is equipment-holder and tree-capacity state
records.payoff_owner: Equipment milestone owns the reward rule; the single character owns retained eligible bonuses
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Pivot from only refining current gear to a multi-item portfolio when permanent rewards justify the Gold/capacity cost.
records.counterplay: Finite tree capacity and item investment constrain indiscriminate refinement; no enemy dispel or suppression is documented.
records.failure_explanation: Show whether a reward was unlocked, active while unequipped, excluded by capacity, superseded or attached to current gear only.
records.transferability: Persistent item mastery can reward horizontal investment if owner, capacity and active-versus-unlocked states remain visible.
records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not assume every star reward persists, every item is desirable or historical values survive into current builds.

records.version_scope: v0.2 rule introduced 2023-12; independent Web-player reports in 2024-01 and 2025-07
records.rule_support: The official v0.2 patch defines Ninja as permanently gaining 4% Crit after buying four items in one round.
records.practical_support: Two players independently report that attempts made with no Gold still count as purchases, allowing repeated permanent Crit gains and, in the later report, 100% Crit in the first shop.
records.disagreement_or_limit: Players call the class Rogue and Assassin rather than official Ninja; no source proves a formal rename, developer confirmation, fix, current 1.0.2 persistence or exact affected versions.
records.mechanism: A permanent stat trigger is exploitable when purchase intent increments progress before payment and item transfer successfully commit.
records.engine: Four-purchase counter, Gold transaction, item transfer and permanent Crit reward
records.state_resource: Gold, attempted versus completed purchases, per-round count, permanent Crit and reward history
records.trigger: Attempt to buy without sufficient Gold and repeat the interaction
records.scope: Historical single-character Web-prototype shop transaction
records.payoff: Illegally accumulate permanent Crit without paying the intended economic cost
records.survival: Dodge may complement the resulting build but does not cause the exploit
records.spatial_condition: Shop drag/move interaction substitutes for a successful transaction; battlefield position is irrelevant
records.payoff_owner: Shop transaction owns validation; class passive owns counter; character owns permanent Crit
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: A failed purchase must never become a zero-cost economic route or advance a build threshold.
records.counterplay: Validate funds and capacity, atomically commit payment and transfer, then emit one idempotent successful-purchase event.
records.failure_explanation: Log attempt, rejection reason, payment commit, inventory commit, counter delta and reward emission separately.

records.version_scope: Official Web-prototype patches dated 2023-12-02 and 2023-12-15

records.practical_support: Together the changes show multiple explicit controls over cross-round economy and inventory accumulation: eligibility thresholds, removal, total caps, per-type caps and cap expansion.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The developer gives no causal explanation, overflow behavior, complete potion list, player outcome or current-version confirmation, so no balance motive or success claim is inferred.

records.payoff: Preserve meaningful accumulation while exposing finite storage and reward eligibility
records.survival: Life and potion resources support continued survival but are not evidenced as direct damage conversion
records.spatial_condition: No battlefield position; capacity state governs reward legality
records.payoff_owner: Run owns Life/Gold and capacity; potion category owns count; selected reward owns expansion
records.recruitment_economy_pivot: Choose immediate resource value versus future capacity under explicit total and category limits.
records.counterplay: Eligibility checks, caps and removal of cross-round rewards bound runaway accumulation; overflow handling remains unknown.

records.incompatible_assumptions: Do not infer why the developer changed rewards, whether they were dominant or how current 1.0.2 handles overflow.

records.version_scope: Historical Demo 2–4 boundary, 2024-02 to 2024-04; component continuity is explicit rather than assumed
records.rule_support: Demo 2 defines Saboteur as a battle-start ranged counter that reduces Attack and may convert ranged to melee, and Poisoner as a death trigger that removes Health from its killer; Demo 4 changes Ahnk to affect the first unit to die, while Demo 10 later changes Saboteur and Poisoner tiers/base stats.
records.practical_support: A player attempting one-unit Demo runs got closest with Saboteur plus Ahnk, repeatedly lost to Poisoners, added Armor, passed that immediate obstruction and still failed to complete the run.
records.disagreement_or_limit: The post does not give stage, unit level, Armor amount, shop timing, purchase/upgrade/sale path or Ahnk outcome; Ahnk's first-death rule is documented after the post, so this is an adjacent-version failure slice rather than a same-build success guide or retained economy closure.
records.mechanism: A battle-start ranged suppressor forms a one-slot challenge engine, while a killer-reading death trigger attacks that solo owner's Health and exposes the limit of a pure Armor pivot; the record remains deliberately incomplete as a build economy.

Text alone does not identify the Scouts' team or prove they caused the later roll. The player only observes that Trapper's stated three damage seems not to occur in one fight; without frame-by-frame or official confirmation this is not a proven bug, prevalence claim, current behavior or exact eighth-turn endpoint.

The player buys, sells, merges and rerolls; after reading Trapper and later mentioning summoning Scouts, the player obtains a second Trapper, upgrades it and gives food, without enough evidence to claim the Scouts caused that choice.
